title: Beautiful, Gentle Cream - So Simple & So Nice - Great For Dry Skin & Sensitive Skin
text:
(Ingredients list is at the bottom of this review.)

I am really loving the TINAZANA Vegan Bakuchiol Comforting Cream (2.7oz / 80ml). Only 9 ingredients. It is so good. Truly comforting and non-irritating. Even when my skin is already in an irritated state.

This is a beautifully thick, rich, white moisturizing cream. Yet, somehow it feels decently lightweight and comfortable on the face and neck. Not lightweight like a gel cream, by any means. But comfortable. This cream glides onto the face and neck smoothly, and it soaks into the skin quickly; But it doesn't disappear. It leaves a lasting, soothing, comforting layer of moisture and hydration on the surface of the skin. It helps to lock-in the moisture and hydration from the previous steps in my skincare routine, and leave my skin feeling so lovely and comfortable.

The scent is extremely slight. It is herbal, but it's almost undetectable, unless you're really seeking after the scent.

The packaging is a beautiful yellow glass jar with a beige twist-off lid. It feels very nice in the hand, and the cream feels luxurious on the face. Much more expensive than it is. The 80ml size is excellent for the price.

The addition of gentle, anti-aging Bakuchiol is also a big win with zero irritation. Plus, Shea Butter for maximum moisture. I layer gentle, hydrating, soothing, calming toners and serums underneath this cream, and I get excellent glowy, dewy results.

I use this cream day and night, as I have dry, sensitive skin. I imagine many skin types might like this for day or night, especially during colder months.

If you have sensitive skin, and you cannot use most skincare products (like me), this is likely going to be for you.

Overall, I'm highly impressed. Why did it take me so long to find this? This cream is so beautifully simple. It's truly an amazing find for someone like me, who struggles with sensitive skin. I will definitely repurchase, and I'm looking forward to trying more simple, gentle products from Tinazana.

I highly recommend this cream to anyone and everyone.

INGREDIENTS:

Water, Butyrospermum Parkii (Shea) Butter, Butylene Glycol, 1,2-Hexanediol, Polysilicone-34, Isononyl Isononanoate, Caprylic/Capric Triglyceride, Ethyhexylglycerin, Bakuchiol.

text:
I ordered this eye serum to add on to my skincare routine. I am 26, and my skin is reaching the point where it no longer "bounces back" quite like it used to! My current routine is fairly simple - cleanse with Cetaphil and moisturize with the standard Olay moisturizer. I also use a mild retinol product every other night.

I first used this eye serum in the evening after cleansing, but before moisturizing. Unfortunately, my first impression of the product was a burning/stinging sensation. It subsided after a minute after I moisturized, and did not leave any residual redness. I chalked it up to my skin acclimating to a new product. I skipped retinol the next evening and tried it again two days after my first attempt. Same results. After a third round of skipping retinol (and waiting 3 days) and trying again with the same stinging result, I decided that this product simply does not work with my skin. For the most part, I do not have any issues with skin sensitivity, so I'm not sure what was going on with this product. I wish that I could have used it for a longer period of time to see how effective it was, but it was too uncomfortable.

title: Too good
text:
It is often claimed that periorbital dark circles are caused by tiredness or working too hard or even just staying up late. While this can be true, the truth is that your genes play a huge role here. So what exactly is happening when you get dark circles under or around your eyes?

Simply put, periorbital dark circles are a result of the thin layer of skin below your eyes showing the blood vessels and the blood they contain more clearly than anywhere else on your body. (For reference, this skin around your eyelids, called periorbital skin, is on average about 0.5 mm thick compared to an average of about 2 mm thick on most of the rest of your body.)

Now, as you may or may not already know, the reason veins often look blue isn’t because the blood inside them is blue; it’s because your skin/subcutaneous tissue only lets blue/violet wavelengths of light pass through it. As a result, only blue light is reflected back and the veins look, well, bluish. (Veins often won’t appear blue if a person has darker or lighter skin. Rather, the veins tend to appear green or brown. On the other hand, people with extremely light skin, such as albinos, will typically have veins that show up as dark purple or dark red, more closely resembling the actual color of the blood running through the veins.)

It’s the exact same concept with the skin below your eyes. Those dark bluish circles are (usually) just the result of light being reflected back off of the blood vessels sitting just below the surface of that incredibly thin patch of skin. This is the same reason facial bruises are more prominent below or around the eyes; the thin skin just shows the blood from the ruptured blood vessels a little bit more clearly.

Again, as you may or may not know, as we age, our skin loses its elasticity and ability to regenerate and as a result, it becomes thinner. This is why more often than not, elderly people will have rather prominent periorbital dark circles regardless of how much they sleep. As with those who are genetically predisposed to having thinner skin below the eyes, it’s just biology.

text: I'm going to give the Etae line 4 stars. I can achieve a blow out using other products that are just as effective. They key to having straight hair, if you're not using Etae, is to shampoo once with a clarifying shampoo, then use a shampoo and conditioner that reviitize the hair. Use a heat protectant, leave-in conditioner to add moisture, blow dry and flat iron. Of course a good blow drier and flat iron are essential, as they save you time and less stress on the hair. Now, back to Etae. When I originally used this product, I thought it was a waste of money as my hair didn't look any different than my normal thermal straightening routine, plus it took more time with the extra step of letting the caramel sit for 20-30 minutes.  However, since I invested in the product, I am going to use it. It was 2 months or so before I used the product again. This time, I let the caramel sit on my hair for an hour while I cleaned around the house. Oh, and prior to the caramel, I did a pre-conditioning treatment to detangle my hair from a rod set. My hair felt different after rinsing the caramel. It was softer than I remembered from the 1st use. I applied heat protect spray and leave-in conditioner sparingly. At the end of the process, my hair felt soft and easy to blow dry and flat iron. Could it be the pre-Condish treatment? Because I modified the steps, I can't say 100% that Etae is 5 stars. title: Proprietary Formula??!! Beware!
text:
I do NOT recommend this product!! It contains a “special formula contains perfumer's alcohol and other proprietary ingredients” as stated in its description, which I overlooked! I’m sorry but if this product uses “proprietary ingredients” it is unacceptable! With people’s allergies and sensitivities to different chemicals (especially) I believe that some of the “proprietary ingredients” should be labeled!! Even extremely large corporations like C***ke for one, who do have a proprietary/ “secret” formula for their flavored syrup list ALL the other ingredients in their products! I realize that this item is from a small company, HOWEVER! This would have been used in conjunction with my essential oils to create my scented items for my customers, my friends, and my family! I CANNOT use and do NOT recommend a cosmetic component such as this specific product for use nor purchase!

I ended up using a 1:1 ratio of distilled water to high proof grain alcohol (173 proof/ approximately 76% alcohol) [the highest proof alcohol legal in my state, some states allow for higher proof vodkas and grain alcohols, the higher the proof, the better] with my oils in an amber, pump style bottle and just reminded people (and printed on label) to shake well before use.

I contacted Amazon and explained the situation, as the item is listed as “non- returnable”, (I believe due to its flammability [although it came via USPS!!!]) and received a refund from Amazon! Thank you Amazon for understanding!

title: The smell isn’t bad, but it is not good either
text:
This is a very small amount of mud. The inside dimensions of the bottle are approximately 1.5” tall by less than 2” diameter. When I opened the bottle and removed the safety seal, the mud was to the top of the bottle. The directions include a step to stir before applying the mud. When I stirred it, I found there was a large air bubble and the bottle was only about half full. A little of this mud goes a long way, so this small amount will go further than some other facial masks.

As per the instructions, I washed and dried my face before application. The AntiAging MegaMud goes on very smoothly. It has a strong minty smell that becomes less overwhelming with time and is partially replaced with other smells that aren’t entirely pleasant. The smell isn’t bad, but it is not good either.

The mud made my skin sting immediately, but it became less intense until I washed off the dried mask. I had removed the mask and I felt my face burning still about 5-10 minutes later, so I washed my face again using cleanser. I was fortunate that there was only the burning sensation and not a significant amount of reddening.

The box says the peptides relax muscle tension by inhibiting the release of neurotransmitters released by the brain. I'm not sure how I feel about having a topical beauty product interfering with my neurotransmitters. I'm probably getting new lines as my brow furrows trying to wrap my brain around this concept.

From the company website (https://www.viacosmedics.com/product/megamud/), this is a list of Ingredients: Deionized Water, Kaolin, Propylene Glycol, Montmorillonite (Bentonite), Glycerin USP, Magnesium Aluminum Silicate, Butylene Glycol, Carbomer, Polysorbate-20, Palmitoyl Oligopeptide, Palmitoyl Tetrapeptide-7, Acetyl Hexapeptide-8, Sodium Hyaluronate, Cucumis Sativus (Cucumber) Extract, Camelia Sinensis (Green Tea) Extract, Matricaria Recutita (Chamomile) Flower Extract, Symphytum Officinale (Comfrey) Extract, Ananas Sativus (Pineapple) Extract, Cucurbita Pepo (Pumpkin) Extract, Aloe Barbadensis Leaf Juice, Alpha Lipoic Acid, Algae Extract, Punica Granatum (Pomegranate) Extract, Calendula Officinalis (Marigold) Flower Extract, Argania Spinosa (Argan) Kernel Oil, Squalene, Eucalyptus Globulus (Eucalyptus) Leaf Oil, Phenoxyethanol, Caprylyl Glycol, Potassium Sorbate, Hexylene Glycol

From the other reviews, I thought I would like this product. After a certain age, many of us probably hope for that product that really will combat wrinkles and give us just a little more youthful appearance. I can’t imagine spending over 20 dollars for such a tiny amount of product that makes my skin burn and may or may not have anti-aging properties. For now, I’ll just have to settle for having my beauty come from within. Not such a bad thing anyway.

The good news is that this product was provided at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review.

title: Very good
text: I have something called Horner's Syndrome, it's some kind of crazy bizarre nerve damage in which part of my face is really dry and doesn't perspire and other areas perspire way too much. Crazy. It also makes one pupil appear small and the other is noticeably larger, so creepy, but the product can't do anything to help me with that. I decided to try this Mehron Skin Prep Pro, to see how well it could help me with the areas that perspire too much. I poured out a very small amount onto a stainless steel makeup palette that I have and decided to use an eye shadow brush to apply it, I only apply the Skin Prep only to parts of my face that have always had the problem. Generally, I start to apply my makeup and need to stop 3-4 times during process to gently blot the same 4 overly sweaty sections, lightly dust powder, sit with a fan, think breezy thoughts, etc. I was careful not to paint the Skin Prep on the alternate, dry areas, those areas do not perspire and can develop a parched, peely appearance. I waited a few seconds for the Skin Prep to dry on my face before continuing with my makeup. I've only used it 4 times so far, but, touch wood, it seems to be working. My makeup has had a more even application and appearance, even before I was done putting makeup on, I feel like my tone was more even and looked better. When it comes to the mirror, we notice things in so much greater detail than anyone else ever would, I realize no one else may ever notice the difference I notice. It certainly has helped a bit with my bizarre harlequin sweaty vs dry issue I've got going, even if no one else ever notices it, that little improvement means something to me.

I first tried this when I was about 2 days out from having shaved my legs. The razor did not remove most of the stubble - I think it's just to short. However, I have always struggled to shave the back of my thighs in the shower, and thus the hair there is longer and finer. This razor did a good job on that hair, though I had to go over it a few times from different directions - it definately cuts best when going against the grain, and the hair on the back of my thighs and underarms seems to grow at all different angles, so I had to shave from all different angles.

While I don't believe this can become my only razor, I am keeping it because a) it does well on longer, finer hair and is easier to use in areas I can't see well, like the back of my thighs. b) It does a good enough job that I'm keeping it for those times when I got lazy, didn't shave, not suddenly find myself going somewhere and needing a quick dry leg shave. If it just got those shorter hairs better, so I could use it every 2-3 days, I would love it.

title: Nice Masks, but Watch Pricing!
text:
I purchased a multi-pack (direct from South Korea) that contains all of the types. They are different in that the essence is not at all watery, but rather a very thick gel. The masks can easily been worn for close to an hour before all the jelly is absorbed out of it. The overall fit is good, and there are enough cuts to fit a variety of face shapes.

The results are nice, and each mask does deliver what it sets out to do. The reason for four stars instead of five is because the remaining gel stayed very tacky (at least on me), even a few hours after removing it. So much so that I wound up wiping the remainder off with a damp cloth before finishing up with my other products. Products do tend to hover over my skin, rather than completely absorbing. So this observation may not apply if you are lucky enough to have the type of skin that absorbs products easily.

Are they worth trying? Yes, absolutely. Are they worth $10 each (the price on the page I'm reviewing is 10 for $99.99)? NO WAY. You can find a 10 pc pack for under $20 (including shipping), and I got a 5 pc pack for $12 and change.

title: Such an amazing and gentle shampoo
text:
I think at last this is my Holy Grail! Having finally understood 8 years ago that regular shampoos were poison to my head, and first trying Wen, which was ok but expensive, then various non SLS shampoos, also just OK, and finally this which is truly in a class by itself- if you read the ingredients.
Very nice stuff, and so super gentle. The smell is pleasant and mild, does not smell like cheap perfume. My only complaint is that the product is very thick and the pump does not work.
I have used this now several times, every other day for the last 2 weeks and my hair is definitely improved. You could certainly use it every day if you so desired. I don't think conditioner adds anything to this, so I probably will use up the conditioner around my house and not re-purchase. This product makes a good 2 in one, for those who like to simplify their routine and de-clutter the bathroom. It is a little expensive, but much less expensive than many other products .You can save money by not washing your hair every day as you probably don't need to, unless you work a very dirty job. I used a quarter size dollop for my very thick, shoulder length hair, but you could probably use less. A bottle should last a couple of months or more.
It was the list of ingredients that truly sold me. This has a very gentle cleaner in it and Wen does not. I have suffered with bushy and coarse hair my entire life and this has actually helped. That being said, I have also been gradually shortening and layering my hair to accommodate its' natural flow.

I wanted to add some length to my short and damaged hair so after some research decided to purchase tape in extensions. I scheduled an appointment with the professional who could install these. After 7 days my scalp was itchy and the bumps were all over the scalp due to the glue in the tape-ins. At that point, I just wanted them out. Thank God I was able to find a good tape in remover. Ladies these are not real human hair extensions. Save your money. I attached the picture for reference.

title: Does a great job in comparison to soaking off.
text:
I hate the soaking process. My hands end up freezing and I just don't have the patience to sit for as long as it takes to soak my gel polish off. So then I end up using a file to remove it - it works but it is very time consuming and at least my hands are "doing" something. Plus, sometimes I go a little overboard and end up with thinning out my actual nail. Oops! And owie!

This is where Gel Nail Polish Remover comes in. Before buying this product I read many, many reviews on various similar products as well as this one. The "worst" reviews I saw complained of this product causing nails to curl. As it so happens, exactly as I thought, the cause of nails curling from this product is THIN NAILS. I had previously gone a little rough on one of my pinky nails, thinning it out to the point that putting pressure on the nail hurt. Of course, that nail curled up when I applied this product. My other nails, all still mostly standard thickness, were fine. Also, it is very important to note that the nail does relax back to normal shape after removal. At least, mine did.

I had also read in another review the suggestion to apply one coat, leave on for 5 or 6 minutes then apply another coat. I can concur that this is the best practice. It is also important to remember to user your nail file to rough up/remove the top coat. If you forget that step, it won't do a darned thing!

I have now used this product no less than 3 times, on both my hands and feet, and can say that the nail curling only happened on the first application. It has not happened again with additional polish removal sessions. Again, it is important to not skip the filing off of the top layer and to apply multiple times, allowing ample time for the product to work between applications.

I absolutely recommend this product just so long as you fully understand the limitations and HOW to use it. Great value for the price, too!

text:
Top it off (gloss) is a big hit. It does a great job with sealing your gel manicure and lasting a long time. I appreciate that isn’t too thick and gloppy.

The matte top coat is an odd duck. It’s not suuuuper-matte, but it works really well for my purposes. I have a crazy nail (after a little accident) with a thin vertical strip that constantly splits. If you imagine that would be painful, you would be correct, so I cover that nail in clear gel polish. The matte-ness is pretty close to the sheen of a natural nail so it’s not immediately obvious unless you look super close (and even then). So I don’t have to wear nail polish if I don’t want to, but if I do, I can just paint regular polish over this. And if you use a non-acetone polish remover, you can even switch shades without this coming off.

The only reason I knock off a star is because the matte isn’t impervious, and it will pick up fabric dyes and other colorants fairly easily. Sometimes I’ll look down and notice that one nail is looking pretty grey (like the lenses on sunglasses), which is frustrating.

Take off is not too bad. Those crazy clips that hold cotton pads to your fingertips and some acetone will make short work of this in about 15 minutes with no scratching that damages your nail plate. People whine that gel is bad for your nails, but if I remove it properly, it doesn’t hurt them a bit, at least not in my experience. In fact, my nails grow pretty long and strong with this on.

title: Combo pack, QB Pro 2019 and Payroll Enhanced
text:
If you have used QuickBooks before, you already know what you are getting. The product works, it doesn't change much year to year, but I will say it has been more stable than in the past, with less crashing and weird issues. Desktop Pro 2019 has a few new features like invoice tracking, and checking for unpaid vendor bills but if you have 2017 or 2018 you don't really need to upgrade to be honest.

However, if you do want to upgrade and you are also looking to use QuickBooks for payroll, this is a decent option because it includes one year of Payroll Enhanced. The service itself is easy to use and ties in to QuickBooks directly, which is the main reason to use it in my opinion. The service has to be activated but once you do it, you are good for a year. Even a novice can start paying employees, and I found the payroll software to be easy to use once I got it all set up and running.

I'm giving this software 3 stars because although it works, Intuit always seems to do the bare minimum it can get away with and still call it a new release. It's been like this for years and although the software is solid, the company and philosophy behind the way they market and sell their products is average at best. They keep trying to push people to QB Online, which is terribly unprofessional and doesn't work with a lot of commercial banking options. Quickbooks Desktop Pro is still the best and easiest option for a small to medium sized company, and anyone can use it with just a little training. Payroll Enhanced ties in to QB and is easy to use once you get through the setup process, which can take up to an hour. If you have more than 15-20 employees, I'd recommend going to an outside service for payroll although you can certainly use payroll enhanced, but it will cost you per employee to use and at some point it's less expensive to use a company like ADP to process payroll. I use QB every day and I've learned to tolerate its quirks. QB Desktop Pro 2019 is an improvement over 2017 and 2018, although it's a small one and only recommended if you are really looking for the few new features it adds.

title: Sonicare is the best hands down!
text:
This review is for people who are trying to decide on the Sonicare or a Braun Oral B (or ANY spin brush for that matter). My previous toothbrush was an Braun Oral B, and in my experience, the Sonicare is way superior.

First of all, the Oral B has a rotating head. Well, after several uses, I've noticed that the head starts getting loose and my lips and cheeks sometimes get pinched in the gap between the head and the neck of the brush. This causes me to have to change the brush even before it's due. Also, it seems that the Oral B allows a lot of water to enter into the metal parts that make the head spin. Therefore, while brushing, the water along with toothpaste seem to clean those parts which results in dirty water in your mouth! It's not pretty sight rinsing out your mouth and toothbrush and seeing grey water in the sink!

So after dealing with spin brushes for several years, I decided to give the Sonicare a try. Besides all the hassles of the spin type brushes, most importantly, the Sonicare cleans better. I was surprised at how well it performed since I thought the Oral B was a huge step above a manual brush. But the Sonicare makes my teeth feel even *cleaner* and I love how it makes my gums feel as well! When the Sonicare first came out in the market, I knew that there was no way the head would even fit in my small mouth (with all my wisdom teeth in tact!) so that's why I never considered it before. However, the current design of the brushes is fantastic. They are compact and angled and I have no problems reaching all my teeth. I have a feeling once you try the Sonicare, you'll never go back to any other toothbrush. It's really *that* great!

text:
I am a self imposed victim of over plucking my brows, and of my lashes seeming to become shorter and more sparse as I'm aging.

I've been wanting to try some of the many lash growth serums for a long time. The first thing I tried was Castor Oil. It seemed to help my lashes grow, and look a bit thicker. I then got this LashRevive serum, and another serum at the same time. I used LashRevive on my right lashes and brow, and the other brand on the left lashes and brow. I will only be discussing results for the right eye, with the LashRevive serum in this review.

I noticed a lot of wonderful reviews for this product, lots of pictures of the bottle, but no before and after pictures.
I received my product on the 11th of June, and today is June 25th, so I have been using this product consistently for 2 weeks.

First for the lashes. I am including a picture of before and after so you can judge for yourselves. The left side is before, right side is after. I really see little difference. When I look in the mirror, I feel as though they are more noticeable, maybe a tiny bit thicker, or darker, but not by much. But as you can see, the picture reflects none of that. Maybe it's just wishful thinking. I can say that on my lower lashes, mostly toward the inner corner, I have seen growth. They are much longer. It's weird that they are only on the inside though. I do not have before/after pictures of that, as I was not expecting this to effect the lower lashes.

On to the brows. I can see a difference in my brow. It appears fuller to me. I'm a natural blonde, so the newest hairs that are growing in are very light, almost white blonde, and difficult to see in the included picture, but I do believe you can see a tiny bit of a difference. Nothing dramatic. It's enough for me to continue to use it for my brows. Again, before picture on the left, after on the right. Judge for yourselves.

Application was super easy. It's a thick, milky consistency, and has a nice large applicator brush to easily cover the lashes and brow area quickly. I experienced no irritation to the skin, or to the eye. Never felt any sort of sting or burn at all. I did have gunk in the corners of my eye in the morning, and weird white stringy stuff in my lashes. Easy enough to remove when I washed my face in the morning. I did notice what seemed like more lashes than normal actually fall out, in the beginning. Maybe it was only because I was paying more attention to my lashes though. It was about 2-3 per day. Obviously not enough to be noticeable as you can see in the before/after pic.

I'm confused with this product. I did not see enough results to give this 4 or 5 stars. But saw enough of a result on the brow to think (hope) that I may get better results with continued use, so I did not give it just 1 star. I am going to continue to use this product until I run out, and I will update this review with any positive/negative results.

I received this product for free in exchange for my review. I hope this was helpful for you.

title: Needed a little alteration, but amazing for the price!
text:
I love synthetic hair because I don't have to worry about the curls losing bounce. This wig is great for the money. Here's what I did to get it lay more natural though. Things you'll need: Verb Ghost Dry Oil, liquid concealer one shade lighter than your skin, powder concealer your correct color, eye shadow brush, mascara in the color of your natural hair, clean and dry mascara brush, scissors and tweezers.

1. First I trimmed the lace to match my hairline. (I cut off a good quarter inch of the front hair with the lace, you don't have to do this but it fits my face better this way).
2. Make the split I like on the side. Tweeze away the space in the middle of the split to make this split more noticable. At the front tweeze a triangle starting point also helps with that more natural split.
3. Put liquid concealer on the underside of the split, use eye shadow brush to brush the powder foundation on the top visible part you plucked. (Any extra powder, just shake the wig gently and it will fall away.)
4. I used the brown mascara to accent the roots of the split and roots along the front of the wig.
5. With wig in hand, spray Verb Ghost Dry Oil on the hair, shake and smooth loose hairs and tangles by hand. Synthetic hair will be soft but not shiny anymore.

Glue in place if wearing all day, otherwise just use hair spray after its tacky to stick the edges down.
(I did not glue it down before taking pics, and I did not blend my makeup into the wig, so please do not judge the edging biased on how seamless. I wanted everyone to see how it looks without these finishing touches.)

I'm very into nail art so this was one of the coolest things I've tried out in a while!
This is a pretty complete set - it includes any brush or dotter you'll really ever need. They're also in a cool case with a little info page explaining the different brushes.

- The case is sturdy and makes the set very, very giftable! It looks pretty great.
- There are 2 brushes for acrylic paint, 6 for regular nail art, 2 for gel polish, and 2 double sided dotting pen/tools. That's a pretty complete set. If you're gifting it, you could sweeten the package by including polish, a bottle of polish remover, a small painter's palette, and precision-tip q-tips! But, all the brushes are included in this set.
- The two dotting pens are double-sided so there are 4 different dotters that give you a fantastic range. Can't imagine you needing any smaller or larger ones. They also have really cool sanded wood handles. I like the feel of them.
- The brushes have an awesome range, too. They're colour-coded and labelled by type (acrylic, regular polish, gel polish).
- Now the info sheet says to use polish thinner (or rubbing alcohol for gel polish) to clean them. I tried this and it just made it clumpy (maybe my thinner isn't a good brand for it!). It specifically says to avoid acetone but I used pure acetone to clean them which worked fine EXCEPT that it stripped the paint off the handle of the brushes. NON-acetone remover cleaned the brushes, didn't damage the bristles, and didn't strip the paint so that's what I recommend, personally. Non-acetone polish remover is your best bet. Just be gentle, no matter what you use, to avoid damaging the bristles.
- Overall, I love this little set and it's a great addition to my nail art collection.

text:
Surprisingly, I really like this mask. I already tried their [[ASIN:B07VQY9ZP2 WeeklyPoint Cosmetic Saffron mask sheet]] and found it to be very messy and just okay. This one is less messy.

There are ten individually wrapped masks in this package. The instructions are in broken English but still easy to understand. I applied this mask to my clean face -- there are holes for eyes, nose, and mouth. It was somewhat wet but not dripping wet as their other mask. I prefer less solution, so this was perfect. I let it stay on for exactly 20 minutes and then removed the mask and wiped off the excess. My face felt moisturized and silky. I reveled in the soft rose fragrance the entire time.  However, the claims that it brightens the skin and protects them from wrinkles is unfounded in my opinion. On the other hand, the rose fragrance is calming and wonderful and the moisturizing effect is silky and these are my two favorite traits of this moisturizing sheet.

title: BARBER CHAIR IS OK
text:
It all started with receiving the box in terrible condition about 7 weeks ago with no protection. I was surprised that almost everything was there. It was missing a center bolt mounted under seat cushion used to maintain the seat assembly solidly on the hydraulic stand. They did not supply the bolt, nor the instructions and they had the audacity to tell me the bolt is not required. Without that bolt, if chair is lifted just 2 inches , it will fall off the base. Went to local Lowes and purchase a bolt and washer.

There were damage problems with the calf rest and the rubber trim at bottom of base which took them 6 weeks to replace and when I finally received them they were damaged in different areas. This company does not take pride in their workmanship nor their quality control. I will not contact company again with their current philosophy that they have on their products.

The Chair itself looks good and works. It lifts approximately 6 to 8 inches and also reclines which is a plus. Some areas of the material is very thin (low quality) and therefore is prone to damage from the smallest abrasion, so precaution is needed when moving chair around. It turns easily after foot rest is lifted using hydraulic lever. Seat and back cushion is comfortable but tight. Its an ok chair all around , but I would probably try a different brand next time around depending on price and presumed quality.

title: Good product but quantity misleading: Only one pen included!
text:
Is it just me? I have purchased this exact product several times--happily--in dark brown, grey brown, and chestnut (red brown). My eyebrows are, like my natural hair, about a level 4 or 5 dark brown, and the grey brown is probably the closest, though the other colors are handy for changes of color to hair and makeup. My brows are thinning, but a little filling in does the trick, and these pens are my favorite tool for the job, as they both color in where you need solid filling and can be used to make feathery strokes for a more natural brow look. This pen came with a useless little razor and three eyebrow "templates," only one of which I might consider useful (if you are new to shaping your brows).
The problem:
In the past I have received (I see now from other sellers) at least two or three pens for $6.99 to $8.99. I can't believe I paid over $8 for just one pen from this seller "Generies." Going back over the seller page, I see that indeed, by the pictures it appears that one will receive two pens. A sneaky little trick, showing the same photos as the sellers with better deals, but neglecting to include the "2 CT." If you are busy or distracted in the least, you might fall for it, as did I--and doubtless, as have many customers.
I really dislike writing negative comments, but am doing this to save others the trouble and disappointment of feeling ripped off. Needless to say, I will be buying this product from other sellers in future--the ones with the more reasonable--and honest--deals.

title: Great for touch-ups
text:
After years of electrolysis, every once in a while, I will get a stray hair that pops up. I don't really feel like driving the hour to the nearest electrologist and buying a whole session for just one hair. For this purpose, this little machine is excellent.
If you've never had electrolysis, I wouldn't recommend it. Knowing what to expect this to feel like has helped me use it effectively.
Looking to remove all the hair on your legs? Unless you want to take this on as a full time job, I wouldn't recommend it. It is very slow.
The included tweezers are next to useless. You probably have some at home that work. Use those.
Since I am not professionally trained, and this is not a professional machine, I find it is easiest to use on thick hairs. I have a very difficult time trying to use the probe on thin hairs.
Like the other reviewers, I find the beep annoying. I'm sure there could have been a better way to design this to indicate when the current is on. But at least I know it's working.
At this price, for touch-ups, it is perfect. Keep your expectations in line with the price.

text: I first learned about this sunscreen from No BS Beauty (a no-nonsense, non-sponsored skincare enthusiast on YouTube). I was looking for something with good staying power, good filters (beyond FDA archaic limits), and no scent/fragrance for both everyday and outdoor activity sun exposure.  This hits all the marks. I have maturing skin (almost 50), and use tret, so UV exposure protection is a must. I've repurchased this one throughout the year (2022). It has never failed me: long, multi-hour summer hikes, summer outdoor wedding, and now, just as an SPF make-up primer for everyday life (work, errands, etc). I would say it does leave a slight white cast on my medium-olive skin tone, but that disappears with my sheer BB cream or foundation. It leaves a not-quite matte, smooth/silky, almost powdery finish that I appreciate because, having maturing combo-skin, I cannot stand all those highly praised "dewy" sunscreens that make me look greasy moreso than "dewy."  If you're seeking "dewy," this isn't it. I wouldn't say it's matte or drying either -- it just hits the sweet spot for me. I am a bit of a skincare nerd who wants to try out lots of different sunscreens, and I have no doubt there are amazing alternatives out there, but when you find something that works? At least in my case, I end the hunt and just hit re-order. Make sure you check the seller's storefront and ratings (always recommend that when purchasing J or Kbeauty skincare products from Amazon). This one is definitely worth trying and adding to your collection!

title: Great for an electric, but still doesn't compare to fusion razor
text:
I gave this to my husband, hoping he would get hooked by even the novelty of it and use it everyday, I like a freshly clean shaven look on him and he had been slacking lately using his fusion disposables.

He's tried a few electric razors in the past but was never happy with them so has stuck to using the upper end disposables.

His take: very comfortable to hold, the heads conform to his face well and it's a comfortable shave... as long as it's very lubricated. He found he got the best feeling and closest share only when he used a lot of shaving creme/gel & had his face very well, making for quite a mess on the sink top. He liked the idea of the dispensing lotion but found he preferred his normal shaving gel and also didn't think the dispenser held enough or that it was cost effective. On the upside this is water proof so I'll get him to try it in the shower next. He also agrees with the other reviewers who said it's just not a close enough shave, and that it takes far to long. The whole idea of a electric is to speed up the process but between loading it with the conditioner, using it, adding more water, cleaning up the mess etc it was taking him 2x as long to shave at least, and with less steller results.

My take: I think his face looks better, the shave may not be as close however there are no knicks or aggrivation and his skin looks better all around. Of course I see his point on the time consuming aspect.

The booklet recommends giving it 3 weeks, I'm not sure I'll be able to talk him into that... wonder how this thing would work on my legs? ;)

title: The good, the bad and the ugly...
text:
My review consists of the good, the bad and the ugly. First,
the good - I finally found a curler that 'fits' my eyelid. Huh, you say? Well, it appears that most of the manufacturers believe I have golf balls instead of human eyes. The tool's shape is long and shallow enough of a curve to catch most of the eyelashes. It is comfortable to use, but takes a bit of practice. Once you are comfortable with the scissor motion (sorry, no other way to describe it) used to make the curl, you are rewarded with a nice, non-crimpy curl. The pad in this one is the best I have used. This tool also opens wide enough that even the most nearsighted or lush lashed amoungst us can get it close to the base of the upper lashes. The design over all is very well thought out. I recommend using an magnifying mirror if you have to use bifocals (I do). All that said, now...
the bad - there is no replacement pad and I am questioning how sanitary this is going to be in the long run. I agree completely with folks here who advise to REMOVE ALL EYE MAKEUP before use. Ain't nothing pretty about an eye infection. I am wondering out loud how to properly clean this curler to be certain it remains safe. If you are prone to sties and other types of infection, I would be asking the same questions. Which leads to...
the ugly - until you practice and are used to it (won't take long) the results are a bit odd looking. The black pad is plushier and looks to be made of silicone and not the usual hard rubber. I have found that the hard rubber pads are chiefly responsible for that weird ugly crimp you can get. Not so with this one. I mentioned before the squeezy scissor action your thumb and index finger have to use can be tricky. If you have coordination issues, well - things could get ugly.
SUGGESTIONS for use...wash your hands before use. I keep the little plastic clip to keep the tool closed. You could follow the advise of one person here to heat the tool with a dryer, but I think I may skip that. Use a makeup mirror to assist you. Practice when you have some time. Enjoy, Ladies - get out there and be lovely.

title: Well made, leak-free bottles for a healthier, greener lifestyle
text:
Since becoming a mom, I've been trying to live a greener, less toxic lifestyle. I've started cloth diapering & using un-paper towels. I've switched to natural body & laundry products. However, for some reason, I had been holding out on switching to chemical free cleaning and fabric/air fresheners. I'm not exactly sure why I was so hesitant. These bottles made making the switch fun and easy!

These bottles have both a mist and a stream spray option, as well as an option to turn off the spraying mechanism. Currently, I have one bottle filled with a 1:1 ratio of water to vinegar for use as glass cleaner. The mist option works well on my mirrors and shower doors. The mist option also works very well for both my homemade room/linen spray and my pest repellent spray. (Peppermint essential oil diluted with water and sprayed on the baseboards/around door and windows.) I use the direct stream option for my tub and tile cleaner. It works very well for spraying directly onto the grout.

At 16oz, the bottles are substantial but are not heavy in hand. The trigger is easy to squeeze, yet not flimsy. The glass itself is a gorgeous, deep cobalt blue. I keep my homemade air freshener in one of these bottles on the bathroom counter and have been asked multiple times about where I got it. They really are just so very pretty. Too pretty to be hidden under the sink like most other air freshener or cleaning supply bottles.

Often times, when you purchase cleaners from the store in inexpensive plastic bottles with these same mechanisms, the spray head tends to leak after a week or two of use. It never fails. These, however, are sturdy and seem to be much more heavy duty. I've used these bottles nearly daily and have not had any leaks whatsoever. As beautiful as these bottles are, this is what impressed me most. I'm extremely happy with this product and would highly recommend them!

title: By far best product out there. 14 years experience with colors.
text:
This is they dye to buy! I have been coloring my hair crazy colors on and off for 14 years now and I've tried absolutely every brand. I have naturally dark hair and bleach it but don't like to bleach it white as it damages it so bad it starts falling out. With this brand, I only need to get it to an orangey yellow and every color I have used looks great. I have mostly stuck with purples, blues, reds, and pinks. I just got the atomic pink for the first time thinking it wouldn't be all that great on the orange bleach job and boy was I impressed!
One thing I have learned from my experience is that the first time dying after bleaching isn't as good. It seems to always fade kind of fast expecially towards the scalp. However, a week or two later when I touch it up it seems to last forever after that. Even when it fades it does so with pretty colors.
This dye does stain everything, but I have a travertine shower floor (very porous stone) and have stained just about everything. Spraying bleach on it does the trick!
One more word of advice before I go, the directions say to leave on hair for 20 minutes or so but I just leave it on overnight (make sure to cover your pillowcases or use something you don't mind being stained) and also use a crummy towel for a day or two after you shower. People complain about it staining but that's the point- it is supposed to stick!

title: Pretty good.
text:
I bought this to upgrade my lotion dispensing Norelco that's now 5 years old. The battery on it barely lasted one shave and it lived in its charging cradle except when drying.

Since I was so used to the old cradle and how it always was in it, I liked the little clock on this. But once I noticed it lasts < month the cradle is now a relic in my junk drawer! It seriously only needs about an hour to charge fully so there is not any need for the cradle. The tiny (not a huge brick that sticks in the wall) will fit inside the cradle or the razor.

When I first used my 9160XL I really irratated my skin, even being a long time Norelco user. But it went away in about a week. I still get red spots from irratation some times but heres my trick: wait until BEFORE you shower because soap strips all the oils off your face, making it hard to glide or try using a TINY amount of shaving cream, spread so thin you can barely notice it and then go over with a splash of water. If you use alot the Norelco could choke on all the extra cream and become less effective. I hardly notice any differences in irritation when using the <S N> dial (sensitive or normal skin)

The trimer is neat but I only use it to shave my unibrow when I am too lazy to actually pluck the hairs out. The trimer + the head array pop up with a flick of a finger. I was used to pulling open the head like my old Norelco but this is spring loaded. Some how when I was store drying it (the recommend to leave it wide open to air dry out the insides) the head came off. I was frightend! But it is designed to snap on and off easily.

The plastic head cover is working like it should. I just prefer my old head cover more because it was easier to tell which side is going on the top. But it is getting easier the top nub is alot smaller the my old one. The travel case is awesome, fits it like a glove and zippers up. Be sure to leave the cover on for double protection.

Be sure to look for a brush to clean the heads before you throw away the box. The packaging is so complex it took me a while to extract all of it's contents.

More cons:
- I don't like how the heads are unprotected during air drying... I wish the cover would fit while its opened.
- Orange? Bold color for something thats mainly blue, silver and gray.
- Maybe my drain needs draino but when washing out the chamber and heads alot of my hair gets stuck to the side of my sink, requiring splashing until it all goes. But it's kinda cool filling my sink the top then start draining and look up close at all tiny hairs it cuts.

I am been using this for 4 months now.

edit, now it's been 5 years and the battery still holds a pretty decent charge. Still working really well too. Only replaced the blades once so I'd say I got my monies worth.

The shave is quick and the receptacle really does seem to catch upwards of 95% of what I'm using.

Cleaning is a cinch.
It's noisy with turbo on, but certainly not in the same vicinity as a hair dryer. It's certainly not anything that's a detraction from the shave.
The only reason I haven't given this 5 stars is because of the area just under the nose, the other reviewers that have mentioned this are correct - it's very hard to get to this area without contorting your nose and/or lip.
I simply remove the protector and do the last few hairs freehand with the open shaver or a pair of cuticle scissors.
The overall performance of this shaver more than makes up for this one shortcoming.

title: Small Bottle, Extends Color
text:
I have been using the Moroccanoil Color Care Conditioner for a couple weeks, and for the most part, it lived up to my expectations. As someone who regularly uses Moroccanoil products, I was curious to see how this one worked.

First off, the scent did not disappoint. It's lovely, as I've come to expect from Moroccanoil, however, I did find it to be a bit too faint for my liking. I've seen other reviews where people have said it's too strong, so it's all down to personal preference. The bottle is very small for the price.

In terms of performance, the conditioner does a good job of keeping my bright pink hair looking vibrant for longer. However, I did find that it wasn't as moisturizing as I would have liked. I have fine thin color-treated hair, and while the product didn't weigh my hair down or leave it feeling greasy, I didn't feel like it added much moisture either.

Overall, the Moroccan Oil Color Care conditioner works well and does what it claims to do. If you're looking for something to help extend the life of your color while also moisturizing your hair, this may not be the best fit for you if you have dry hair. However, for those with fine hair who want to keep their color looking bright, this is a good option.

The one down side to the brush is that the heat protectors on the hot bristle head are somewhat jell like. If you do not let the brush fully heat up to the temperature you would like to use, I have noticed that the brush will pull on more of your hair, possibly ripping it out.

Heck my straighter was was twice that much and is nothing compared to this hair straightening brush with my sisters hair.
All in all, if you have thin, blonde hair like myself, this brush is nice to have but huge need to upgrade your flat iron straightener. BUT if you have super curly, thick hair, you should really think about getting this brush! You will not regret it!

title: OK, but outperformed by a $10 foil electric
text:
I got this shaver in early January of 2007. For the first month or so that I had it, it worked decently. The shave was relatively close and it did get most of the hair, but it did take a few passes over the skin, and a touch-up using the on-board trimmer to get the ones it missed. I also found myself having the stretch the skin quite a bit to get a close enough shave. However, it did offer an irritation-free shave (I have sensitive skin, thus why I stay away from blade razors).

Over the next few months, though, I noticed that the shave started to get more irritating: more 'pulling' instead of cutting (had always pulled a little, but got more frequent), takes more passes to cut what it once would, etc. I changed the blades after 3 months (short period, yes, but I tried anyway). It helped a little, but it still wasn't as good as it once was. Then, I started to realize that the shaver wasn't holding as strong a charge as it once did. It would come off the charger and be 'full power' for less than one shave, and would need to go back on the charger after 6 shaves (far less than the advertised two weeks). A call to Norelco led nowhere, as they said it was 'expected' for the battery to wear down over time (4 months?).

I kept using the razor as I wasn't about to waste the $90 investment. On a trip in late July, I had forgotten to pack the shaver, so I purchased a $10 Remington battery-operated foil razor at a local convenience store. Sad to say, but from Day 1 that foil razor has outperformed the Norelco by leaps and bounds in all areas (closer shave, gets all areas better, less passes needed, etc.). Also on a sad note, the Remington is kicking the bucket (a year later), and I am forced to go back to the Norelco for the time being while I look for an acceptable foil shaver as a replacement.

In short, this razor performed decently at first, but it seems as though compared to a $10 battery operated razor, this $70 shaver isn't a good value for the investment.

text: I would give 6 stars if possible. For only $25.00 this is an extremely well engineered item. I also have an ORIGINAL Sonicare Advanced and it is nearly 13 years old now.  I learned a long time ago how damaging water can be.  My brother in law and my sister got Sonicare brushes for themselves and me for Christmas over a decade ago. Theirs went out quick, due to water and calcium buildup. All my Sonicare products I take extreme care of.  When using, I try and never let water drip down the brush head.  After use, I remove the brush head, and store it and the handle upside down.  This keeps water from going down into the device or the threads and causing problems.  If not stored upside down, not only can water get into the item, but, calcium and contaminants can leak down and get in the brush head threads.  All can be resolved by simple care and upside down storage. Of note, my original Series A over a decade old, looks like NEW from pampered care, excluding the discoloration of age. A little care goes a LONG way. A little lack of care/abuse and anything will deteriorate. With the top of the line Sonicare Diamond Clean being over $200.00 versus the HX3351 at only $25, you can't expect bullet proof.  For $300 to $400 they could make this out of aircraft aluminum like LED Flashlights and make it 100% waterproof but you wouldn't buy it, the cost would be prohibitive. title: This sponge set achieves a natural looking skin! Quality product. great value.
text:
I spent a few days before purchasing this particular silicone sponge set or any kind of silicone sponge set for that matter, but, I am very glad that I decided to give it a try! With few reviews and real life photos of the items from the customers, I hesitated to decide on ScionBeauty's sponge, but, I am a satisfied customer for the following reasons.

First of all, this is a great value for a set of 5 sponges (2 beauty blender and 3 silicone sponges). The size is not too small nor big and is perfect. Upon opening the package, I recommend washing all sponges. At least the silicone sponges. I used a very very small amount of nice hand soap and very gently washed and rinsed them well. Here are what I noticed about and did with each sponge.

** BEAUTY BLENDER:
The beauty blender indeed expand in size! I would say about 2.5 times the original size. I washed it yesterday and squeezed out excess water with a towel to make sure it doesn't build up mold inside. It did shrink, but, is still bigger than the unwashed one. And, it certainly did NOT become stiff or rip, which I was initially worried about. It became very slightly harder than the unwashed one, but, the washed one is still MUCH bouncier compared to the unwashed one. I actually like this medium level of softness/stiffness. Another reason why I hesitated to wash the blender is because I read some reviews about an inexpensive blender bleeding out pink dye. That is not the case at all about this ScionBeauty blender. At that point, I felt very comfortable using this product. When you wash it, you do need to rinse thoroughly to remove soap bubbles. If soap residue remains in the blender, the blender probably will disintegrate over time and it won't be good for your skin either. Upon arrival, the blender has a very faint smell to it. But, it does go away next day if you keep it out of a plastic bag that it comes in. Also, once you wash it, the smell completely goes away.

** SILICONE SPONGE:
It feels good against the skin! It curves well when I try to bend to fit the curves of my face, so, I can say this particular sponge is flexible. It curves but bounces back is a good way to describe it, I think. On the back side of the plastic bag this sponge set comes in, there is a sticker attached - "How to use ScionBeauty Silicone sponge." I read the instructions as well as referred to Youtube videos and online tips. You do need to dab and pat on your skin rather than glide along on your skin as they say. Then, you can successfully apply a thin and natural looking layer of liquid foundation. I like the natural look, so, this silicone sponge works well for me. Do not remove the sealing (a thin layer of silicone on the edge of the sponge). You need to use the raised side of the sponge to put foundation or any other makeup item on. I used the liquid foundation, but, all I needed was about the size (amount) of a rice grain or two and it covered about a half of my face. It did not smear (Again, dab and tap!). After I finished applying liquid foundation on my face, I again washed the silicone sponge with a very small amount of hand soap and dried with a towel. I also used the silicone sponge to apply serum and it did work extremely well. I always wasted too much with my hands soaking up the serum more than my facial skin did.

This may be a makeup fad that goes away before too long, but, I'm sure I will be using this sponge set for a long time. It was a bit disappointing that I did not receive a reply from the seller when I contacted about the warranty they mention on the Amazon product page, but, I'm sure this product will last long enough to worth the price, so, I'm ok with that in this case and decided not to deduct a star from my review. The product itself and its value still deserve 5 stars in my mind. I highly recommend this sponge set for those who are hesitating to try. It may not be your kind of item, but, if used right and if you happen to like the texture of the sponges, you will understand what I'm talking about.

I'm posting real life photos (not photoshopped, I mean) of the product, so that you can see how the sponges actually look like and how big/small they are. The sponge set does not come in a cute bag or case as you can see, but, it is good enough for yourself and casual gifting.

It is sort of a cliche, but, I DO read customer reviews very carefully before purchasing items, so, I know it is worrisome to buy an item with few reviews or from a company you have never heard of. I care about the quality over the price, but, I do care about the value, too (Is the product cost effective?). You don't have to have this sponge set, but, it really helped me and I decided to take the time to write a review here. Hopefully, my review was helpful for some of you :)

title: BBs are revolutionary, this makes it easy to find out why
text:
I had heard that BBs were the new rage but my brain was stuck on the need to match my skintone to the makeup, so I didn't feel comfortable buying it online if I couldn't see the color. Buying this kit helped me to realize that my hesitation over color was a silly concern. While it does look like foundation, it does not behave like foundation. I'm not sure what it uses to create the effect but I'm going to say that rather than pigment, it contains some sort of magical light diffuser. Up close, you cannot tell you are wearing any makeup. You can still see your sunspots and tone issues. However, step away from the mirror and suddenly they all disappear and your skin looks dewy and spot free. This is as revolutionary to makeup as Spanx was to the fashion world. You're wearing makeup but no one can tell. Brilliant!!!

Although the color is not something you need to worry about, the package does allow you to experiment with the different types of BBs that are out there. Some offer more coverage than others, some don't work as well with oily t-zones. I will definitely be purchasing a full size BB from this kit and am glad I took the risk to try the products. Additionally, the shipping from the seller was very fast. I ordered another sample kit from the Mischa (sp?) brand and it's been 2 weeks and I still haven't received it. It must be coming by boat from Korea and then will be walked to DC from the west coast, as it is not slated to arrive for another 2 weeks. Ridiculous!

title: Great primer!

It is for sure comparable to Smashbox Photo Ready Primer. The texture is very very similar, and it goes on just as smooth as that brand.

I use it after my morning facial routine of cleansing, serums, toning and moisturizer. I squeeze about two pumps worth onto my hands and apply it all over my face. I concentrate on areas that need filling in, like around my eyes and mouth where I have fine lines. Then let it settle for about 5 minutes and apply my normal makeup routine. My foundation glides right over it and doesn't settle in to any of my fine lines or wrinkles.

Overall this is a solid choice for a good primer. It fills in where I need it to and lasts all day. I highly recommend!

text:

I loved the neat packaging, the pump of the bottle makes it easier to use and does not cause any wastage. Contrary to a lot of reviews, I did like the smell and given the fact that it has all natural ingredients makes it very effective.
Its been two weeks since I had used it, the cream is a bit thick and little goes a long way. Since I have dry, red skin it worked well on my skin type. I found this to be very hydrating and my acne scars seem to fade away. title: Eye Replacement Head Fits Glo Pro Perfectly & Makes It Easier To Use Glo Pro In Eye Area
text:
I’m using the Glo Pro eye attachment head with my Glo Pro that I bought from a department store that included only the face attachment head. The eye head is slimmer and less than half the width with just four rows of needles. The eye head is an authentic and high quality attachment that snaps on easily and fits Glo Pro perfectly. I definitely prefer using this slimmer eye head for the delicate area around my eyes and between my brows and even my forehead (which is small). The smaller head gives me better control and greater ease of using Glo Pro in small areas.

I wasn’t sure of the boundaries around my eye area, so I emailed Glo Pro and was informed the eye head can be used right up to the bottom lashes (but not on the eye lids). Still, this device is new to me so for now I don’t go much beyond the orbital bone- where I apply my night time eye cream. The Glo Pro needles are short and feel just a little prickly and give me a slight burning sensation. But it’s not uncomfortable or painful and hasn’t caused any excessive redness or irritation. I definitely recommend the smaller eye attachment head for Glo Pro users and rate it 5 stars.

I wasn’t provided a Glo Pro device and this review is only of the eye attachment head. Still, I’m sure people wonder if Glo Pro works. I’ve used a Glo Pro about a month, twice a week, and don’t feel I’ve used it long enough to know. I’m in my 50’s and my skin does happen to look good lately. I don’t see dramatic changes, but my skin seems firmer and my fine lines around my eyes and elsewhere seem less noticeable. But I feel I need to use Glo Pro longer to decide if it’s the device, my skin care products or both that are providing a benefit. I do like Glo Pro enough to keep using it.

i purchased both the chrome and holographic powders, however i DID NOT use gel nail polish. I know these powders are meant for gel, but i used regular nail polish and the picture polish Revolution glitter base coat and foil top coat.

After that I tried the same black polish with the base coat on top and then powder. The chrome CAME THROUGH. the chrome looks great on top of the black, but i wasnt able to get it to cover my nail completely (had a few patches that were just thinly covered) but i blame that mostly on myself, and not the powder.

overall i 100% recommend the chrome powder. I personally would skip the holographic unless you just want light coverage

title: Works much better than acetone, but watch your surfaces!
text:
Do you see “100% Natural” and think “Yeah, right!” or do you assume it won’t work as well as products that have chemicals? I do this all the time especially when it comes to cleaning products or makeup. In this case I was offered a bottle of Pure Body Naturals™ 100% Natural Nail Polish Remover and the skeptical part of me was sure this wouldn’t turn out well. But in the spirit of trying new things, I agreed to review it and put it to the test. **See the images for before/after photos**

For my test I painted my nails several different colors. We all know deep reds are harder to get off and glitters can also be a pain to remove. I dedicated my left hand to the Pure Body Naturals™ 100% Natural Nail Polish Remover and my right hand I used a drugstore brand of acetone polish remover (the super cheap stuff I usually use.) Both hands got two good coats of polish.

To remove the polish the Pure Body Naturals™ remover instructions say to drop or dab it on and wait 2-3 minutes before wiping. For the generic acetone remover I just apply and wipe with a cotton ball.

The Pure Body Naturals™ remover wiped right off, taking most of the polish with it. I did have to reapply a small amount, wait a few more minutes and all but one tiny trace of the red polish was gone. The acetone remover left polish near my cuticles even after a hard scrubbing and a second try.

So what did I like?
-I like that it works better than the acetone remover, even on the darkest red and glitter!
-I like that it did not make my nails feel dry.
-I like that the Pure Body Naturals™ remover doesn’t have harsh chemicals.
-I like that it isn’t tested on animals.
-I like that it comes with a handy glass dropper.

The only problem (and it could have been a BIG one) is this polish will eat through any polish, including vanish on my dining room table and styrofoam plates. No kidding. I started out thinking to drip the remover over a plate to keep it off the table but it quickly melted the styrofoam and one small spot of the table varnish.

Only use this stuff in the bathroom over tile or a sink with no finish/paint/lacquer, etc. never over a delicate surface like your dining room table!

I received a free sample of this remover to review. I have given my honest opinion and the real test/comparison results.

Problem #1- I bought these because they are stated to be reusable. I assure you that they are NOT. The attached microbead is literally glued onto the extension, so you cant even use a new microbead. Problem #3- the ends of the extension (closest to your scalp) are frayed edges. Instead of being keratin bonded and smooth, they are like little brooms of sharp hairs that constantly itch your scalp. I mean, insanely uncomfortable.

I attempted to contact the seller. She stated she would send me a new pack of beads to try. She never sent them. It wouldn't have mattered anyway because she has clearly never seen the product or she would realize that you can't use a new microbead with these as here is literally no way to get the old, broken bead off.

These were purchased for approximately $325. I spent another $300 to have them installed. $625 to have them in for less than a week. If you want to spend over $600 for a week of slipping extensions, then these are for you.

title: Hair feels like silk afterwards.  Very pleased.  But, I'll need a second treatment.
text:
I wish I'd taken pictures. As soon as I put this on my hair, I could see the difference between this and other products. I have colored my brown VERY fine, VERY thick split-personality hair (curly under, straight on top) for years ranging from a bright burgundy red to black, to various browns. This last time, I had used a bleaching prep product to add a few vibrant blue streaks. But all I got was black that won't go away.

SMELL

I've tried bleach and non-bleach products. Those smelled terrible. This didn't have much smell in comparison. It definitely didn't smell like the other reviews.

COMPARISON TO OTHER PRODUCTS

The other products I tried destroyed my hair leaving it crunchy and damaged. They also only managed to lighten the color from the crown and left the near black almost exactly as I started. (Beware of the competitor non-bleach product that says it only takes 20 minutes. The box doesn't say you have to rinse it a MINIMUM of 20 minutes. That one also required a recolor, which stabilized the hair. I think my hair would have snapped off had I not recolored it.)

COST EFFECTIVE

My hair is so thick, I had to use 2 boxes of other products just to get coverage. This product went on so easy, my hair sucked it in and softened as it went on. I only used 2/3 of the solutions in this product. I'm impressed that I didn't need it all. (Hairdressers always charged more to color my hair because it's so thick.)

PROCEDURE/OUTCOME

I left it on for probably 40 minutes, used a cap, but didn't heat. The top lightened to my natural light brown color (I forgot what that looked like!) and the black is now a rich brown, not even really a two-tone, which I've had since my experiment. But, it still needs another treatment to get it the rest of the way. My hair has blond overtones now, not brassy at all.

BONUS!

My hair is really, really soft. I would do this as a conditioning treatment! I am ordering a second batch to retreat since what I have left isn't enough. Next time, I will heat my hair slightly to see if it will take it the rest of the way. Anything left over will be used for a future treatment to condition my hair. (I live next to the ocean and the salt and wind has been really hard on my hair so I'm very happy to find something to help.)

title: It's okay but not what I was expecting
text:
This is a tricky review to write. When I received the product, my initial reaction was, "What is this?" The photo on this item's page is very misleading. The product is not a dark creamy brown looking thing. It's basically pale brown colored sugar crystals. That's it. I contacted the seller with a photos (see photos) and said there seems to be something missing. They assured me "As for the packaging, thanks for letting me know, we will have it modified accordingly this week." I'm not sure what that means, but besides the photo being completely different, the description indicates it's 8.8 oz and it's an organic brown sugar. The ingredients don't indicate "organic" at all and the label on the jar states it's 7 oz. So it's not the product I thought I was purchasing. I'm bothered that the photo was SO different than the product I received. I honestly thought the cream or oil must have evaporated or something.

That said, my testing of the product has been odd and I'm torn about an accurate star rating. The first day, I wet my arm and took a scoop of the crystals and rubbed them over my arm. All of the crystals fell off into the sink within seconds and other than being wet, my arm was exactly the same. I was thinking that even one star was too generous for a useless product. Today, I gave it another try. I scooped the crystals up with my fingers instead of the plastic scoop. I did my best to keep them on my arm this time. My arm turned pretty pink during this process and I really didn't know what to expect. I was only able to do this for about 40 seconds before I lost the last of the crystals. I rinsed my arm and was impressed by how soft my arm felt. However, I know you can take salt and product a similar softness by using some oil along with it. So I don't know....it softens the skin but at the rate it's been disappearing on me, the product won't last long and there's really nothing extraordinary about it.

Note: I was able to purchase this item, at a discount, for my honest review.

title: A fairly basic 'stache wax with good hold and tackiness
text:
I'm the proud owner of a rather glorious handlebar moustache (though I say so myself). So when a 'stache wax or grooming product comes available on Vine I'll usually request it if it's anything in the neighborhood of what I usually like.

I like firm or strong hold waxes with significant tackiness. I won't even consider a wax unless it either states a strong hold or a tacky hold or both. As a reference my other favorite common varieties of moustache wax include (in order of preference descending):
Firehouse Moustache Wax - Tacky (Wacky Tacky)
The Vintage Grooming Company - Death Grip
Can You Handlebar - Primary

All of these are either exceptionally tacky or very strong in hold or both. I have tried many other waxes by various brands over the last several years but the ones above are my favorites and the ones that I feel are most worth mentioning in comparison to this product.

I would rate this wax as slightly less tacky than the Firehouse Moustache wax Tacky and slightly less stiffness than the Can You Handlebar Primary wax. Death Grip has it's own unique and weird properties (and I don't love the way it smells) so it is hard to direct compare :-)

As far as my general ranking I'd put this solidly in the top 5 waxes I've ever tried though, probably just under the three above and maaaybe 5th place after maybe Fisticuffs Strong Hold (which also has some pine resin for stickiness).

Unscented is good! Nothing worse than a cloying scent right up under your nose holes all day long!

Anyway, it has a strong hold for shaping if you like a strong curl as I do, combined with a tacky hold if you get a lot of stray and fly away hairs as I do. While my "go to" product is still Firehouse Tacky, and this has not replaced that, this is a worthy offering. The tree embossment on the wax is cute and I kinda dig that they give you the recipe.

The price point at the time of this writing is very fair. If you're in need of a good strong hold tacky wax I'd say give this product a shot!

title: Pretty good rotary shaver
text:
When I was a teenager I got a Norelco as a gift and at first I got a really good shave, I really liked it over a razor. Then, I started to get such bad rashes that I finally had to give it up and went back to a razor for about 25 years.

I was too dumb to know that you had to periodically replace the heads. I just assumed that they lasted forever. Oh well.

My first new electric was a Remington, and I'll say that their adverstisements, for me, were true; It gave the closest electric shave.

The problem was my beard grows at a steep angel to the skin and electrics have a hard time getting all of the whiskers. If you missed a whisker on day one, you might get it on day two, but after that, forget it.

I went to a Braun after the Remington wore out, and it has a coarse cutter on the inside that can get those errant whiskers. It was not quite as close as the Remington, but was a lot faster because it would find the longer hairs.

This has all been to give background to the Norelco.

I've had it for over 2 months now.

It falls somewhere in between the other two. It is not quite as close as either, but very close to the Braun.

It will get those stray whiskers usually, but every 4 or 5 days, I need to use the trimmer to get ones that have gotten away.

As far as irritation goes, it borders right on the edge of a problem on my neck. The cause is obvious. The screens on this rotary are a lot rougher that a foil shaver. That is to say that you can feel the grid of depressions and holes. Be careful in pressing too hard or using repeated passes, to avoid irritation.

Because of the large surface area of the heads, I find shaving to be about 1/3 faster now, as long as I don't try to get a blade quality shave.

This razor is extremely quiet, with only a very soft whirring versus the loud buzz of any foil.

The trimmer works adequately with my only complaint that it does not lock in the up position. If you push it the wrong way, it folds back down.

The batteries last 3 to 4 weeks on a charge. If it starts to get low I just plug it in and continue shaving. To get around the lack of a low battery indicator I will charge it up before a trip so that I don't need to take the charger with me.

I consider the lack of an indicator to be a non-issue.

Overall I like the shaver a lot

I bought this product for the stretch marks on my butt, behind my legs and knees because I saw that this product is affordable and has so many great ingredients such as:
Organic barbadensis leaf juice or aloe juice: as we all know that aloes have many many benefits due to its anti-inflamatory properties due to the two hormones called Auxin and Gibberellins. Together they help treat acne and reduce the redness from acne. Aloe also has healing properties that have been used to treat sunburn, help prevent scarring and treat existing scars.

Organic helianthus annuus (sun flower oil): Sun flower oil is rich in Vitamin E which is a well known antioxidant for its healing properties. It also contain many great oils such as coconut, vitamin E, jojoba, rose hips, argan oil and many more which are all very healing and moisturizing for the skin

cordifolia callus culture extract (plant stem cells): Derived from Globularia Cordifolia, a species of flowering plant native to the mountains of central and southern Europe, Globularia Cordifolia Callus Culture Extract detoxifies skin by eliminating damaged proteins and other accumulated environmental wastes. It also provides protection from oxidative stress thereby reducing the effects of cell aging.

Matrixyl 3000: Matrixyl is palmitoyl-pentapeptide 3 and this is a peptide that specifically stimulates collagen synthesis and skin repair. this is a long term skin care ingredient. The two new peptides palmitoyl-tripeptide and palmitoyl-oligopeptide. They are supposed work synergistically to mimic the appearance of this broken down collagen, causing your skin to react by producing more collagen, as well as elastin. The company that owns the patent has conducted research on two panels of 23 volunteers aged from 39 to 74 to demonstrate that matrixyl 3000 is more effective than the original matrixyl at regulating skin cell activity. In early 2013 University of Reading researchers found that Matrixyl can nearly double the amount of the protein collagen needed to give skin its elasticity.

Gotu Kola: has been used to treat many conditions for thousands of years in India, China, and Indonesia. It was used to heal wounds, improve mental clarity, and treat skin conditions such as leprosy and psoriasis. Gotu kola has chemicals called triterpenoids. In animal and lab studies, these compounds seem to help heal wounds. For example, some studies suggest that triterpenoids strengthen the skin, boost antioxidants in wounds, and increase blood supply to the area. Based on these findings, gotu kola has been applied to the skin, or used topically, for minor burns, psoriasis, preventing scars after surgery, and preventing or reducing stretch marks.
