text:
Super happy with this product so far. I randomly found it at Ulta and decided to try it out. After a couple of years of cheaping out on my highlights, my hair is in really bad shape and I am working to bring it back to being healthy and strong again. Was happy to find a multi-pack of this on Amazon since I plan to use it at least once a week for a few more months.

The product is easy to use - heats up well in the microwave and then is in a thick enough package that I don't feel like the hot oil is going to spill out as I open it. Putting it on my hair is easy and it stays well without dripping down my neck, which I was worried about since coconut oil gets runny when warm. I leave it on for a few hours and then heat my hair up periodically with a hair dryer. Then, washing out is easy and clean. I've only used this once so far but I swear that my hair seems to be in better shape already - it feels like it is thickening back up to its old state. I plan to use this at least once a week, before every twice-weekly hair wash if I have the time, until I get these locks back to a healthy state.

title: Love it
text:
I was ready for a change in my hair care products. I tried a different all natural product but didn't like how it made my hair feel. I bought Morrocco Method's Starter Kit wanting to like it. I read up on their products before purchasing and liked that it was vegan and raw and that I actually had some inkling as to what the ingredients are.

After buying the kit, I went back to their website while waiting for it to arrive and watched their videos and the testimonials. I wasn't looking for anything negative - because I wanted to like it. I was looking for how other people were using the product, what they found worked for them and how Morrocco Method recommended using the product. This worked out very well for me in that I picked up a few tips.

I've now been using the shampoos and conditions for 6 days. Your hair and scalp does go through a transitionary phase while your scalp gets used to not having to produce as much hair oil since you're not stripping it from your hair with synthetic shampoos. I had started with the other product I was using about 2 weeks before starting with Morrocco and my hair was very oily and heavy after starting that. I'm hoping I've gotten through most of the transition because I've only had 1-2 days with Morrocco where my hair has been oily. The other days my hair has looked awesome. My scalp has felt lighter too!

It's an adjustment to learn how to use their shampoos. For example, they don't lather up. I expected this and don't have an issue with it. The first day I used a Morrocco shampoo my hair felt really oily and greasy. I didn't see how the shampoo would get my hair feeling clean, but it did. Not only was it clean, but felt smooth and silky.

I've now ordered the larger sizes of the shampoos and will continue to use them.

title: Great moisturizer!
text:
I ordered this Retseliney Retinol Moisturizing Cream for the retinol and other natural and organic moisturizing ingredients in it. I have rough, dry and sensitive skin that desperately needs moisture. I've been using this twice a day, once at night after washing my face and again in the morning before applying make-up. I love how moisturizing it is, and I have not had any skin irritation or discomfort. It makes my skin feel so much softer without the after greasy-feel that other products sometimes give. I think it is too soon to tell if my fine lines will become less apparent, but I think moisturizing is step 1 for me.

As I said above the ingredients are natural and organic, no hard chemicals or phosphates. Aloe, shea butter, green tea, jojoba, sunflower oil, palm oil, vitamin E and B5 are just some of the ingredients. In the past, I would never look at what chemicals were in the products I was using and putting on my skin, which absorbs into my body. I am excited that there are now so many companies looking at this to and making the change. I received this as a complimentary sample for review and feedback purposes, the above thoughts are definitely my own and I think this is a 5 star product!

title: Either You Love it... or you hate it....
text:
I can see why this shampoo gets either 5 stars or 1 star from its reviewers — and almost nothing in between.

PROS: I like it because it contains only healthy ingredients with no SLS or other detergents nor any added fragrances — a blend with these features is such a rare thing, not easy to find. Also, it's very mild, with no stripping action, and leaves my hair soft + easy to comb even without conditioner. It's also one of the few shampoos that does not make my scalp itch. So, it's become my product of choice!

CONS: Often (depending on how dirty the hair is) it doesn't suds on the first application... which is not what we're used to and can be frustrating... so, you could end up pouring on way too much of it toward that end. But just be patient: Don't add more, just rinse and do a second application, if needed... it will suds nicely.

I first used this shampoo years ago and was glad to rediscover it a year or so ago via Amazon. I am definitely a fan.

title: No noticeable results after over a month - UPDATED 11/9/14
text:
NOTE: I received a free sample of this product to review.

Like the hair on my head, my eyelashes are thin and fine. Without mascara, they are barely noticeable. I have never before tried an eyelash growth serum and was frankly somewhat skeptical, yet at the same time, I was excited at the thought that this product might be beneficial.

This serum is packaged in a tube that looks like mascara. However, the inner wand ends in a tiny brush that is like a VERY thin paintbrush. I would have preferred a slightly thicker applicator; the brush was SO small that it was difficult to see the serum for precise application.

I followed the instructions for this product, applying nightly along my lash line. I used this product daily for over a month (since late August). Unfortunately, I am not able to discern any noticeable results. I actually took photos, thinking that might show more of a difference, I but do not see any changes in the photos, either. (It looks like Amazon has finally posted my photos, so you can see what you think for yourself.)

The only small improvement I have noticed of late is that AFTER applying my mascara, my lashes seem longer than they normally would with mascara--it's almost as if they are somehow adhering to the mascara better than they would normally. I'm not 100% sure if this is a real effect, but that possible sign combined with the fact that I didn't have any adverse reactions to this product is the reason why I gave it two stars rather than one. Perhaps others will have better luck than I did.

UPDATED 11/9/14: Despite my lack of results after one month, I continued to use this product. It has now been over two months, and I believe that I have seen SOME results. At this point, my lashes DO appear longer--I think that's why my mascara has seemed to be working better, as my lashes are a bit longer than before. However, my results have been nothing like the miracles in the photos posted on the product page--yes, my lashes are a bit longer, but the effect is hardly noticeable to the bare eye (I asked my husband, and he didn't notice). Furthermore, my lashes are neither thicker nor more plentiful; this product gave me a bit of length only, not thickness or any other effect. So, in summary, I upgraded my review from two to three stars, but I don't feel like I can go beyond that at this time.

It shows that the cleaner is a 2% salicylic acid wash, which is a pretty tried and true formulation for treating acne. It is a low-lather, but still effective cleaner, but I didn’t experience any difference with this compared with other 2% salicylic cleaners that cost far less. It’s a fine cleaner, but way overpriced for such a tiny (0.51 oz) container.

The repairing night cream is a combination of retinol (0.05%), niacinamide (3%), and hyaluronic acid (2%). All are proven performers, but again, it’s quite overpriced considering how low of a percentage of retinol is in the formulation. It does a decent job of moisturizing and did not cause any skin irritation. I am a fan of retinol, but the concentration in this cream (0.05%) is well below what I usually use (either 0.1% or 0.5%).

While this product combo is on the right track, the value is just not there considering the amount in the container (one-half an ounce for each). While I would certainly recommend a salicylic acid wash and a retinol-based cream, there are many other options that provide these options at a far lower cost. Four stars for performance; 1 star for value; overall rating of 2.5 stars.

title: Works as advertised and better
text:
I have been using a Norelco T370 trimmer for several months. I bought it for the mini-shaver initially, decided to grow a beard, then trimmed the beard with the beard trimmer attachment. It did a great job of shaping and trimming, but left a mess of clippings in the sink. After reading a million reviews, I decided to try the T980 for it's vacuum feature.

The T980 is great! It does a perfect job of trimming my beard evenly (setting at 7, ultimate beard length to be a 9). The best part is that about 90% of the clippings go into the vacuum receptical with only about 10% being lost. I have not come across any of the negatives (adjustment slips, tugs hairs and on and on) mentioned in other reviews. Unlike my T370, this trimmer lets you know when it's fully charged or about to go dead, and even if it does die in the middle of a session from a dead battery, plugging it in finishes the job. Most other trimmers only work when charged, not on house current.

I can't think of anything this trimmer could do better. In my estimation it's looks, design and operation are flawless. The clipper works well on my beard's 'neckline' and the mini-trimmer keeps the bottom of my mustache trimmed perfectly. I really think the T370 does as good a job trimming as this one does, but will not run with a dead battery when plugged in, and does make a mess with beard clippings all over the place. For those two reasons alone, this trimmer is a BEST BUY!

I am not putting the T370's abilities down in any way. For the price it can't be beat. It trims well and the mini-shaver is still the best way to shave the short hairs on my cheeks above my beard on a daily basis. I use it daily along with the T980 and will continue to. They both have their place. If you don't mind the beard trimmings everywhere, you will be happy with the T370, however if you are serious about perfect beard grooming (and I DO mean PERFECT), with none of the mess, both tools are a must.

title: A great falling sand picture
text:
In short, excellent product with well thought out characteristics. I am purchasing more.

I thoroughly enjoy the Golden Sun sand picture by Paradise Vision. It appealed to me so much I purchased it as a gift to myself. Now I am purchasing more for gifts for others. I provide below more details that may not be apparent in the product description or that are notable for me and might be important for others.

Mounting Features - The "picture" comes with design and parts for both table top placement and wall mounting. Frame is angled so that it will not stand on just the frame. Even if it could stand on the frame it is much too susceptible to falling over (and breaking glass) and the provided tapered frame prevents its support is important. It appears Paradise Vision also concluded this and, according, effected this taper. For table top support, a slightly flexible plastic "leg" is provided that supports the picture from behind. The leg attaches to the picture by press fit compression of the leg's two-prong fork feature to be around a sort of rubber grommet. If securely attached I find the leg does not come off when picking up the picture and placing it again on the table top in the same orientation. The leg must be removed and replaced 180 degrees on circular grommet/mount on back of picture if the picture is turned over for the falling sand effect. Bottom line, pick up picture, remove leg, turn over as many times as you want, when satisfied, reattach leg and set picture on table top.

Glass Face - Face is glass, not plastic. Perfect. Plastic is more susceptiple to scratching in my experience and opinion.

Great Scene - Picture has a perfect photograph for complementing the sand (OK this might be apparent in the Amazon photos). What appeals to me is that there is the photograph where other sand pictures that have no photo leaves the viewer seeing what is behind the sand when the sand settles. I find seeing whatever happenes to be behind the picutre less appealing. Also, in this (Golden Sun) version, the sand includes yellow and orange sand (small amounts of both) that complement the photograph and make the sand scene appear like the tops of hills/mountains still receive sunlight.

Great Frame - Solid frame with small grain/fatigue surface features, also painted a shiny gold coler (thing shiny dark gold gift bow). It might have a clear coat of some kind, but I am not sure. Tight, quality joints and surfaces at corners with no mis-alignment, mismatched thickness problems. I am nearly certain it is wood, but I cannot be absolutely certain.

Good Dimensions - Dimensions are big enough to accomodate more than one "hill/mountain". My experience with smaller sand pictures tend to create only one or none or more very small ones.

Air/Water Adjustment - Parts includes a blunt syringe and instructions for adding air or removing air contained in the picture. This is done by inserting the syringe through a normally blocked, one-way gasketed hole feature (about 1/8 in. diamteter) in the side of the frame. I have never seen this feature for users in water-filled sand pictures by other manufacturers. I will confess to not having tried adding/removing air because I don't want to alter the amount that seems to be working just fine as received from the manufacturer. Instructions for doing so are provided and I found sufficiently clear.

Tilt Angle Potentially Problem - The only thing I would have changed if I could was to shorten the slightly flexible plastic leg so the picture doesn't tip back , it appears, by only 10 degrees or so from vertical where it is easily tipped forward if bumped. If it falls forward, it could break, particularly if the glass strikes an object when falling. I would have suggested, perhaps, 20 degrees tip for a little more stability.

Slightly Flexible Leg Feature Good - I suspect the leg is slightly flexible, rather than rigid, so that, if the picture is bumped from the front or set down on the table top surface a little more "vigorously" that the leg will flex a little rather than, otherwise, possibly resulting cracking or breakage of the leg or picture. Great idea Rainbow Vision.

I know I have written a lot. I hope it helps.
Steven

I have sensitive skin that develops dry patches, itchy rashes, (or both at once) if I use a product with remotely harsh ingredients. The foam cleanser spreads generously, so it lasts for quite a long time, and it rinses off very easily, reducing the need for unnecessary scrubbing and rubbing. For the last 10 years since I discovered this line, Caudalie has never caused such reactions. The scent is also quite pleasant.

The serum really helps restore elasticity and mousture with ZERO oily feel on the skin. It is one of the very few products labeled "serum" that I find perfectly suitable to use morning and night, before another moisturizer (or without), and under primer and makeup. Again, it's perfect for sensitive skin. It's not lying about helping replenish moisture. It's especially great in the colder months to counter the dry air and constant temperature changes.

The night cream is absolutely fantastic, even without the serum (but using them together is basically a guarantee that you'll wake up with healthy- looking and healthy- feeling, clean skin). It spreads well, so a little goes a long way, absorbs quickly but isn't "disappeared" to the point your face gets dry in the night, and is not cakey or oily (you won't leave a lotion stain on your pillowcase). I HIGHLY recommend this trio. The price is fair and matches what you'd pay at the Caudalie.US store or Sephora.

title: A good smelling essential oil - we really like it.
text:
I love using essential oils in my small humidifier / diffuser. Not only does it make my office smell better, I have found certain oils are beneficial as well (ex: headaches / allergies). As such, I have been trying out different oils to see what I like, and reading how they can work either by itself or mixed with others.

The oil arrived in a nice glass bottle. Also included with the bottle is a dropper. I always tell people new to using essential oils to take it slowly at first – you can add more later. I made the mistake of putting too much a couple of times, and the smell was very strong.

I am not an expert in essential oils, and I do not pretend to be. Near as I can tell, the oil is of very good quality both in feel, clarity, and scent. I will trust most of the other reviews which say this is a good quality oil.

For the most part, we have used the oil mostly for simply scenting an area, although my wife and I have been trying it out recently to assist with sleep. I have never been a good sleeper (especially falling asleep), but I have seen an improvement over the last week since I have been trying it in this fashion. Is it the oil / mental / combination? I do not know, but I plan on continuing to use it as long as it seems to keep working for me.

Overall, we have been happy with the oil and it seems to have performed well for us.

title: I finally found my holy grail dark green hair color! I love the muted shade range.
text:
I have been looking for a dark, truly green hair dye for ages. Most dark greens skew hard teal,and mixing colors to get the desired shade usually fades to blue annoyingly fast. Green Tomato is the color of tomato vines and is very pigmented—it's such a dark green that it looks almost black when it comes out of the tube. It has a gray undertone rather than a blue or yellow one. I love this color. It's a muted, deep green that fades to a dark mossy tone after many washes. The result is a more natural, "lived-in" color right from the start.

The dye has a gel-like consistency that makes it very spreadable. I have shoulder-length, fine hair. Even using this completely undiluted and unmixed, I will get at least a dozen uses out of this one tube. I've used it undiluted to achieve a dark green that passes for black in dim or soft lighting. (Side Note: be careful to avoid applying undiluted dye directly to your scalp, this stains your skin quite badly.) I've diluted it with white, silicone-free conditioner to create a pastel version. Using a lot of conditioner creates a slightly grainy mixture, but it hasn't affected the quality or longevity of the results. I've also mixed it with several other brands of dye (e.g. Pravana, Iroiro, La Riche Directions, and Bigen Vivid Shades) with no issues and positive results. It smells sort of like markers, with a hint of perfume. It's not particularly terrible, but it's one of the worst-smelling brands of semi-permanent hair color I've come across.

I really think Sarangsae is doing something special with the shade range they offer. I've used over a dozen brands in all the colors of the rainbow, but nobody else is creating such soft, understated colors. It's not too hard for me to achieve a soft pastel (either by using a pastel dye or diluting a dark dye) but dark shades are usually extremely bright. I love mixing my own colors, and the hardest thing to achieve is a muted dark hue. I've added silver dyes,the Pravana Vivids "black" additive, and/or small amounts of opposing shades (i.e., a dab of pink or light orange to a green to tone it down) with various success. I'm really excited to try some of their other muted colors in the future, like Black Rose, Deep Grey, or Mustard Yellow. If they can make a truly soft, deep, dark green, they can probably make any shade!

title: I don't know a ton about razors but I do know when the man is happy with his
text:
I got this shaver as a gift for my husband who normally uses those shavers where you keep the handles but have to constantly buy the disposable heads. I've always seen pictures of these types of razors in shaving commercials so I figured I would give him a little gift. And WOW! I really didn't expect it to go over as well as it did! I don't know a ton about razors but I do know when the man is happy with his.

As soon as I got it and gave it to him, he was a little reluctant to change his routine. But then I couldn't get it back from him even to do a review for it! He loves it! He says it gives him a much closer shave (probably due to the fact that there's an actual razor blade inside the shaver) and that, while it's a little weird shaving with just the edge of a razor (instead of having those disposable heads against his cheek) he's starting to prefer it because of the results he's getting.

And it's really easy to clean! You simply turn a knob in the handle and the shaver opens and you can take out the blade inside and give it a little rinse and you're done! My husband applies a little oil to make it go further but it's a less than 30 second job and he sets it to dry to be ready for the next use.

After his experience, I really recommend this shaver to anyone else in the market who may have the same experience as him! My husband is a very hard man to impress and the fact that this has immediately become his new favorite razor says a lot to me and I hope it does to you as well.

*Disclaimer: I received this product at a discount for my honest and unbiased feedback. I do not review anything I wouldn't trust to use on my own body or on my family. title: My Favorite Beauty Helper
text:
OMG !!!!!!! I have been cruising Amazon for this exact item for quite some time and was thrilled to see it for an excellent price. I had been to retail and beauty supply stores everywhere I went, only to be told I could not order just the unit. I had already purchased extra rollers with my original unit. My Caruso Steam Unit gave up the after some major miles, through many hair styles.
I have very thick, straight American Indian hair that was prematurely gray hair before I could graduate high school. I purchased the Caruso Steam set and many extra curlers years ago when it first came on the market. I had tried various kinds of steam roller sets that were difficult to wrap my straight hair around. They were pokey and heavy with painful steel pins to hold rollers in my hair; only for the curls to fall out almost immediately. I tried ceramic, adjustable heat settings, and many different curling irons and dryers that was new on the market. I combined hair gels or mousse with them only to have curls and waves fall out within minutes. I went to beauty school (lol) after high school. Really not my thing
The new unit I received is not round like this picture. It is kidney shaped.
The old version I had to add a small amount of salt to the water.
The newer version has a slider switch for OFF, STEAM and IONIC STEAM.
I love, love, love the Caruso Steam for my hair.
I used 6-8 curlers for my whole head.
Literally seconds to put each in and about the time I get them all in it is time to take them out. Just like my old Caruso Steam unit (without the salt).
My curls last three days minimum.
I DO NOT use hair products on my hair ever.
Curls are soft and natural feeling.
Caruso Steamer does not damage hair. Stopped perms many years ago after finding this steamer. This amazing steamer adds shine to my curls. I can run my fingers through my hair as much as I want.
There is never those bent ends of hair, curls just fall, I shake my head, move a curl or two with my fingers and I am out the door.
I have missed this little time saver and am continually complimented on my hair and how much younger I look.
I hope this helps someone, lets me know how you use your Caruso Steamer

I was like...three minutes? Only? Huh.

It burns. It burns with the passion of a thousand menthol suns. My skin was straight red after around the ten minute mark. There IS no leaving this on overnight, that comment was for the sleep mask.
Which I do frequently for that product.
Because it soothes.

I won't give it one star because I did notice it pulled things to the surface immediately, and I am aware I might just be sensitive to the product itself. It wasn't as drying as masks can be which was also a huge plus.

I guess ultimately if you get this, be careful and don't leave it on too long!

title: Not bad for a cheaper face and cellulite messager
text:
I didn't think the unit was working, it has vague instructions, but just touch it to dry bare skin and you'll feel it. I did not come wit a AC plug, (minus one star for that), you'll have to use one from another gadget, I used my tablet one. When it is charged, press and hold the button in until it beeps and lights up. There are two levels of power, I think, press the button one more time, the indicator light on the power button is orange, press it one more time and you'll see red. It runs for 3 minutes and then shuts off. You can use it a total of 30 minutes in one day. Diagrams in the booklet show you which way to use it effectively. This is important- you need to use a hydro gel or a oil, like rose hip oil or such like I do or you will feel a slight electric shock against your skin.
Have I seen improvements? YES. I had a NUface facial and this gadget seems to being doing as well as the NUface mini. I use it every day and I notice tighter skin, less redness, and less wrinkles. I use it just 3 minutes every morning. For the price I think it is a nice portable massage. I use it also with my cellulite cream on my legs and without changing anything else, the cellulite is fading (been only a week).

title: Less than Great....
text:
I really wanted to like this product, but unfortunately, it was less than great quality, and one of the brushes I received was broken. Quite a few of the brushes had frayed bristles and had uneven thickness to them, which made even application hard to come by.

When I used some, it didn't seem like they blended the colors together well (mainly for eye shadow). I wish there were smaller round brushes for blending out shadows on your eyes because I feel like all the flat brushes are just about all the same. There is barely any size difference between three of them, and they can all be used for the same things so why not replace those with some rounder ones?

I tried to contact the seller about the problems I had with this product, but, after two days, I haven't heard anything back from them. I was waiting before putting this review up to see if there was anything they cared to do to help with these problems (new brush that's not broken, or a new set all together that has better quality to them), but I have gotten no response back from them to lead me to believe that they're willing to do anything to help.

I have attached photos to this post to show the problems I got with these brushes. The broken one was a foundation brush so I didn't get to try that one out to even see if it applied the foundation well, so I was a little disappointed with that. The larger powder brush seemed to do ok, but it didn't pick up powder that well. The larger fan brush I tried to use for contouring (I saw someone use a large fan brush for this purpose in a tutorial so I wanted to try it out), but even though the brush picked up the color, it didn't seem to apply it very much at all. The contour powder I used is super pigmented so I shouldn't have had that problem. The eye shadow brush I used (one of the smaller tapered brushes) actually worked pretty well so I don't have complaints about any of those except that some of the smaller brushes had frayed bristles, too. The smaller fan brush I used for highlight, and, though it did well with applying it, the unevenness of the bristles made it apply in a weird and uneven way, One of the larger tapered brushes I used to pack on a setting powder, but again, it didn't seem to pick it up well and left a ton of fall out once it hit my skin. I understand setting powder typically leaves fall out, but I've never experience so much before using this brush.

Basically, the best brushes in this set were probably the eye shadow brushes.

I hope this review helps give some insight on this product. I also hope the seller finds a way to fix the problems I had for future customers.

I received this product at a discounted price for my 100% honest review. I tried contacting the seller (as noted above) before leaving this review since it's a poor one, but I made sure to leave enough information to work with and to help others decide whether or not they would like to purchase this product.

text:
I really wanted to LOVE this wig like some of the other reviewers, but I ran into some problems with it for my Halloween costume (Daenerys Targaryen). Don't get me wrong, it helpped me execute my costume wonderfully, but fell short in my opinion in three categories.
First, when I initially opened the wig, the fibers at the part/crown were for lack of better words bent in a strange way that could not be corrected, even with light heat from my flat iron (luckily for me this was a non-issue for my costume because I needed to pull the front pieces of hair back into braids, but re-wear is going to look a little strange). Second, because you are purchasing a light colored fiber wig that is woven on to a nude headpiece, some of your natural hair/the wig cap is bound to show through. My issue was that you could starkly see the edging of my nude wig cap through the wig. Lucky for me, I naturally have very light blonde hair, but I couldn't imagine what show through would look like with someone with dark hair (just something to keep in mind). Third, thank the lord I remembered my brush. This thing got crazy tangled, now I knew some would come because of the length I went with, but I was brushing at least once an hour to keep a "fresh look."
With all that being said, I would purchase this wig again (just hopefully ending up with one that has a better crown/part). It looks 10X better and more realistic than anything I could have picked up at a Halloween store for my costume, especially keeping cost in mind at $43.

title: Cue the squeals of delight: rose-shaped cleansing foam is basic, but big on the cute factor
text:
OK first of all, I did not pay an outrageous price for this. Only $16 usd at a Hong Kong drugstore chain called Mannings. This foam is pure visual pleasure -- shake the pressurized can, and press down on the sides to expel a rose-shaped dollop of cleansing foam. Cue the squeals of delight and instagram envy from beauty junkies.

title: Disappointing - Razor IS NOT Washable As Depicted & Cutter Block Got Dull Very Quickly
text:
I wanted a USB-chargeable pocket razor to use on my face while in the hospital. I especially liked that the WIOR Razor was listed as washable, and that the photos in the listing even included one showing a hand holding the razor under a stream of water.

The razor is nicely boxed, but I noted the unit itself was quite light compared to other travel razors about the same size I've used in recent years (my favorite one is no longer available in America, alas). Still, a lighter razor is no big deal, as long as it works.

I read the instruction leaflet - only to immediately see a warning not to expose the razor to water! ( ¿ ?) I double checked the Amazon listing to make sure I was sent the right razor, and I certainly was - however, the depiction of it as washable - particularly the image of someone holding it under a faucet stream - is highly misleading. One must remove the foil screen frame and then pull of the cutter block (while being careful the tiny spring does not fall out), and then wash the block separately.

I quickly phoned Amazon's product support number, to explain the major discrepancy, as was told measures would bet taken to correct the listing so no one else would be mislead. I had the option of returning the razor, but given my immediate need, decided to keep it.

It worked reasonably well the first week or so, but the cutter block quickly dulled and shaving became a bit painful over the course of the next couple weeks. I certainly did carefully wash the cutter block by removing the foil in its frame, and then pulling off the block (and each time the little spring would pop off, but fortunately was never lost). However, by last week, just 32 days after purchase, the shaver was cutting quite poorly - even causing a bit of pain to use. In only a month, with light use, the cutting block had dulled to the point of uselessness.

I must point out that despite my call about the misleading product description and imagery, the washability feature remains in the listing as of this writing, five weeks later.

I am very disappointed to see that no action was taken, despite the assurances I was given back in April.

Melty turquoise on my straightener! I never saw the purple again. IDK if I did something wrong by following the directions to a T, or maybe it doesn't work well with thick, coarse hair types. Either way, this was definitely not what I saw advertised. I'm not necessarily upset about it, I guess I had fun testing it out and making a mess lol. I would have been ok with the waste of time and money if the color change would have actually worked, but oh well, now I know.

title: Not my favorite lash serum
text:
This is the second brand of eyelash growth serum I've tried, and decided to try this brand because it was considerably cheaper. This is another example of "you get what you pay for".
In the past I have used Rapidlash. I was amazed at how long and full my lashes were after only a few weeks. I'd say it took about 3 weeks for it to really show, and the results were amazing. Over time I got a little lazy and took my new full, long lashes for granted and stopped using Rapidlash. Gradually my lashes returned to their normal short, thin condition.
I knew I needed to start using lash growth serum again and decided to try Uptown Eyelash Growth Serum. It was cheaper, and advertised longer, thicker lashes in just two weeks.
It's been about 3 weeks ... and, yes, my lashes are somewhat thicker and longer. If I hadn't tried Rapidlash in the past, I would think lash serum a waste of money. Not really enough difference to justify the price or inconvenience. What this experience did show me is that there are great lash serums out there, this just doesn't appear to be one of them.

title: Works for Eye Puffiness & Amazing Off-Label Headache Relief!!
text:
This eye cream was far different than I was expecting -- but in a GREAT way. I'm 29-years-old, so the lines around my eyes aren't terribly deep, although they are probably deeper than many other females my age due to my sun-worshiping in earlier years. I do suffer, however, from severe seasonal allergies and am constantly plagued with dark circles ("allergic shiners" as they call them) and extreme puffiness of both my upper eyelids and just under my eyes (the infamous "bags").

To be honest, my impression of this cream at first glance wasn't too great. For starters, the jar of cream was much smaller than I had imagined, but I guess that's my fault for not noticing the (very) small-printed "0.5 fl oz" on the label in the picture. (I do think that this was a little deceitful though, because the size/amount of this cream is not listed anywhere on the product description.) In addition, while trying to read the teeny tiny print on the jar, I also almost immediately noticed a spelling typo on the front of the label that reads "Nautral & Healthy" rather than "Natural & Healthy." I know this seems like a rather minuscule and knit-picky detail to point out, but it did make me at least wonder about this company's quality control standards.

Despite my initial impression, I gave the company/cream the benefit of the doubt and have been using it for the last few days. With my first application under my eyes, the cream felt more on the "thin" side (similar to a lotion rather than thick cream), but while rubbing the cream into my skin in a circular motion, the moisture that the cream delivered was far better than I anticipated. It takes at least 3-4 minutes before your skin feels like the cream is completely absorbed, which gave me ample time to slowly massage the area during absorption (and felt very soothing and relaxing). I had absolutely no issues with any side effects or skin reactions such as burning, tingling, redness, or irritation. I noticed a small "immediate" reduction in the pores and fine lines of the areas I applied the cream, though not as impressive as some of the Retinol and Vitamin C serums that I've used in the past. There was no obvious difference in the dark circles or puffiness right after application, however, within about 30-45min, the puffiness started to visibly decrease and the area all around my eyes felt less tender/achy in general.

With each subsequent application, I noticed the same resulting decrease in puffiness as was observed initially. My puffiness did return each morning, but I expected because I'm still constantly being exposed to my allergens. (After all, the cream is meant to relieve a symptom of my allergies, not be a miracle cure for my chronic systemic condition.) I've noticed that if I apply the cream immediately before bed and spend more time rubbing it into my skin in the circular motions, I do have a noticeable decrease in the morning when I wake up compared to before I started using the cream. As far as the under-eye dark circles, I can't tell a difference so far - but in all fairness, I've only been using the cream for 4 days (twice daily) so there's still hope.

Now for the best part (in my opinion, at least). On the second night of using this cream, I had yet another one of my throbbing headaches (allergies are the worst!!) About 15-20min after my evening cream application, I noticed that my headache felt a little better -- I'm not saying that there was some miraculous change here, but it did feel less severe. This was very unusual for me, as I hadn't taken any ibuprofen or Zyrtec at that point (my usual go-to medications when my headaches are severe). The only thing I could think that I had done differently this time than any other time was that I applied the cream -- it was a strange connection, but stranger things have certainly happened to me. I went back to look at the ingredients listed on the jar and saw that it had rooibos in it. I had absolutely no idea what this was (and probably didn't notice it the first time I looked because I don't have a magnifying glass), but I looked it up online and read that it's an herb from South Africa with a laundry-list of health benefits -- including antioxidant properties and... headache relief?!?! Although still relatively skeptical that this was just a coincidence and that I had gotten "lucky" on my google search, I was still optimistic and proceeded to rub the eye cream on my temples and at the base of my skull to see what would happen. After a good 30-45min, my headache was almost completely gone. I know this headache thing sounds ridiculous and obscure, but I encourage anyone to research this mysterious Rooibos for themselves. I haven't had a headache as severe as that one since, but I have had a few headaches start to come on, and with each headache, I applied the cream to my temples, under my eyes, and to the base of my skull and the feeling has gone away each time within about an hour.

With all of this said, I couldn't rate this "eye" cream turned headache remedy anything less than 5 stars despite my initial less-than-thrilled first impression. Because the cream is light and only requires a very small amount with each application, I think the small jar will actually last me a reasonably long time, too. Between the headache relief and the disappearing eye bags, I would be confident in recommending this product to others. I was also fortunate to receive my first jar of this cream at a discounted price or free in exchange for my honest and unbiased review.

title: A fair diffuser
text:
I've been diffusing essential oils for almost 30 years, ever since I purchased my first diffuser from Whole Foods back in the 1980s. This diffuser is not representative of the latest generation of diffusers, but it fits nicely within the last generation. The latest generation of diffusers are not waterless, cordless (rechargeable) and portable. I have both types of diffusers in my home and much prefer the latest gen.

This is a nice diffuser but is slightly more expensive than it should be, even with the ceramic appointments. Like all water diffusers you put water in the chamber with a few drops of oil and let it go. The light is nice but doesn't serve much purpose other than to remind you that the unit is on when you cannot see the cold steam. I'm not a fan of the whole thing being lit because it does cause me to take a second look if my eyes slightly open while I'm sleeping. I prefer a thin band of light. Of course on this unit you can turn the light off.

It doesn't come with any oil which is actually good. I find that when an oil is included in with a diffuser it's often the cheapest brand around and smells awful. It might be enough to turn a newbie off of diffusing if they don't know that high quality oils exist. I recommend Plant Therapy.

I don't buy into the claim that this can be used as a humidifier because the output is just not strong enough. After shut-off there is always water still left in the chamber. This is not a good thing because if you want to change oils, you have to diffuse water with vinegar for a couple of run-throughs and then wipe down the inside. Of course there is nothing wrong with left over oil if you don't mind a blend, but sometimes I want one pure smell for a specific purpose.

title: Beard/Stache Facial Hair Growth Supplement Support
text:
Beard/Stache Facial Hair Growth Supplement Support
27 Beard and Mustache Facial Hair Growth Nutrients in 1 Formula. Supports healthy looking hair growth by providing Biotin (5000 mcg) + herbal extracts + vitamins + minerals for maximum beard growth / mustache growth / beard health.

i've only begun taking these supplements a week ago, so i think it is too soon to say what the effect will be for me, but i will come back and update this review in a few months to report what happened. in the meantime, am reviewing the contents of these supplements.

aside from the usual and common Vitamin C, Vitamin E, Vitamin B-6, Pantothenic Acid, Zinc, Selenium, Copper, Manganese, Citrus Bioflavonoid 50% Complex, Goji Berry 40% Extract, Olive Water Extract, and Silica, there are some ingredients i am not very familiar with so i researched them to see what i could learn. here's what i found out:

Biotin Biotin plays a key role in the body. It supports the health of the skin, nerves, digestive tract, metabolism, and cells. Biotin may also help to treat some types of nerve pathology, such as the peripheral neuropathy that can result from kidney failure or diabetes.
Biotin supplements have been studied as a treatment for a number of conditions. In people with type 2 diabetes, early research suggests that a combination of biotin and chromium might improve blood sugar. On its own, biotin might decrease insulin resistance and nerve symptoms related to type 2 diabetes.

Hydrolyzed Collagen Type 1 & 3 are a family of proteins that are part of body tissues, including skin, cartilage and joints. While there are more than a dozen types of collagen, 80 to 90 percent of collagen found in the body consists of types 1, 2 and 3.

L-Methionine Loss of methionine has been linked to senile greying of hair. Its lack leads to a buildup of hydrogen peroxide in hair follicles, a reduction in tyrosinase effectiveness, and a gradual loss of hair color. Methionine is an intermediate in the biosynthesis of cysteine, carnitine, taurine, lecithin, phosphatidylcholine, and other phospholipids. Improper conversion of methionine can lead to atherosclerosis.

Hydrolyzed Keratin is one of a family of fibrous structural proteins. Keratin is the protein that protects epithelial cells from damage or stress. It is the key structural material making up the outer layer of human skin. It is also the key structural component of hair and nails, and it provides the necessary strength for masticatory organs, such as the tongue and the hard palate. Keratin monomers assemble into bundles to form intermediate filaments, which are tough and form strong unmineralized tissues found in reptiles, birds, amphibians, and mammals. The only other biological matter known to approximate the toughness of keratinized tissue is chitin.

Hyaluronic Acid Hyaluronic acid is found in many tissues of the body, such as skin & cartilage. it is well suited to biomedical applications targeting these tissues.

Alpha Lipoid Acid essential for aerobic metabolism. It is also manufactured and is available as a dietary supplement in some countries where it is marketed as an antioxidant. In Japan, LA is marketed primarily as a "weight loss" and "energy" supplement.

Gotu Kola Extract used as a medicinal herb in Ayurvedic medicine, traditional African medicine, and traditional Chinese medicine. It is also known as the Asiatic pennywort or Indian pennywort in English. In traditional herbal medicine, Gotu kola has been used for varicose veins, chronic venous insufficiency, psoriasis, and minor wounds

Grape Seed 95% Extract. Grape seed oil from crushed seeds is used in cosmeceuticals and skincare products for perceived health benefits. Grape seed oil contains tocopherols (vitamin E) and high contents of phytosterols and polyunsaturated fatty acids such as linoleic acid, oleic acid, and alpha-linolenic acid.

MSM MSM is sold as a dietary supplement and marketed with a variety of claims, often in combination with glucosamine and/or chondroitin for helping to treat or prevent osteoarthritis.

Fo-Ti Root Powder F. multiflora is used in traditional Chinese medicine as a tonic and an anti-aging remedy.

Indian Gooseberry Fruit Extract hair oil are traditionally believed to nourish the hair and scalp and prevent premature grey hair.

Bladderwrack Powder. a seaweed found on the coasts of the North Sea, the western Baltic Sea, and the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, also known by the common names black tang, rockweed, bladder fucus, sea oak, black tany, cut weed, dyers fucus, red fucus, and rock wrack. It was the original source of iodine, discovered in 1811, and was used extensively to treat goitre, a swelling of the thyroid gland related to iodine deficiency.

Nori Yaki edible seaweed species of the red algae genus Pyropia

Wakame Powder New studies conducted at Hokkaido University have found that a compound in wakame known as fucoxanthin can help burn fatty tissue. Studies in mice have shown that fucoxanthin induces expression of the fat-burning protein UCP1 that accumulates in fat tissue around the internal organs. In Oriental medicine it has been used for blood purification, intestinal strength, skin, hair, reproductive organs and menstrual regularity.

Natural Astaxanthin The primary use for humans is as a dietary supplement. Research suggests that, due to astaxanthin's antioxidant activity, it may be beneficial in cardiovascular, immune, inflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases.

as you can see, there's is not much mention of these ingredients as far as hair growth goes. the closest i can tell, some are good for slowing the aging of hair. maybe this translates into darker hair, which makes a beard seem fuller. i am not sure. but.... these ingredients have many other beneficial uses, as you can see, so i figure if my body is benefitting, this is a worthwhile investment, at least for a few months.

title: Above-Average Coffee Man Release From O Boticario
text:
O Boticario is a prodigious South American house not especially popular elsewhere. Paradiso, a fairly new launch in their Coffee Man series, is pretty darn good. The others have left me wanting more, well, coffee. Interestingly this one doesn't. Maybe my expectations are lower as I understand this isn't intended to be a monolithic "coffee-scent" but the note seems surprisingly prominent. Fragrantica proclaims it an Oriental Vanilla whilst O Boticario themselves state it's a Gourmand Woody ("Deodorizing Cologne" -- a South American thing). So what IS it!?

Cop out: all the above. I think Coffee Man Paradiso is a pretty well blended chocolate coffee with a tablespoon of sweet vanilla syrup and a pinch of spice and woods, the latter of which become subservient to the edible notes in the heart but add depth throughout the life of the fragrance. A quite wearable and versatile decent quality masculine semi-casual/semi-formal fragrance. Performance is professional: the above-average longevity exceeds the projection/sillage.

I am compelled to liken Coffee Man Paradiso to "tiramisu" scent Ferragamo Uomo, which I just didn't get (figuratively nor literally except for a decant after doubting my own nose). I can say Paradiso is nicer and less synthetic to me once the alcohol has fully evaporated and the echoes of the distant hype-train's whistle have subsided.

Final note: buy this ONLY through reputable distribution channels as there is a huge cottage industry in Latin America of selling fakes to touristas, especially gringos.

Okay so I have used this product more than a dozen times more than a year. I love it. Works great for my eye brows. Here is what I have learned:
1. It can stain your counters/sink. Put a towel or rag down. If you do get it on your counters clean immediately. Soft scrub works well!
2. It doesn’t stain your skin. Don’t worry about trying to be neat about it and being detailed to your eye brow. Just slap that crap all over and set your phone timer for however long you want for how dark you want (I prefer 3 mins for a dark brown)
3. Set up. Mixing in that little bowl can be messy. I like to use a Q tip to slowly mix it. This way it does not get everywhere on my brush and I make sure I don’t leave any unmixed powder on my brush when I apply to my face.
4. Clean up. Cleaning that bowl again don’t want to get on the counters when you have extra left in the bowl. I use a baby wipe to get the extra out before rinsing the bowl and brush. This way I make sure my counters stay unstained!

text:
I've never posted a review on Amazon before. That should be all the explanation necessary.

First something about the man behind the product. I've known Andy on and off over the better part of the past decade. We both have continually run in to each other at modeling castings, jobs, social events. As such, I feel confident in making the following assessment of his character.
I can absolutely 100 percent validate and testify to the the genuine sincerity and humility that radiates throughout Andy's life. He is unflappably kind and exhaustively gracious both in his business and interpersonal life.

Why would a character assessment of someone matter in this space? Because you know his word is worth something. Andy would rather be thought a failure than thought a fraud. He has no interest in pushing a product that does not do exactly what it says it does. He has no interest in swapping out inferior ingredients to increase profit margins. He has no desire to play fast and loose with marketing talk and salesmanship b.s. His primary goal is to make a product that makes people feel better about their appearance and do so in a way that is ethical and healthy.

I know very little about beauty products and the beauty world so I can't say that this mask is far superior to anything else on the market, although my mom, girlfriend, and sisters all absolutely swear by it. (I got my girlfriend on to it after she got a sort of burn scar on her cheek. The scar wouldn't go away for a month. As far as people go though, you won't get a better breed of entrepreneur than Andy Hnilo, and for that fact alone I will support any product he stands behind.

title: My experience with Harry's was "meh"
text:
Just to be clear, I didn't buy this exact set...but Amazon does not list the Winston set (that I bought) which was being sold prior to the holidays. I would assume the only difference is the cosmetics. The razors should be identical.

I decided to try Harry's after being a Gillette guy for years (I'm 57). I've used the OLD blue plastic, twin blade disposables...all the way up to the Fusion Proglide. I was typically happy with the Gillette shave, but was looking for a better ROI. After reading a lot of site reviews at sites like AskMen, I chose Harry's instead of one of the other options like Dollar.

Harry's Pros:
Looks good
Trimmer blade (all razors should have one)
Aftershave balm feels and smells nice

Cons:
Feels a little cheap for the price
The 5 blades are tough to get clean
The foaming shave gel is REALLY tough to get out of the blades and it doesn't lubricate that well

The shave delivered by the razor is neither a pro nor con...just run of the mill. I didn't notice a real difference between it and my Mach 3 or Proglide. Also, the blades seem to last about as long as the Gillette's. One thing that was disappointing (I should have read the fine print), Harry's doesn't recommend it's razor for your head. I shave my face or head every day...I have a close-cropped Van Dyke and a shaved head, so I alternate shaving each, each morning. I've been using this set for several weeks now, so I've given it a pretty good shot.

I can neither recommend nor reject Harry's...and as well all know, your mileage may vary.

title: Clean & lube your blades while running
text:
I am not a beautician or barber, just someone with 2 dogs needing regular clipping. I remember seeing this product or a similar one in barbershops where my Dad would go to get a haircut. It was in a good-sized flatish round jar and the barber would dip the tip and bottom of his clippers in it while running and they would come out shiny and hair free. Now the jar looked like a pot of disease waiting to get passed on to the next customer as it had floating bits of hair and residue from who knows what.

I had been cleaning and oiling my clipper blades after each grooming and using a coolant on them during clipping to keep the blade's surface from getting too hot. Cleaning the blades afterwards never seemed to get all the hair from between the teeth even using a tooth brush and sliding the two blades back and forth. This stuff really CLEANS all the hair off and you can hear that the blades are better lubricated by the reduced noise. I do wipe them quickly so as not to drip any of the H42 onto the dog. They are shining and humming pleasantly after dipping them into this stuff. I will continue to buy this product as I feel it will extend the life of my clippers and make for a better cutting blade.

Now for the down side and why I took off one star. This stuff still comes in the good sized flatish round "tub-like" container and is seems intended that you dip the blades (not the motor, just the blade tips and bottom) into the whole container full and continue to reuse this stuff over multiple cuts. I don't care if it is Virucidal and Anti-bacterial, that seems like a really unclean way to use this. I solve this problem by pouring a small amount into another container (at least 1/4 inch deep) and dip my clippers in that. I discard the stuff after each groom. Unfortunately the container it comes in does not pour without dripping and yes, you use more of this stuff using my method. I continue to use oil and coolant, but this stuff truly cleans off the bits that get between the teeth and seems to get the blades running much smoother. I do recommend this product, but not for using the reservoir full repeatedly over several cuts or clippings. That method just doesn't sound like a healthy way to go. So if you use clippers on humans or dogs, I feel this product may be of use to you.

title: About this book ...
text:
The first edition of The Presence came out in 1945 and went through two printings. Berthold von Schenk had by then been a LCMS parish pastor for 27 years and was serving his third parish, Our Saviour Lutheran Church in the Bronx, New York. The material came from years of sermons, lectures and retreat meditations. The Presence is his confession of what the Holy Eucharist means to him and what it can mean for us: the actual presence and self-giving of the living Christ.

The 65 years since its original publication have not diminished the power of The Presence to illuminate the well-known narratives and doctrines of our faith in striking ways. It would be a rare pastor or layperson who reads it through without recognizing thereafter holy ground not seen before in worship and life, and without an ever-deepening love for Holy Communion.
This edition is an updated printing of von Schenk's original 1945 edition. Footnotes and an introduction are provided by The Rev. Paul Robert Sauer, current pastor of Our Saviour Lutheran Church in the Bronx, New York.

title: Great set of gentle clippers
text:
This is an excellent set of clippers for more than just younger children. My nephew is on the spectrum and has trouble with various sensations and noise, so haircuts have always been an exercise in patience.

Unlike other hair clippers, the sound level with these is lower and less irritating to him. The ceramic blades and guides are also more gentle on skin. He's been nicked before by barbers and stylists, and that has only added to this apprehension of getting his hair cut. The blades on this set of clippers isn't as sharp as what you'd find in a barbershop (probably because they are ceramic versus steel), so you do have to make a couple more passes to cut hair and to get a close shave on the neck, but that's okay because he doesn't fear being cut by these clippers. The blade covers are also smoother without any edges from the plastic molds or those sharp little nodes from where plastic was injected into the molds or where the guides were snapped apart. It's almost as if they went through a sanding process. It's a little thing, but then again it's not, you know?

Battery life is pretty good as well. One full charge is more than enough to get through a haircut even if the person has thick hair.

title: Has the tools needed to handle our face/hands/feet/skin issues.
text:
Short summary: I like a number of the instruments available in this set; they work well for my needs, and for the needs of our family members.
The case securely holds each instrument in its slot; but some instruments are tough to remove from their slots.

More details:

a) Case is soft to the touch and comfortable to hold. There is a tab that I press in to open the case; to close the case, I press both parts of the case together.

b) One compartment (the side with the tab) holds:
--- Nail File
Works well to smooth out my nails after I trimmed them.
--- Fingernail Clipper
The curved blades cut my nails well. The lever has square-shaped divots that give good
grip. It is a bit hard to rotate the lever around the pin; but, with continued use, it should
be easier to open and close the lever. There is no nail file attached to the clipper
--- Nose trimmer
I did not find this to be as good at cutting my nose hairs.
---.Cuticle nipper
This trims my cuticles well.
--- Eyebrow trimmer
This does a decent job in trimming eyebrow
--- Cuspidal/Obtuse push-type broach
I didn't have a need to use this; but several family members used this, and they say it
does an adequate job with their nail polish routine
--- Ear pick
I tried it, but I didn't like the sensation of it scraping against the inside of my ear.

c) The other compartment holds:
--- Toenail clipper
Curved blades cut my toenails well; however, it does not cut my big toenail because
that nail has too much fungus and is too thick. I used a different toenail clipper
recommended by my foot doctor.
--- Oblique nail clipper
I don't use this often for cutting my nail; but I like how easily it cuts the nails. Other
family members love it, and are more familiar in using it
--- Nail cleaning knife
I don't use this; others in my family say it works well to remove the debris under their nails.
--- Tweezers
My family members do not like this, because it doesn't open enough for them to use; so they went
back to using their preferred tweezers
--- Zig Zag callus remover
--- Oblique callus remover
--- Flat callus remover
note: so far, those of us with calluses (including me) do not have them so thick that
they need removal using these instruments.
--- Dead skin fork
a family member used it; she says it is quite useful in removing the loose skin right
around her cuticle area
--- Ear pick (has something like a serrated shape, perhaps)
I much prefer this ear pick; it felt more natural and is like what I used in the past.
--- Acne tool (one end with a circular loop; other end with a pick)
--- Acne tool (one end with a circular loop; other end with a scoop)
None of our family members currently have acne, so we haven't had a chance to try it;
but, we have similar instruments just like these, and those worked well when we've
needed to deal with our skin issues.

Lastly: I would have liked the case to be slightly larger, so that it is easier to remove all these instruments. When I removed all the instruments, some of which I used, others which my family members used, and then put the instruments back into the case, we couldn't get it to close. Finally, we removed the toenail clippers, and that easily closed the case.

Overall, this is a good manicure set, with instruments that I and/or my family members find to be very useful for our particular needs.

title: Love these paper sheet masks, but pricier than others
text:
These are pricier than other compressed facial masks, but they have the advantage of prime shipping (as opposed to 2-3 weeks for international shipping) and of being individually wrapped. I wanted to try making my own masks asap, and also want to take these when I travel and to throw in beauty gifts (spa in a jar) for friends and family. So the fast shipping and individually wrapped masks were worth paying more for me.

I love the concept of soaking these in whatever you like, or placing over a mud mask so that my skin can soak up the benefits and detoxify without drying out too fast. However, these are a bit too small for me width-wise and definitely too small for my hubby (who is willing to sheet mask with me!). I'll probably buy these again just because I can easily travel with them and use in gifts, but I am going to look for larger ones that I can use on a more regular basis. And once you see the difference sheet masking can do for your skin, you might just look forward to using these as often as you can! I know I do!

(I found a really good recipe to brighten and moisturize the face: one egg white, teaspoon of honey, and the juice of a lemon/lime slice. Whisk it together, or shake in a jar, and dab all over your face. Then soak your mask in it and place on your face. It feels sooo good! And is cheap :)

title: Love it - Favorite One - Right now
text:
This is my favorite body scrub. The sugar chamomile one. I have tried a lot of different ones. One years ago that is no longer on the market was my absolute favorite, which is why this only gets 4 stars. I did get a bad batch recently, which I attribute to either sitting too long in some warehouse or supply chain issues. It has been a little tough to find.

I have very sensitive skin & even worse allergies & this does not break me out or set off my allergies. When properly mixed & emulsified, it’s great. It works on my skin the way I want it to. It doesn’t dry my skin out or make it sticky, oily or itchy/flakey. It also doesn’t destroy my shower/tub. It washes politely & completely down the drain & doesn’t stain or send grit everywhere. There is no remaining residue on my skin or my surroundings.

I don’t love the smell. It’s a mostly pleasant natural smell, but it took some getting used to. In my opinion, it’s way better than the other 2 products this company makes in this category. They reek to high heaven & make a terrible mess. I still regret using the pink-salt one, the perfume was too strong & awful. The grit was too strong & stained the silicone sealant on my tub. It’s still there.

I like this one for all the previously stated reasons, but I don’t love the smell or the tube. The seal on all of there products is strong, which is great for assurances, safety & transport, but it’s also tiny & a bitch to get off in the shower. So, don’t forget to take it off 1st, the way I sometimes do. I usually have to use my teeth & you know how that goes… yeah. The bottle could be a little bigger too. I don’t know what sizing the product would cost, but it would be nice for the consumer. Also, the last inch or 2 of product, in the tube doesn’t always come out. Again it’s the tube’s design & they all work that way. It’s VERY annoying. If they would make the inner nozzle/outlet a little bigger & the “top” a steeper pitch, it would be 100% better. Work with gravity & let me use all the product I pay for please (especially at these prices)! Thanks!

Anyway, this is currently my go to scrub. I don’t usually use it on my face, but I have been considering trying it on my scalp, it seems gentle enough. And it dissolves enough. I will add to this review if I do. I have been able to find this product at Sprouts, grocery store as well as on Amazon. I think I have seen it at Natural Grocers & Whole Foods too, but it’s been since before COVID, so not sure. I have never seen a sample product, but if you can find them, I would suggest trying all of them that way - if that works for your needs - before you buy. Depending on quality, which has been wonky the last 3 tubes, I get between 3-9 showers out of 1 tube. The better blended it is, the closer to 6 showers it is. I tend to use a lot. I am generous & I use it on most of my body. I do really like this stuff & can say I would recommend it to someone I know, whose skin care I know about, given the opportunity. It is a natural product, if you are allergic to chamomile tea, do not use this product, ever. If not, it’s, in my opinion, one of the nicest body scrub products out there. I like a lot of Desert Essence products.

text:
Well they say “expectations are the source of all unhappiness”, and maybe that’s the problem. I was expecting this soap to be significantly better than the glycerin-based soaps I’ve been using (which cost a third of what this does), and it just... isn’t. It does a good job, and it lasts a long time, but I didn’t notice any improvement in lubricity or lather richness over my previous soaps.
And the scent was inoffensive, but underwhelming.
As for long-lasting, see the attached picture for what the soap looks like after two months of daily use. It (quite literally) barely made a dent in it. So that’s a plus in the “value” department.
One other issue that may or may not be the soap’s fault: the steel travel tin I was using it in had been used for months with other soaps, and no problems. With this soap, it rusted to uselessness in two months. (The inside, around and under the soap, was completely oxidized and flaking off.) That was curious to me, but I don’t have enough data to say it was definitely caused by the soap.
In summary, it’s a decent soap. Kind of expensive, but I don’t mind paying for quality. But somehow, I was expecting something like mythical powers out of a lanolin soap, and they’re just not there.

title: A fairly aggressive razor
text:
Coming from my mild Rimei and Baili razors, I'd say this razor is pretty aggressive. Significantly higher blade exposure than what I'm used to. I have very coarse, tough facial hairs, but pretty sensitive skin on my throat and upper lip, so as you can imagine, shaving can be a nightmare for me if the razor and blade combo is wrong.

I like this razor, but it will take some getting used to. I would recommend using a less sharp, smoother blade at first, such as a Derby or a Big Ben, unless you already know you can handle the combination of an aggressive razor with a very sharp blade.

I first ordered the Rapira Swedish Supersteel razor, but it came with a bent guard (looked damaged in shipping), so I sent it back. Aside from that, that razor has a metal handle (zinc?) and the weight was more balanced towards the handle. This razor is overall lighter and the weight is more balanced towards the head, which I prefer. The head on both razors is the same Tech-type design.

The handle is good, probably not as tough as a metal handle though. I'd prefer a better grip on it, similar to a rougher checkered surface like on a plastic rifle stock or something, but it does the job.

title: Love it, with a few conditions
text:
Okay, I've got crazy sensitive skin and basically can't use any antiperspirant and many natural deodorants without having a reaction. I've tried at least 20 different brands- Tom's, Herban Cowboy, Lume, Weleda- and I've tried roll-ons, sticks, creams, powders, you name it. I work up a sweat at work every day and unfortunately for me and my laundry basket, I can be a stinky person. This is one of my favorite natural deodorants I've tried, but it does have some drawbacks:

Pros:
1. Smells delightful. It is an earthy, aromatheraputic type scent (not perfumey). If you like Aveda products you'll like how this smells. And an extra pro, the smell is not overwhelming- I can't even smell it when it's on unless I smell my armpit directly. Nice!
2. Good staying power. Unlike most roll-ons I've tried, it dries quickly and at the end of the day I can still smell it if I smell my armpit. I do smell some sweat, too, but it doesn't smell like b.o. Nice!
3. No bad skin reactions after 2 months of use. First product I've used in YEARS that I got away with using this long. Very nice!
4. Washes out of fabrics. Some other essential oil type deo's I've used in the past have left oil marks on the armpits of my shirts. I've had no issues with this product. We love it!
Cons:
1. Pricier than a lot of other brands. I've been using it as recommended, morning and evening, for about 7 weeks, and I have about 1/5 left of the bottle.
2. Like every other roll-on, does nothing to soothe chafing if you're wearing a tank or t shirt or you move around a lot.
3. On hot, busy days, a midday reapplication goes a long way. I don't have time/access to do this at my work, so some days I just get stinky. But I will say, I don't get as stinky as I have with a lot of other products.

Bottom line, I'll buy it again so I don't run out, but I'm still on the hunt for the *just right* one for me. Overall, 8/10. Tics most boxes for me, and the scent is really lovely.

title: I love snails!
text:
I love snail slime. I have been reading about it for a while and am so glad I pulled the trigger to purchase it. I get occasional acne and scar easily. After two uses I saw a profound improvement in my skin. Nothing works that fast.I am a believer and am buying up all the slime I can find. The use of snail slime to improve skin dates back to ancient Greece, where Hippocrates, the famous physician, reportedly prescribed crushed snails and sour milk as a way to rid the skin of inflammation. In more recent times, the use of snail creams started when Chilean farmers who handled snails for the French market noticed their skin was visibly smoother. Nowadays, it is the secreted slime discovered by these farmers that is harvested to produce snail cream, not crushed up snails.
How the Slime Works
When snails are agitated, they excrete a thick fluid as a means to protect themselves. It may sound odd to use something like that on your skin, but remember that humans and most other animals also excrete oils as a way to protect their skin. In fact, the oil your body excretes to moisturize your skin is made up of lipids, sebum oil, and dead skin cells. As a snail protects itself, the slime that is excreted from its body is packed with nutrients like hyaluronic acid, glycoprotein enzymes, antimicrobial and copper peptides, and proteoglycans. All of these nutrients are already commonly added to beauty products and are thought to provide many benefits to skin.
The science behind snail slime as a viable beauty cream is mostly derived from lab studies where the effects of the slime have been tested on a variety of cell cultures. In these studies, research suggests that snail slime will stimulate the production of elastin and collagen, increase fibronectin protein production, and stimulate increased proliferation of fibroblasts. While all of these traits could be beneficial for skin, there have yet to be significant cosmetic trials or research into how snail slime actually affects the skin, and how long those effects last. In fact, there haven’t been any significant clinical trials on how a specific beauty product containing snail slime actually works on this skin – just the slime itself.
One of the main difficulties in conducting clinical trials on the benefits of snail slime is that the market has not fully figured out how to guarantee the results of testing. After all, if snail creams are to be effective, then the slime has to have a consistent concentration of the various chemical compounds, but this is difficult to guarantee. Because the success of trials leans heavily on the quality of snail extract used, the concentration of slime and the way it is excreted and processed, test results can sometimes be misleading. Some companies that manufacture snail creams do choose to keep a steady supply of their own snails so they can better regulate the extraction and formulation of the slime.

My SO and I had hit a MAJOR rough patch..barely speaking for almost two weeks.. the day it arrived, I showered that evening and rolled some on the back of my neck, and a little on my wrists, then went down to plop on the couch about 18” or so from him..within 2 minutes, (I swear this is true) he turned towards me and in that sweet voice that I hadn’t heard in so long.. really seemed to be looking deeply at me and uttered ‘Damn baby. I don’t know what it is but you smell effing fantastic’ as he reached over and put his face deep into my neck. AFTER BARELY SPEAKING FOR OVER TWO WEEKS!! And now THIS?? You’re not getting details of how the rest of the evening went ; )
but I promise it wasn’t easy stifling a giggle while wondering if this stuff is REALLY that powerful..or what other forces were at work? And yes, three weeks later, the magic is still happening?? It’s not that expensive, I like the roller ball, the scent is very pleasant, and it sure does what it’s supposed to! Oh..I’d just started a new job and today my Mgr told me I smelled nice and I sent her the link! This is my story, every word is true and no one asked me to write this..
Just found the whole experience interesting and thought I’d share?
Order it and see what you think?

text: I've used two other Norelco's. An older 7885 with just straight slots in the heads (but lift and cut). and one with the combination of shaped slots in the head. Once you learn how much pressure to use, there is little irritation, the same or less than with the earlier models. I found the spring adjustment in the head to be fine at the default setting, so the "more sensitive" settings won't be useful to me. It seems well made. The one gripe i have is it has a converter in the cord and the cord is straight (both of my earlier ones had coiled cords which I prefer). title: My new favorite wig. Great if you have a big head.
text:
This arrived a day sooner than expected, in less than a week! I am so happy with it. It is the second lace front I have bought. My first was also from Amazon, but it had a middle part and was completely straight and very long. It looked pretty, but it wasn't right for me, and tangled so so much. I realized I needed something closer to my preferred look when I have long hair, with a side part (I buzzed my real hair recently to remove bleach-damaged hair and a cut I didn't like).

PROS: This has the perfect round-brush blowout look, and the hair itself is a mix of dark purple and dark brown, very cool and subtle. The layering is PERFECT, and the hairs are soft but realistic, with a slight kink that keeps it from looking too fake (although I still chose to mist it with some dry shampoo to tone down the shine a bit). Most importantly it DOES NOT TANGLE. All the wigs I have tangle SO much and its the one thing I can not stand about wigs. It also fits my head really well. I have a big head and usually have to do some fiddling with wig caps and lace to get it to fit right and not squeeze my head too much, but I practically just popped this on and was good to go, no glue/tape needed!

CON: It sheds. I cut it a little around the hairline to make the all-important baby hairs, and later when I brushed it I thought I was just brushing out the long hairs I had cut, but the more I brushed it the more I saw hairs were falling out around the whole wig. This doesn't bother me too much, as long as not too much comes out. Overall, I love this wig and I intend to buy it again in other colors.

EDIT: I took this on vacation soon after receiving it. I wore it every single day of my trip and it looks so great in my vacay pics and random people would compliment the purple highlights.

text:
Okay so I received this about 6 weeks ago.

First impressions:
Upon opening my package, I noticed the box was already sort of opened and not sealed... I assumed it's because it is a cheap product. I also noticed that in the serum, I had white clumps which I assumed was due to the freezing temperatures outside at the time. I also noticed this product had a very astringent smell -- similar to alcohol.

Usage:
I had been using it twice daily after cleansing, toning, and my essence. I am used to using a serum, but this product seriously made my face super red every time I applied it. I assumed it was due to a niacin conversion on my skin, but after a couple weeks, I started breaking out more than ever. I noticed that my skin was completely sensitive, red, and everything would sting my face. I did not think it was this product at first, but after i stopped using this product completely, the redness and sensitivity stopped.

Conclusion:
Do not buy this product. In my case, this product made my skin worse than it has ever been along with being super crazy sensitive. I do not recommend this to anyone, but perhaps I received a bad batch? The lot/manufacturing stamp on the product is "8LB" if anyone with the same lot/manufacturing stamp is having a similar issue...
However, if you are looking for a niacinamide+zinc formula, I would recommend Revolution Skincare Niacinamide+Zinc from Ulta instead. I have now been using that for about 3 weeks without any of the same issues from the Ordinary.
