title: Almost perfect
text:
I purchased an sleep mask just like this in a store and, when it went missing, searched for it high and low until I found it here on Amazon. The mask blocks light well with little or no light leaking in around your nose and none around the eyes. The contoured eye coverings place no pressure on your eyelids. I never felt comfortable sleeping in a traditional sleep mask until I used this style. I can even open my eyes in my mask and my lashes don't even brush it.

The comfort in wearing meant I quickly adjusted to its use and now can't hardly sleep without it. As someone who has had trouble sleeping and finds napping almost impossible, having the routine of perfect dark when I sleep at night has allowed me to build a trigger. Now, when I need to sleep early, want to catch a nap, find myself in a plane, or other times I might ordinarily find it hard to sleep, I can place my mask on and it signals sleep perfectly. It's improved my sleep length and frequency, as well as reduced the time it takes me to fall asleep, which I think anyone could appreciate.

My only gripe is that, while I thought this one was exactly like my previous mask, there's a little difference. There's a little plastic piece on the side of the elastic that joins loops for the adjustment system and they sit very near my ears. I can sometimes feel it digging in and I never remember feeling that on my previous mask. For occasional use, you may not notice it, but using them nightly, the little part can bother me sometimes. My solution plan involves breaking the part and replacing it with something soft or hand-sewing that connection point. Customization is a very small price to pay for the amazingly comfortable contoured foam that makes up the main body of the mask.

title: Not for me
text:
I'v tried several types of products to remove facial hair: coil groomer, tweezers, electric face trimmer, and these. The coil groomer was the most difficult to use. No matter how much I twisted it, I could only get a hair or two after a few tries. Tweezing was faster and more effective. The electric face trimmer was designed for removing all facial hair, including nose and ear hair, so the cutting tip was very small and the cutting mechanism was gentle on delicate skin. It was great at removing the peach fuzz on my cheeks; I just needed to make several swipes to get my whole cheek.

These shavers are well made. Unfortunately, the instructions were all written in either Japanese or Chinese. I figured they looked self explanatory, so I didn't look up videos on how to use them. The cutting tip is long, which should make shaving go faster as it can cover a larger area. However, the larger blade also means that it is more difficult to reach certain areas. I have a lot of small moles on my face, so I made sure to be extra careful while using them. Despite this, I managed to nick myself a few times. What's ironic is that the nicks weren't on any moles.

I think my skin is just too delicate and uneven to use these shavers.

title: Totally awesome, not perfect, but nothing better out there!
text:
This toothbrush is amazing. Initially, I thought it was going to scrub my teeth out of my mouth, making me feel uncomfortable using it. After a few day's worth of continous brushing, my teeth adjusted to the device.

Let me just say that this brush is highly recommended. My girlfriend uses the Sonicare toothbrush, and side-by-side comparison, my Oral B Sonic toothbrush looks much nicer. hee hee.

Performance? The Oral B Sonic I have uses three speeds. It's about the same compared to the two speed Sonicare. Both have 30 second interval timers. The noise produced by both toothbrushes are comparable as well, although, I believe my toothbrush might be a little quieter.

We have tried out both and I have to say that I feel more comfortable with the Oral B Sonic, because Sonicare has that extra piece of plastic surrounding the brush.

Prior to using Sonic Complete, I was using Oral B's rechargeable 900 series. Sonic Complete blows it out of the water in performance. I still keep my 900 series, because Sonic Complete has one flaw... the main reason why I am not giving it a 5 star rating. Sonic Complete will shutdown automatically at full speed if the battery power is drained. Unlike my 900 series, the battery power as it drains will not weaken the toothbrush, giving you some kind of notification that it needs to be recharged. So I keep my 900 series just in case I need to recharge my Sonic Complete.

The battery power lasted at least 2 weeks from full charge. I brush my teeth at least twice a day and sometimes 3 times, depending on my mood.

Sonic Complete came with a charger, toothbrush holder, I believe two brush heads, traveling case, and a whoop-arse on plaque.

I have thick curly coily AA hair.

It smells a tad too strong and perfumy, and does remind me of waterfalls and springs. It is thicker and creamier than other Suave naturals. It provides great slip, makes my hair soft and fluffy hours after drying, and my hair curls instantly, which lets me know my hair is moisturized.

Waterfall Mist is a great conditioner but not the best Suave bargain. You can find it in stores for as low as $0.85-$1, but it's only available in 12 ounces, whereas Suave Coconut is $1.50 for 33 ounces. So in the long run, this particular scent is not the best purchase for your money. My favorite Suave is Everlasting Sunshine and Coconut, which work even more amazingly on my hair but come in larger sizing with more pleasant scents. If you don't mind paying the same price for less product and really like the scent, then this is a great buy for you.

Everything appears to be quite well made, of sturdy construction. The scissors and nail trimmers came out of the box sharp, and have a good weight to them. The nail trimmers have a good locking mechanism, metal, not plastic; I think it will last. The set comes with a convenient little storage pouch, which I hadn't noticed on the item description specs list. I like the colors of the pouch. They're cute. The pouch easily fits everything in the kit, except the brush. You can make the brush fit, but I dont think you can make the brush and electric clippers fit. I couldn't. The electric clippers come with a usb powered charger cord, but not a charger block. This is not a standard charger. If you lose this charge cord, you may be hard pressed to find a replacement.

The brush is of good construction, and the ergonomic handle grip is a joy to hold. For real, it just feels good in your hand. I like the push button hair dislodger for easy brush cleaning. Our dog is fairly short haired, straight and wirey, and our cat is fluffy but on the short side of medium length hair. It took very little hair off them, and I haven't found a product better than the Furminator for brushing them. But I've had and worked with longer haired dogs, and for a Great Pyrenees, Burnese Mountain Dog, or Saint Bernard, I think this would be the perfect brush.

The nail file worked great. The comb I intend to keep for myself- it's perfect for my wiry, sometimes wavy, sometimes curly, always disobedient hair.

The electric clipper charged fairly quickly, enough that I could take it for a test spin about 15-20 minutes after plugging it in. I love the electronic digital display, showing how far along in its charging it is, and the RPMs of the clipper blades. I love that it came with a little bottle of lubricant solution for the blades (none of my personal trimmers ever have). The little obligatory cleaning brush to sweep between the blades looks much the same that any electric trimmer does, but I found it shed a wire or two with every pass throughthe blades, which my personal trimmer brushes do not.

I tried the electric clippers out on myself first. I was a little bummed that the nearly universal gaurds that come with clippers designed for people did not fit. The clippers are much more quiet then most clippers, which is good for not startling pets. I used the clippers with the guard on the sides of my head and with no gaurd to shave my face. It went easily through my hair, had no trouble, and gave me a close, even shave. And I went a little rough to see if there was any danger of maybe cutting a squirming or struggling pet, and it seems very safe.

The clipper blades came off pretty easy for cleaning, but were kind of tricky to put back on, and in trying to do so, I hit at a funny angle and the entire clipper assembly fell apart in to 4 pieces. That was annoying, but after messing around with it for about a half hour, I was able to put it back together, and it still worked fine. I would be hesitant to take it apart for cleaning again, though I'm sure I will. Despite this one design flaw, I still think overall this is a pretty quality product.

title: Good flosser for the money
text:
DESIGN:

The chrome-plated plastic buttons and cap add a nice touch to the look of the flosser, but it feels a little cheap and will probably wear off quickly. The overall fit and finish is good. It has a nice weight to it—not too heavy or too light. It fits rather comfortably in the hand, even small hands, but the placement of the on/off button creates the sensation that you may unintentionally push it. It doesn’t seem to be a problem, though. The charging port comes with a small rubber insert to protect it from water. It works well, but because it is not attached to the unit, it could easily be lost. It does come with an extra one, though, so that it nice. The portability of this cordless flosser is what I like the most.

PERFORMANCE:

The performance is very good. The power of the water is perfect. One thing I did notice, in comparison to my countertop flosser, is that the third level of power on the cordless flosser is about same as the first level of power on the countertop unit. So, it does not seem quite as powerful as the countertop unit, though the advantage of the portability outweighs the slight loss of power. As for me, I don’t use the highest setting on my countertop unit, anyway, so it is not an issue. A great thing about this flosser is that it is quiet. It doesn’t sound like you are using power tools in your bathroom every time you are flossing. Bottom line, I love this flosser. I think it is a great product for the money. The experience is pleasant, and it does its job well. All in all, a good buy.

I was interested in trying this night cream because it claims to be especially formulated for oily to normal skin.

PACKAGING:🌟🌟🌟☆☆

The night cream comes in a squeezable tube. I am not a big fan of this type of packaging because as you continue to use it, it becomes harder to get the product out and it can be wasteful. However, this type of packaging is great for traveling. Also, while I am not super impressed with the packaging, it does a nice job at keeping the product fresh.

FIRST IMPRESSION: 🌟🌟🌟🌟☆

It has a light to medium consistency. It has a yellowish color but it does not stain your skin. It has a light scent and it is creamy. It is easy to distribute and apply. It does not irritate or cause redness. While you apply it it has a almost glossy finish and the skin feels soft but as it dries the skin looks matte and it feels smooth. There is no visible residue.

PERFORMANCE:🌟🌟🌟☆☆

After I used it the first time I thought, "Actually this is nice, I think I will really like it", but after using it a few more times, I have changed my opinion. It has great benefits and it excels in some areas but in others I am not very impress with it.

I am impress with the quality and its natural ingredients. It feels really nice when you put it on and the scent is not overbearing which is great. It has no parabens or dangerous chemicals. It is cruelty-free. It does not irritate my skin and it does not cause breakouts. It dries very fast which is great for those long days when I can wait to long to go to bed. It does not have a sticky or greasy finish.

I have been using two different serums and they do not seen to get alone with this cream. So I change it to another and the same problem occur. After my serum is absorb into my skin, I apply this cream but it does not go on smoothly. It looks like brush strokes and it is very patchy. At first, I thought that I was applying to much but the results were the same with less product. This is not a big deal since it will dry either way. But it bother me for some reason.

I enjoy how soft and supple my skin feels as soon as I apply it but then it losses that quality and becomes very matte and it is not longer super soft. My face feels a bit stiff. I would not mind much since it might be helping my skin stay firm. Buw when I wake up in the morning my skin does not feel very moisturize which I do not like. Every time I use it, I want to add a sleeping pack on top for moisture.

However, I have to mentioned that while my skin does not feel supple and hydrated in the morning, it is not greasy or oily either. I am not saying the it will remove all of your sebum/oil but it just makes your skin look matte. I give it points for that but honestly, I rather give my skin hydration at night and I do not care much about looking oily.

OVERALL ASSESSMENT:
Price Point: 🌟🌟🌟🌟☆
Quality/Durability: 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟
Need: 🌟🌟🌟☆☆

title: Get it!
text:
I have been using the Helen of Troy Brush Iron for twenty years. Recently, the one I owned for 10+ years finally died. I tried to see if there was something better out there thinking something newfangled would be better. I hunted online for hrs and finally found a more expensive tourmaline model by Conair. Hated it. It's going back. Unlike my trusty Helen of Troy, it was scorching to the touch and easy to burn myself. Unlike my Helen of Troy, it was hard to get my hair to hold to it so I had to wear expensive protective gloves to try to hold my hair to the hot tool. Wearing those gloves made it impossible to section my hair with my fingernail to curl my thick hair all over. The tourmaline model was complicated, painful, more time-consuming and less effective.

Helen of Troy has three settings: High, Low, Off. I set mine on high and it is just right. It gives a very natural full-bodied polished look to hair. I have a lot of fine, straight hair in addition to some curly thick grays. This tool tames and styles them all for a very cohesive polished look. It gently curls the ends under or over with no unsightly crimp on them like a regular curling iron. One of the only shortcomings of the H of T model is that it takes about 5 minutes for it to fully heat up. I heat mine up before I go in shower. When I come out I use mousse in my hair, dry it with my negative Ion hairdryer and give a gentle curl with my trusty Helen of Troy afterwards. It only takes me about 6 minutes to curl my thick straight shoulder length hair. While looking for an alternative tool from my trusty Troy I read that some styling tools take 30-60 minutes to style hair. Personally, I have better things to do than spend that much time in front of a mirror each day. I have had many compliments on my hair over the years. THE EFFECT IS MUCH LIKE AN EXPENSIVE BLOW OUT. The bonus is you don't have to go to the salon to get it. Sometimes I look at Kate Middleton and think I could do a better job on her hair with this trusty inexpensive tool.

Look no further. Just get it.

title: Beautiful Multichrome Pigments!
text:
[[VIDEOID:bde866136544c24b41b9800127851a48]] These come with the 2 jars in a little bubble wrap bag. Inside the jars are held together with some strong plastic sealing (see photos). I really liked that because it helped ensure the jars didn’t break or the lids didn’t come loose and end up with powder everywhere! So I loved that!

The jars are plastic. On the lids is a sticker with the brand name, it’s placed on there unevenly so probably done by hand. The lids twist off and there’s a protective seal on the jars inside. Be VEEEERRRYYY careful when you pull off the protective seals. They are easy to lift and pull off, but I ended up dropping one of the seals after I took it off and it got pigment all over (see photos). I don’t have nails, which probably would have helped me hold onto them. In hindsight I should have used tweezers to pull them off. But, no big deal! The jars are both look to be filled up pretty evenly and the jars are pretty full.

These are beautiful! The shift is definitely more noticeable with the teal one than it is with the purple, but they are still both really beautiful. The shifts I see with the teal are the dark teal color, a brighter teal, dark purple, a pinky purple and a dark green. The shifts I see with the are the purple color, a royal blue color, a brighter blue, and a pinky purple.

These are loose pigments. I touched my finger on the jar to pick some up and swiped it onto my arm. It goes on pretty thin and then when I try to build it up, that only works so well....if I put a swipe on then add another swipe it builds up okay. But, if I try to add more swipes than that, it kind of moves the pigment around and I end up getting uneven areas. When you try to apply them with a brush, a brush picks the pigment up really well, but when you go to apply it, it just kind of blends it away. The more you try to add, the more it seems to blend away. But, since these are pigments, they really should be applied to a sticky base. I always use NYX Multitasker Mixing Medium as glitter glue, but really it’s to use to mix in with loose pigments. So, I took a very tiny dot of the NYX Multitasker Mixing Medium and put that onto my arm. Then, I took a brush and picked up a small amount of pigment. I applied the pigment I picked up with the brush onto the area I put the NYX Mixing Medium. The pigment stuck to it really easily and made it look beautiful - smooth, pigmented. The NYX Multitasker Mixing Medium is just a clear gel like consistency. You get a sticky area wherever you apply it. So, you don’t have to use a mixing medium. Anything that leaves a sticky area for the pigment to grab onto will work, like glitter glue, cream eyeshadow, concealer - just apply it while the product is still wet. I show a photo of the teal where I applied it on the NYX Multitasker Mixing Medium, on a white cream eyeshadow, and on a concealer (LA Girl Pro Conceal in Fairest). I also have a photo of the purple where I applied it on the NYX Multitasker Mixing Medium, on a white cream eyeshadow, and on a concealer (LA Girl Pro Conceal in Fairest). They all held onto the pigment perfectly and the pigment looked beautiful! I also tried all 3 as bases with the pigment on my eyes and they worked just as well. They lasted all day without fading. I definitely want to try more colors!

Overall, I think these are beautiful multichrome pigments! They have beautiful shifts. As I said, I can see the shifts in the teal one a lot easier than in the purple one, but that’s usually the case when I have dark purple multichromes - for me, it always seems like it’s harder to tell the different shifts in a dark purple. In my opinion, most multichromes are usually pretty pricey. At the time of this review, these 2 multichrome pigments were $25, so that’s $12.50 a piece. Considering you get a little jar full of pigment, I don’t think that’s too bad. For example, a JD Glow multichrome eyeshadow (pressed in a pan) is $15. I don’t mind paying more for an eyeshadow over a pigment because I just prefer working with eyeshadows pressed into a pan rather than loose pigments. So, for these jars to end up being $12.50 each, I don’t think that’s too bad. They look beautiful and perform well!

title: I bought this why...?
text:
The only reason this razor works--and the only reason I rated it with even 3 stars--is because it's a Venus razor. Venus razors work excellently, so when this new version came out I was excited to try it. I've owned mine for over a year now, and was unimpressed with it from the moment I started using it.

The vibrations are useless; I get the same quality shave whether it's turned on or off. The battery lasted quite a long time, but as soon as I replaced it the razor stopped working properly (not that it mattered, since it didn't do anything in the first place). So not only do we have a "power" razor that has no power, but the company decided to charge even more for replacement razor cartridges. I thought I had to use the corresponding cartridges, but finally I inserted one of the old Venus cartridge heads and it worked exactly the same.

I don't know--maybe I'm just a no-fuss girl who really doesn't notice subtle differences in the quality of leg-shaving. I would recommend Venus brand razors in a heartbeat, but I do NOT recommend this particular version.

title: Works well overall - but "bristles" vary in length year to year, become brittle and break off too easily.
text:
It is difficult to find a large barreled curling iron/brush. HELEN OF TROY offers a broad range of assorted sizes, and they work well. This is my third or fourth purchase of this same model in about 10 years. Even though I purchase the same model, I find that the hard plastic "bristles" vary in height from year to year. The short "bristles" sometimes place the hot barrel too close to my skin, especially when the "bristles" break off (which is fairly easy and common, possibly due to overexposure to heat). The models that arrived with longer "bristles" are more suited for longer hair, however they sometimes "tangle" in the hair -- and THEY, too break off all too easily. (I have recommended to the manufacturer that they add something slightly more flexible to the "bristles" to keep them from getting brittle and breaking, or perhaps design the barrels so that new sets of bristles can be installed, however -- why would they take my suggestion when consumers can simply replace the entire unit with a new one?) The heating elements in these units have never failed; only the "bristles" are problematic.

Overall, I like this model, but I find that I need to replace it after about 12-18 months of use due to loss of "bristles".

text:
I've been searching for products that I can use for my unique skin concerns - my skin is sensitive, and I'm starting to notice visible signs of aging like dark circles, uneven skin tone, extremely dry winter skin, acne prone chin, and scarring due to a disease called HS.

I'm always happier to use stuff that is all-natural, organic, and cruelty-free, and I prefer to buy from smaller companies if possible. This serum is definitely worth the money - you get 6 oz, which will last a while! The formula is light and gentle, doesn't irritate my skin, and I can use it on every part of my face, chin and neck! I am not breaking out, and I've been using this product for a few weeks now. My skin definitely looks brighter, feels smoother and is well-moisturized.

I love products with AHA's - hyaluronic acid is an example of an Alpha-Hydroxy acid, and these ingredients are especially effective at aiding the shedding of old skin - which reveals a healthier complexion underneath those layers! This is an excellent serum and I've incorporated it into my skin care routine! If you're like me and you're looking for good stuff, look no further! Your skin will thank you! And you can feel good about your purchase because Skin2Spirit is a good company!

Also, I really loved the sample of the eye cream - it definitely helps wake up my eyes, though my sister ended up taking the sample because she also loves it!

title: You can stop looking--THIS is "The One"!!!!
text:
This Eyelash Curler is the BOMB! I'm over 40 and have long eyelashes enhanced by several years of using Latisse. The only issue is, while my lashes ARE long, they are "Unruly". They stick out in multiple directions and if I don't use a curler, they look horrible. Over three years ago I purchased a Shu Uemura online from their site. I was happy with it and it performed well, but the pads wore out and when I went online to purchase another one, I was disappointed to see that not only were they purchased by L'Oreal, they were completely out of stock on eyelash curlers on their own website! The internet is FLOODED with counterfeit Shu Uemuras and frankly I didn't want that either. So I went in search of an alternative.

I purchased another high rated curler, the Billy B Eyelash curler online hoping that it would do the trick. The Billy B one is "different" from the Uemura--it has a more rounded shape and I was hoping it would do a fabulous job. Unfortunately I found that I had a harder time getting the rounded Billy B up next to my eyelash base, and inevitably it would miss my corner lashes entirely. I'm sure the Billy B works well for people with smaller, more rounded eyes, and in all honesty the pads on it were great. It just wasn't the right fit for me.

So again I went searching and that's when I stumbled across the Bella & Bear. This thing is awesome and with a single coat of mascara for work, my eyelashes look a mile long and very well separated. I can't say enough good things about how easy this was to put up against my eyeline and get a good curl. The handle fits my hand well and the spring loaded mechanism on this means you don't have to press all that hard to achieve a good curl. It's flatter and not as rounded as the Billy B, so if your eyes are longer and flatter, this one should be able to easy grab from corner to corner without missing any lashes. In fact, when I lined up my curlers side by side, you can see the shape of this one is more like the Uemura than the Billy B.

The curler arrives packaged in a box, so you won't have to worry about it being broken in shipment.

In all, I'm so happy with this eyelash curler that I will never go back to another brand. So long as this one never gets broken I should be in business for a very long time. I've already recommended it to a friend to use on her daughter's long eyelashes during dance recitals. My search for the perfect curler is over!

text: I have tried using soooo many different products to fill in/obscure a deeply indented scar in my cheek. And most creams don't work well when filling in such a deep scar, as they don't set up solidly. Finally--success with this Ben Nye product!! First, I apply some Aveeno Baby lotion around the perimeter of the scar area. Next, I put some lotion on a little flat-head "tool" (not included) that I use to scoop out a small amount of wax and fill in the indentation. Finally, I put a small amount of lotion on my forefinger and smooth out the edges (if any) of wax extending past the indented area. title: Opinions may differ but I've searched In earnest, tried It all, and I've found *THIS IS THE BEST*
text:
I'm pretty particular, got a pretty good eye for discerninbg fine detail, worked in production for Universal Studios where where cosmetic detail is priority, , and for my aging beard, I've tried every product I can find. It's been a little over 2 years since I tried the Grizzly product and have not looked for or tried anything since. It's settled in my mind that you'll get the most realistic, undetectable, natural looking color enhancing of your beard. I mix about 1/3 Dark Brown with 2/3 Black. I do leave it on much longer than recommended sometimes 2-3 hours.

I also do it before I go to sleep to avoid down time waiting. IT DOES LOOK FUNNY WHEN YOU FIRST RINSE..."but"....it slowly changes to a natural look so you may want to DO IT AT NIGHT BEFORE BED or at least 6-8 hours before you venture out. I've gotten both green and purple tint upon rinsing but again, *this is part of the process* and the exposure to air and time slowly oxidizes the pigment and it will look amazing in several hours. Don't be afraid to mix shades to nail exactly what you want. I've used it with 3-4 inches beard length but lately keep it the "unshaven" stubble look with 1/8" to 1/4" length. As far as cost goes, I buy two shades, I apply twice a week, and from those two bags I get a full year. My last purchase was Oct. '17 and I'm just coming back to re-order. The previous year my beard was longer, maybe 3", and I re-ordered twice in a 12 month period. ..so it's now costing me around $2.50 per month to keep my beard looking much younger and natural looking.

My beard has much more gray than my hair, I'd say about 90% is white hairs. It took 2 or 3 applications in the first week or two for it to fully "take" , then it's just maintenance. I find the second and third days the best as it begins to fade just a little.... so the blend of just a bit of your natural gray with the treated looks impossible to detect any unnatural coloring. I find day four fading a little more than I want so hit again on the fourth night. I can start at 9pm, have the colors blended in a bowl, mixed with hot water (microwave), and applied on my beard by 9:05. I'm retired now so sometimes I'll watch movies and leave it on until 4am... but I could rinse at go to bed by 10:30 and still wake up with the best, most natural looking color enhancement out there.

The BOTTOM LINE:

1. If you just use the basic shades Grizzly should look better than anything you've tried before but don't be afraid to experiment by mixing colors if you want to nail your natural shade. Even if you miss it will still look presentable and natural because many have hair/beard color differences.

2. Don't panic, freak out, or get discouraged when you first rinse. The oxidation that will take place from exposure to air is part of the process that will give it the most natural appearance. The browns will have a bit of a green tint, the black will be purple. THIS CHANGES and transitions into a natural shade over the course of a few hours so it's best to do it before you go to bed. I've also found you can't leave it "too long". I've actually fallen asleep for the night with the stuff on...it hardens as it dries but softens with water then rinses right off. i find much better results when I leave on longer than instructed. I try to go at least 90 minutes and much longer if time allows. You forget it's on but don't leave the house. I usually keep mine on until it dries and hardens before washing off.

Henna is also a plant leaf so you'll smell like spinach until you rinse it off. Pretty weird at first but I no longer even notice the smell.

3. If there are negative reviews or you try and don't get what you want, it's only because you didn't use the patience to allow it to work. With a few tries I was able to come up with exactly what I wanted. If you'll give it a chance, (it's a quick, simple, 5 minute process to mix and apply but does take an hour to "take" before you rinse, then few hours afterward to transition) use a little patience, THIS IS THE BEST product you'll find and you should be able to get exactly what you want, sharpen your appearance significantly ,with a completely natural, undetectable enhancement to your appearance. 5 STARS !!

title: This is the best razor for me
text:
Everyone's experience with a razor is different. I've tried a lot of different types, and I was more than happy to let go of my Gillette Fusion Power early last year. I bought a Shick Hydro Power. I thought it was great, cheap all around with an amazing cut. I even have the highest rated review on the product on Amazon currently. Now, I looked at the reviews for this saying Hydro 5 is better. It might be better for one person or another, but I have used both extensively and like this one better.

I have been using the Proglide POWER (yes, power) version for about 6-7 months now. I just purchased this manual version to take with me to basic training (in case the power version would be confiscated). I'll backtrack and talk about my experience with the Hydro 5. When I used it at first, it was kind of rough. I figured it would get a little better and it did, but it still was uncomfortable. I fooled myself into liking it because of its price and how long the lubrication strip lasted. I was getting only a week on my Fusion Power before it started to become uncomfortable because the strip faded out, and I was getting 3-4 weeks with the Hydro 5 until it ran out. The lubrication on that thing is funny though, because sometimes the whole thing will fall out of the razor.

My experience with the Proglide has been positive in every way as soon as I took it out of the box. I have learned long ago to not hype up any product until I've used it for a long time. With 6-7 months of experience I'm telling everyone how it is. The proglide can cut through thick stubble as good as it does on your 5 o clock shadow. I hadn't shaved for about a week and used the Proglide and it cut me down smooth with no pain and with ease. I bought myself a replacement pack of 8 cartridges and I have run through 6. That means in 6 months, I have used 6. Actually 7 if you include the one it came with. For those of you out there who know how to make a razor last, one of these can go up to a month or two. For beginners or average shavers, you will get at least two weeks worth before you even consider changing it, and, the lubrication will still be there.

One thing I hated about the Hydro 5 was the grip. It was a horrible design. With the Proglide, it was made with you in mind. It just feels natural holding it, and every stroke feels just right. As we all know, replacing Gillette cartridges can be a pain in the neck (not physically). To buy a pack of replacements, you're looking at about $30 for a pack of 8. The same will cost you under $20 with the Hydro 5. Not everyone cares to pay for it, but it's more than worth it. It's the best shave I ever had in my life, and I don't mind paying $10 extra every 6-9 months for a better experience.

Think of razors like gas, and you are the car. You only require regular gas, but if you decide to go with the premium (Proglide), your car will run faster and be more responsive.

I will state again I have not used the manual proglide yet, but it's the same thing without vibration (which I don't use much anyway).

Hopefully your experience is as good as mine.

Here is a run down of stats in my own opinion for the Proglide.

Fusion Proglide
Standard: $9.74 (comes with 2 cartridges)- replacement pack of 8 - $28.99
Power: $10.94 (1 cartridge) - replacement pack of 8 - $31.99

Comfort level: 5/5
Effectiveness of each stroke: 4.5/5 (sometimes you have to run the blade back over)
Smoothness of shave: 5/5 - Your experience may be different, but this is the best shave of my life
Cartridge life: 4/5 - Depends on how you use it. Will get you 2 weeks minimum and up to 2 months maximum
Design: 5/5 - The thing I hate about most razors is the design. This one feels great in hand

Overall: 4.8/5 - It's not perfect, but the best razor I've ever used in my life

It comes out of box with a razor holder which most gillette razors have, but others don't. Also, I strongly recommend buying the Proglide shaving cream. it's the best I ever used in my life. You can literally see your hairs rising in seconds if you look closely.

Good luck everyone!

title: So Much More than Just an Air Freshener
text: I never in my life would have thought I'd consider an air freshener as a giftable item, except perhaps as a gag gift to one of my brothers. This Florona Hibiscus Air Freshener, however, is in a class all by itself. Even the box it comes in is beautiful, with soft sweeping white and beige brush strokes in the background and beautiful flowers embossed in gold. The pattern wraps all the way around the box, with each side being different. The inside of the box is a vivid lime green. The spray bottle for the air freshener looks more like a perfume bottle, light and dark pink with more of the gold embossing, this time with leaves instead of flowers. The key ingredients of this air freshener are water, hibiscus oil, and hydrogenated castor oil. The bottle contains 3.38 fl oz (100 ml). The directions say to wash linens and clothes before spraying this linen mist on them. It says this spray can be used on sheets, furniture fabric, drapes, pillows, and directly in the room as an air freshener. It also says to shake the bottle well before using it. When sprayed, the hibiscus scent is very subtle and faint, but definitely there. My wife had me spray some on the blouse she was wearing so that she could enjoy the hibiscus scent all day long, and she plans to spray her pillow before she goes to sleep. For a soft, gentle hibiscus aroma that stays pleasantly in the background without overwhelming my senses, this Florona Hibiscus Air Freshener works well.

title: If this is your first electric shaver
text:
I've always used razors, as I like a very close cut. I've tried once in the past an electric shaver and since I had left my beard grow 1/8 of an inch or so, it didn't cut a thing and I never looked back. I got a Braun portable as a gift and I tried it with just a 1 day beard and it worked (never as close as a razor, forget about electric if that's what you want, don't care what anybody tells you, it's not even close) but it was good enough that I could go to work without looking like I have not shaved.

I did some research and this Norelco came on top (second best was another Braun, but it had a washing system with a liquid that you have to replace once a month and that was a deal breaker for me). I've tried it twice now and is very similar to my Braun portable, that is, just good enough.

Instructions say to use only this shaver (don't mix with razors) so that the machine gets "used" to your beard...which sounds like a lot of crock (don't see any A.I. chip buried in the machine) but will humour the manufacturer. Anyway, my main reason to get it is that some times after shaving with a razor often my skin does get irritated and some times in the morning I'm not feeling like doing that to my face. The other nice thing is that on a Saturday afternoon if I decide to go out, I can just touch up with the electric instead of having to wash my face, apply shaving cream, and maybe getting my shirt wet in the process...much simpler with this thing.

But it really depends on your beard I guess, I have a not very dense beard, which grows parallel to the skin (specially around the cheeks) and so it is difficult for electric razors to do a great job. Around my chin for example, where hair grows more perpendicular is where I get the best shaving (also, it's the most dense there, so it is were the razor hurts the most!).

But if you are on a budget and $80 is a lot for you, don't buy it, it is not worth it, if you are just itching to buy a new gadget though, I would recommend this.

Hope this is useful.

title: Sweet, lovely, smells just like the name
text:
I am not an impulse buyer. So before I spend $$$ on a parfum, I did some extensive research. First, I knew I wanted to have a Tom Ford because of his reputation in making parfum. Then I narrowed down the choices to the 5 most preferred private blends by online reviewers. Then I bought .5ml sample for each. After trying them one by one, my husband made the choice for me: Noir de Noir, but my favorite is Amber Absolute.

Vanilla Tobacco is really sweet and nice, with straight forward vanilla tabacco notes. Vanilla is sweet and yummy. The tabacco smells like Turkish tobacco: sweet and sexy. I can imagine that whoever wears this could be quite irresistible. This is one of my favorite. However, compared to Noir de Noir, I feel that it lacks a bit complexity. It is a bit straight forward Vanilla and tobacco.

From my research and trial, I find that parfum is very personal, and you have to try it in person. It is better to try it at home and wear it once or twice before you buy it at a store. The 5 scents I tried:

- Noir de Noir: complex, sweet, lovely scent. Not overwhelmingly floral, not overpowering, and not sharp/edgy. This is my husband's favorite when I wear it.

- Vanilla Tobacco

- Amber Absolute: Unique, herbal. Stronger than Noir de Noir. Initially, I couldn't stand Amber Absolute. It smelled to me like Chinese medicine box. But then I am totally in love with it. It is very unusual. It has a very unique dried herb fragrance and very complex. It reminds me of the fragrance in the air in Big Sur, CA or Mono Lake, CA when the flowers and plants are drying in fall. The fragrance is not floral, not particularly sexy or feminine.

- Tuscan leather: couldn't stand it, very leathery.

- Neroli Portofino: didn't like it at all. Just like some reviewers said, it smells like Tide.

title: A great shave with a few quirks
text:
I bought this shaving system in the hopes that it could make shaving a bit less painful, as I've always had fairly sensitive skin. In the few months I've owned it, I've been very pleased with the performance and the overall results. Here are a few things I've found...

Pros:
- The moisturizing system does work very well. I get substantially less skin irritation than I have in previous razors that I've used.
- I've discovered I enjoy shaving in the shower. I always tried to avoid mixing shaving before a shower due to the irritation, but this works well.
- The charging and refill system is nice (more on this later).
- Comfortable to hold and use.
- I shave more often using this than any other razor I've used previously.

Cons:
- You'll be compelled to shave daily, since it works best and most efficiently that way. That can be a pro or a con, depending on your lifestyle.
- While the charge and refill station is great, it seems that I always run out of moisturizer before running out of battery, so I have to remember to refill it myself, since they suggest not leaving the razor on charge all the time.
- I haven't found a great shower mirror yet, so I wind up starting my shave prior to the shower, to trim around sideburns and the like.
- Works better as a wet razor than as a dry one.
- While I like the scent of the moisturizer, it took me a bit to get used to it.

Overall, I'm very pleased with this razor and would suggest it to anyone looking for a new electric. If you are OK with the pros and cons, then I say go for it, you won't regret it!

text:
I'm a bigger girl, size 42DD for reference. I've started walking at least 2.5 miles a day wearing a weighted vest. Even in cool weather, with all the hills in my neighborhood, I end up drenched in sweat.

And that means, of course, boob sweat. I have ruined multiple bras and the smell is so gross. Since adding the vest, it's gotten so much worse. It's absolutely disgusting until I get a chance to shower. But I'm a busy mom of two special needs kids, so there are days I get back and can't shower right away, so then I'm feeling gross until I can.

I finally had enough and started looking for a solution. I found this stuff and figured I'd give it a shot. I was realistic in my expectations that it would help a bit, maybe even just help the smell, since is a strenuous activity and not a stroll through a grocery store. I wasn't expecting it to keep me from sweating at all or anything.

I tried it out for the first time today and it blew my expectations out of the water! I was slightly damp, but not even enough to drip. No smell. My bra was almost completely dry! And it's lasted ALL DAY.

I'm one of those ladies who hate wearing a bra at home, but hate how the girls rub without fabric there. I usually tuck whatever shirt I'm wearing under there. But that means that if I end up sweating for some reason, my shirt ends up wet and gross. Today, I realized that after taking off my bra, I wasn't bothered by the skin on skin. The lotion leaves a silky softness on the skin and it kept me comfortable all day.

Now on to the description. The bottle is smaller than I expected, but I learned that a little goes a long way. The lotion goes on creamy and dries quickly. It left no residue on my clothing or any I could see on my skin, except for on my hand from where I applied it. It rinsed off easily. The smell is supposed to be lily, according to the bottle, and I guess it kinda does smell like lily, though the product description listed apple in one place, so I dunno. But it's not a strong scent and it completely disappeared after application.

I love this product. I'm going to be a habitual user from now on and I'm recommending it to all my lady friends!

get all of the hair out. The mechanism is small and delicate so you have
to be careful. The instructions indicate that water can be used but I haven't
tried that yet. The instructions are brief and awkwardly worded. There are

title: The Base Enhances Results, Extends Time Between Next Dye
text: I think many guys are just buying the dye because it works well enough on its own.  But after a couple applications of the brown dye alone, I decided to buy the Organic Base just to see if it makes a difference...and it does.  When I just use the dye for 30 minutes and then wash it out, my beard/skin has that ever so slight green tint for the first 24 hrs, then a natural brown color with blondish highlights (where gray used to be) settles in nicely and lasts for about 4 days before the dye's color starts to fade away.  When I use the base first for 20 minutes, wash it out, then apply the brown dye for 20 minutes and wash it out, I don't notice any green tint at all, and the dye's color lasts about 7 days before needing another application.  So for me I'm going to continue to use the base first so I only have to dye my beard once a week to keep it looking good.  Very happy with Grizzly Mountain products.

title: Sheer formula, builds well.
text: This is a nice Nautical gift set with 4 pretty polishes.  They are 13.5 ml each, and made in the U.S.A.  Initially I thought I would love Stay Nude the most, but it ended up being my least favorite of the set, only because it is pearl and streaks are unavoidable due to the type of finish it is.  All 4 have a shiny topcoat built into the formula.  The 3 cremes are all very sheer formulas, not super opaque.  The thickness of the formula for all of these is good.  If you like a sheer formula, where you can see your nail bed thru the polish, then these are your jam.  I did several manicures with each of them, and found that if I wanted a sheer look then 1 coat worked perfectly, otherwise 2 or 3 coats for full coverage and less peek thru of your natural nail and smile line.  I did 2 easy coats for each of my manicures.  The blue (Hypnosis) seemed to have the best coverage, and the formula for that was my favorite of the 4, it dried the fastest at 8 minutes to the touch.  They all go on easily, with a regular round brush (not flat) and they dry fairly well, in about 10-15 minutes each layer.  I did find that using my own quick drying topcoat that these wore much better, but from the manufacturer neither base nor top coat are required.  I did not get any staining from these, which I love.  The pink and white will both be really good polishes for doing either French tip or pond manicures when you just want a sheer base, where you do a layer, do art over it, then cover it again, and more art on that layer-it gives a layered effect that is fun to do.  The color palate is a fun one, with lots of options for artwork.  These are not quick drying-more of the typical 10 minutes per layer, and I expected them to be hardened on their own, without the help of a quick drying topcoat, but that was not the case with them.

Purchased as a replacement for an older Norelco razor that was in need of some minor repair if it was to continue in daily use.

It may not be required but I figure it can't hurt anything either since it was recommended for the Norelco that just went into semi retirement.)

Shave quality is excellent, close and smooth with no irritation. I do use a preshave and the Norelco shaving gel packs that go in the razor.

In another 4 to 6 years when this razor starts to get tired, I won't hesitate to get another Norelco.

title: Works on Bites, Burns, Cuts and Stings Really Quick
text: I live in a very hot, dry area of Southern California. We are constantly in the sun because there's actually no way to avoid it. We have been using the Shea Butter for about 2 weeks now. We have used it for insect bites (specifically spiders and mosquitos), mild sunburn, burns from chemicals and of course as a daily moisturizer. The smell is a little stinky, so what we do when we use it as a daily moisturizer is soften it and mix it in with our store bought cocoa butter and shea butter lotion. The store bought lotion really does smell like cocoa so mixing it with the raw shea butter eliminates the shea odor. It actually allows the cocoa butter smell to overpower it. I feel and smell like a nice, soft milk chocolate bar after showering. A friend of mine had to crawl under a house full of mold, mildew, spiders, etc. Although he was fully covered in protective clothing and a gas mask, his arms were swollen, stinging and very painful when he came out. I gave him a chunk of the shea butter to rub all over this arms and hands and he felt instant relief from the stinging and pain. There are many uses for this shea butter and I'm sure most people will discover a use no one else had even thought of yet. Don't be afraid to put it on any part of your skin that needs some relief from pain, no matter what the sourse was. It truly is like real butter, so use it plentifully and use a clean towel to remove any excess after most of it has absorbed into your skin. This is a big chunk of shea butter, but I think it will come in so handy it won't be long before I need to order more. The price, shipping, packaging, etc can't be beat either. I definately give it a 5 star rating.

While some of the juices from the chicken did get under the mat, NONE of the solids did and it was just simple to do.

It's perfectly sized for a 1/4 sheet baking sheet, but that's really what I consider a 'small' sheet unless I'm in the RV where my oven will only barely even fit this mat.

title: They work!
text:
First, this product really *does* whiten teeth--it's not a gimmick as some people think. (It uses a peroxide, which is probably how your dentist would do it, although this is a less concentrated form and takes two weeks.) Of course, it only whitens natural teeth, not dental work, but for most people, they should work.

Now, on to the product itself. Some people have complained about them being difficult to apply, but after the first couple strips I didn't have any problems, and even the first time I applied it I didn't fold a strip or mess up anything major. Keep in mind that some tooth sensitivity is normal; personally, mine was only mild at worst and really only noticeable right after I applied a strip, but I know some people who aren't as lucky. If this is you, using a toothpaste for sensitive teeth may help. Also keep in mind that eating, drinking, and probably talking (unless you have better luck than I) are pretty much out of the question while you're wearing these, but I simply did one application on my drive home from work and another later in the night. My only concern was that the strips, especially the top ones, are a bit short and only cover your front eight or so teeth, but for most people that shouldn't be a problem.

A year after my first use (teeth still looking good), I am currently using a generic brand--Equate, available from Wal-Mart for about $15, about $5 less than these--and have to say that I like Crest Whitestrips better because the strips are more flexible and easier to apply, and they stay in place better. The Equate ones have a bit harder plastic and tend to slide off my teeth if I open my mouth. Hardly worth it to save $5.

It is also worth noting there are two other versions of Whitestrips: Premium and Premium Plus. Both contain a more concentrated peroxide that works in less time (7 and 10 days, respectively [the 10-day version is the same as the 7-day version but includes three extra days of strips for extra whitening], as opposed to the 14 of this Classic version) but are more expensive and--based on their reviews--seem to cause more problems with sensitivity and such. Therefore, unless you're in a hurry, I think you'd be fine with these.

In summary, I am happy with this product and think that most people would be, too. Not bad for the price (certainly cheaper than a professional whitening), and they really do whiten!

title: so it can get pretty hot down here
text: I live in the South, so it can get pretty hot down here. I also have some skin problems (mild to moderate acne, redness, dry flakes), so I like to wear base makeup whenever I go out. I bought this because I was hoping that combined with a primer and fixing spray, the skin prep pro would help my makeup stay put and not get swept away by the flood of sweat that comes crashing in every summer. The primer and fixing spray I use work well for me (or at least are the best I've tried so far) and sweat is still an issue for me. When this came in, I had high hopes, but unfortunately this is not a miracle product. It did make my face feel tight, so I applied a small amount of moisturizer over it after letting it set but before applying my makeup. I'm a college student, so I walk to class all the time, and after a few classes I could tell that my face was fading and melting as usual. It wasn't a pretty sight. So the next day, to see if it was due to the moisturizer, I just applied the skin prep pro before my makeup. Sadly, I got the same results. I break it out every now and again to see if it's a certain product that it won't work with, but after going through all of my routine taking one product out at a time, I've determined that this just doesn't work for me. I gave this two stars because while it didn't do what I wanted it to, it also didn't make any of my skin problems worse. text: When I first sprayed this product on my hair, I noticed the smell right away. It's not bad at all, but one can't help but notice the chemical-like smell at the end of the almond note. I used it in combination with a water and oil mixture as well as some flaxseed gel to bring out and define my curl pattern. I did this for several days straight since the leave-in states it's light enough for daily use. I live in a very dry climate, so keeping my hair moisturized is important because my hair dries out quick and feels becomes brittle. I think this leave-in conditioner dried my hair out faster!!! And I would say the butylene glycol, which is the fourth ingredient, is the culprit. It probably contributed to the chemical smell as well. It's unfortunate because finding alcohol-free hair products is comparable to searching for a unicorn. But living in a  dry climate, I really don't need another hair product drying out my hair. Luckily, I bought another leave-in conditioner in unison and it's actually containing the moisture in my hair so much better. So overall, I'd give this product three stars. It doesn't really look (or smell) all that much like a leave-in...at least compared to the ones I've used in the past...but it did help with detangling, the smell was still decent, it was light on my hair with the few days I applied it, and I like that it didn't contain a bunch of harmful ingredients.

title: Excellent Hold, I'm Really Impressed
text:
I bought this specifically because of the anti-humidity and anti-frizz claims. I had an outdoor garden party to attend and we thought it might be damp. It turned out to be dry, so I can't speak on the humidity factor as of yet, but I can say I was extremely impressed regardless. I did my hair in the morning, traveled a couple hours away to a party where I sat outside all day long on a fairly windy day. Not strong winds, but more than a breeze for sure. I brought the bottle in my bag but I never needed to use it to touch up. I then drove home 16 hours later and went straight to bed because I was exhausted. I woke up the next day and my hair still looked good!

It's a fast drying "freeze-hold" type spray. It's a bit stiff to the touch but it doesn't look stiff at all, and it comes out easily later when you brush it. I have thinning, fine hair so it was important to me that my "strategic styling" to cover the thinner areas held in place and this did the trick, so I'm sold. The scent isn't pleasing but it's not bad either, a little perfumey but I can deal with it for the great hold I get. This is the best bottle of hairspray I've tried in the last couple of decades actually.

title: Good soap, good value
text:
First, I have to echo the other reviewer's sentiment about the picture being misleading. The text does state that you're buying a single stick, but the picture makes it look like you're buying a box of 'em.

I was initially disappointed with my [[ASIN:B002A5OLHQ Arko Shaving Soap Stick]]. I prefer using a brush and mug, so I unwrapped the stick, cut it into shaving soap coins (which I believe are legal tender in Venezuela and Costa Rica, and certain counties in Arkansas), put them into my mug and stuck it in the microwave for 30 seconds to melt them. What a mistake! That's what I do with [[ASIN:B001A3DNY6 Van Der Hagen Deluxe Shave Soap, 2.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 12)]], and it works great--the soap liquifies, adheres to the bottom and sides of the mug, and once it resolidifies, I'm good to go. This stuff softened, yes, but it didn't really liquify. Instead, it kind of foamed up and over the top of the mug. I tried to use my knife to moosh it back into the mug, but it resulted in a very rough, craggy top surface. Figured I'd just use the brush on it anyway--eventually I would wear down that rough surface and leave behind a smooth top that would work perfectly.

I'm glad I did! This soap lathered up like nobody's business when I put the warm, moist brush to it. It made a little thinner lather than I usually get from VDH, but despite it's thinness, it wasn't runny at all--it stayed right where I brushed it, and didn't dry out before my razor got to it. My habit is to do three shaves in different directions, and the Arko lather held out for all three.

I used an older blade, an [[ASIN:B001QY8QXM 100 Astra Superior Premium Platinum Double Edge Safety Razor Blades]], probably about two shaves past when I would usually have replace it, but I was being lazy. I kind of expected to nick myself a couple times. But with the Arko shaving soap, that did not happen. My blade glided across my face as smoothly as I could ask. No nicks at all.

As many have mentioned, the scent is kind of strong, and not entirely pleasant. Some have compared it to citronella, which I can understand. I though it was kind of a cross between the original Old Spice scent from when my dad used their cologne, and some industrial chemical smell. VDH is more or less unscented, so I usually mix a few drops of my favorite cologne ([[ASIN:B00AATHC52 ASPEN by Coty]]) into the liquid when it comes out of the microwave, but I didn't think that would be a good idea with Arko. I didn't think the cologne scent would mix well with the cloying scent the soap came with. But while the scent isn't my cup of tea, after you rinse your face well, it's not very strong at all, especially if you wash your face afterward and use a scented after-shave balm.

The bottom line is, for a single stick, the value isn't great. It's a lot more affordable, and just as usable a product, as some of the much more expensive soaps out there, but at the single stick price, plus shipping, you could buy several pucks of Van Der Hagen locally. When you buy more sticks at a time, the per-stick price comes down, and if you can manage to get free shipping in the deal, it starts looking really attractive. The lather is very nice, the scent, not so much, but all in all, you can't go too far wrong with it. I'm dinging it one star only because of the scent. While I would rather it liquify in the microwave like VDH, that's not how the product was designed to be used, so it wouldn't be fair to dock it for that.

title: good things never last
text:
My wife LOVES her Micro Peeling Sensation cloths. The unfortunate fact of this world is, good things never last. Haha. This applies to the Micro Peeling cloths. She bought her first back in the mid-2000's. She loved it so much, she posted a glowing review on this beauty board she frequented, and literally caused the online retailer she mentioned to run out of stock! True story. True story also, for some reason, the German manufacturer decided to discontinue the product. My wife managed to track down what stock she could on ebay and stocked up. This stuff is AMAZING - need to slough off dead skin? Done! In the shower, of course. Not recommended using dry - doesn't really do squat if you try to use it dry. And it's so effective, the directions that came with the original cloth said to not rub for more than 20 seconds in one spot. You will literally slough off too much if you do so and give yourself a BAD "burn". Ouch! Yup, wife's done that also. Anyway, fast forward to 2016. She accidentally came upon these cloths on Amazon and was happy beyond words. So happy, she went and bought 2 sets of 4 cloths.

Well, imagine her disappointment when she opened the cloth and noticed right away that it was NOT the same as the original. True, it said "Micro Peeling Sensation Cloth". But, the feel of the cloth (dry) was not as plush as the original. The weave just wasn't as tight, and when she ran her fingers over the cloth, the fibers didn't cause any "drag". See, the fibers of the original was so tightly woven that when you run your finger through it, the fibers out kind of snag on your skin. A bit hard to explain. That was the first indicator they were not the same cloths. Next, she tried using it and compared it to the original - the new cloth sloughing one leg and the original on the other leg. BIG difference. The new cloth barely even sloughed off any dead skin. To say my wife was bummed is to put it mildly. She sadly returned both sets to Amazon.

So ... if you're looking to get these thinking they're the original Micro Peeling Sensation cloths, think twice. They're not. They feel basically like a regular microfiber cloth, only you're paying way more for it.

title: A quick hack fixes the over-dispensing problem
text:
I thought I was so great. Yes, I had read all the reviews saying these tubes dispense far too much sanitizer at once. But I was going to be careful, not like those *other* Amazon customers who don't know how to work a squeeze bottle. Well, the bottles arrived, and sure enough, they are so determined to be leak-proof that when you squeeze them, nothing happens until all of a sudden an olive-sized dollop of product comes out in one big "blurp!" Being gentle does not help; the dispensing is all or nothing. I might try to MacGyver a solution by poking a small hole somewhere to try to fix this problem, but for now these bottles are too annoying to use. The good: 1) These come in black to be less obvious when dangling from a dark bag, though this camouflage is slightly undermined by the white cap. 2) The carabiner for clipping to a purse/backpack is handy.
EDIT: Fixed the all-or-nothing dispensing problem by using scissors to make a tiny slit in one of the "petals" surrounding the tiny opening. Now a slight squeeze gives the desired small amount of product.

Not to mention the bathroom looking like it had snowed in there...all the time. I had such a hard time my entire life just trying to stay ahead of house cleaning...dusting, cleaning up powder residue.
A lady that used to clean told me that people that powder...There was no way for them to have a perfectly clean house. That the powder drifted everywhere.
And....then I had 2 daughters that I raised to love powder too. And when all had been said and done and the kids were grown and my sister and I moved in together, we both lived in a cloud of powder! Gold Bond.... we were all hooked on Gold Bond!
Then....one day I happened to notice the spray and I thought. . .. I wonder?
I bought a can and the rest is history, as they say.
And our house is clean!
And we just moved into a new home in October so this house will never have powder in all its crevices. LOL!
BUT....wait!!

WELL. ...
I also love the effects of the powder too....of course. ..on my body. It doesn't take much and a can lasts me a long time. My sister's lasts longer than mine so I guess I use more than she does.
I think it's a great product. I

title: I'd recommend googling some info about them before buying
text:
If you've never used a boar bristle brush before (or any natural type of natural bristle, I suspect), I'd recommend googling some info about them before buying. You don't use them quite the same way you'd use a brush with hard plastic bristles. You definitely want to comb the tangles out of your hair first, for example, and wait until your hair is dry to brush it. (Maybe you're supposed to do those things anyway, for all I know -- I have shorter hair so it's easier for me to use brushes incorrectly without too much damage, but I find plastic brushes more forgiving.)

Because of those things, I'm not sure a boar bristle brush would be great for styling my hair -- but I didn't buy it for that anyway. I bought it more as a type of hair treatment, to get the benefits of boar bristle brushing: distributing oils evenly, improving the condition of the hair, stimulating the scalp, extending time between washes, etc. I have oily hair, but all that oil just build up on my scalp. With this brush, my hair feels and looks much more balanced. I do get some static while brushing, but it settles down quickly.

The brush itself is durable, seems high quality, and has a ton of nice stiff bristles. It feels great on my scalp, and I love being able to help my hair's health without having to slather on a ton of extra treatment products!

title: One of my favorite eyelash curlers
text:
I have tried many eyelash curlers and while most are sufficient and get the job done I can honestly say this is my favorite eyelash curler along with the whiplash curler (by crave naturals also available on amazon).

I read once on in a beauty magazine that eyelash curlers tend to wear out after about a year and a half. No way!! A good eyelash curler with proper care (not getting dropped or crushed in a makeup bag) should last a lifetime, the pads are another story...but not with this one!.
I have tried the famous Shu Uemura and while that did a very nice job of getting a natural curl I could tell statement about wearing out after a year and a half as the metal connection did not seem very strong. This curler however is rock solid in it's build! The metal is thick and reinforced as is the connection. Another thing I preferred over the Shu Uemura is that this is strongly spring loaded where as Shu Uemura isn't.

The finger holds are very comfortable and smooth plus, also importantly, the curler looks classy! The pad on this curler, as said by the company doesn't need to be replaced. This is impressive as you can tell by looking at it and feeling it the pad is thick and does not have a lot of give to it but is still gentle enough not to harm your lashes.

As for curling. I get the curler as close to the roots as possible by about half opening my eye and the no pinch design allows you to do this easily. Then I hold for about 7 seconds occasionally pumping the curler. I then raise my eyebrows and move the curler a little farther down my lashes and pinch for a second for two while bend the curler backwards and raising the handle up a bit. The main issue with certain eyelash curlers is the over curled and bent lashes effect which also isn't good for your lashes. This curler, when not over pressed, gives a natural curler that is noticeable on it's own without even using mascara.

And a shout out to the wonderful company Bella and Bear with their wonderful customer service and wonderful products that they wholeheartedly back up! Can't go wrong here.

title: 2 coats - lasts about 8 hours
text:
This kit was an experiment. I look better in brown eyeliner and mascara, but only could get black magnetic lashes with black liner. (The double magnetic kind are also black). Thought this would be a good thing for me. Well . . . somewhat. The brown is exactly right for me for both the liner and the eyelashes. Just like all the others---of every ilk---they are too long. The problem, though, with magnetic lashes is that I would need to cut off the very end magnet. This leaves a rather long piece of unsupported lash band which I would then have to glue down. Hmm. And then, the affect only lasts about 8 hours. Might be good for going dancing (not me re COVID) where you get there at 9pm and leave about 2am with some time on either side for arrival and departure.

I'll probably still wear these on occasion, but I find that the plain old glue-on lashes work best if I (a) use the dark quick-dry glue and wait 10 seconds or so and (b) put the glue on my lids and then stick the lashes to it. I can wake up with these puppies still on my lids not budged. I don't though.

text: I bought this product probably about a month ago. Right before my eyes. I am in my mid 30's and have always had freckly skin and the sun makes them get bigger and run together but I've now started to get age spots. They appear out of nowhere and they're big and darker than my freckles.Coincidentally, after receiving this product and using it for a few days, I woke up one morning with a big, brown AGE SPOT right under my eye. I was really upset about it as it was very noticeable. I was using Wonderpiel for a few days morning and night already when the spot appeared, so I continued using it, making sure to apply to the spot as well. I wore concealer to hide this thing and it was noticeable again by the end of each day when the concealer wore off. But one morning (9 days after the spot's arrival) I woke up and didn't see the spot. So I washed my face again, thinking I must have left the concealer on overnight, but it was GONE! I know I'm being dramatic, but I really am having trouble aging gracefully and am very self-conscious. Wonderpiel really made me happy, and is one of the few products I've used that has basically worked magic for me. Now, I do still have freckles and "discolorations" and uneven skin tone, but I've had that all my life so I don't expect this product to work as fast as it did on my brand-new age spot. I THINK I see them fading a bit but want to keep using until I'm sure of it. But, for all who are wondering whether or not to buy this product, do it. I saw it work, and will be buying another bottle.

title: Awesome Figures for an awesome deal
text:
As a die hard Final Fantasy fan and collector, I was excited to get this set. I believe this is/was for retailers. The box looks like it can be manipulated to create an open display where the blind boxes can be purchased separately. I think this is super cool. The box is black, labeled Dissidia Trading Arts vol. 2 set and has pictures of all five figures.

Inside the outer box are six blind boxes (even though there are only five figures). For those of you who may not know what a blind box is, it's a box where you can't tell what's inside. The UPC and artwork are the same on each box. That's why you can't be assured of getting all five figures. If you get duplicates, you're encouraged to trade them with friends (hence the Trading Arts). I opened five boxes and got all five characters, so I'm going to leave the sixth box unopened. I'll display it with the figures because the artwork is cool. I'll try to upload pictures of the boxes.

There is some assembly required, but not too much. Mostly connecting the upper torso to the legs and connecting weapons. I had a tough time assembling them because their pieces fit so tightly together. I had to get my husband to help with two of them. Finding a safe area to grip was part of it. You'll want to be careful around Firion's ponytail and the hilts of their swords. They can be snapped off with little effort.

I agree with the other reviewer that Terra/Tina is difficult to put and keep on her stand, but I've got a solution. Any doll stand that fits around her waist will solve that problem. Tina is about 5" tall, so I'm going to get a mini doll stand where the waist gripper is 2.5" high. (I had to do the same thing for the Warrior of Light.)

It takes a while to get them put together. Seriously, Firion has like five weapons you need to attach and Cecil has one that attaches to his lower back. You have to keep it from falling off as you squeeze it under his cape, but once assembled, they are something to look at. These are actual Square Enix figures (not knock offs) and they look it. The detail in their hair and clothing is amazing! My favorites are Cecil and of course, Sephiroth. Be mindful of his Masamune katana, it's accidentally knocked a couple of my other figures over.

Overall, this set is an awesome deal. If you bought all the figures separately, not only would the boxes be opened (necessary to find out who was inside) you'd spend over $200. Sephiroth is around $60 by himself. Terra/Tina is more than that and not only would you not have Bartz/Butz (I couldn't find him separately), you wouldn't get the sixth blind box either. I highly recommend this set to any Final Fantasy fan.

It works well as an eye cream, but I like the fresh and well rested effect I get when I put it on in the morning. The cream feels a bit tacky to the touch a few moments after application, but this effect quickly fades as the cream soaks into the delicate skin around the eyes. I have very sensitive skin, and there was not a trace of stinging or irritation. The product has a pleasant and subtle smell. I love that this product uses great ingredients. You can tell how high quality the product is when you smooth it onto your eyes. The eye cream gets a 5 star rating from me for all of these reasons, but mostly because it simply works. text:
I bought this direct from an advertisement on amazon. Everything about this package was stylish, beautifully presented and arrived quickly in perfect order. The DVD was excellent and there were clear simple instructions on a sturdy pamphlet. The included conductive gel and Serum with peptides were pleasant to use and fragrance free.

On page 12 of the manual "precautions" "headache and other painful sensations have been reported during or following electrical stimulation" was omitted from the website.

It was very unpleasant during use; causes visible twitching and muscle contraction. Even on the lowest setting I found this frankly painful especially in the jaw. My muscles felt tightened alright afterwards but to the point of face ache and a headache. My eyebrows were so lifted on one side it was a bride of frankenstein look. I think this unit needs a redesign to lower the current again by half rather than chasing quick results. Decreasing the time of application by half didn't help much - the overall sensation was still of having been kicked in the head rather than of having had a facial. I didn't want to use it more than twice before asking for the company to honour its 100% satisfaction guarantee and issue a refund number which they did.

If the website upfront about the level discomfort I might have left another star on this for other users who are probably not as sensitive. My advice is don't buy it unless you can try it first. Very disappointed as I wanted this unit to work in tandem with my [[ASIN:B000JIN0OG NuFace Microcurrent Toner for Lifting and Toning the Face]] - which leaves me feeling relaxed and fabulous but can't be used around the mouth or eye area.

here is the response:
"Your FaceMaster passes less power to your skin than a good static discharge might on a dry day after walking on some carpet (less than 20 microamps at intensity level = 1, less than 200microamps at intensity level = 10). There is no possibility of nerve damage.

We recommend that you try a couple of techniques:

1. Use a bit less conductive serum (a perfectly dry foam cap will not conduct any electricity, while a completely soaked foam cap allows almost 100% of the current to pass). Using less conductive serum should be similar to having intensity settings below level 1.

2. Use less pressure on your wands. No current will pass to your skin if the wands are not touching it; likewise the most current would pass if you press hard enough such that 100% of the foam caps were surrounded by skin. Using less pressure to reduce the surface area of contact is also like having intensity settings below level 1.

The sensation caused by the e-stim is something that you will become accustomed to. In fact, it is possible with prolonged use that the sensation will be eliminated completely (we receive comments from people saying their FaceMaster is no longer working because they no longer feel it - it is just that they have become use to it).

Feathering mode has a significantly different output characteristic than Eye or Face mode. The treatment is meant to stimulate collagen and elastin within the skin and will not provide any muscle stimulation."

I don't feel like toughing it out as a professional session is completely painless there is an easy alternative.

I wish the beard wash came in El Burrista scent. Now on to the scent portion of review. The Burrista has a fantastic smell of fresh roasted coffee. It isnt a loud scent or overwhelming in any way. Its subtle but noticeable. As a woman I find the scent attractive lol. Its masculine but not like trying to hard and in your face strong. Its quite lovely. Its most certainly on our to buy often list. My husband doesnt usually have much to say beyond its ok when asked if he likes a product but he said this stuff is awesome. So its definitely good. We both also like that its made in the US, and free of chemicals or unpronounceable ingredients.

title: An 'essential' for my skincare
text:
I am loving Essential Smooth! You can smell the all natural ingredients they make it with. A bit of aroma-therapy action while you're replenishing your face with those healthy and vitamin-rich essential oils that get stripped from you after a good cleanse. It truly feels like a refreshing drink for your skin as you massage it in. And a little bit goes a long way. I figured that out pretty quickly. You don't really need more than one pump on your finger tips...maybe two if you want to extend it down your neck using the excess to moisturize your hands. And don't worry - that orange, Oompa-Loompa look goes away real quick as you massage it into your pores! I read a review somewhere that says each bottle may have a slightly different hue and that's down to the harvest each batch gets made from - how cool is that! Mother Nature has every color for every season!
I can't wait to try Essential Repair which I've read is an over-night cream with soothing but intense regenerative properties.
It's nice to find a company that has a conscience about what it's mass-producing. Essential makes only Eco-Certified and Cruelty-Free skincare which is more rare than it should be these days. It's hard to avoid placing your carbon footsteps everyday but this is one small way to be environmentally conscious and gives me such peace of mind.
They've also created a neat community of like-minded people over at their Blog and their Facebook. Some really neat articles they're posting about general health and wellness.
[...]
All aboard the Essential-Train. I'm a happy convert, for sure! =)
