title: 4 years of use; the Best Yet!
text:
I've been using this for four years now. Don't do as they say, do as I say and you'll be as happy as I am with it.

Don't charge/clean it every day. If you want your battery to last, do what I do! Only clean it in the Jet Clean when your battery level is at the bottom bar. Tap out cuttings once in the middle of the cycle and once just before cleaning. In fact, run it under the sink before you clean it. Your cleaning solution will last a very long time and you'll only need to clean the solution tray once when you change the fluid. The nice thing about the tank is you can pull it out to check it. When it's about empty, clean the tray and refill the tank. I've only used 6 bottles of cleaning fluid in 4 years.

The cleaning solution also lubricates the blades and it works! After two years, I bought new blades and there was NO DIFFERENCE to the old ones I replaced just because of their age. I wasted my money, the Jet Clean lubrication works that good, even only using it between full battery charges.

Also, after four years, my battery life is still around two weeks. You won't get this type of battery life if you charge this thing in the cleaner every day. Obviously, don't EVER just leave this thing in the charger as it will ruin the batteries. Besides, the blades won't dry out there anyway.

Also, don't, and I repeat DON'T EVER get the cleaner/ charger circuitry wet. If you do, give it two days to dry out before you plug it in again or the cleaner will be quite erratic in it's operation and could quite possibly burn out.

I've had four Norelco razors in my lifetime and this is BY FAR the best! When the new models came out, I actually saw no need to upgrade. For me? That's saying something!

Good luck folks, Danny

Things to note: I waited 5 months to review the hair so I could give a fully informed review. I've colored, curled, cut, styled, washed, deep conditioned, blow dryed, you name it! Here's my review:

Pros-
• Affordable hair, 30+ inches will definitely cost more elsewhere, upwards of $350
• Takes coloring very well initially, I've only used watercolor meathod on any of my 613 hair.
• Straightens without much effort
• Holds curl but ONLY with flexi rods and mousse applied
• True to length with no odor or bugs after inspection
• Hair retained similar quality after being washed with swimmers shampoo (to remove gold tone/clean hair).

Cons-
• After 2-3 months of consistent wear, brushing and styling (Heat used sparingly, always with heat protectant) hair sheds uncontrollably. We're talking hair all 9ver every place I've stepped foot inside of.
• Hair will not hold heated curls, they fall within minutes
• Hair tangles and matts fairly easily in the nape
• Tons of split ends resulting in stragly looking hairs everywhere
• This is NOT 100% human hair, it is mixed with synthetic fibers, (I did do the burn test to confirm my suspicions).

Overall if you are looking for something cheap and quick with minimal styling, this is it..
If you want an investment, hair you'll be able to revive and re-wear for a few months, baby, this ain't it. I'd recommend this hair for an event but not for a unit/ like in you want to get the most out of. Hair performed as expected for the price.

title: Most comfortable electric shaver I've used
text:
As someone who's never grown a beard or mustache (I can go maybe a day or two but after that it drives me crazy), this has to be the most comfortable electric shaver I've ever used. The three pivoting heads move over facial contours very easily, and I appreciate that it's quieter than others I've used. In spite of that, it took a week or so to feel like it was doing a good job - perhaps because my face needed time to adjust (as claimed in the manual) or because it takes me a while to figure out how to use it most effectively - but I'm happy with the job it does. The neck has been the hardest area, and I've still got a few rough spots on the jawline, but it's much less than at first. The only real "negative" is the very small trimmer, which is placed rather awkwardly and doesn't seem to work very well.

Another nice plus is the LED display showing exactly how much time is left before needing to be recharged, and each charge seems to last much longer than others I've used (betweeen 2 to 3 weeks, and it only took an hour to fully charge). You can't use it plugged in, but it will allow you to plug it in for a "quick charge." The display also shows when to clean it (about every other use) and the heads flip up for easy cleaning under running water (much easier than using the tiny brush). It looks great, too - very sleek and cool and stylish - with a nice little charging stand, which looks good enough to leave out on the counter (minus the cord). It also comes with a "charging pod" which will be good for travelling.

Overall, I'm very pleased with it, although $240 is pretty steep. It's still not "as close as a blade" but I've given up believing that any electric shaver truly can be, but it's a whole lot more convenient that using shaving cream. (Others have complained about the "excessive" and difficult packaging, and I must agree completely on that point - use a knife carefully or scissors).

title: My one and only
text:
Bottom line: this is the only cleanser I will use.

I got into Mary Kay products because my sister in law was selling it. I thought it was pretty over priced at first but I purchased it anyways since I wanted my sister in law to make her commission. I used it the same night I purchased it.

As soon as I opened the cleanser bottle I smelled a wonderful aroma. It's hard for me to explain it. It was like a very light, sweet fragrance. I love the smell so much! As I was rubbing it on my face, all I could do was keep sniffing and sniffing. I know! I'm such a freak!

The cleanser felt awesome on my skin too. I could feel the little exfoliating beads however it wasn't too much and it wasn't too little. Mary Kay seemed to get it just right. A little bit of the product went a long way too. I only need about two or three small squirts of the bottle to cover my face.

The moisturizer I wasn't as impressed with. I thought the smell was not as nice as the cleanser's. But the moisturizer felt pretty good. It was very light. It felt like my skin could breathe. However, I felt like it wasn't enough of a moisturizer, but then again, I have REALLY dry skin especially during the winter. So I used a small dab of my Elizabeth Arden cream in addition to this moisturizer, so problem fixed. An added bonus is that using the velocity moisturizer I only need a little bit of my Elizabeth Arden thereby extending the life of that expensive cream!

Fast forward a few years, when I was in college. I was a BROKE college student. I couldn't really afford this product anymore. So for about 3-4 years I was using the cheap over the counter cleanser (only $3-4 a pop!). It worked. My skin stayed clear althoughout college but I found myself missing Mary Kay! My skin feel cleaner, more supple and softer while on Mary Kay.

Now that I am a graduate and am working, I am finally able to afford it. I purchased this almost immediately. From now on, I will not skimp out and will order this every time. Actually, now that I am as approaching my mid 20's (eek!) I'll give the Time Wise stuff a go.

I highly recommend this cleanser and moisturizer. The cleanser does its job and does it well. The smell of the cleanser is delicious; I cannot get enough of it. Even though I have to supplement the moisturizer, that's alright. I understand that my skin is probably drier than most normal people. Although this product is a little pricey and not easily accessible, it is so worthit!

text:
I read a lot of the reviews on this item before buying it. I've looked at several other Henna hair dyes, and this one is certainly the best bang for your buck. Others I've looked at retail for $36 and are much more complicated to use than this one.
I followed the instructions exactly and found it was such and easy process. Washed my hair twice with a clarifying shampoo, towel dried my hair, mixed the henna powder with warm water and applied. Although it said to leave the product on for 1 hour, I left mine on for 2 since I have blonde roots. Surprisingly, it covered my roots great and I have consistant color all over.
The smell might be off-putting to some users, although I regularly use a henna based shampoo, so I am used the the grassy/dirt odor it has. I follow up with a mixture of 4 parts water, 1 part apple cider vinegar, and a few drops of lavendar EO, which leaves hair shiny, conditioned, and smelling great!
Overall, I would recommend this product to anyone and will continue to use it myself instead of chemical based hair dyes.

Since I have hyper pigmentation from not using sun screen in my youth, I've been trying to find ways to stop or reverse it. My skin is somewhat sensitive, so maybe that's one of the reasons, or some ingredient I'm slightly allergic to? I'm not sure. But I wasn't completely surprised as I did notice my face felt just a tad tingly and extra sensitive after using it (even with just one drop, no more than two, each night). During the time I did use it, which was for a few weeks, I have about half the bottle left, I didn't notice my spots lightening or even staying the same. Actually, they got very slightly darker; even though, I used sun screen. I don't necessarily attribute that occurrence to this product though, but certainly I was disappointed that this did nothing for me even after being patient and using it consistently for a while to see its effects. Maybe it'll work for others as the other reviews seem to suggest.

I’m absolutely obsessed with this product. After spending $50 on a brow tint at the salon, I decided that I was entirely capable of doing it at home and set out for a good kit. And let me tell you, this is the one!!

I would suggest that when you’re applying, don’t over fill your brows as you would using makeup because it will come out looking too big. I’ve definitely overlined a few times and had to scrub hard at my skin to get the product off. Applying to the areas with the most hair is your best bet.

title: Nice look; feels pretty solid; but average in performance & value
text:
This is a “dressed up” version of the Wahl “LifeProof” shaver (which I also reviewed). It has a more upscale look and feel to it, plus adds a battery gauge to show the charge level. However, the shave quality is the same – OK, but not a standout.

The case feels more solid than the LifeProof and, while it’s more of a traditional look, I think they did a nice job with the overall aesthetics. It is pretty grippy even with wet hands. It does not, however, feel as comfortable to hold as the more sculpted models such as most of the Panasonic shavers and some Braun shavers.

The shave quality of this model is identical to that of the LifeProof: very Remington in how it feels (close, but rather aggressive). Performance is best on the easy spots (cheek) but not as good on the more trickier spots (neck and jawline). The flex head helps with dealing with face contours but it lacks enough travel to do an excellent quality job.

The aggressiveness of the shave is dialed down when using it wet. It needs a very, very thin layer of shave cream (the gel style creams work well) or the head gets bogged down.

Love the trimmer! The positioning could be improved to make it easier to use, but it cuts very cleanly on sideburns and ‘shash trimming.

The controls are clean, easy to read and tell you all you need to know (charge and battery status).

I like the feel of this better than the Wahl LifeProof, but the shave quality keeps this at the same rating (average, which is 3 stars). It’s a very workable shaver, but for the price there are better choices available from Panasonic (anything in their Arc line) or, for less money, from Remington.

title: Eyebrow game changer
text:
Uh, hello, this product is dope AF. I have suffered my whole life from pretty sparse and invisible colored brows. It's weird, because my hair is pretty dark brown, but my brows look like fishing line and I look like an alien with no makeup on them. I was snooping around the internet doing some research on microblading, which is basically like tattooing on your eyebrows, but it's pretty expensive, and only lasts a few years, and also I don't really trust other people to semi-permanently choose the shape of my brows. I stumbled across this product on Instagram I think and decided to give it a shot.

If you regularly draw on your eyebrows, then applying this will be a breeze. If you have dark hair and wear your brows dark, then you don't really even have to worry too much about how long you keep this product on. I usually do 3 applications at about 7 minutes at a time each time I dye my brows.

I noticed in other reviews that there was some discrepancy on how long this product lasts, and I think I figured out where the difference is coming from. If you have pretty full and nicely shaped brows, but they are light colored and you want them darker, and you are only using this product to dye the ACTUAL HAIRS of your eyebrows, a single application of this will last for weeks. HOWEVER, if you have thin, sparsely furred brows and are using this product to dye the SKIN under and around your actual brow hairs (like drawing or tattooing would do) then this will really only last between 2 and 4 days depending on what you're putting on your face and what kind of activities (like sweating) you are doing.

Either way it is still worth it. It is so nice to wake up in the morning with eyebrows instead of looking like Bob Geldoff in The Wall. I also get about 3 applications from each little "pill" so this product should last a good long while before I have to reorder. Overall very good purchase that I would recommend to anyone who wants darker, fuller brows.

text:
UPDATE 5/3/21: Got my second shipment today. All in tact! And great color selection!

This is a really great deal. If it is packaged right. The first time, unfortunately the bottles arrived smashed due to poor packaging. This is not the vendors fault as it was shipped by Amazon. I told them about it and they gave me a full refund. I really wish they would take a little more care when shipping. Hopefully my next round will go better.
**UPDATE** 5/3/21: Got my second shipment today. All in tact! And great color selection!
This is my guilty pleasure. It is definitely like gambling. But once every month or so I take the chance and roll the dice. Some times I get colors I do not have and other times I get 4 of the same. But guess what!?! You can mix these colors and get something that you like. That is what I do. I have mixed some shimmery colors with solids and came out with a beautiful shade that didn't exist before! And for around $1 each it is such a great deal!!! Dollar store price but top salon quality. This polish has been discontinued which is really sad because it is my favorite by far. It goes on smooth, love the wide brush and consistency. It helps my nails grow and keeps them healthy and protected. Also it lasts forever. I mean the polish in the bottle will last forever. Like no expiration date. I have some that I have had for over 10 years and they still glide like they were new.

** This is copy of my review from same product but bought different times and vendors***

This a great price for 20 polishes. Buying them in the store would be like $6 or $7. I have to admit this is my favorite guilty pleasure. It is like gambling lol. For around $1 a polish this is such a fun way to try new colors!

I absolutely love this polish. I have used it for years. The nice thing about these polishes is that even after years they still perform as well as the new ones. I love how easy it is to apply. If I am in a hurry, one coat is fine. I like to take my time with my nails so I have steps (below). I like to change my polish every week so chipping isn’t a problem for me. Also I wear gloves when I do dishes or clean to extend the life of my nails.
I love that this polish dries fairly quickly if you don’t put it on too thick. I mean, put on a coat while watching TV or on the PC. Careful not to touch anything! But let it dry thoroughly.
Then if you need a little more tint slap a little thin layer to make it pop. Also here are couple tips I learned through my years of doing my nails:

1. Use the SH Complete Care 7in1 or 170 Clear'd for takeoff as a base coat. (I am pretty sure that is why it’s called that... It makes sense to me) I know they say you don’t need one with this polish, but really it is for easier removal. It makes your life so much easier! Especially with darker colors that seem to get in the creases and under your nail that are a pain to remove.

2. Use a white polish (121 let’s snow for example) under any color to make that color really pop. You don’t need a really thick coat of white either. Just enough to give a canvas for the bright color to pop.

3. This polish is a little thick so mind that when you apply it. Put one streak down the middle of your nail (your first application to each nail) this will be a little thicker then go to each side and touching the outskirts of the middle line to grab some of the excess there to spread to the sides.

4. I use Sally Hansen Salon Manicure Top Coat as well to seal the color in if I am not using a Salon Manicure Glitter Overcoat. I think they both help preserve the color.

4b. I know glitter can be intimidating because it’s such a pain to get off. Don’t let that deter you. If you like the look of glitter go for it! There are polish removers designed for that now. As well as the polish remover in the jar that you put your finger in to remove color. There is one that has little ridges (or brushes) inside the center wall that help strip the glitter. Can’t tell you where or who. But I can say you probably have one in your town.

5. For those of you that like a little shiny nail but not necessarily color. I use the 170 Clear’d for takeoff and add some drops of any sheer color (Arm Candy, Sheer Ecstasy, Sweet Talker, Shell We Dance, Pink Slip) it just looks like a natural nail with clear polish only it hides blemishes! And your nails look super awesome! I get compliments all the time about how healthy my nails look when I do that.

I hope these tips help. These are things I have learned over the years. I love doing nails and I am glad to share the things I have discovered to save someone else some frustration or time.

text:
I've used this toothbrush, the essence 5600, and the flexcare r910. The flexcare is more powerful and has better brush heads (it also avoids the problem of having water trapped inside the brush and growing mold), but it's also far more expensive. The essence 5600 is a waste of money in my opinion as it has the same performance as this toothbrush, but suffers from a shoddy li-on battery that dies after about a year or so of use. This avoids the battery problem by using replaceable AA batteries and lasts quite a while on each replacement.

The only major con is with the brush head design. There is a a gap between the brush body and head, and this gap tends to fill with water after use. This unfortunately leads to black mold growing in the cavity. It's easy to avoid this by simply unscrewing the head after brushing and rinsing out the cavity, but it's an annoyance nonetheless.

All in all, this is a great cheap way to get the benefits of sonicare.

title: Pay attention to the directions.
text:
A word of caution: if you have very sensitive or thin skin then this will leave marks for a day or so. My skin is very thin, so popping a pimple will leave a red mark for about a solid day normally. I still use this though, but I plan around work and social outings.

OK, now, the directions will tell you which tips to use with which suction levels. Follow them. Certain tips are very painful with the wrong suction levels. I can use the broad tips on max suction for stubborn blackheads just fine, but the pinpoint tip on low is too much for me. Odd.

Anyway, you are only reading this to see if it works. So, does it? YES! It actually does. I pulled all kinds of gross "stuff" off the filter inside that it sucked from my skin. I only used it around my nose to test it, as I have a bunch of those really tiny blackheads that look like freckles that I wanted to get rid of. One single treatment after washing my face with my normal acne routine and more than half the blackheads are gone. The empty pores are larger now though, and I can still see them but they look so much less noticeable than they were before.

I found that using small circles worked best and hitting the same spot over and over again. Only one popped like you can see online, the rest didn't really look like anything special while I was using it, but afterwards my skin was definitely cleaner and the screen was no longer clean. So yes, it is doing something and makes a difference.

I still use my regular acne routine to keep the oil at bay, but I am going to keep using this once a month to finish cleaning out all the pores. I only charge it every other use and even then it is not dead, I just don't want it to die while I am using it. Takes about an hour to charge. Comes with a nice little drawstring bag to hold everything in there and extra filters. I use alcohol wipes to clean them off and the tips as well. I folded up the instructions and shoved them in there too for reference.

I would recommend this, but with caution. It WILL leave red marks so watch out. People with thin skin need to be really careful when you start out so that you don't look like a racoon for several days. If used correctly it will do it's job and you can cover any extra redness with some concealer just fine. Or at least, that is my experience.

I purchased this from another site (Modern Man UK) at a lower price. But about the product itself... fantastic. Absolutely wonderful. It has more of a "croap" type of texture, and very easily picks up on my badger brush, forming a dense, slick lather. I don't normally do as well on the first go, as every soap/cream has its quirks -- but this one performed brilliantly on my first try. Not only that, but I also decided to use this in combo with a brand new razor (an EJ) and a new blade (which can sometimes a bit rough on first use), both bad ideas when you're trying a new cream/soap for the first time. Too many adjustments. All those risks aside, the shave went PERFECTLY. Not a nick, weep or burn. Just a nice, clean shave and a fine smelling mug to show for it!

Be aware that the scent can seem a bit strong while in use, but it tones down very nicely after shaving -- which makes me really appreciate the care with which the manufacturer scents their products. As for the scent itself -- I took a while to really take to it, as again, it comes across a bit overpowering at first -- but it mellows into something unique -- all at once sweet, woodsy and spicy, but decidedly masculine -- if that makes any sense. I highly recommend this product.

title: Great...BUT Beware of Size Issues
text:
EDIT - I wrote the review below and then I realized that each page has it's specific style AND varied SIZES. I didn't realize this at first. This fact alone will lead me to not buy them again. It's common to mess up on ONE brow in a pair. Its nice to be able to go to your page and just cut off a new one and not worry if it's the same size as the others. I only like the bigger (longer) brows, so I won't even want to use half the brows on each page. Major issue for me. I'll leave the tips below, because if you don't care about size differences, maybe this info will help you.

1- They are overall amazing!
2- They take some practice, but it's worth it.
3- When I mess up, I remove them with alcohol and toilet tissue. I wet it with alcohol and rub with dry toilet tissue. The dry helps rub the transfer off. It's not super pleasant, but it works.
5- They last for me for two full days.
6- As crazy as it sounds, I followed the advice of someone here and shaved my (small) brows after trying to apply over my natural brows. I was very freaked out about shaving my brows, but my brows sucked anyhow and it improved the look of these by far!
7- My advice is to try all or almost all of the varieties sent in the package. It can't hurt to try, right?! Remember you can always remove them if you really can't stand them. Some of the ones that looked very odd on paper, looked not bad on me! Some look better on "natural" days and some look better with make-up. I wear the ones I don't hate on days I'm just staying home and I save my favs for the days I go out.
8- The eyebrow print is on the front AND the back, so you can hold them up in the mirror to place correctly. Super helpful.
9- Again, overall these look very natural! To eliminate the shiny look they can have a little brush of power foundation works, but I have found that a little water splashed on my face after helps too.

I am not typically someone that puts a lot of time or maintenance into styling my hair, but it grew very long during COVID and I chose to try this curling iron for the rare times I want to look more classy. For reference, I have relatively straight hair with a little bend/wave/frizz to it in spots.

This curling iron heats up fast and uniform. The clamp-style makes it easy to hold and style - just clamp the end of your hair and wind the strand around. I like a 1-inch barrel like this one has, you can create tighter spiral-y curls or you can wind the strands looser and create less defined waves. It was a nice bonus that this curling iron came with a carrying bag, two styling clips, a glove to protect your hand from heat, and a comb. The iron itself looks attractive and stylish with the rose gold color.

I have used this curling iron to create both a tousled, bed-head wavy look with volume, and to create more tight curls that I arranged into an updo for attending a wedding. I have been very pleased with it so far and would recommend it!

title: Great for all those Dollar Shave Club razors you've got sitting around
text:
I was subscribed to Dollar Shave Club for quite a while, but then the pandemic hit, and I felt the need to shave regularly . . . less pressing, shall we say. But even when I shaved every other day, my razors would start to pile up, even though I switched my billing to every two months. Eventually I stopped my DSC subscription, but I still had all these blades. And the handle that came with the blades -- let's just say that I kept in in the cup that we keep the toothbrushes in, and you know how gross that cup gets. So I tossed the handle.

That's where this handle comes in. It says it fits DSC's Executive series blades, but it also fits their OLD 4X standard blades -- the ones I have loads of. NOTE: DSC now uses a 4-blade and 6-blade pricing scheme, so this handle may not be right for you if you've got DSC's newer blades.

So, if you've got a bunch of old Dollar Shave Club 4X blades taking up room in your bathroom drawer, this handle will work. That's all I asked of it, and it delivered, so five stars.

title: Not the BEST lift...but lift, for a low cost
text:
I'm amending my review, because when used correctly, this really does work, or at least it does for my hair.

No, it doesn't give me GIANT hair...which I'd love, and which I've seen on Youtube vids in realtime with other brands of a similar type of product. So one star off for that. On the other hand, what I have to work with is very, very, very thin hair. Not thinNING, I'm not losing hair, I just never had a lot to begin with. My ponytail circumference is tiny.

With that said, I wear bangs, and this really does lift the hair behind the bangs up so my hair isn't just lying flat and stringy against my head. The trick is to use LESS rather than more. Sprinkle a TINY bit more if you feel you need it and keep going until you find your sweet spot.

I use it in my center part, then down one or two partings on either side (underneath), then one or two partings at the top in the back. If it falls a bit I can put my fingers into my hair, and the voodoo magic comes to life again and I'm no longer flat-headed.

It does feel icky and tacky. No way around that, that I can see.

text: I bought this after watching some youtube reviews and decided I would try it out. The tin is also nice since it catches any shadow that trickles through the sponge, it also seems like it will be great to travel with since it won't get make up everywhere if you toss it in a makeup bag.  They do sell refills for the tin, but I think I will just wash the one it came with and see how that works out. title: Pretty, But Totally Magnetic Lashes With No Regular Adhesive
text: FanArti False Eyelashes and Glue Pen Kit,5 Pairs Fake Eyelash & 2 in1 Design Lash Eyeliner (Black+Clear), Easy to Apply and Comfortable,Tweezer Included,All Day Wear come with a glue pen and an eyeliner pen. You have to test the products on your skin first to make certain you have no allergic reactions before using them. I thought the glue pen is just an adhesive and the eyeliner pen, as with all false eyelash eyeliner pens was magnetic, but I was wrong. The glue and eyeliner seem to be both magnetic. You have to wait until both are completely dry before applying the lashes, as the magnetic properties are what keep your lashes on. The 5 pairs of lashes are all very lovely and there is something for every occasion from work to play to dress up. I wish it had been made more clear that these are magnetic lashes, as I only use glue adhesive lashes, and only hypo allergenic glues to protect my eyes. To remove these lashes with the magnetic liner or adhesive on your eyes, you need a good liquid make up remover and cotton pads. For not making the magnetic properties totally clear even though the lashes are lovely, 3 STARS.

title: A fun & quick way to clean up those grody makeup brushes!
text:
First off, the seller, Creatique, is AMAZING. Concerning my makeup brush cleaner order, there was a tiny, Amazon related issue. I contacted the seller & they immediately replied & solved the issue right away.

Onto the makeup cleaner itself, after seeing oodles of youtube videos on this style of brush cleaner, I figured I'd "give it a whirl"... ; ) I purchased mine from Creatique due to the price, their seller rating & a few perks, including a nifty storage bag for the cleaner!

I finally had a chance to try it out, on my very-makeup-filled brushes (due to medical issues, it's very hard for me to stand at a sink for any extended amount if time, so my poor brushes were getting neglected). It worked just as shown, took much less time & was rather fun too~ Since my brushes needed a major cleaning, they took a few more runs through the cleaner & I also ran them through a rinse, using the same method with just plain clean water, which really helped. I'm sure they'll be much easier to clean from now on!

The cleaner worked, again, as described, was easy to use & fast. The wand part has one speed setting, but it was definitely fine on my thicker brushes as well as the finer ones. When done, the thicker brushes were very slightly damp but the finer brushes spun nearly completely dry. Remember to hand mold the bristles back to shape when they're done being spun, to maintain their shape.

If you don't wait too long between cleanings, it'll work just fine : ) I plan to give one of these cleaners to my daughter (in her 20's) too, she'll really enjoy it!

text:
Brush + Case + Sponge:
The Kabuki brush is a little bit long for my taste for being a travel size brush, but it is still much smaller than a lot of other travel size kabuki brushes on the market. The case is cute but a little bit heavy. I hope in the future the company will consider making it lighter and thus even more portable. Some people might like the substantial feel though. Instead, I placed it directly on top of the foundation to serve as a cushion when I'm moving around to prevent the foundation from shattering.

Foundation:
The foundation itself is pretty great. It doesn't feel grainy on skin and helps even out my complexion without drying my skin. I have light to medium Asian skin tone, and the shade Supernatural works just fine. It is slightly lighter than my skin tone when I'm tanned, but I only apply it around the center of my face anyways, so there is less concern about blending to the neck to begin with. I might try a shade darker if I get tanner in the future.

I use a brush to apply the foundation and have it settle into my pores before I apply another layer on top with my own sponge (purchased from Muji) to give more coverage if needed. When I'm on the go, skipping the brush step is usually fine. I can sort of squeeze my sponge into the designated slot.

title: Thick, rich, and natural moisturizer
text:
I'm on the "Youth Express" -- as the bottle says -- with this moisturizer. The list of ingredients takes up the entire length of the bottle, but it's good, "98% natural" stuff: organic aloe, organic sunflower oil, avocado oil, green tea, rose hip oil -- you name it, if you've seen it in the healthfood store, it's probably in this moisturizer.

The first time you use it, you'll have to pump the lid several times to get the lotion going. The dispenser is handy, allowing you to dispense the amount you want. The moisturizer is thick and has an aroma I can only describe as "earthy" or "plant-y." It's definitely not perfumed. The moisturizer works into the skin nicely without leaving residue on the hands. I did notice, several minutes after rubbing it in, that my fingers felt so satiny-soft -- so they were moisturized too. My hands can become pretty dry so I am using this for them as well as my face.

I prefer this moisturizer for winter because it's so thick, but you could use it year-round. Recommended.

title: They’re Okay for What They Are
text:
These Koruser Type II disposable face masks are okay for what they are. They’re as good for my wearing-to-the-grocery-store needs as any.

Unlike most versions of this type of mask on the market, these are pure white rather than pale blue. The ear loops are well attached and make donning and doffing simple. The flexible wire nose bridge bends easily to seal on the face, which supposedly minimizes glasses fogging. But exhalation moisture and perspiration still quickly build up inside these three-ply masks (as they do in ALL the masks that I’ve used) and make them uncomfortable after just a short time. The accordion folds adapt them to any facial size and shape.

Being compelled to wear a face mask in public is an unpleasant fact of modern life, and the need for them should—but doesn’t—transcend political, cultural and religious differences. Any decent person with the slightest trace of compassion for others, or any sense of personal responsibility, will wear a mask to help control the spread of COVID-19, which continues to surge as I write this because hordes of ignorant, selfish, stupid, oblivious morons can’t even take such a simple, tiny step in the interests of public health.

As a commodity and a necessity, at least for those who care more about the greater good than about imagined attacks on their “freedoms,” these masks are okay but nothing special, so I rate them at three stars.

title: Easy to fill and easy to use!
text:
My daughter loves using Chapstick, so I decided this would be a fun rainy day activity to do with her! Since these were for my daughter, I wanted to keep them fun with color and "flavor." We made our Chapstick with Kool-Aid! I used Kool-Aid specifically because these tubes are clear and I love seeing the color through them. These containers were fairly easy to fill. It takes a little more coordination than just a lip balm tin, but I like it in these containers better (especially since they are clear). They have held up well so far too. The caps stay on tight and the Chapstick "twists up" perfectly. I haven't noticed any other issues.
Here is the Kool-Aid Chapstick recipe we used:
4 Tbs Coconut Oil
3 Tbs Shea Butter
1 Tbs Beeswax, shaved
A Squirt of kool-aid (we used fruit punch)

1. Mix first three ingredients in a microwave save bowl.
2. After blended, heat for 1 minute.
3. Mix in the kool-aid until desired colour is reached.
4. Pour mixture into your containers and pop it into the fridge for an hour or two.

*I think these would make great gifts! Chapstick/lip balm is very easy to make and can be completely customizable which would be perfect for gift giving!*

There is a label on the inner package with Japanese writing, that's not translated into English on the package. It says to make sure to use the plastic box to store the wipes to ensure quality and peel off the sticker completely; don't remove the wipes from the bag; make sure to close the lid after use. I'd suggest that the manufacturer add a translated version on the package. The package says to use the entire package within 45 days after opening, so if you don't wear make-up every day, you may not finish the package before they start to dry out.

My wife loves these! Highly recommended, especially for those who have sensitive skin!

title: Sturdy organization for a modest makeup collection
text:
This is a fantastic storage and transport option for the casual makeup user. If you have a smallish makeup and brush collection, this will keep your stuff organized beautifully. I loved it for the ten months I used this. Before I had this, I'd tried makeup bags (too much digging for stuff I wanted), a single-compartment train case (also too disorganized), and Caboodles and tackle boxes (too much wasted space in the boxes, and needed too much room on the counter when open). Those storage options always left me feeling frustrated because they got in the way of putting on my makeup efficiently. This was the answer to my prayers!

I ended up having to buy a simalir organizer case in a larger size when I started ditching individual eyeshadows in favor of large palettes, and expanding my brush collection. This case held my Naked Smoky and Sugarpill Pro Palette just fine, but when I got the Modern Renaissance palette and a large Z Palette and couldn't add either of them, I downgraded this case to storing things I only need to dig out occasionally.

That said, this is a sturdy and well-built case that I had no issues with whatsoever. I used this pretty regularly, frequently taking it to/from performance gigs, and nothing ever ripped or tore, even toward the end when I had it packed to the gills. The zippers work cleanly. The strap is sturdy. The dividers stay put.

I have no reservations recommending this, unless you are a makeup junkie and/or have several large palettes. It's a great product!

text:
Everything stated in the description is true. Though it's not a cure, it sure does help. I have been using Clobetasol cream via RX to help clear up the outbreaks of Psoriasis (it's a cream that is rubbed on the effected area and helps heal psoriasis lesions that pop up on the skin); but the problem is you have to keep the affected area covered all the time; in my case it's mainly my hands; YOU TRY WEARING PLASTIC GLOVES 24/7! So I give myself a break with this lotion.
This lotion definitely keeps my hands moist and I have less outbreaks. I still use gloves to help hold in the moisture a bit more, but not all the time. Moisture is what psoriasis needs to help heal this condition. This lotion helps with that. Will most certainly will reorder again.
My hat's off to Fay Farms. Remember, skin conditions like Psoriasis, Eczema, etc. are auto-immune diseases. They are incurable. Think twice before taking prescription medications; they do NOT cure, are loaded with many unpleasant side effects, some even lethal; their outrageously priced, etc. Unfortunately, just because you're healing doesn't mean you're cured. Breakouts come and go. You never know when, but I notice I get them more often when I'm ultra-stressed. I have had this condition for many, many years. Took me until now to find the right product.

read what else I found:
If you haven’t been using makeup primer, then you’re really missing out.

Whether you wear a full face of makeup everyday or you prefer to keep it simple with BB cream and tinted lip balm, makeup primer is a godsend when trying to combat shine or create a smooth base for foundation.

Yet, many people often skip this step because they believe they don’t really need it, are unsure of how to use it or don’t think it’s worth the investment. However, using primer underneath your makeup will make everything last longer, whether that’s on your skin or in your cosmetics bag. We asked two beauty experts to discuss the ins and outs of primer and why it’s a must-have. Here’s the deal.

Makeup primer is a base for foundation or face makeup that allows it to go on smoother and last longer.

Formulas are available in cream, gel and powder. While moisturizer softens skin, editorial and celebrity makeup artist Stephen Dimmick points out that primer prepares skin for your favorite tinted moisturizer or foundation, giving it something to hold onto so it lasts throughout the day.

Many makeup primers are formulated with silicone-based polymers like dimethicone because of their ultra-smoothing effects. But for those who struggle with cystic acne and other skin conditions, do a patch test or check with a medical professional before use, as there have been reports of allergic reactions to dimethicone.

Physicians Formula’s celebrity makeup artist Joanna Schlip adds that makeup primers can also help smooth any fine lines, wrinkles or large pores. If you are searching for a face primer to help color-correct rosacea or conceal acne spots, Schlip’s go-to is this light green primer as that hue cancels out redness.

Primers are even available just for your eyelids to prevent creasing. “I’d recommend pairing a primer with extra long-wear [eyeshadow or eyeliner] formulas for a look that will really stay put,” says Schlip. If you have oilier eylids, Dimmick advises that you use a mattifying eyelid primer.

Using your fingertips to apply makeup primer allows you to really work the product into your skin.

Schlip thinks it’s best to apply primer with fingertips for areas larger than a quarter. “If only using for small areas, I’d recommend a brush. I like to use a concealer or lip brush for this,” she said. This spot-treat technique gives the look of a more natural finish, according to Schlip.

Taking this routine a step further, Dimmick considers the process “an exercise for the face.” He explains that massaging primer onto skin with fingertips helps “to get the blood flowing underneath.” We’ll consider that the next time we’re meditating while putting on makeup.

Primer is a life-saver for getting your makeup to stay-put in extreme weather.

If you live, visit or plan on traveling anywhere that experiences hot and humid or cold and dry temperatures, Schlip suggests having primer handy to help your makeup wear longer. However, Dimmick advocates for using primer year-round. “No matter what the weather is like outside, this extra step will save you a lot of time and effort.”

Primer can even be worn on its own.
Love the fresh no-makeup look but want to look a bit more polished than when you first woke up? Primer is your answer. The product can be worn on your eyelids and double as a light eyeshadow, or it can serve as a lighter alternative to foundation.

title: One coat coverage, buttery smooth formulas & special FX finishes! 😍 Amazing set of polishes!
text:
This set of gel polishes from Pine Gel really blew me away! These cover in one easy coat and have a nice glossy finish. The glitter polish was a little bit thick, but it's packed with glitter so I guess that's to be expected. This set of six shades contains (1) Glitter, (3) Crèmes, (2) Magnetics, and a cats eye magnet wand needed to work the magnetic polishes. All of the colors cure for 60 secs in an LED lamp or 90 secs in a UV.

The crèmes are all buttery smooth in application, and self level beautifully. Each dry down to a nice glossy finish. The magnetics are easy to manipulate with the enclosed magnet stick. I was able to do a double cat eye line on my first try! (These are gonna be a lot of fun to play with using different shaped magnets for different effects.) Both magnetic polishes covered completely in one easy coat. The glitter shade is jam-packed with small royal blue glitters and is accented with a sprinkling of medium sized blue hexagons. The depth and sparkle to this polish is incredible. The glitter load makes this shade a little bit thick - but it's still workable. None of these gel polishes have a bad odor. None of them gave me any issues during application or the curing process. I cannot speak to the wear time, as I always use a peel-off base coat or full coverage tips, with gel polish products.

Because these are so rich in pigment, (and a lot of them are dark colors), it is best to work in thin coats. They do cure with a sticky layer. All of these (except the glitter) cured for 60 sec in my LED lamp. With the thickness and opacity of the glitter polish, I did a double cure on that one to be safe. All swatches in this review are ONE coat and are shown WITHOUT top coat.

I think the coverage, formula, and finishes of these polishes is amazing and absolutely worth the price. I highly recommend these! Thanks for reading. :) If my review and photos were helpful to you in any way, please click the button below to let me know. Thanks!

title: Super soft and silky results! Works fast on breakage and split ends!
text:
Wow! I've tried a lot of different Argan Oil shampoo and conditioners (and sprays and masks and hot treatments etc) and I can 100% say this is my All time favorite for no other reason than how incredibly fast I'm seeing a difference in the ends and improvement on breakage. I color my hair and have been for close to 10 years now and just in the past year or so I've started having really bad problems with breakage and split ends. I've tried probably 10 different brands or more with some kind of argan oil treatment and it really helps. But I didn't get results like this from anywhere else, and I've tried some pretty pricey stuff. After like, 3 days of use I happened to look down at my hair one day and it just hit me that I didn't have any frizz or areas that looked wild and untamed from breakage, the hairs that would normally have 2 or 3 splits or frays were just smooth all the way down. I tried to take a picture of the hair up close so you could see but couldn't get a clear shot at such a short distance. The color looks richer and has a healthy looking shine, it isn't greasy or stringy like you might worry about with Argan Oil.
This stuff even smells amazing! I usually like coconut scents, it's always been my favorite, but this smells more floral and a little spicy, which maybe sounds weird but I think it's soooo good.

It lathers up surprisingly well for an Argan Oil shampoo and I don't have to use much for my bra strap length hair. My hair is really thick, too, but a good quarter sized dallop works out to be about the right amount for me. I do the ends and body first and work my way up to my scalp, backwards from how I use regular shampoo. (I do this because some brands seem to leave my hair oily if I don't get it rinsed out well, that Argan Oil can be stubborn.) I usually let it set for a couple minutes while I wash my body so the hair can absorb the nutrients before I rinse it away. I follow it with their conditioner and my hair gets sooo soft when it dries. I really can't stress enough how well it helps my hair. I know everyone responds differently but for me, it's better than anything else I've tried. I'll be ordering this again for sure.

I did receive my Argain oil shampoo at a promotional price for testing and evaluation purposes. I was not paid for my review and was asked only to provide whatever feedback I may have about the product, whether it be positive or negative. I welcome both positive or negative feedback as well. My review is solely based on my experience and honest opinions of this shampoo.

title: Other Indy Top Coats Are Better
text:
I purchased because I was trying to find a top coat that was more long lasting in the bottle and more friendly to work with. And this product is both of those things - it's easy to work with and doesn't dry out in the bottle. But, I have two issues that make this unusable for me.

First is a personal preference - I prefer for a top coat to be super hard when dry. I have super soft flexible nails and top coats that dry to a hard plastic-like finish give my nails structure to avoid tears and bends. Seche Vite is not this. It's thin and stays too flexible for my needs.

Second is an objective problem - shrinkage. After about a day, this top coat shrinks. It pulls away from the edges of my nails, either exposing the polish underneath or pulling the polish with it. This leads to chipping and lifting. Searching online I found this is a common problem that people face with this product.

Instead, I'm going to stick with other brands until I find my goldilocks (if there are people with my above concerns, I'm currently trying Glisten & Glow and I'm pleased so far).

title: Excellent quality. Very attractive assortment of confetti and glitter polishes. Small bottles.
text:
This is an excellent assortment of attractive, quality gel polish, with base coat and top coat (no wipe and matte versions). The presentation elevates the worth as a gifting option. One of the best features of this set is the bottles of gel polish provide actual representations of the contents. On the top of the cap is a sticker with proper identification of the color (including glitter, confetti varieties). Also on the front label is a small circle, under the brand name, that has an accurate portrayal of the contents. Finally, a company gets it. So, this boosts the rating a bit.
There are 16 varieties of gel polish, with confetti and glitter. The consistency is perfect, allowing application of a thin coat. An ability to apply a thin coat is essential, mainly due to the size of these bottles. They are 5ml (0.17fl oz), which is one of the smallest bottles of gel polish that i've encountered. This is actually a disappointing size/quantity of gel polish. Based on the size of the bottles of gel polish, I consider this to actually be a sampler set, as opposed to a set of 'normal' sized bottles of attractive confetti, glitter gel polishes. So, i guess one can try out the various polishes and then purchase larger bottles of desired varieties.
Overall, I feel all of the polishes in the assortment are visually attractive. The polishes are excellent quality, and produce excellent results. The significant other tested the gel on some fake nails, and i commented that it looks beautiful as is...no need to add any embellishments/decorations. She agreed., but said she'd combinde solid color gel polish with these, and add some rhinestones or other decorations, maybe create a marbled effect. I could see her creative juices flowing.
The product does match the descriptions and pictures in the product details. The presentation is effective and top notch. We like the quality and consistency of the gel polishes and base/top coats. If the bottles were at least the size of the base/top coat bottles, this set would be perfect and worth 5 stars. As currently configured, based on observations and impressions, this quality 'sampler' set earns a 4.5 - 4.75 star rating, with a high level recommendation.

title: Avoid. Buy a 'true' Sonicare
text:
The lifespan of this device seems to be quite limited. A couple of years ago, I bought 2 of these for my 2 boys. One of them stopped working after a couple of weeks - was able to return it to Amazon and get a replacement - and the other stopped after a little over one month. The replacement stopped working after about one month as well.

The big problem with this toothbrush is the battery compartment. Since it's using 'throw away' batteries, a bad thing by itself, there is a need for a lid to allow removal/insertion of batteries. At this price, the lid does not close tightly and water creeps in. Eventually, the entire thing stops working.

Pros for this toothbrush:
- low price.

Cons:
- short life due to almost inevitable water damage
- use of 'throw away' batteries

My recommendation: avoid.

Spend a few more and get a true Sonicare. You won't regret it. I've been using Sonicare tooth brushes for almost 10 years now. My first one was replaced after more than 5 years, mostly because I wanted a new one. My current is alive and kicking and it's likely to last for many more years if I don't choose to replace it.

I LOVE THESE. I have fairly light eyebrows that looks a bit bizarre with my naturally dark hair. The dark brown is easy to apply and natural looking. I love the results, but in terms of longevity I need to reapply about every two weeks.

- Per the above, love the angled brush included for application. It helps eliminate mess and keeps things precise. An even and thin coat of Vaseline applied with a q-tip under and around the eyebrow area keeps skin from staining, just make sure not to get the Vaseline on the hair to be dyed as it will prevent the dye from taking. I usually do one eyebrow at a time and leave on each for about 90 seconds. After, I lightly exfoliate the area with a little bit of sugar and coconut oil to remove any surface staining of the skin under the hair.

This is a great toothbrush! I have gingivitis and after only ONE use I could see improvement. title: Leaves feet noticeably soft for weeks
text:
I love this type of peeling foot masks. It's so satisfying to peel off large swaths of skin and be left with softer feet for weeks. I've used masks from a few brands, and this is a pretty solid one.

Unlike some other brands, this mask starts having noticeable effects on the very first day after application. I noticed my foot was itchy on the side and didn't think much of it until the afternoon, when I looked down and realized it was itchy because the skin was already beginning to dry out and peel.

Unfortunately, this mask doesn't work like the others to dry out large pieces of skin that you can just peel off. Instead, small tiny bits of skin start peeling, as if you were chapped in various different spots. I found that it was most effective to sit down after a shower, which helped loosen the dead skin, and carefully rub or pull at the dry bits. Only then larger areas start coming off, though still in small bits at a time.

However, this mask leaves your feet softer for weeks! Of course, the first week after is the softest, but even three weeks later, my feet are noticeably softer than before. I'm honestly tempted to use this mask once every 6 weeks just to maintain the softness.

title: Best liner to brighten your eyes and turn shadow into liner - I'm a believer!
text:
I was initially skeptical of a rose-gold liner, and when I first applied it it didn't look that dramatic on my very pale skin. However, I quickly learned how to use it best for my skin tone: to line the rims of my lower lids, which are frequently red and tired. It makes me look more awake and gives my eyes more of a shine than using basic white liner on that area. It's a godsend when it comes to getting ready for work in the morning after a night of insomnia or whatever else you've been up to. If you have darker skin, then this color will look fun on you just as a liner! But I also like to use it to line my upper lids to use as a base for using eyeshadow as a liner. It's basically like primer for a softer liner look, and I apply eyeshadow with a flat brush on top of the rose gold.

It will stay for as long as you need it to - I recently put it to the test when I was unexpectedly called to the hospital when my best friend went into labor! I put on my makeup in the morning, had been at work all day, called to the hospital at night, barely got any sleep, and the baby was delivered at noon the next day...so that was almost 30 hours of wearing the rose gold liner under my eyeshadow liner and on my lower eye-rims, and my eye makeup was STILL in place after that baby arrived! (I also wore Blinc mascara, which I also love for its staying power!) I've also worn it on several cross-country flights (including red-eyes) in order to arrive looking somewhat rested. It definitely works!!

You do have to sharpen it fairly regularly - I'm not a fan of the sharpener that comes on the cap, so I keep a small sharpener next to my makeup mirror. I do, however, LOVE the smudgy tool on the other end - it works great! I should buy this in bulk, that's how much I love it! I went from being a skeptic to incorporating it into my makeup routine every single day.

title: Norelco finally got it right!
text:
I have used electric razors for over 35 years all have good points and all have weaknesses. Norelco razors have two problems.

Hard to clean. As the cutter and blades fill up the motor is not able to maintain the speed and nicks result. You must take the blade and cutter assembly apart to clean properly and if you cut longer hairs by accident(side burn area etc.) it will wrap around the cutting blade and really slow the motor down. The motor slowing is the worst on the new "3 blade" called the Speed XL, they just seem to be underpowered.(just as a note the older Spectra blade replacements fit these razors and seem to work better). Think of this problem like a paper shredder that has not beeen emptied and hasn't room for more papers in the bin.

Hidden Build up. I have changed batteries in several of my Norelco shavers and the build up of gunk where only disassembly could find and cure it, is remarkable(same with most brands). I suspect this is gunk is high in bacteria and the cause of most skin infections from nicks. The stuff you never knew was there is nasty!

Now for the cure: Norelco 8060x! This razor blade assembly has open backs for the stubble to fall through as you shave. I use mine in the shower so no mess. The blade assembly is completely seperate from the motor unit= no place for gunk to build up! The unit is entirely water proof. The blades disassemble easily so you can get at those occasional "longer hairs" that wrap around the cutters. The cutters have more blades on each, so the shave is faster and the motor seems stronger than previous models, hence less slowing. The Nivea solution is great, but you can use regular shave cream or gel. I like the Nivea Gel for Sensitive Skin, it seems to be the right thickness for the razor and works alomost as well as the cream you load in the razor.

The only negative for some people might be the size or shape of the handle, it is smaleer and lighter than most shavers. Some people with larger hands may find is inconvient and others may find it easy to drop.

Overall this is the best all around razor I have owned, there is a brief time required for your face to get used to any new razor... This ones worth it!!

Some of the attributes that stood out were…

* The label proudly and boldly proclaims the product to be cruelty free as well as paraben free. I appreciate that not only is it free of animal testing but they clearly disclose it. All of the ingredients are clearly listed and for the most part familiar or identifiable as opposed to sounding like a chemistry experiment or something you need a PhD to decipher.
*The value to quantity is complementary to the quality. I have seen and used other products that you pretty much just are just paying for the name on the label. While I have not heard of Struck Studio until now, it does not in any way diminish the quality.

I will gladly continue to use this product and look forward to seeing what else the company has to offer. Even though I received this at a discounted rate, I feel it is still worth the full retail price.

title: Ingredients for all three currently offered in this listing
text:
Type:A considers this a hybrid of natural and synthetic that's more effective than purely natural deodorants. The emphasis is on safe ingredients.

This is the first deodorant I've tried with a cream-extrusion applicator. Took a few tries to figure out how much to use. After that it seems to work pretty well, though it's hard to tell if it's better than others I've tried. Goes on fairly dry feeling.

As with others, it seems to me the scented ones create a better overall effect than the unscented. Masking helps.

The Evergreen Forest (Adventurer) scent is very much what the name implies, much like pine sap, fairly strong when going on, not as noticeable later. I love that smell, but I've heard some don't.

Modern Spice (Maverick) is indeed spicy. I mainly smell something cinnamony, but there's no cinnamon in it. Maybe the balsam. There's also eucalyptus, patchouli, vanilla, cedar and peppermint.

The Fragrance-Free (Minimalist) does have a scent, no doubt due to some of the plant ingredients. It's a dull earthy, slightly spicy scent.

Here are the ingredients for each:

Adventurer: diisopropyl adipate, glycerin (organic, vegetable derived), beeswax, dimethicone, heptyl undecylenate, Maranta arundinacea (arrowroot) root powder, sodium bicarbonate, Zea mays (corn) starch, triethyl citrate, sorbitan oleate, Copernicia cerifera (carnauba) wax, glyceryl stearate, Cocos nucifera (coconut) oil (organic), tapioca starch, Aloe barbadensis (aloe vera) leaf extract (organic), Thuja occidentalis (northern white cedar) leaf oil, Thuja plicata (western red cedar) wood oil, Abies sibirica (siberian fir) oil, Eucalyptus globulus (eucalyptus) leaf oil, Pogostemon cablin (patchouli) oil, Pelargonium graveolens (geranium) oil, Lavandula hybrida (lavandin) oil, Canarium luzonicum (elemi) gum nonvolatiles, raspberry ketone, Mentha piperita (peppermint) oil, zinc citrate, water, bisabolol, titanium dioxide, silver chloride.

Maverick: diisopropyl adipate, glycerin (organic, vegetable derived), beeswax, dimethicone, heptyl undecylenate, Maranta arundinacea (arrowroot) root powder, sodium bicarbonate, Zea mays (corn) starch, triethyl citrate, sorbitan oleate, Copernicia cerifera (carnauba) wax, glyceryl stearate, Cocos nucifera (coconut) oil (organic), tapioca starch, Aloe barbadensis (aloe vera) leaf extract, Eucalyptus globulus (eucalyptus) leaf oil, Pogostemon cablin (patchouli) leaf extract, vanillin, Myroxylon pereirae (Peru balsam) oil, Vetiveria zizanoides (vetiver) root oil, Juniperis virginiana (Virginia red cedar) oil, Mentha piperita (peppermint) oil, Cistus ladaniferus (rock rose) oil, Dipteryx odorata [tonka bean] seed extract, zinc citrate, water, bisabolol, titanium dioxide, silver chloride.

Minimalist: diisopropyl adipate, glycerin (organic, vegetable derived), dimethicone, beeswax, heptyl undecylenate, sodium bicarbonate, Maranta arundinacea (arrowroot) powder, sorbitan oleate, Zea mays (corn) starch, Copernicia cerifera (carnauba) wax, triethyl citrate, glyceryl stearate, Cocos nucifera (coconut) oil (organic), zeolite, tapioca starch, Aloe barbadensis (aloe vera) leaf extract, zinc citrate, water, bisabolol, titanium dioxide, silver chloride.

Ok so I have pretty thick hair (it’s naturally voluminous and a pain to brush if it gets longer than my shoulders). I hopped out of the shower and towel dried, hair only slightly damp/leaning towards dry, and used this brush on the middle heat setting. Just a few seconds running it through (and I go through thick portions of hair at a time) and it worked!

I love how easy it is to use because for my kind of hair I just can’t stand doing the classic round brush/hair dryer combo (arms end up hurting or it slips) or the flatiron alone (which takes FOREVER to do my hair). This brush does the job of both so well.

This is a small but mighty brush! Light in my hands. Material looks and feels pretty top notch too. Cord is swivel, so no tangling, and it’s smooth rubber, not crappy stiff plastic like I tend to see. I really like this brush and I’m excited to take it along with me on trips too!

text:
I moved from wet blade shaving to electrics 8 years ago now. Shaving against the grain with a blade makes a real mess of my face and shaving only with the grain doesn't give me a brilliant result. I'd figured that technolgy marches on and that electrics would be better than they were when I'd first started shaving and I was right. I was pretty happy with the remington that I bought, but after a year or so I saw a Braun activator 8585 at half price in a local store and as at the time it was close to the top of the range, I bought it. That was a revelation to me. It shaved even better and the cleaning station left it refreshed again and again. 7 years later, the battery isn't holding charge and so I looked again. I was amazed to find 'shaving forums' on the web! You guys are nuts ;) but thanks for all your craziness and for sharing the tales of your hunts for the ultimate shave!

A lot of these shaving enthusiasts were raving about the new Panasonic Arc 4 Nano wet/dry and many thought that the cleaning station version just isn't necessary as this one can be cleaned easily with liquid soap under the tap (fawcet?)(yes, I'm english). So I bought this model (8423A) and it arrived today..... Ok you want to know what it's like, so I'll tell you,,,,

- It looks great!
- It charged in about 40 mins
- It shaved off 3 days of beard in about 7 mins (I was being careful bearing in mind its a new type of shaver on my skin).
- It's shaved me SO close that I'm absolutely Amazed.
- I have no irritation (the foils just don't seem to pick up my skin at all).
- I used it dry - can't wait to try it in the shower.
- It did miss a few particularly flat hairs on my neck, but I was able to get them with the trimmer and then shave over.
- I had a go at the cleaning routine - it's not difficult.

Technology continues to march on!

Whether you go for this one, or the cleaning station version, I'm sure that you will be delighted. This shaver is FANTASTIC!

title: The best I've had yet
text:
I've been using electric shavers of one form or another for over fifty years, and this one I rate as the best yet.

First it's one of the most comfortable. I can comfortably shave the back of my neck with this shaver where others irritated. Second, it's by far the fastest shaver yet, plus it gets any long hairs in its path. I attribute at least part of its speed to the third row of cutters which sets this one apart from many others. Third, it works fine wet, lotion or water, or dry. I'm using up some of the lotion cartridges from a previous Norelco dispensing shaver and it works very smoothly with them. Fourth, it went well over a month on the initial charge. Fifth, the built in trimmer is effective and convenient as opposed to some trimmers I've had that had to be attached in place of the shaving head. And finally it's easy to clean and packs light and compact for traveling.

The battery level meter is nice for checking when the charge is full. When the battery does finally give up and you're in the middle of a shave the charging cord can be used directly into the shaver to finish, then when ready for charging it can be connected to the charging stand for a regular charge. Charging is done relatively fast also, in roughly about an hour or so it's full and ready to go another month or longer.

There's often the argument between basic types of shavers, foil or rotary being two of the subjects. I recently tried one of the newer and recommended foil shavers and it's now on the shelf. Foil shavers for me miss too much, long hairs for sure, but they are not as effective on the regular stubble for me as a rotary shaver. That would be bad enough but my experience with foil shavers was if you missed a place in the previous shave, you won't get it next time either even though you go over it. I often had to use the trimmers on foil shavers, even the best of them, for just regular shaving chores.

I've bought and used a lot of electric shavers, but I've never had one this good before of any brand.

title: Disappointed - went back to my T800
text:
I bought a T800 quite a few years ago when I found the Austrian-made unit on sale at the local Target store. It lasted very well, and I was somewhat disappointed when the battery eventually would no longer accept a charge, though it continued to work while plugged in.
After carefully looking into alternatives, I went with a T970 from Amazon.com, hoping for the same quality. Major letdown! This Chinese-made unit just is not up to the same standard as my T800. The charger is a seperate seperate and bulky transformer, instead of the simple cord of the T800. The T970 is larger, more awkward to hold and to use, and more fragile in every possible way. The vacuum, which was one of the initial attractions, works, but only marginally well, and the unit is unstable when laid down on a solid surface. If the mile-long charging cord is attached, expect to have to prop the unit against a wall to prevent it rolling over.
I spent $6.00 on a top-quality replacement cell for my T800 (shipping was $4.00, for a 700mA Sanyo AA), and after careful disassembly and reassembly, successfully replaced the ailing cell without breaking anything. Unbelievably, The T800 now outlasts the T970 two-fold.
I wish I'd stuck it out with the T800 in the first place.
.
Updated June 29, 2009.
After about two years of irregular use and the resulting regular complete self-discharges, the T970 stopped functioning even while plugged in, unless first given time to recharge. Initial time to start working after plugging in has increased to the point where it no longer works even being plugged in for 24 hours.

title: Razor came with a frown honed into it
text:
First razor came with a frown honed into the blade. I put the edge on a straight edge and I could see the frown. It was also not shave ready. I sent for a replacement. Other than this the razor was impeccable. I will update when I see how the next one comes.

Update: not sure about the positive reviews here. I have been honing for years. I finish on Japanese stones and get edges that wipe the hairs away with zero resistance. But I could not get a good edge on this blade. I had to use two layers of tape as the geometry was off. I got a decent bevel set but the blade just swarfs and swarfs on every stone. This tells me the steel isn’t hardened properly. Usually swarfing will stop when the steel is finished on the stone.
Although for a knife this is probably okay for ease of sharpening but a razor needs to be very fine grain and very hard in order to develop a keen edge that would probably chip on a knife.
I have honed stainless steel blades before and this blade although beautiful will not build a shave ready edge.

title: Nice wig!
text:
I purchased this wig in black for a Halloween costume for work. I was planning on dressing up as Mia Wallace from Pulp Fiction. I had purchased a five dollar black wig from Walmart and it looked awful and had to be returned!! I decided I would give this a go, but at this price I didn't expect much. Boy, was I wrong!

This wig is a great quality! The product picture is an accurate representation of the actual product. The hair looks real and doesn't scream "fake". It held almost it's perfect shape right out of the bag. Couple of shakes and it was fine. It came with a hair net which was nice. The hair on the wig is very thick.No thin spots like you would find on cheap Halloween wigs. The bangs were not too long on me (I read from other reviewers they were too long and needed to be trimmed). However, the front pieces meant to scoop under the chin just came straight out and were kind of funny looking. They could have been easily adjusted with a little trimming.

In the end I decided not to wear the costume. This was in no way the wigs fault. No matter how much makeup I put on I looked absolutely awful in jet black hair. I'm about as fair a complexion as you can get, so I looked almost sickly in this color. However, at this price I might by a wig or two for fun in different, more complimenting colors in the future.

title: Banana Cream Pie Scent
text:
When I first tried this Marshmallow Vanishing Crème in a sampler kit, I purchased five more kits and then a 1.5 ounce glass container of this product. Can I say it is addictive? Yes, I guess it does have a banana scent and the texture is similar to a banana cream pie topped with whipped cream.

To say this is decadent is an understatement. You will be very tempted to slather your entire body in a good helping of this cream. Fortunately, it goes a long way and absorbs extremely well. In fact, that is why they call it "vanishing" crème. The ingredient list is impressive and contains rose water, mango butter, beeswax, grapeseed oil, rosehip seed oil, Vitamin E, marshmallow extract, willowbark extract, calendula flower extract, and a heady fragrance.

Grapeseed oil is one of the most powerful antioxidants and is high in proanthocyanidins, a group of bioflavonoids that are superior because they are water soluble. This ingredient also prevents skin cell damage caused by pollution and sun exposure.

"Marsh Mallow" is actually a pink flowering herb found in marshes and damp meadows. It has been used for centuries as a food and a medicine. The leaves and roots secrete an emollient fluid with healing properties for inflamed skin. In the past, people boiled the roots in wine to make a cough remedy.

I found this luscious creamy dreamy product to be healing for the body and mind. Not only will you feel comforted by nature, your skin will be baby soft and this product can be used for all-over body healing. The silver lid and glass jar have an unusually cute appeal. If you love this product, you might want to try the Pore-refining mask, Evening Primrose Overnight Crème and the very unique parsley blemish stick. To take luxury to the next level, try the Shea Butter Decollete Crème on your feet, hands or all over your entire body. What an amazing line of products. They heal, protect and soothe your mind.

I'm still trying all the Burt's Bees products, and love how these products make me feel. They add a level of protection to your skin care routine and the clay mask I recently tried cleaned my pores like a dream.

~The Rebecca Review
A Total Burt Bees Fan Until the End of Time

title: Does not feel like it can straighten hair at the roots but love the low heating temp.
text:
I have tried a number of these brushes. What I like about this one is that it goes down to 80C (176F). It was so cool that I was not sure it was on. I have fine hair, high porosity that is 5 months post-straightening relaxer. And, I find that light heat with a silicone-based glosser helps to gently close the cuticle and to keep my roots from tangling. What I don’t like is that this brush design does not have the round guiding bristles around the edges that help to pull your hair into the hearing plate. So, it feels like you are brushing your hair with your elbow and that it is not penetrating to the roots. You have to grip the hair with your other hand so it feels like you are only getting the shaft of your hair. So, the brush is best for people with longer hair who do not have curly roots or those who need the super low heat setting as an option.

If you would like to be able to rake the brush over your roots to tame curls at 250 F and up, other bushes to consider are https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07FGV9NQG/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o01_s00?ie=UTF8&th=1 or https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B071HFQGJX/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1. Note - My glamfields brush malfunctioned after first use which is why I ended up trying this one, but I decided to give Glamfields another chance because it is great when it works - never had results like that before. The BuTure mini is like the Glamfields brush but smaller. Both feel better (more like a real brushZ) than this one.

title: Close to Perfect
text:
Quite a while back my Remington Microscreen needed the screen replaced, and for a few dollars more than the cost of the screen I bought Norelco's bottom-end cordless. It was under-powered, seemed like it was always at the end of the 30-minute shave time, and didn't cut well at all. All of the people I know who use a Norelco love them, and said that in Summer you won't get the razor burn on your neck you get with a screen razor, so I bought the 8894XL.
The shave is good, and when set to the softest setting the heads easily hug your face. (A firmer setting caused some razor burn, noticeable in hot weather only.) It's amazingly quite and powerful, shaves quickly, and cleans up easily. It doesn't shave as close as the Microscreen, nor as well my dad's corded Norelco of 15 years, which he almost never changes blades on. I have naturally wavy and very thick hair, which it misses occasionally, but is nothing to complain about. A quick shave only takes 3 minutes; a detailed shave takes 7. It takes some time to trim around high sideburns accurately and the area under the nose, and is useless for trimming extra eyebrow hair, all of which the screen razor does well.
As far as features go, they're great. It really does charge in an hour and last 100 minutes. I let mine go past the 0 minutes left warning the first few charges until the motor slowed regularly while shaving and then recharged it. (It automatically turns off when the motor can't stay close to normal speed.--recharge before this.) It lasts about 170 minutes, and the readout gets closer to the actual run time each charge cycle. Once you set the firmness to what you want it doesn't need to be adjusted again. The pop-up trimmer could be better, and is kind of like a plastic knife that's hard to cut yourself or anything else with, and doesn't bog the motor. The clear LED cover scratches amazingly easily, so you'll want to keep the razor in the thin bag when not in use. The cleaning indicator is accurate, and rinsing under hot water, blowing the water out of the inside, and drying the outside with a towel is quick and easy. Just keep the trimmer extended until the razor air-dries completely. I haven't heard any complaints about the battery other than online, so it may be the problem is fixed in the newer razors.
In summary, it's a fun razor that won't wake the family early mornings while giving you a quick shave. There's no razor burn when the firmness is set correctly, but it also won't shave as close as a blade or screen razor. There's no guessing on how long the battery will last, which is at least 100 minutes.
