title: The razor does what it was designed to do
text:
Having used the disposable razors now for 25 plus years i decided to try an electric razor again, given the fact your considered a terrorist if you have shaving cream cans in your luggage while traveling, the electric razor seemed like a viable solution. After much reviewing i decided to go with the 9160xl at christmas, it was almost march before i recharged it, and after a few days of use, i was used to how it works, its much faster to complete a shave, trim my mustache and gote, and off i go with no worries of water on my shirt, or shaving cream to wipe off. You can also shave while walking around as your not tied to the sink and running water to clear off the razor. The key to any battery operated device is to properly charge it when you first place it on the bathroom sink. And do not return it to the charger until the shaver shows low battery, that way you keep the battery life good. And yes its quiet. Does not sound like a small airplane nor does it make a high pitched whinning noise. Comments about not having power or cutting of skin are ridiculous, i have never had a problem, all i do is clean it out each use, and rinse the head out when the razor indicates it wants a water cleaning. Simple as that, follow the instructions, and youll be fine. Remember the key to the battery as that is the life of the razor, same rules apply to your cell phone.
Good luck.

title: easy for sensitive teeth
text:
GLO Science Teeth Whitening Pen 35 Aplications, Safe and Efective, No Sensitivity, Easy to Use Dentist Invented Whitening Treatment, Travel-Friendly

Are my teeth whiter? Yes. It's not so white that anyone will see me and be like 'wow your teeth are so white!' but it is whiter and I notice it, which I prefer. I have very sensitive teeth and almost no enamel. The pen is a click pen, and you have click quite a lot to get it started. I thought mine was faulty at first, and the clicker even got stuck half way down but I smacked it and it popped back and I kept clicking. The silicone tip has little bristles and it does a good job of coming off on your teeth - I was worried the gel wouldn't grip onto my teeth and would slide, but it didn't. It does have a cinnamon taste, and it does dry in 30 seconds, it was easy enough to smile for 30 seconds and it was on there. Truly I forgot about it after that (don't eat or drink for 30 min if you can). Are my teeth whiter? I couldn't tell after 1 use, but after two, I also couldn't tell... BUT I took a before and after photo (which I'll save you from because my lips look awful right now) and my teeth are definitely visibly whiter! I'm happy with this, it's easy to put on, doesn't make my teeth sensitive, works for whitening, dries quickly, and you don't even have to spit it out.

title: An Honest Review
text:
My friend introduced me to epilating about 5 years ago. She had a double headed one from Spain it was amazing you could barely feel a thing. I searched for one similar everywhere and did some research that said the 40 dollar epilators do just as good as the more expensive ones. So I settled and bought a 40 dollar one, it did the job yes and I got use to how it worked (I usually waxed though since the epilator never removed every thing) Well it died about 4 months ago after, I decided that I wanted an epilator that would last and actually get the job done.

I went back to researching, I read so many reviews and many of you probably have and will. It is from my experience it depends on the person and the day that makes the review (I am having normal day.)

I decided in the to buy the Braun 7281 and crossed my fingers. Since I had grown use to my last epilator I was extremely surprised that this one felt so much better and barely noticed any pain; as well as I don't have to wax anymore saving so much more money now by spending more on the better epilator. But I decided I would give myself about 6 weeks and see how it did pain wise. It didn't feel the worst but it did sting for a few minutes and then I got use to it again. I must say that it still didn't hurt as bad as the 40 dollar one did and it still did just as good as a wax would. (Any epilator is going to sting if you haven't waxed or epilated in a 6 weeks +, I recommend waxing if you have sensitive skin before you jump back into epilating.) In the end I would even say this one is equal if not better then one my friend had and would recommend it to anybody. Added bonus is that it comes with many different tops as well as an electric razor.

If you are still on the fence about buying this one verses the 40 dollar one you have also been looking at. Buy the 40 dollar one first and in a few months when it dies, come back and buy this one. But if you want to save yourself time and money then make the jump and buy the Braun 7281 you won't regret it.

Also if you aren't familiar with how to use and epilator read the instructions it doesn't work like a razor and if you use it like a razor it will hurt. I feel it is the only reason people would complain about this epilator.

text:
I replaced a different manufacturer's very old electric razor with the Arcitec 1050, and have been using it for about three weeks. My primary shaving method has been the razor blade, supplemented by the electric for a fast shave now and then. I am so satisfied with the new Norelco that it has become my primary shaver. It delivers results virtually as close as a blade, and sometimes I think it is just as good. I don't feel that I need to use a blade to get a close shave any more, and I'm really amazed by the results. I didn't think that an electric could ever come this close to a blade. I guess that the technology has improved over the last twenty years, like everything else!

The shaver is not perfect, but the disadvantages are minor in my opinion. It does produce hair shavings, so I just shave over the sink. I don't mind cleaning up a little. The trimmer is quite small, but it does work well enough to clean the sideburns with an up and down motion. I have found that the shave is quite comfortable if you don't overdo it - just shave until you are clean, and use an after-shave cream to avoid minor irritation. I would prefer being able to leave the plug in the shaver, rather than remove it right after the charge is complete. It's a small inconvenience for such a great shave. And it is more economical than blades in the long run.

text:
It was tough to decide whether or not to give this product one or two stars, but I gave it two because it doesn't completely suck, it's just not as good as other razors that aren't as expensive The manufacturer recommends waiting 21 days before deciding to keep this product or send it back. I would also give the same recommendation to people who are looking at purchasing this. I bought it because I needed to replace my old razor. My old Remington titanium R9710 was a good razor but it ripped the hair out of my neck area and left me with very irritated skin. The thing about my old razor is that it had floating heads and it handled long hairs pretty well if I was lazy and didn't shave. This new Arcitec worked very well when I first got it but I really wanted to try it out and only had stubble on my face at the time. It worked very well with short hairs and left me with no irritated skin on my neck.

Well I wanted to see what it would act like if I let my hair grow a little and it did not perform like I thought it would. It took a long time to shave and I had to go over the area multiple times in multiple directions and with different pressures just to get a few long hairs. This new head style has really been a downgrade because when you apply pressure, the heads seem to pull away from your face on the outside part of it and it makes it harder to shave. It was either that or the fact that it doesn't have a hair collection area. It fills up with hair rather quickly so maybe that has an impact on how well it shaves. Cleaning the unit was very simple but I think I would have the cleaning system of one of the speed XL models over this. You have to pop open three separate chambers rather than flip the whole head up to clean each blade. A nice feature of this razor is the tube trimmer. You can take the razor head right off and pop out the trimmer. There really isn't much else to say about the trimmer other than I thought it worked great.

Overall, this is a very nice looking razor, but the functionality of the razor itself is pretty bad. It does come with a nice travel case and charging stand as well. The travel case is made of hard plastic and does not have room for the charger, but it does have the capability to charge the razor, so you do not need to bring along the charging stand. If you want to try this product I would say go for it because Norelco has such a generous return policy and maybe you will like it better than I did. If you think you like the functions of this razor but really aren't sure about it, I would not recommend it because it doesn't work like I think a razor should (it takes a long time to shave and it doesn't work well on longer hairs). It looks nice and has nice features, but I think its functionality isn't worth the high price tag.

text:
I am always on the lookout for really nice simple skin care. Let's take a look at this ampule.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a clear solution that comes out with an eye dropper.

HOW TO USE
The idea is that you use a toner on your CLEAN face, apply this to the face and neck and chest, and then follow up with a moisturizer.

WHAT DOES IT PROMISE TO DO?
This promises to lighted dark spots, and add firmness, glow, and hydration.

DOES IT DO WHAT IT SAYS?
I used this with another Korean toner which is pretty simple, and also the BE PLAIN Aqua moisturizer. When used, this did not seem to moisturize that much on its own, and for brightness and glow, I would say not over WOW factor after using for a month.

DID SKIN LOOK FIRMER?
I guess you could say my skin looked a bit firmer, but nothing so dramatic that people said, "WOW, WHAT ARE YOU USING ON YOUR FACE?"

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a scent free, easy to use serum for the face. It works well with moisturizer, is simple, scent free, and gives a moderate amount of what it says it will do. It is not remarkable, but it is not terrible either.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. This is decent, but not my favorite product at this point.

title: Great for curly hair
text:
I've been using Eufora products for maybe 10 years or more now? I love all of the products I have used. I have naturally curly hair which can be prone to being frizzy or dry, and these products really help. Some I use regularly and others on occasion. The scent on this stuff is amazing.

In fact one of the reasons I got so hooked on trying this stuff was because my hair dresser uses them along with many other products and I was always going around smelling how good she smelled and wondering what perfum she was wearing. However this is the type of scent that doesn't interfere with regular perfumes.

It reminds me of just a light natural scent you might get if you walked by a flower stand. Not overwhelming or sweet or musky but just light and fresh. I get a lot of comments on my hair smelling nice as well.

I use these products:

1. Moisture solution conditioner - regular conditioner
2. Moisture cleanse shampoo - regular shampoo
3. Hydration leave in conditioner - leave-in conditioner
4. Urgent Repair - on occasion as special treatment
5. Beautifying serum - to tame frizz and dead ends daily
6. Sculpture Styling Glaze - when I need some hold on occasion
7. Illuminate Shine Mist - to finish off a look with a light gloss
8. Fortifi Strength Spray - daily to enhance strength of hair
9. Pure Polish Finishing Drops - Works the same as the beautifying serum, except I was say for situations when you have especially course, curly or dry hair. Beautifying serum is a little lighter.
10. Curl 'N Defining Solution - when I need some hold on occasion
11. Curl Revitalizer and Spray - when I don't have time to wash my hair and just want to plump up and freshen the scent of my curls
12. Smooth 'N Straightening Balm - on the occasions when I want to straighten my hair
13. Fixation Styling Wax - Tame the baby hairs around the face, the little fly aways with this

text: ***  Just received the Limited Edition "Sugar Cookie" in the mail today.  My 21-month-old daughter is already asking for a bath while yelling "yummy" -- yes, it smells great! *****  I first tried Sweet Baby Organics Shampoo & Wash in Coconut Baby for my daughter last fall when she was 10 months old.  I liked the scent right away, but I was also impressed with the fact that it rinsed so clean.  I have tried other natural and organic baby washes with a coconut base, and they seemed to leave a "film" on my baby -- I liked that this formula was rich, and thick, without being sticky.  It's true that the foaming is minimal when comparing Sweet Baby Organics to washes with chemical lathering agents (such as SLS) but I found the lather from the coconut base to be "just right" without being bubbly.  We live in Kenya, so when I buy on Amazon I have to wait for my family to send me a box in the mail, or for someone to come over to visit (last fall I brought a supply of it back in my luggage).  My next package arrives in April, and this time we are trying the Vanilla Baby scent. The shampoo is NOT tear-free, but again, that is because of the lack of numbing chemicals in it's formulation -- I simply hold one hand over my daughter's forehead, and rinse her hair with a cup of clean water in my other hand.  One other fact to note is that a little goes a long way.  At first I was concerned that there were only 8oz bottles available, but even at 15 months old, a dime-sized amount cleans my daughter's entire head and body (though I have to admit that being a blondie, she doesn't have a whole lot of hair yet).

title: High-Quality Synthetic Hair Extension! Will Buy Again!
text:
I was immediately enchanted with this hairpiece from the second I tried it on. I've tried wearing it a few days in a row now, and I'm not tired of it yet. First, I'll start by saying that I ordered it as an add-on item in "dark blue to peacock green." With Prime, it only took two days to get to my house; very fast and convenient shipping, and the hairpiece was encased in a clear plastic bag; I threw that away, as I keep my extensions in a silk hair case. This hairpiece is actually pretty high quality for synthetic, eccentric hair, so I would suggest something like that to keep it safe and untangled when you're not wearing it.

In my opinion, the product images do not really do this hairpiece justice. I can't say anything for other colors yet, but the dark blue to peacock green is pretty true to the product images, with sapphire blue roots and aqua-blue tips (although I will say the hairpiece I received is not half-and-half blue and green like the picture; mine is like an ombre gradient, approximately 2/3 blue and 1/3 aqua tips).

Many of the reviews here also have mixed comments on the thickness of the hairpiece; maybe the people who say it is "thin" are comparing it to their own natural hair? I will say that this piece is very thick for a single-weft hair extension. A weft is like a curtain of hair with a seam holding it all together at the top. I wear extensions almost every day after a butchered haircut took 12 inches of my hair. Authentic human hair extensions come in wefts of varying widths, usually one clip wide or four clips wide, and the hair is very thin because the wefts are meant to be layered on in sections, like natural hair. This blue hair extension is 5 clips wide--wide enough to fasten on your head from ear to ear. Because of my experiences with authentic human hair extensions, I was expecting this blue piece to be thin and underwhelming, but I was wrong and am very happy about that.

I also have an asymmetrical haircut that is close-cropped on one side, so this extension is actually too wide for me to wear across my nape (as the model does in the product image), but I am still able to use it. I curve it to clip from my left nape to above my right ear and it suits my needs and still looks real, despite its unusual color.

Since there is so much hair on a single weft, as other reviewers have stated, this hair extension is a bit heavy. That may take some getting used to, as improper clipping could cause some discomfort and irritation from pulling on the roots. However, once you get practice putting it in, you will learn the best way to clip it without any tugging or pulling of the hair.

It is synthetic material, and while I noticed that mine was shiny, it was not like "Barbie hair," as some reviewers said. I did not need to rub any baby powder in; I just wore it to work for a few hours a day and the shine eventually dulled to look a little less like synthetic material. I will try to add some photos to this page of what the extension looks like in my (straight black) hair. I also noticed that it became easily tangled after a few days of wear. This is not really a problem; I am afraid to brush it too often though, as it sheds (which is normal, but I want it to last).

Lastly, despite being synthetic material, I have tried straightening it on the high setting on my Conair flatiron with success. You can also use a razor or scissors to make any modifications to the style or length, if necessary.

Overall, I think you will be very satisfied with this product if you buy it. I liked it so much that I placed an order for dark pink/light pink and yellow/lime green. These were not add-on items, however, so I will be waiting until mid-August to September to receive these other hair extensions. Hopefully they will be as nice as the blue/peacock green, because I was not disappointed!

title: Roll on Wax Bar
text:
The wax warmer is very color pleasing and so are the bars of wax that go inside the warmer itself. It comes with two roll on wax bars, along with finishing wipes (just oil towel) and a pack of paper. The directions are very easy to read on how to use the wax warmer but the pack of papers is awful in the direction department. So many spelling/grammar errors - but the pictures are more explanatory then the actual words themselves.

It took about 5-8 minutes for the wax to melt and be at a good use of temperature. I would wait until MAX temperature and then wait a few more minutes for the wax to go on smoother. Then slap the paper on.

Now, you are wondering why 3 stars?

1. The time it takes to warm up - 1 Star
2. The materials that are given plus directions - 2 Star

If you are doing a spot on shave sure go ahead but to do your entire leg and not to mention BOTH of them, you will be sitting for a very long time. Its too time consuming and I am impatience. I would suggest to buy more papers if you are thinking about getting this. I do feel that it is a learning curve and that is ok, I will continue to learn how to do it.

It does work though, works decently well once the wax is at the perfect temperature. Oh its not painless, but it is tolerable if you have a high pain tolerance, but if you DO NOT, I would suggest waxing to not be your thing.

I tested these under a number of use cases and noted how long the blades remained effective (clean shave, non-nicking) for:
[benchmark: 4-5 good shaves per edge with Astra Platinum]
Dry shave (2/edge)
Dry shave after a hot towel (2-3/edge)
Wet shave - soap (2-3/edge)
Wet shave - cream (3/edge)
I personally prefer to dry shave after a hot towel in the interest of minimizing hassle on frequent camping trips. Worth noting, I have a medium-coarse beard and sensitive skin, so I prefer very sharp blades rather than medium-sharp like these. I'm not really impressed with the polymer coating - it doesn't glide as well as blades using other finish coats (and notes on the blade that you're not to wipe dry - likely as it'll only accelerate roughening the polymer coat to to the skip-and-nick stage).

I just finished nursing my child and wanted to take care of myself starting with skincare. I had acnes back in highschool. I tried multiple laser treatments and it did very little to clear up my acnes scars. Plus one laser treatment cost atleast $500 and they quoted that I would need about 10 sessions to clear up my skin. That would be $5,000! So I did 3 laser sessions which had very little result and tried to do home treatment such as salicylic peel, retin a and dermaroller.
I strongly advise not to use salicylic or other peels at home as I burnt my skin and have permanent scar from it.

Retin a is good that it brighten up my skin but did little for my acnes scar or shrink pores. I tried dermaroller with vitamin c & hyaluronic serum but it really did nothing for my skin.

I read a skincare article that human stem cell containing EFG could reduce pore size & acnes scars. As I have tried many methods before, I was hesitant to purchase another item but just gave it another last try.
I searched and found Anterogen human stem cell skin pack. I read all the reviews and googled more information about stem cell skincare. There are two stem cell that is in the market. One is plant based( apple stem cell) vs human stem cell. You can google this yourself but all the articles state that plant based stem cell does nothing for your skin. It has to be human stem cell! So I purchased this brand as it had the highest amount of human stem cell.

I sanitized my dermaroller (1mm) in boiling hot water for 5 mins. I washed & dry my face then apply Anterogen white silk timeless machine serum on my skin. Then roll dermaroller roller over my face applying more serum on punched skin. Then finished it with this human stem cell mask. I left it on my skin for 30 mins. I also squeezed left over serum from mask on a facial bowl and tapped it on my skin and left.

The next morning, omg my pores &acnes scar finally looked smaller!! I literally teared up as I have found something that could help my skin look better. I am planning to do dermaroller every 2 weeks using Anterogen human stem cell serum with mask. Remember, don't over do it as skin needs downtime to recover and produce new collagen to fill up pores, scars or wrinkles.

title: Looks great, mediocre shave
text:
This was kind of a last ditch effort to find a more comfortable shaving experience. I've tried several electrics with the hope of finding a more comfortable shave since I have sensative skin and am prone to razor burn. At the end of the day, I've found frequently replacing the Mach3 blades is the best I can do. It gauls me to keep spending on money on something I have to toss, but it's better than the alternatives to date.

The Norelco Architec 1090 looks great and shaves better on the neck than the foil shavers I've tried including the Panasonic Nano and Braun Activator. However, it still misses a critical area in the middle cheek just along where a goatee would start to back about 1.5 inches from there. The hair in that part of my face tends to lay down. The Braun seemed to get that area OK, but did not do well in the neck area.

When I push harder to get those hard to get whiskers, I end up with road rash and sporadic ingrown whiskers. This and other electric razors may work with people who have different types of beards or face shapes, but I've yet to find an electric that works for my whole beard.

In my opinion, a $250 razor ought to do the job quite comfortably. I think there are better ways to use the funds, like on three years worth of blades and shaving cream.

title: Great coverage - a little goes a long way. Gentle for sensitive skin
text:
I might not be terribly picky when it comes to face makeup, but my skin sure is. I've been recently battling with a case of perioral dermatitis on one side of my cheek that was caused by a concealer I've been using by a well-known brand. It looked horrible and red. I wanted desperately to cover it, but every time I used the concealer it made it worse! I said 'enough' with this vicious cycle and aimed to buy a mineral powder makeup that potentially did not have any of the ingredients in it that my body was reacting to. I have had bad experiences with mineral makeup in the past due to bismuth oxychloride (my face was raw and hurting after putting it on!). IQ looked like it would fit the bill as it says it is a natural makeup with only mineral oxides and nothing potentially irritating. I know that an ingredient is always irritating to somebody out there, but I took the chance.

Two days after using it, I can say that my skin tolerates it well, even when I don't wash it off at night. It also covers great for a mineral makeup. The concealer is a little darker than my skin tone, but it works out well as it's kinda a midde-ground between the red patches that are on there, and the foundation I put on on top of it. The 'fair' and 'fair 2' colors both work for my skin. And I LOVE LOVE LOVE the brushes it came with. SO many times a makeup set comes with a kabuki brush that I just can't use due to how sensitive my face is (the brush is too stiff and harsh to rub over my face). The brushes this set came with are petal-soft and there are no issues whatsoever with that.

Overall I would say that for the price I paid, it was well worth it and I am a happy customer. I would buy this brand again as it stands right now. I know two days isn't much to go by and I will update the review if I feel differently. But usually I can tell pretty soon how my skin will react to something and it's not hating this. That's a big deal for me.

title: Not bad!
text:
I've always been wary of electric razors, but I have to say this one works pretty well for me. It took no time for my face to get "used to" this razor (in the past it was hell to try to get through a couple of weeks with other kinds). The first day I used it I got a nice, close shave with no irritation.

A single charge lasts me a couple of weeks, so even though I've brought the charger with me when traveling I've never had to use it (I'll be leaving it home the next time). I haven't actually used the cleaning system yet, because you can run the entire razor under hot water and clean it out no problem. I just leave it on the counter to dry until I come home from work.

My only complaint would be that like most other people (and all other electric razors that I know about) it doesn't get all of those hard to get hairs on my neck without several passes, and the trimmer doesn't get close enough to my sideburns. Not a problem though, I just keep a disposable razor in the shower and touch up---just a few seconds with no lather so not a big deal.

I would recommend this product to anyone looking to make the switch.

text:
This set of scrubby brushes with silicone points is a cheap but effective way at getting your scalp clean from all the products and dead skin that build up on it every day. Compared to the similar version that has hard plastic point, this style is much kinder to your skin while working just was effectively. The first time you use one of these to help wash your hair you will notice a difference in how much cleaner your scalp and hair feels. These little scrubbies are also fanatics for giving pets a bath because the points get down through their fur and help get their skin clean. They also help do a better job than just spraying water to get all the product out of your pet's fur while rinsing them off. I highly recommend using a hair catcher for your tub drain as these will also help your pet shedding process.

Besides washing hair, these also work well for head massages if you have a headache (help increase blood flow), massaging in and distributing any serums/oils/tinctures you may be applying to your scalp to heal with hair growth, relaxing and gentle back massage (us lotion or oil so the points move easily across skin), grooming your cat or dog, or giving a gentle hip and leg massage to your pup if they are older and have arthritis. Heck, you can even use one for planting seeds - gently pack the dirt a little, level it flat, then use one of these to create perfect holes to place seeds in. Kids can also use these to paint - dip in washable paint and make giant spirographs. Oooh, they also work to gently itch things like hives or an allergic rash when you can't use something sharp like fingernails, and these can be easily disinfected.

If you were to turn it inside out to use to keep your hair from getting wet, it would work fine for a bath but not for a shower. title: quiet and convenient
text:
This razor is my second norelco rotary, my first is a 5100 series about 20 years old. Compared to that, this razor is much cleaner, quieter, and more comfortable. The new razor doesn't *sound* like it turns the blades as fast or as powerfully as my corded dinosaur, but it seems to me that it cuts more effectively, which is what I hoped for.

Cleaning this new razor is a breeze - just a quick rinse under hot tap water and I'm done. Having cleaned it this way, I can't imagine paying for the extra cleaning station and chemicals - I note with some interest that the printed user instructions and website FAQ also recommend the hot tap water cleaning method...

Comparing my shave to a triple-blade disposable system I use, the electric doesn't cut quite as close - I can't tell immediately after shaving (my face feels smoothly shaved in either case), but I notice stubble somewhat earlier with the electric razor.

I shave about once a day - maybe 5-10 minutes or so. So far, the battery life is about a month as advertised. Very convenient indeed.

title: This Stuff is AMAZING!
text:
I’ve been dealing with a skin rash for a little over a month. I had tried bag balm (which would typically work for rashes) to no avail and stumbled across some information on social media about colloidal silver. I was intrigued and figured I’d try it. Before purchasing this I had heard about “nano-Silver” and how it was supposed to be more effective than colloidal silver because it was eon charged (or something like that) so I went with some of that, in liquid form. I was ingesting it and spraying it on my skin. It did absolutely nothing. As a matter of fact, it dried the rash out and made it look more pronounce than it already had.

Then I searched to see if they had a moisturizer with silver in it. I was determined for this stuff to work. That’s when I saw the Silver Miracles soap and cream. I bought both. I received the soap first and began using it. I noticed a difference in a little under a week. Then the cream came. No joke, after TWO days of using it (morning and night), the rash was GONE. Completely.

I recomm nd this stuff to anyone. If you’re thinking about it but you aren’t sure, just go for it. I’m not gaining anything by writing this review so I have no reason to lie. I’m only writing it because I’m excited about it. I’ve had that rash for over a month and it’s completely gone after using this for two days. Silver Miracles Colloidal Silver is awesome and I will be using it exclusively from this point forward.

On a side note, don’t bother with “nano” silver, especially the liquid. Not for external use at least. It did nothing.

text:
This serum goes on nice and lightly without leaving a sticky or oily feeling residue, which is an issue I've had with other serums I've tried. It's a thick liquid that's easy to apply with the included dropper, and it dries quickly to a clean-feeling finish.

It's a little too early to make any statements on wrinkle reduction since I just started using this serum about a week ago, but it does seem to have calmed down my skin. I haven't noticed any new zits or blemishes on my face, when before I would usually get one every other day or so. I think the retinol is helping my skin cells to refresh themselves more quickly, preventing bacteria from being able to take hold. The hyaluronic acid component of the serum also seems to be helping with my complexion-- I'm noticing less flaky dry areas around my eyebrows and chin that I used to have problems with, especially in dry weather and winter conditions. My face overall seems to be more moisturized and even in tone, as well as less oily along my T-zone. My pores also seem to be less prominent and I've been able to get away with less makeup on my skin during the day.

Overall, I'm very satisfied! This product seems to do the job of keeping my facial skin and complexion balanced and healthy.

title: Great Price, Some Decent Ingredients, but Some Bad Ingredients as Well
text:
I really like products that contain Retinol. They work really well on my oily, acne prone skin. They also work great for combatting fine lines and wrinkles in between Botox injections. Yes, I do like my Botox twice a year.

I like the jar dispenser. It keeps things nice and clean and sanitary and I can control how much product I dispense. This 1.7 oz jar will last a very long time.

I use it at night only for fear of drying my face out, but on rare occasion I have used it in the am and it is a nice cream that glides on smoothly, quickly absorbs and doesn't leave my skin feeling greasy. I am a stickler for that. I won't use a product that makes my face feel greasy, sticky, or tacky.

The amount of Retinol is consistent with that on the market. It also contains Vit B5 and E which are great for repairing damage to the skin and Green Tea.

What I don't like about this product is that while it is 71% organic, it contains Cetyl Alcohol (can dry out the face), Xanthan Gum (a filler) and Phenoxyethanol, which is a very controversial ingredient. It is said to disrupt hormone imbalance amongst other issues. This is very important to me because I am a Breast Cancer Survivor. While I tested negative for hormone receptors and hormone driven cancer, I still proceed with caution. My ob won't even put me on Birth Control because of the hormones. So for me, the ingredients would make me steer away from this product in the future.

text:
So I wear and review a lot of wigs and I have started breaking the review down into sections that I think will be helpful.

Color - The color is very similar to the person pictured wearing it in the examples but not the one that is on the mannequin look. This wig is very light silver / grey. It is not that fake, overly shiny texture, and is the same solid color throughout.

Styling- This has an adjustable headband and is fairly easy to fit and style. As it is a costume wig you have to be careful if you are looking to pull it back for anything as the amount of hair in the wig is really designed more for it to be worn as is (which is normal for this kind of price point)

Comfort - This wig is light and comfortable and there is plenty of airflow. This was a little weird around my ears (because my head is a little smaller) but nothing too difficult. This would be suitable to wear all day although I personally wouldn't.

Overall - I really liked it but for what it was - a costume wig. If you are looking for something for a Halloween type look this is perfect.Great for pictures and videos but not one I would probably wear out (other than possibly to a costume party if it completed the look) just because I have others that look way more realistic.

title: Fit 80D well, but potentially beware of static/dust attraction
text:
I bought this for a new (refurb) 80D that I just got a little while ago. That 80D was factory refurbed and it, and the sensor, was very clean when I got. I put this case on (a black one) the camera almost the same day that I got the camera, and I actually didn't have much time to use it over the next couple of weeks, but then, one day I was out trying to do some shooting of planes and BIF. When I looked at the images, I noticed a large piece of dust on the image (which turned out to be on the sensor). Looking back at some test images I made when I first got the camera, they were clean. Anyway, so I used a blower and was able to get rid of the large dust, but then I did a white wall shot to check the sensor and I was SHOCKED that there was a lot of dust on the sensor. What was weird is most of the dust looked like it was around the perimeter of the sensor. I used a sensor dust brush and that got rid of some of the dust, but I eventually had to send the camera to the Canon service center to get it cleaned off.

To be clear/honest, I am not 100% sure about this, but I was trying to figure out how that happened and I am guessing/theorizing that maybe the case, which is rubber, might have been attracting dust. The case is very close around the base of the lens mount, so I am thinking that, maybe, there was dust attracted around the lens mount, and when I unmounted the lens (which I did once or twice and always with the camera pointed downward), some dust would get onto the sensor.

Mind you, I think this case does provide some protection for the body, so that part is ok.

title: Why argue with centuries of dental success?
text:
I really don't understand people who think the flavor is so heinous. It's a little strange, but nothing that's going to make you gag. I also wouldn't say that it tastes are smells like synthetic chemicals. These come pretty fresh sealed inside the packages and are at first really easy to peel and loosen the fibers. Once it dries out, you will need to employ the water-soaking method, which makes it simple enough. Just make sure it soaks for at least an hour for very easy handling. I've been using the same stick for months. It usually takes about a week or two for the end to get ratty enough to cut and start over again. I wouldn't say this stick eliminates flossing. It depends on the way your teeth are situated. I have some problem spots that I absolutely need to use floss for. That being said, I've noticed a significant reduction of plaque that is removed with a floss after brushing with a miswak (vs. after brushing with a good conventional toothbrush or even a sonicare toothbrush). In my personal experience, a miswak works better than a Sonicare. However, if you like the convenience of the Sonicare, stick to that. It depends on each person's habits and personality. You can damage your enamel with a Sonicare, so please be careful and follow the instructions carefully. You really don't have a problem with hurting gums or the enamel with a miswak. It is also the perfect travel toothbrush.

Pros: Lasts a long time, is completely natural, no need for toothpaste, minimal flossing, travels easily, gentle on teeth and gums while getting into nooks and crannies better than a traditional western brush, dental study shows improvement of gingivitis with regular use of miswak.

Cons: Awkward handling for back of teeth, must peel to get a new layer, some people don't like the taste, not easy for children to use.

title: The best value in the Sonicare line
text:
With Amazon now selling this directly for < $20 this is the absolute best value in the entire Sonicare line. You get the same drive, the same brush head compatibility, 2 min timer and the ability to use your own rechargeable batteries. 5 years ago I purchased a Sonicare Elite 7300; the internal NiCad battery eventually died and the unit is not designed to swap out the battery. I tried, but ended up damaging the rubber molding and had a lot of difficulty finding a comparable battery that didn't require paying a high shipping cost. I eventually purchased the E3000 on a whim at a retail store for nearly twice what it sells for on Amazon nowadays and started using the newer low self discharge NiMH batteries. I get about a month of usage before I have to charge the batteries. And when the batteries finally start losing their capacity -- they haven't yet in 2 years -- I don't have to worry about performing major surgery on my toothbrush.

I'm not sure I understand the water seepage/contacts/failure issues. I own 2 E3000s now, one for travel and one for home, and have used them both for 2+ years now. Neither have failed. I take care not to rinse the base of the unit under running water and I don't leave it sitting in a pool of water or anything. I definitely see the potential for failure as nothing but a plastic cap and a rubber gasket protect the AA batteries from potential moisture, but I think standard, common sense can prevail here. Let me stress -- I do not baby this thing. I use it daily in a bathroom that gets very humid during showers and summer weather (no exhaust fan and no central air conditioning). I clean it every usage under running water and I don't dry it off afterwards. I also have done the same types of things with 2 different E3000 units and have used them for over 2 years now and they have worked perfectly from day one.

Highly recommended. I would actually feel comfortable recommending this over a higher-end Sonicare that was discounted to be within a similar price range as this unit. Being able to use your own rechargeable batteries is simply way too powerful of a feature since that seems to be the limiting factor in keeping this brushes for the long haul.

When I was removing the nail polish, I had oily residue on my hands but nothing gross or greasy feeling, it just felt like I had argan oil or cuticle oil on my fingers. This was exceptionally surprising to me because we all know Acetone not only dries our your finger bed, but also your nail bed. This product, due to that oily-ish consistency that it has going on, it doesn't dry out your nails, I would even go so far as to say that it hydrates your nails simultaneously, AND it was so easy to wash off.

I promise that you will NOT be disappointed. In fact, I would suggest that this brand go and start putting this in salons to use for polish changes, beauty supply stores, walmart, everywhere! If you don't wear fake nails and use only polish, you need to buy this and never let anyone use acetone on your fingers again. Maybe they'll eventually come up with their version to take off gel/acrylic nails but better and healthier than acetone! I'm still seriously so blown away from this product, and while this product was sent to me for review, this is 10 million% my honest opinion. title: Little to No Damage Easy Curls
text: I absolutely love hair curl & wave forms. I have used these before but the wave curl form set when I had longer hair. These curl forms are super simple and easy to use! It is important to take small enough sections, but large enough to be able to cover your entire head. Taking too large of sections can create a pulling out of the hair and scalp, so be very careful! This set is the perfect length for my medium to short, shoulder length hair... give or take a few inches depending on whether or not I had a recent trim or not. I usually shower in the morning, but these curl forms definitely work best if you shower at night then dry or air your hair first about 50-80% of the way before using the hook to pull your small-medium sections of hair through. This cuts down on the drying and setting time. I like to put these in my hair before bed then wear a silk hair cap over night. You could also do this after a morning shower and let them dry and set while you do things around the house, but this always tries my patience. You can also use a dryer cap to speed up the process if you do this during the day or your morning routine. These create the perfect little ringlet curls. I always use hair spray, let set for approximately 5 minutes,  then tassel and/or finger comb through my hair after for a more natural curl look. I highly recommend trying these curl formers if you would like to try a little to no damage heat option for your hair!

title: Reasons I wouldn't recommend this
text:
I'm not sure if this just wasn't product tested with the shower actually on or if my product is defective. "suction cup bottom grips to any floor." The suction cups are a great idea for a shower product, but do they work on this one? ABSOLUTELY NOT. I don't know whose idea it was, but I would like to see someone actually cup this thing in the shower, put some soap in there, turn the water on and use it without having to superglue it to the floor.

It absolutely does not stay in one place no matter how light you try to get your foot in there. And I don't know why the pumice stone is there at the heel because you're lucky if you even get your arch in before it starts sliding away. I literally almost fell and broke my ankle the first time I tried to use this because I went into it thinking the suction cups would work. So just be warned, you need something sturdy to hold on to while using this product.

Another problem is the over-the-foot plastic. Why plastic?? If i'm not water skating through the shower on this thing and actually get my foot in all the way, that plastic hits the top of your foot and it's painful. I get the whole car wash appeal it looks like they're going for but that plastic needs to be made out of a softer material.

Since i'm assuming the paying customers are the only product testers in this case, I found it easiest to use one foot to hold the product down by stepping on the pumice stone and one foot doing a combined up/down left/right motion inside the "foot wash" while holding onto the shower rod with both hands. This did crack my pumice stone after 2 uses but at least it wasn't my back.

So as far as likelihood I would recommend this to a friend to use for its intended purpose, I would have to take a hard pass.

text:
I recently picked up this face mask at my local CVS for $7. I applied the mask and waited 20+ minutes, following the direction. When the time came to remove the mask, it wouldn't peel off in pieces any larger than a dime. Eventually, I gave up on trying to pick/peel and just washed it off.

The second and last time I used this product, the mask peeled off nicely, but I quickly noticed that it had torn multiple small pieces of skin off of my upper cheek/just below my eyes. These areas stung to the touch (and still do, I'm writing this the day after).

Overall, I guess you get what you pay for. In this case, I spent $7 and in turn received a cheap, poor quality product. I would not recommend this product to anybody and would suggest that you spend your money on a product that will function as advertised (even if it means spending a few bucks more).

title: Moistens
text:
Cucumbers are supposed to be amazing for the skin. So, I wanted to give these a go.

Pro: - moisten. Very moist.
- mask doesn't rip or tear
- plastic backing for easier application
- gentle, pleasant aroma
- sinks quickly into skin after massaging at end

Cons: - thin
- hard to slide into place...and then doesn't fit quite right
- suggested wear time is 20-25 mins....longer than usual

These masks come individually packaged in robust and easy to open pouches. The mask has a sturdy, plastic backing, which is the only reason it can be unfolded and placed on without any trouble because these are thin. Surprisingly, they don't rip or tear easily, though. After taking off the backing, it takes a little maneuvering to get these to sit in place. Firstly, the thin material wanted to bunch and roll along the edges of the face, and the lack of thickness made it difficult to get to lay flat. Also, the eye holes aren't quite right. I, my son, and my daughter tried them (each with very different face sizes) and all of us had trouble with the eyes. When they were in position, The bridge of the nose wouldn't stay pressed against the skin, but kept lifting up. The suggested wear time is 20 to 25 minutes, which is longer than the 15 to 20 I normally see on masks. Removing the mask, however, is no problem, and there's a good amount of moisture left over to massage into the skin....which also works well

The masks are moistening and have a gentle, pleasant odor (although I can't really place it). These are refreshing and leave the skin shiny. If only they'd sit better, I'd enjoy them more.

The 16% gel I bought from my dentist 8 years ago took about 6 weeks of everyday overnight use to change very yellow teeth (53 years of living and lots of tea) to white. I could see the change on a weekly basis.
Since this stronger product by Watts gives no results in even 3 weeks on less stained teeth, I am very disappointed.

title: Works well. Be careful I thought the eyebrow razor was a shaper
text:
I got an electric Epilator awhile ago that I like a lot. It keeps you hair free for long periods of time and I've noticed the hair comes back thinner each time. I've used my electric Epilator everywhere but my eyebrows, for fear I might not have anyone I'm done. I saw this product and thought I'd give it a try to get the stray hairs and to do my eyebrows (hate wasting a Saturday morning to wax)

The directions on the back of the box are a bit vague. I was able to figure out how to maneuver the stainless steel coil and here's what I found.

I want to note at first glance I thought The free eyebrow raiser enclosed was an eyebrow brush to separate the hair. Thank God I have somewhat bushy eyebrows or they be gone 'd be gone! Now that I know how to use this razor I do really like it, I didn't want to knock off the star for my stupidity, it clearly states when I bought it it comes with an eyebrow razor. Just in case there is another woman tired coming home from work tired that wants to shape their eyebrows while cooking dinner, doing laundry and taking care of the kids .....there is a heads up '

I found by trial and error if you want to get the hairs between your eyebrows above your nose hold this horizontally and go side to side.

If you want to shape your eyebrow you can actually curve this below or above and gently move the coil around to get rid of strays.

If you have a single strand let's say on your chin you want to get I found that moving this down will grab that hair.

I was surprised at how much hair I took off with this thing

This does not hurt as much as the electric epilator does, I don't think the electric hurts that much either. When it gets to hear it hurts a little more than a wax and a lot less than a tattoo.

Once you get used to maneuvering this around it works great. It took me a couple days using this to be able to pinpoint to hear and I can now get it in about 20 seconds. It also does remove like here but it would take a long time to do.

This definitely works your wrist some, if you like the results I would say get an electric epilator and use this for your eyebrows and touchups. I have a little bit of carpal Tunnel, after about 15 minutes of twisting in moving this around it does get to my wrist a little bit, that being said I don't think this is meant for large area hair removal.

Hopefully my tips will save you some of the time I've spent experimenting with this. It's a neat little tool that I will definitely use. This may sound gross but I was actually able to even get a nose hair (if someone else is nervous to try it, I did, survived and like the results) lol

I did receive this product at a discount for my honest review. I thoroughly use any product before giving a review whether I get it for free at a discount or pay full price

title: Good for clarifying but questionable ingredients
text:
I have color treated hair that I've been dying for about 8 years now and I have to really maintain it to keep it healthy and looking smooth. I learned some time ago how much better my hair looks when I use Argan Oil treatments and would do them once a week or so to make my hair super soft and pretty. I started using shampoos and conditioners with Argan Oil when I saw how well my hair responded to it. Some brands left my hair feeling heavy and oily so I really wanted to find a good clarifying shampoo. I started with just a little bit so I could gauge how it would work for me but once I lathered it up in my hair I realized how much a little bit can cover. I don't need nearly as much as I do of most other brands. I washed it that night and followed it up with my regular conditioner, another Argan product. My hair felt really clean. I have a lot of hair and at the top I couldnt feel the heaviness and resistance I had been from over moisturizing. The smell was ok, I like something that is stronger and prettier, this one just kind of smelled like soap, and it faded quickly after It was dry. As long as my conditioner smells good I don't mind it too much but if you're planning to use it alone you might notice. I think it worked well for getting it clean without leaving it dry or feeling like straw. I don't feel like my hair is as soft as with most Argan Oil shampoos, at all, but I think it'll be a good one to use intermittently to clear the buildup from all of my oil rich products.

I was surprised and disappointed at the ingredients list when I looked. From a company called InstaNatural that boasts this as a holistic treatment I didn't expect to see so many chemicals. I would have preferred more familiar ingredients, and natural, obviously. Argan oil isn't even listed until the second to last ingredient. I like how it worked but I'm not sure how hard it would be on my hair if I used it regularly.

I did receive my shampoo at a promotional price for testing and evaluation purposes. I was not paid for my review and was asked only to provide whatever feedback I may have about the product, whether it be positive or negative. I welcome both positive or negative feedback as well. My review is solely based on my experience and honest opinions of this shampoo.

text:
Norelco consistently ups the ante by continually improving their products.

This is my third Norelco, (my second wet/dry shaver) and by far the best of the bunch.
I've had this shaver for about three years and have never regretted the purchase. It's light, easy to handle, holds a charge for a decent amount of time and provides a nice, comfortable close shave.

One beef I had with my old Norelcos was their inability to get in close under my nose. Not so with this model. It can get in close under my nose and tackle bothersome neck hairs.
Don't feel obligated to run out and purchase more Nivea,[[ASIN:B002GJTYDW Philips Norelco HS803/14 Nivea for Men Shaving Conditioner and Replacement Cartridge (Pack of 3)]] as you can get a terrific shave with a decent shaving cream. Plain old Edge gel works great.

You can spend a ton more dough on a different shaver, by why bother?
And of course, you must make sure to change the heads on a regular basis[[ASIN:B002GJU2YW Philips Norelco HS85 Nivea for Men Shaving Replacement Head]]. Norelco's are notoriously unforgiving if the heads needs replacement: You might as well shave yourself with a damn rock.

If you're a dyed-in-the-wool foil shaver dude and have decided to try out a Norelco, this would be a great model to check out. And just don't try it for a few days and decide it sucks; Be fair and give your beard a chance to get used to it.

title: Taming mustaches and planting trees!
text:
My husband has a ridiculously oversized, extremely thick and wiry handlebar mustache. He started growing it several years ago as sort of a joke / challenge and it somehow became his signature look and now he can never shave it off. He's tried lots of waxes to defy gravity and hold his hair in his desired shape. He really likes Death Grip and the old-fashioned Clubman soft wax that comes tinted in a tube.

This Tree-Topped Mustache Wax is solid in a little tin like the Death Grip, but it's slightly softer - soft enough you can dig some out of the tin and apply it just with the warmth of your hands without having to warm up the whole tin in hot water or with a blow dryer. But since it's a little softer instead of a rock-hard wax, it's also has a little less hold. I'd call it a medium-firm hold.

Absolutely love that it's simple, clean, and UNSCENTED! And that they're planting trees for each tin sold! And they even give you the recipe if you want to whip some up and refill your tin yourself. I absolutely will be ordering from this company again!

title: Fades, but very vibrant color
text:
This color is pretty good for the price. There are a few pros and cons to it that I will explain below, but overall I don't think I will buy it again.

Pro:
Comes with 2 containers which is enough color for any length hair
The ability to adjust the shade you want by adding conditioner to the color
A little bit goes a VERY long way
Price is very reasonable
When it fades, it fades all the way out so it doesn't look like some weird shade of orange when it starts to wash out
You don't need any heat to get the color to stick
It doesn't smell like anything

Cons:
Fades INCREDIBLY fast - I had it in for maybe a week or two before it washed all the way out
You have to use a ton of conditioner to create a light soft pink color - the size of a dime with about 2 cups of conditioner do the trick
It will dye everything it comes in contact with - use thick gloves
If you are diluting the color with conditioner, it will take some time to sit on your hair
If you are diluting the color, you'll never need both bottles - it would take 5 years to use all of it

I think overtone color conditioner is an easier system to use and the color stays longer.

text:
I love these! They puff up in liquid like little marshmallows, and are easy to peel apart to form the full mask. It works for my face size/shape just fine (a smidge small for men maybe). They appear to be high quality, and I love that they're individually wrapped! I throw these in my travel bags to use with my serums and lotions, and give them away for people interested. I've used these with blended aloe vera, gels, serums, hyaluronic acid, high moisture "lotions" and so much more.

I usually remove the packaging, drop the "tablet" into the well-mixed up liquid/gel concoction I chose that day, and wait for it to puff up. Then I peel it apart to form the full mask, plop it back in the liquid/gel to absorb some more, and throw it in the fridge (because I like the masks cold). I use these after showering and cleaning my face, and watch tv or read with it on. Once I feel the edges start to feel slightly dry, I peel it off and massage the rest of it into my skin, and top off with another moisturizer before bed.

text: If you thought that only the European Union produces quality shaving products and that American shaving was all about multi-blade contraptions and goop-out-of-a-can, think again. I am accustomed to good shaving soaps.  In addition to the foregoing, I also regularly use Institut Karite and Provence Sante.  I have also tried some of the artisanal EU shaving soaps; with one exception, I have found them over rated and way over priced.  However, I have not found Supply Tallow Shave Soap inferior in any way.  Moreover, it is a GREAT buy.  If it were from an EU country and had it been in production for 100 years, it would be wildly praised in the various shaving forums.

title: Perfect for DIY sheet masks!
text:
I love these!
I had read about doing lotion masks using cotton pads that peeled apart into layers, and bought the stuff to try it. It's good, and not hard to do, but takes a bit of time to prepare. So I bought these compressed sheet masks for doing quick lotion masks. I really like these. The compressed size makes it easy to travel with them, and they don't take up hardly any space when you store them. When you get them wet, they expand like the snake pellets you get on 4th of July. =)
I keep a shot glass in my bathroom just for doing quick lotion masks. I unwrap one of these compressed masks, toss it in the shot glass, then douse it with skin conditioner, hyaluronic acid lotion, and a bit of rose water. Once the mask is nice and saturated, I put it on my face for 3-5 minutes. (Since I like to listen to music while I'm getting ready, I leave the mask on for about the length of a song.)
The cotton material feels nice, not scratchy. When the sheet is wet it has enough stretch to cling to the face like it should. The fit is wide, the the nose flap is short. At least that's the fit on my face. I fix this by carefully cutting the excess width at my temples with scissors and placing one of strips I've cut over the end of my nose where the nose flap doesn't cover. The main thing I like about these is that the flaps on the eye holes are attached at the top. So, while I'm wearing the sheet mask, I can put the eye flaps on my eye lids so they get some moisture and still see what I'm doing. I really like that.
I plan on repurchasing these as soon as I run out.

title: Great for thin hair!
text:
As someone with thin hair, it is difficult for me to find styling tools that work for me without flattening the small amount of volume my hair will carry. I've done a video review so you can see this brush in action, but I find that this is an ideal brush for thin hair and people who hate to spend time doing their hair and generally prefer to walk out the door in a bun or ponytail. It took me about a minute to complete my full head of hair and look walk out the door ready.

Pros to this straightening brush:
*cost effective
*easy to hold
*instructions are simple to read and easy to implement
*Works very well
*whole head ready to go in one minute
*fast heat up
*pretty in pink
*easy to read temperature gauge

Cons:
*may pull some hair
*could scorch hair if hair is not completely dry when using
*easy to burn hands, be very careful
*over time may not be as hair friendly as other hair straightening brushes

Overall, this is a great value and I plan to continue using it. If you have longer hair or thicker hair, you may want to consider a straightening brush with prongs that are more wide-set. For me, this was a great purchase.

My 7yr old, and I were so excited to get these to hold her many, many large Jo Jo Siwa bows. I was expecting the ribbon to be a little thicker, and longer. It holds 4 large 8 inch bows comfortably. title: Very generous for a sample kit. Provides two shades of light-toned foundation to try.
text:
While a sample set, the amount you receive is actually quite generous. There are two different shades of beige here for foundation, a very light 'all-purpose' powder, several eyeshadows, a bronzer, a package of travel-size brushes, and sheer setting powder. I would consider the eyeshadows full-size really and each jar is packed to full capacity, but does not have a little plastic cover on top so be careful when opening them!

It took some experimenting on my end to see what worked for me. With my skin tone, I have two different shades between summer and winter. My summer foundation is now too dark, so I purchased this because I go between light to medium depending on the sun/weather. What works for me is using the lightest foundation as a base, the medium beige as natural color 'bronzer' for normal sunkissed areas, then the all-purpose as a highlighter. The coverage is amazing for the price and hides my under eye circles quite well. I have not used the actual bronzer since it's rather dark and dramatic, but if you're into contouring like that, it should be fine. The finishing powder is nice as well, but I prefer a setting spray to get rid some of the drying effect of mineral make-up.

I also recommend you use a primer and a moisturizer beforehand, letting it dry for a bit before using the powders. My acne medication causes dry patches and the first attempt I did with just primer made it pretty obvious. I also didn't use the brushes because I have my own set as well.

title: Practice makes perfect
text:
I also had never used a clamp-less iron before, but I have spent a lot of time trying to achieve that nice loose spiral that holds but doesn't look too rigid. This really does the trick. I have long,straight, baby fine hair and summer humidity is pretty much death to anything I try, and the curl falls right out. Somehow this holds up really well.

My complaints with it are just that even though it does get really, really hot, it seems to take longer to heat up than some of the "instant heat" irons I've been used to. So even though it doesn't take too much time once it's fully ready, there is a longer wait time on the front end, and not really a clear way of telling when it's fully ready either--it doesn't have a color-change light or dot like some of them do. Also, the glove is kind of dumb. I took a stab at it the first few times. It's weirdly small, for one thing--so it's awkward putting it on, you can still feel a good amount of heat through it, so it's not that effective at sparing your hand, and I could never get the hang of using it with the glove. It just felt really clumsy and took at least twice as long, so I stopped using it, and it's totally doable. You do have to be a little careful, sure--but honestly, I was hand wrapping my clamp curling iron almost the same way when I was trying to fake the spiral curl look so this isn't all that different---only this time it works. Now that I've had it for about a week, I feel like I have it really down. Since it takes longer, I can't use it every day during the morning rush, but it's kind of a fun way to shake things up.

text:
The gel soap seems fine - the cedar scent is strong but nice and not flowery (which is what I wanted) but the container has some serious flaws.
The bottle is attractive made of smooth metal - so when it's wet it becomes very slippery (which is the normal status when taking a shower). However, when I pressed the button to dispense the soap - nothing happened - no soap came out but the button didn't really depress, so I thought it must be locked and I'd need to twist it to unlock it.
Wrestling with this slippery wet bottle with my wet hands didn't seem to be working - I couldn't feel any give or clicks as I tried to twist the very small nozzle button in the wet - and without my glasses on I couldn't see if there were any markers or arrow directions....but I braced the slippery bottle as firmly as I could and kept trying until I suddenly noticed a stream of foamy soap coming out and dropping to the floor of the tub.
As I proceeded with my shower, I continued having challenges. This bottle has a VERY firm button. It wasn't actually locked, but my small 54 yr old female hands didn't have the strength to manage it at all (one handed). Especially as the bottle was wet and smooth and dang slippery! I ended up having to brace the bottle with one hand and push the button with the other - which left me with no palm available to catch the actual soap coming out. I wasted a bit of soap before I figure out I needed to twist the hand holding bottle to catch the stream of soap which let me catch about half.
There's definitely a design flaw in choosing that bottle and button dispenser!! It's very attractive but the tension spring for the dispenser button is crazy strong. Maybe they took the idea of masculine soap too far and have chosen bottles that can only be used by men with stronger hands too? Added with the smooth but hard bottle (metal doesn't provide any give when you squeeze hard) that becomes super slippery when it's wet (which is the expectation when taking a bath or shower) this doesn't seem very well thought out. Bad operations and marketing choices!

title: Works Well on Dry, Cracked Heels
text:
I have for years dealt with dry, cracked heels, and I have tried a number of things to correct the issue. While my heels haven’t hurt or anything, they have been ugly. In a search for solutions, I found this foot scrubber and decided it was likely going to work better for me than a foot rasp, and I ordered it. It’s a great tool and it works well, though I do offer some caution for those who haven’t worked with a foot scrubber or rasp in the past.

This is an odd-looking instrument, vaguely similar to a comma in shape. The scraping side somewhat resembles a mirror with a patterned rough edge. It feels a lot like an emery board though it has more of a “bite” to the surface, if that makes sense. The overall size and shape make it easy to grip and hold, even when wet.

The first time I used it, I scraped away a fairly large amount of dead skin, to the point that I had feeling in parts of my heels where I have had no feeling for quite some time. It left my heels soft, pink and looking much better. However, I did discover that one can overdo, and I had nicked myself on each heel in one or two places, just enough to require blotting but not enough to really be a concern (it was less serious than a cut while shaving).

I discovered the following day what happens when you remove too much dead skin and don’t put enough lotion on an area that deals with weight and stress – my heels split in a couple of places and I ended up having difficulty walking without pain for a couple of days. I had put high-quality lotion on my heels, but apparently not enough. That was entirely my mistake, and it was a painful one.

After that finally healed up, I tried again. I have fallen into a daily routine where I gently scrub my heels for a couple of minutes each, then apply lotion. My heels now look much better, they’re not splitting when I put weight on them, and I have avoided nicking myself. At least in my case this is not a tool that gets used intensely every couple of weeks, but rather it is a daily tool that gets used very gently.

I got curious and put this tool under a digital microscope to see what the rough surface looked like. The roughness resembles a series of crescents, not dissimilar to a rasp, but much more fine.

This thing really works and it does a good job. It’s slightly more expensive than the average foot rasp but it seems to work well. I do recommend using some caution when working with this instrument as it is possible to overdo if not careful, which is probably very true of any tool of this type.

text:
I'm a 23 year old female that has battled acne for 10 years. It's not just mild acne- it's cystic, life-damaging, skin-destroying acne. I get it mostly on my outer cheeks and chin. I've tried exfoliants, cleansers, toners, masques. I've done home remedies. Egg whites, oatmeal and honey, hydrogen peroxide, oil cleansing. Things will start to work, or work for a small time, and then my face will be back to it's oily, cystic self.

Recently I've been using an Aveeno daily exfoliator with an Aveeno moisturizer. It wasn't really doing the trick. I thought, perhaps I need to use toner. Since Aveeno is all natural, I decided to stick with that theme.

I *LOVE* this product. I will take off my makeup at night, spritz my face with toner, then apply moisturizer. After the first day I noticed my skin was less greasy/oily. It just felt better. I started to get concerned when I began getting small white pimples appearing, but friends told me that was my face getting rid of the junk. I was just thankful they weren't huge cysts! A week later, my skin is almost completely clear. I only have one active pimple on my face that is in the process of healing. I hope that it stays this way!

Also I must say that the smell is divine! My boyfriend even likes it. I wish the bottle would never run out, but I know that when it does, I'm buying another.

text:
I recently started wearing wigs, just to change things up and have a little fun in life. I was actually amazed at how many compliments I received while I was wearing this wig! Of course, even though the description on this is completely accurate, it's much shorter than it looks in the pictures, but I'm learning that's the case with all wigs. They must all use tiny little mannequin heads when photographing!? But now that I know this, I go by the measurements, and not the picture. The bangs were a little too long and I didn't like the way they looked with then off to the side (like in the description photo), so I cut them a bit. After that, I was very happy with it.

There's a couple small hooks in the back so you can adjust the size to fit any size head, and a netting on the inside which appears to be well made. Also, this wig is surprisingly comfortable! I wore it all day without any itching, or the wig shifting at all.

My teenage daughter laughed at me when I told her that I was gonna start wearing wigs, because I naturally have very long, very full hair, and she didn't see the point. But I explained to her, "to have fun and change things up without doing something permanent that I end up hating, but then can't change!". But once the wig arrived, she "jokingly" tried it on, and she fell in love with it too. Now she's looking forward to helping me pick out more wigs to add to my (or should I say "our") collection. I can't wait to get more colors, lengths, and styles!

title: Snozzle with Xtava Black Orchid and Conair Infinity Pro
text:
Similar to some of the other reviewers experiences, I find that the SnozzlePro works pretty well for me, but I do have to be very careful and make frequent adjustments -- it sort of exploits design problems with the tools you are using. I used it with a Conair Infinity ProPro and an Xtava Black Orchid.

Pros:
-It definitely fits my Conair Infinity Pro and probably won't have any trouble fitting other hair dryers.
-It's thick enough to be sturdy, but thin enough that I can stretch it onto the hair dryer.
- I don't experience any leaking or weird smells.
-I can use it (carefully) with the Xtava.

Cons:
-It is made of rubber, so when it heats up the rubber becomes more pliable and loose around the diffuser. I would recommend using this with cold air if possible. Unfortunately, my Conair Infinity Pro has a setting for "Cool" that isn't cold enough. So, I find that this works best if I keep my finger on the blue "Cold Shot" button the whole time.
-The Xtava has a very short connection point, so even though the SnozzlePro works pretty well, there's not a ton of space for it to hold on. That's a problem with the Xtava though, not the SnozzlePro. In particular, it seems to detach most at the top of the connection point and it will fall off while I'm using it. I just sort of use it gently and keep an eye on that top part to make sure it isn't slipping out.

Overall, I think the SnozzlePro is a great product that would probably work best with a diffuser with a longer connection point than the Xtava and potentially a hair dryer that has a truly cold setting.

title: Shaves as good as a blade - if you use it right
text:
This is the second 7775X I have owned. The first lasted two years, but this after extensive travel all over the world. It does shave as well as a blade (I use one of those too now and then) if you use it right (see below)

Positives

1) Quick charging - less than an hour to charge.
2) Long lasting - I have used it 10 days without recharging - great if you travel.
3) Seems to prevent ingrown hairs - which is something I run into when I use a blade consistently. My face definitely breaks out much less when I use this razor versus a blade (and I own some expensive blade razors as backup!).
4) So long as you follow instructions (don't press down hard, but when you need to go over an area again, do it firmly) you won't get nicked. Nice when you are in a strange hotel in a strange time zone and waking up jet lagged but needing to look presentable for a meeting.

Negatives

1) A little expensive
2) The shaving lotion cartridges are also expensive - I would just buy a can of regular shaving Gel (eg Edge).
3) Constantly pressing the dispenser for more gel can be a pain in the neck, and you go through those cartridges quickly (one every 10 days at most). If I wanted to redesign this shaver, I would junk the shaving dispensor entirely - I now find it just another moving part with the hinged lid.
4) I wish Norelco had come up with a way for this razor to use a standard charger jack of some kind, as having another electrical cord when I travel (especially one that does not work with multiple corded adaptors such as I-go) means I don't take the cord unless I am gone more than 8-10 days.

To use this right, just buy regular shaving gel, put it on your face, wait 30 seconds for the gel to soften your beard, and go for it. This is the best way I have found to get a clean, smooth shave. Gel in a can also has the advantage of going on thickly (versus the Coolskin dispensor) and not drying up quickly. Also, having a can of the shaving gel when you travel (checked baggage of course) can also come in handy if your Norelco runs out of charge, and you need to switch to that backup Gillette you should have in your shaving kit (I travel with enough cords as it is).

title: cat LOVES the brush, but hated it initially..
text:
When I first opened this brush I was very excited to see how my spoiled cat would like a nice brushing with it. I pulled it out of the package and showed it to him as he needs to inspect everything before he will allow it near him. He unfortunately ran away as soon as he got one sniff! I was puzzled, but I quickly realized that the silicone was not smelling great. That sometimes happens with new silicone and it just needs to sit out for a few days to have the smell dissipate. In a couple days the smell went away and I gave the brush another try. At first my cat pulled away because he remembered the smell, but once he realized it didn't smell, he let me give him a pet. He generally likes gentle petting, but this brush by nature makes even the most gentle brushing a little more rough. He accepted the new level of brushing and I proceeded to brush him. I was immediately amazed at the amount of cat hair this brush was removing per brush. This hands down is the most efficient cat brush I have ever used! I had to clean the bristles every few strokes, which is very simple to do by peeling the hair off in one large section. My cat is a short hair and does not shed very much at all, so I was confused as to how so much hair was being removed from my cat. He was in heaven so I kept on going until each section I was brushing would not brush out any more hair. When he got up from brushing, the cat looked better to me. Maybe because all of the loose hair was no longer holding down his shiny Tuxedo hair. In all I took out a handful of hair from my 7 pound cat. His coat looks shinier, fluffier and healthier now because of a simple brushing.

One thing I do need to mention about this brush is that it is not the most comfortable thing to hold for long periods of time. I pet my cat for about 45 minutes and my hand was hurting from gripping the cube for so long.

I removed 1 star - for the initial smell and the uncomfortable hand grip.
