title: Great Idea, Needs Some Fine Tuning
text:
I own a foot filer (Amope-style) already and was intrigued by an electric nail filer. The product came well-packaged and with some toe seperators, which was a nice bonus. I also appreciated that it comes in a plastic, TSA-type storage pouch.

As for the product itself, there is still some work to do before it's a great product. Firstly, the fact that they do not offer refills yet is a huge deterrent. I've only used mine a few times and the heads are still functioning adequately, but soon I'm sure they won't (particularly the filer) and then it will be useless until they offer refill file heads.

Secondly, the file head itself could be of better quality, in terms of filing power. The buff and shine ones are pretty good, but not amazing, as it still takes a little longer than I'd expect to get great results.

Finally, because everything just work "okay", the end result is perfectly fine. Fine is not bad, but I can achieve a better, more fine tuned result with a quality multi-way filing block in only slightly more time. Changing the file heads vs using 1 block for my hands, it's a no brainer I'm better off just using the block. I have found the buff & shine heads useful on my toes, though, for a quick shine boost when I'm in-between polish and letting my toenails breathe. For my toes, the speed of the machine is a little helpful to be bent over lslghtly less long.

All in all it is a pretty okay little device, but for the price it's not quite "ready for prime time". I can only see this being beneficial to those with hand problems, such as carpal tunnel, arthritis, etc, because then not having to grip a block and make a repeated motion for so long would be helpful.

I did receive a discount on my purchase, but my review is honest & unbiased.

title: NOT HUMAN HAIR
text: Okay, so I figured I'd give these a try as I usually spend way too much money on high quality tape in extensions. When I saw these I thought they'd be a potential cheaper alternative. When I received the hair it looked good, very thin, but the hair was soft and felt great. After application, my hair looked and felt great (my natural hair is about shoulder length, so all of the hair below my shoulders is only the extensions). I got them trimmed, layered, etc, to blend my hair. A few days after installation I decided that I wanted to curl my hair. Well, once I put that curler to the extensions on LOW HEAT, I heard the horrific "sizzling" noise and smelled a burning plastic-y smell. I instantly pull my hair out of the iron and the hair was literally fried, as synthetic hair does when heat is put onto it. At most, this hair is partially synthetic. If you look closely you can even see the synthetic hairs. They're super shiny (not a healthy human hair shine, but a plastic shine. Think of the shine or reflection on a water bottle). If I had known these weren't 100% human hair I would not have ordered them. Not only do the extensions basically get ruined after putting heat on them but they tangle easily, and just always look fake too shiny, and the hair clumps together, which I do in fact blame on the heat. If you're in the market for short term hair extensions that you can not put heat on then these are perfect for you. If not, you've got to invest in something more expensive that actually IS 100% human hair.

title: I don't think you'll find a better all-purpose product for your skin.
text:
I love this product. It's so light, looks like paraffin and turns from a firm salve like consistency to a very light oil when it touches your warm skin.

I knew a woman in her 70s - 80s and always admired her beautiful skin. One day I got up enough nerve to approach her and tell her how much I admired her soft, supple skin and asked her if she used any special creams to keep it like that. She told me that for many years the only thing she used on her skin was Albolene. It was what she cleansed her skin with and what she moisturized with...day or night. I purchased it and used it for a long time and loved the way it made my skin look and feel. Now and then I would stop and use other creams and serums when reading all the magic results they promised, but my skin never got better than it did with Albolene and I always went back. Once again I find myself trying out other creams but I have a backlog of Albolene and I'm pretty sure I'll be going back to it again.

I also discovered that many stage actors use it for removing their heavy stage makeup. A little of it goes a long way and I do love the scented one. The fragrance is very light and doesn't last long, but I always love my cosmetics to smell nice. It encourages me to use them. Not strong scents, though. They interfere with my perfume. Not my Albolene! And you have your choice of scented or unscented! Same great product with just the tiny difference of a light fragrance that doesn't last long at all.

title: Get lash glue instead
text:
Well, I purchased these same lashes without the dandy little tool. I had such a bad experience, but I was determined to get those little ****s on my eyes. Well, the tool was of no help whatsoever. Those little lash pieces still fell and fluttered around. I could not even find one piece until I looked in the mirror and found it on my nose. I even watched YouTube to get tips. One model put hers on, claiming that it was easy after you get the hang of it... but even her lashes did not fit next to her eyelid. There was a space of about 1/16 of an inch. She said that they look really good "from a distance". Hey Hey Hey... from a distance??? You've got to be kidding. How many of us want to stay across the room to look good??

In addition, I really don't know whose eyes they are made for. These lashes do not follow the contour of anyone's eyes who I know. Who has straight eyelids??? These lashes look like wings on your eyes. They stick fly out at the edges and I could not find any way to get them to fit the lid, short of a lot of nail glue.... that sort of defeats the purpose of them.

Now I can look back at this experience and laugh. I'm quite certain that an observer would have found it to be hilarious to watch me. At the time, I saw no humor in it. This was funny enough to be on the "I love Lucy" show. I would have loved to see Lucy and Ethel trying these out.

The concept is great.... wow!! But, it makes me wonder if the developers did these to determine the lengths that we would go to for beauty.

In closing, I even tried to get ahold of the company.... and wouldn't you know, there was no contact number on their site. Amazon was gracious enough to receive them back from me. Thank goodness for Amazon's commitment to trying to ensure that we are satisfied.

Now do you see why I procrastinated in doing this review??? I have never submitted a review as negative as this. BTW, I finally admitted to some friends my experience with these.... and they confessed that they, too, returned their magnetic lashes.
No difference whatsoever. Don’t waste your money.

title: A good idea, but has design flaw
text:
I really wanted to love this. It seemed like the perfect alternative to my aging WaterPik brand water flosser. It's smaller, light weight and doesn't have a huge tank and curly hose like the Water Pick. BUT,
it is a poor substitute. First the water tank is pretty small and I usually run out of water before I'm done.
The tank has a design flaw. There is a curved hose that is inside the tank that delivers water to the head. If you don't hold the flosser in the right position, the hose is out of the water and doesn't work. I can turn the head, but I have to turn off the flosser to do that.
It makes a loud noise, especially when the water gets low, that is irritating to me. The Water Pick makes a noise too, but this is louder and more shrill.
This set included little plastic tips that go on the end of the flosser head, but it constantly falsl off and tries to go down the drain so I just leave it off.
It comes with several replacement heads. That's good. It has two settings. One is pretty hard the other is very gentle. You have to push the on button quickly after it starts to get to the gentle setting which is not as easy as it sounds when you are squirting water in your mouth and trying not to make a mess.
It's not perfect. It may be okay for travel, but I guess I'll keep my WaterPik until it dies completely (it's 10 years old) and then get another WaterPik. In the meantime I'll keep trying to like this one.

title: Small Angled Blending Brush This is a good set of brushes for someone just getting into makeup
text:
This set contains the following brushes:
1. Round Blending Brush
2. Angled Blending Brush
3. Flat Blending Brush
4. Tapered Contouring Brush
5. Angled Contouring Brush
6. Small Tapered Contouring Brush
7. Small Flat Blending Brush
8. Small Round Blending Brush
9. Small Angled Contouring Brush
10. Small Angled Blending Brush
This is a good set of brushes for someone just getting into makeup. The larger brushes are intended for face/contour, but not blush; the smaller brushes seem intended for eye contour and blending. The brushes are very soft; however, the ferrules are not as full as they could be, leading to somewhat floppy brush heads, which means less control of the brush and product. The smaller brushes should have lower ferrules so the use has more control over where color or product is laid.

The brush set comes with a plastic coated brush roll which needed to be aired out upon arrival. Once the odor was gone, it proves to be a pretty durable case for toting the brushes around, with individual pockets for each brush and a protective flap that folds over. Since it is coated in plastic, it wipes clean easily. The design is a little gaudy, but, each to their own, right?

This vibration stimulates the skin and gets those hairs to prick up a little bit so that razor blades (all three baldes, i.e - Mach III/M3) catch better creating a cleaner smoother cut. I've sprinkled a bit on my body pillow, too, when I feel like I want a much stronger dose of the relaxation.

I read somewhere that mixing it with a carrier oil (I'm using rosehip oil) and rubbing it on the bottom of your feet can help with insomnia, so I've been doing that. I don't know if it's working, but it is making my feet feel softer, so that's something. I haven't experienced any respiratory or skin irritation with this product.

The bottle is a dark brown color so that the light can't get to the oil and break it down. They sent a dropper along with the oil, which I appreciated since I didn't have others. Next I'm going to try to make some kind of reusable sachet for my drawers--I just need to figure out what scent to mix it with first.

I was fortunate to receive this product at a free or discounted rate in exchange for my honest review. I am always conscious and aware of the number of items and possessions I bring into my home and try to make mindful decisions, because The Life-Changing Magic of Tidying Up told me to. For this reason, I only accept items that I feel will serve me, my family, and my needs. I do not accept items that seem useless or that do not speak to me. If I post a positive review it is because I had a positive experience. If I have only positive experiences, I chalk that up to a successful exercise in mindful purchasing and decision-making. title: I LOVE these!
text:
I just have to say it, I HATE WEARING A MASK! I have glasses that fog up terribly with most all traditional fabric masks. I have low-grade asthma and wearing a mask where I am breathing in my own air makes me very anxious and I end up being unable to breathe well at all. Thankfully I found that I didn't have to worry about any of that once I began wearing a face shield instead of a fabric mask. Because I began working in retail around the holidays and was required to wear a mask for 8 hours a day, I was able to survive with the shield. But I really didn't like the way that I had to wear the elastic band around my head over my hair, and it was much like wearing two pair of glasses, since I had to view the world through my glass lenses as well as the plastic of the shield.

One day I saw a woman in my store wearing one of these masks and I immediately became a fan. I found this seller online and I can't believe how much I love wearing this! It feels almost like I have no mask on at all - in fact, I was once heading into a store and the greeter there offered to give me a mask, not realizing that I had this one on until I got closer to her. It is great that you can sanitize this between wearings very easily without having to put it through the laundry, and I just keep it hanging from my rearview mirror and use hand wipes to clean it.

However, there are a couple of things that I'd prefer on this mask. The plastic is a hard, formed plastic rather than a pliable one. I no longer work in retail and am no longer required to wear a mask at my new job, but I feel like if I had to wear this one 8 hours a day like before, it might break within a few days. Although it does not fog up my glasses at all, it actually fogs up when I am wearing it outside. Once I enter the store and an ambient temperature though, the fog goes away and it is clear once again. I am sure that this mask would not be allowed on an airplane, but then neither are many other styles of masks out there. The other thing that is a bit bothersome is that when you are talking or singing with this mask on, it moves with the movement of your mouth since it holds onto your face with a chin guard that keeps the plastic away from your mouth. But all in all it is worth it to be able to breath and remain compliant with the current laws of my City regarding masks. For those reasons though, I gave it a 4 rather than a 5 rating.

title: Excellent hand cream
text:
UPDATE - 09/30/16 ========================================
Still loving this moisturizer and just ordered another package. This stuff goes on well, absorbs quickly into the skin and doesn't leave a greasy feeling! My skin feels truly moisturized. I love using it on my hands and feet before bedtime, this way it really absorbs into my skin overnight.
Love it, love it, love it!

========================================================
Not many people know this, or give it another thought sometimes - anything you put on your skin gets absorbed through the skin and ends up in the blood stream. This is why I am rather careful when picking my skin care products. I have been staying away from most hand creams for a while now just because for the most part there's at least a few potential carcinogens lurking among the ingredients. Even though the big famous brand creams make your skin feel wonderful the question is if the trade off is worth it.

Unfortunately, even so called organic products aren't always that safe. Provided, manufacturers of this goodness are disclosing all the ingredients on the label (and not hiding anything) this cream looks safe enough to eat. Therefore, I have been happily slathering it all over my hands (and any other body parts needing additional moisture) in the past few weeks and I am quite pleased with the results.

This white fluffy goodness feels surprisingly light and absorbs quickly into the skin. I must admit, it is a tad thinner in texture than I had expected but on the other hand this lightness ensures there's no oily residue left on your hands. The cream has no scent whatsoever which is a definite positive for those who are sensitive or don't particularly appreciate scented products. I'm adding a drop of essential oil of my choice (whatever I feel like that day) when I apply the cream if I feel like smelling something nice. Basically this cream is your blank canvas and leaves much room for creativity.

One thing I would probably change about this product is the packaging. (At least maybe as an option for buyers to choose from) I really think that tubes are better for hand creams - way easier to dispense and so much more hygienic (sticking your fingers into the container doesn't really help keep it germ free). Other than that I am happy to give this product my approval.

I purchased this product at a discount in exchange for an honest and unbiased review, all opinions are based on my own personal experience with the product.

title: Great for making buns, and helps curl your hair too!
text:
I had one of these when I was a kid, and I LOVED it, but at some point I got rid of it, and I really wish I hadn't. This "Hairigami" or whatever you want to call it is AWESOME. I have long hair that doesn't hold a curl well, but after I put my hair up in this for several hours, my hair comes out almost perfectly curled in a really natural-looking way. It does take some practice to get it right every time, but once you know how to do it, it's super quick and easy. I took some pictures to show my friends the steps, so I figured I'd include them here too (sorry for the quality--taking pictures of the back of your head isn't easy!).

STEP 1: Place your hair between the two arms (I don't know if that's the technical term, but that's what we'll call it here). I took these pics after I'd already had my hair up in this thing for a couple hours, so that's why my hair is already curly (my hair is very straight and thick)

STEP 2: Drag the Hairigami down a little over halfway down your hair (I tried to roll it up from the bottom of my hair the first time, and since my hair is slightly layered that was impossible to do. Also my arms aren't long enough to do that comfortably). Then, roll up until the Hairigami is snug against your head. (Note -- roll UP, do not roll under, it doesn't work if you roll under, or at least it didn't for me)

STEP 3: Snap the Hairigami (which is basically just 2 cloth-covered snap bracelets) so that it curls into a bun. This is a great hairstyle for work, or anything really, so if you want to just leave your hair in this bun, you may need to gently spread your hair out so that the entire Hairigami is evenly covered. **NOTE: As a former dancer, I would exercise caution when using this for dancing. While it may feel very secure, the bun WILL NOT hold up well if you're doing lots of turns. It may work great for younger dancers who are not doing so many turns, but even then that's iffy. If using it for dance class, TEST IT FIRST to make sure your bun isn't going to unravel in the middle of class!**

STEP 4: After a few hours (that depends on your hair -- I only waited about 3 hours and my hair came out super nice and curly, but everyone's hair is going to be different), unroll the Hairigami and see how nice and curly your hair is!

Bottom line: this thing is great for making buns, and great to help curl your hair too. It seems like a weird invention, but it's actually great!

I'm sorry folks - every time I decide I have a favorite hair care product, whether shampoo, conditioner, or a styling product, the manufacturer discontinues it within a year. That's too bad, because this stuff is close to perfect. I like the hold - it lasts, without being stiff or sticky, the easy application, and the fact that it leaves you with a natural matte finish and doesn't look slick or greasy. At $4 it was an incredible value, but now you might be able to find something better. I don't know what try next, because I've never been a fan of paying $10-$15 for higher-end brands (didn't like the ones I tried), and I'm not counting on this being available here as what is becoming old stock. title: They Are Not Bad 👩
text:
I received 3 packs of "Revive Rinse Free Bathing Wipes". Each pack contains 12 wipes.

I wanted to try these wipes because I thought they could be a better option for me than regular baby wipes for my period accident clean ups & they are pretty nice (not perfect).

I have heavy extended length menstrual periods and have always used regular baby wipes for any messy / accident clean ups. That way I can just throw them away after I'm done with them.

These bathing wipes are way larger than a typical baby wipe. They are white in color and have a light perfume type of scent (which is probably the Chamomile Extract).

They can be microwaved (for no more than 15 seconds according to the pack) if you wanted them warm but I just used them "as is" right out of the packs.

They are wet enough to get the job done but not dripping wet (leaking) everywhere. They are also a nice thickness and soft to the touch.

They didn't irritate my sensitive skin at all. They also aren't soapy at all, they left my skin feeling okay (clean) maybe a little bit sticky but nothing that I couldn't tolerate.

I do like these wipes overall because they are large in size and affordable.

title: Not just cotton and silk - contains polyester
text:
I won't say the product is necessarily bad, but I certainly do not like it and am not pleased with the disparity between the description and the actual product.

While the amazon page says these eye-covers are made of cotton and silk, the product packaging and tags both indicate the product is cotton, silk, AND polyester. I would not have bought these had I known this as my wife reacts to polyester. This just leaves me with another useless set of eye covers that my wife can't use.

Also, I personally find these uncomfortable. The silk is nothing like my nice soft silk shirts. It is still a shiny and smooth fabric, yet also an uncomfortably rough (I'm not sure how better to describe it -- it's like running your skin over tiny closely spaced wires), fabric that is very hot to wear on your face. Furthermore, I found that I got a headache both times I tried wearing these.

My wife has previously made some passable eye-covers out of cotton socks that we both can wear -- and I find significantly more comfortable. She's suggested that maybe she can try taking these apart and using the straps and cotton parts and making better cotton-sock eye-covers. I'm skeptical and am considering returning these. I'm certainly not happy.

If you like the really slick-abrasive feeling fabrics like cheap silks or cheap satins, and if you don't have any issue with the polyester in these, I can't really see a problem with them. They could probably benefit from being a bit larger, but they're 'pillowy'-enough (for lack of a better word) to block out most of the light and fill in the gaps around the edges. Mystery as to why they give me a headache, but they've enough good reviews that it can't be common.

I'm giving them 2 stars because I think the description is misleading and I don't like them, but also because I think a more moderate rating would get this lost among rating of people who are happy with the item. I always read some of the reviews and I wish I'd seen a review like this before purchasing.

title: Thank You, Earth Therapeutics!!
text:
My bedroom faces the east and has an uncovered half-moon window above the one with blinds. In the summer the light begins to pour in before 5 AM and, being a light sleeper, I would wake up and have a difficult time getting back to sleep afterwards, which eventually, led me to search for a sleep mask.

I purchased these masks and another, molded one that came with earplugs. This is my very favorite and I shared the second of the set with my night-shift working daughter, as I felt it might help her get more rest during the day as well. I've been using mine for a few months now and absolutely love it.

It does take a little bit of getting used to, just to the feel of something on your face and around your head. I've felt a little irritation on my ears occasionally but can easily adjust it to relieve that. It fits my face and stays in place quite well without having the band on tightly. I am a "tummy sleeper", and this mask is so soft that it doesn't feel uncomfortable against my pillow. It's just wonderful!

I have not noticed any scent on the ones that I received, and I checked because of the other reviewers comments. I've hand-washed it numerous times now, then let it air dry and it's ready to go again. If anything, it's just become softer but has not shown any signs of wear beyond that. I'm now looking to order more, just to have on hand when this one is ready to be replaced.

The other, molded one seems a bit bigger but sits off your eyes, if that sensation would bother you. I have a little more difficulty getting it to block all the light as well as this one, but it could be more attractive for larger faces or folks that are bothered by having something constantly touching their eyes like this one does. Just my thoughts on that. . .

I've read many articles recently on the importance of getting adequate sleep for your mental and physical health. If you are looking at sleep masks, you're probably wanting to improve your rest for some reason. I'd recommend you give this mask a try. I don't understand why some seem scented and some aren't, but I am 100% pleased with the masks I received. Most of those reviews are pretty old if you note that.

When the entire process was completed, I ended up with only a small amount that got on my hands. Not a big deal, at all. I have one small complaint. When you're finished using the suction tube, there's no real way to clean the tube. I chose to wrap the tube with saran/cling wrap. title: The Negative Reviews Don't Do This Shaver Justice ⚖
text: I will start out by saying that I did not purchase my Wahl Smart Shaver from Amazon since I found it cheaper elsewhere.  With that being said, I'd like to comment based on my usage of this shaver thus far. First of all, I just recently used a Braun 9 series shaver. Unfortunately, this shaver does not have a cleaning/charging station but I'm not convinced that is a deal breaker. I am also puzzeld by some of the negative reviews here. I literally turned on both shavers, and in my honest opinion, the Wahl was slightly quieter. The Wahl does have some similarities to a Remington shaver. For example, the two inner blades resemble the Remington as does the sound of the shaver. The outter foil seems to be very unique to the Wahl brand. So in using the Wahl Smart Shaver, I found it to be very effective on 2+ days of beard growth as it went through the facial hair with ease. The shaver head is thinner which in my opinion allowed me to get closer than both Braun and Remington shavers. The hypoallergenic foils that have symmetrical and asymmetrical foil slots provided me with an exceptionally close and clean shave. Almost 12 hours after my initial shave, and I barely felt any stubble growth. To me that speaks volumes about this shaver. I was very skeptical about trying this shaver based on the prior reviews here and the fact that the Wahl shaver was cheaper than the leading brands (e.g., Braun, Panasonic, Remington, etc..). However, for now I'm glad I took a chance and decided to give the Wahl Smart Shaver a chance. Also, if you view other sites, this shaver ranks significantly higher than it does amongst Amazon shoppers. Not sure why this is but something doesn't make sense to me. So if you want a clean shave and also don't want to go into debt buying a shaver, I suggest giving this shaver a try. By the way I'm retired military and this would've been nice to use while I was active duty. Lastly, if you're still not convinced, please take into account that Wahl guarantees this shaver for five (5) years. Take a chance. You'll be glad you did!

text:
I use this product nearly on a daily basis, and I really like it. If used correctly, the amount of product in this tube will last for months. The operative words are "used correctly." Too many women try to apply foundation, of any kind, with their fingers. Thats never a good idea, because it will always lead to the streaky, too dark appearance mentioned in the last review. Also, since you are using too much product that way, the tube will be empty far sooner than is should be.
The best way to apply foundation is with a kabuki style make up brush. The long handled one with the small, soft head is best for applying all skin foundations. Apply two or three drops to the back of your hand, dip the brush in as needed and swirl onto your face. Do this and I guarantee that your Botanilift foundation will give you that air brushed look of naked skin. That being said, I still recommend the use of a light weight sunblock under this or any other product, regardless of whether or not it has an SPF. A girl who wants to ensure the long term health and appearance of her skin can never have too much sunblock! I hope this helps others who are having difficulty with this and other foundation products.

title: So Far, So Good
text:
I bought LightStim for Pain to help with arthritis that developed in my knees after an accident. The right knee healed fairly well, no pain, just a little stiffness, and I can easily live with that. The left knee, however, has severe pain in one area. Cortisone injections help, but that help doesn't last long, and it sometimes weakens the muscles until it wears off, and I believe the muscle weakness is worse than the pain. It's certainly more debilitating. I was tired of taking so much Tylenol, even though I always kept my dose way below what is toxic to the liver.

One morning, I woke very early, and even though I'd taken Tylenol the night before, my left knee was really hurting. I cleansed it, then used my LightStim on the affected area, 15 minutes on two areas. To my shock and surprise, the pain was gone. Now, I know the pain will return. One has to treat an injury for some length of time before the healing is permanent. But I do know LightStim is going to speed up the healing, and I'm doing other things to heal my knee as well, such as taking collagen, using BioSil in my morning orange juice to encourage my body to produce more of its own collagen, etc. But when I have to go out, to the hairdresser, to synagogue, to see friends, etc., I know I can do it with greatly reduced pain if I use the LightStim before I go. And, I try to walk at least 60 minutes a day. LightStim treatments help me walk a lot more easily than if I hadn't used it.

I really don't notice my skin getting warm when I use this device, but I do have to say that after a 30-minute treatment, the bulbs are warm, so I do think it's working. I just hold my device against my knee very gently. Don't press. That could hinder progress rather than help it.

I like the fact that LightStim uses a cord and that the bulbs are meant to last 100,000 hours. I also like the fact that we can use this device as often as desired. It does have an automatic 30-minute shut-off, and I don't use it right away again. I wait at least until the bulbs have cooled. No use tempting fate. I also like the fact that we don't need to apply any gel, etc. Just cleanse the area to be treated, plug in the light, and use it. (Make sure you cleanse the area to be treated. If you don't, any oil will simply reflect the light rather than allowing it to be absorbed.)

I do wish the light were a little bigger, though, so I could treat a larger area at one time, but this is a minor complaint. Also, the goggles that come with the device are mostly junk. Mine arrived broken, but I don't use goggles with red light anyway. Red light is an approved treatment for the eyes, although this device is not approved for eye treatments, and I've never worn goggles with my red light panel when I treat my hair. Don't look directly at the light, however. Not without your doctor's okay. That just wouldn't be a good idea. If you really want to wear googles, just invest in a really good pair, and make sure they block out all light. (If you can still see light with your eyes closed or with goggles on, you know the light is hitting your retinas.)

All-in-all, I really love my LightStim, and I'll be using it daily on my injured knee. It's allowed me to reduce the number of Tylenol I take, and, along with the other treatments I'm using, I hope some day soon, my healing will be permanent. (Still think I'd use the LightStim daily, just for good measure.)

Highly recommended.

title: TL;DR Not worth hassle, better off with glue ons
text:
Bought these as a test to see if the magnetic eyelashes are worth it. I’d never tried them before and figured, what the hell. As a long time eyelash fan, I completely understand the idea of spending hours on make up just to have that final step of putting glue-on lashes ruin it all, they’re not easy... so the appeal was here to give this new way a try.

Let me be frank, they’re terrible and not worth the money. I’ll take my chances on the glue...

To explain why... I can’t speak to all brands but the magnetic eyeliner for this has not been perfected yet. Despite shaking the container vigorously for 10-20 shakes per instructions, the eyeliner is thick. Even using my tiny regular eyeliner brush to apply I still ended up with thick raccoon lines. Fine, a night out it might be a little thicker than normal... I looked past it... however when it came to putting the lashes on...

They provided a metal applicator?! Why? The eyelashes stuck to it and make applying it to the eyeliner difficult. I switched to a plastic applicator that I get from my regular glue on lashes. That made it a little easier. However, you have to be excessively careful not to get the eyeliner on your actual eyelashes or it will stick to them.

Okay, second try, reapply trying to make the eyeliner thinner and avoiding my eyelashes, waiting a little while for the eyeliner to fully dry, bam they stick! However, they’re a little higher than my lash line so I go to adjust them, the eyeliner flakes off and there’s a chunk of eyeliner missing (it’s attached to the magnet of course.) I take my small eyeliner brush, fill in the hole, wait for it to dry and place it right back.

They’re on, they look decent (albeit thicker eyeliner than usual even for a night out) however I can’t apply any mascara to make them blend with my natural eyelashes (or they move and I do the patch job all over again) and I feel as though one swift gust of wind and they’ll be out of alignment.

There’s a few reviews here with people who have had success and if that works for them that’s great, I will be going back to my regular glue on eyelashes. It takes practice, I’m sure, just like regular glue on eyelashes but if the convenience isn’t there why would I buy them over glue ons?

title: You get what you pay for
text:
Buyer beware!
Pros:
Packaging was great. Nothing spilled out or burst open. Colors are gorgeous.

Shipping was ok. I got a message basically saying shipping was delayed due to my error of not providing the right address, yet I ordered 4 items the same day and provided the same shipping address. They supposedly corrected the error and got it shipped to me in less than a week.

Now, let's talk about the cons:
I can't say this product is a true polygel. When using the slip solution or isopropyl alcohol, the solution dissipated and the brush dried out within seconds. Once I was able to start smoothing the product out, I got one good pat before the product became extremely sticky and unmanageable due to the brush drying out. It definitely took some finesse to get it to work. Also, do not use the dual forms as the product is not thick enough to hold it's own without moving under the light. If you have paper forms or nail tips, you will have much better luck with this product. I will say it definitely took me way too long to do one set but filing the product was great and so easy.

After trial and error, if you want to take the time to make it thicker, put some on a smooth flat surface and add clear acrylic. Make sure to use a metal spatula to mix the 2 products if you so choose to. Also, THIS PRODUCT IS VERY STICKY. If you are not careful, you will get this product everywhere.

I would give more stars if the polygel was a thicker constancy and the brush didn't dry out seconds after dipping into the slip solution or isopropyl alcohol.

I will give this kit a try again when it's time for me to change my set, but I'm not sure I will purchase this kit again.

title: The best trimmer I've yet used.
text:
First off, I have to say I'm severely disappointed with some of the other reviews of this product, as I have found them to be light years from my experience with this trimmer. Thus far, I have found it to be well designed, well built and very easy to use. Also to my surprise, the vaccum works just great! Yes, there are still hairs that hit the sink, but whadda ya want, perfection? The vaccum collects easily two-thirds to three-quarters of the trimmed hair and that's a good thing.

That said, I've found the most impressive aspect of the trimmer is the extended precision trimming head. While not as wide as the standard trimming head, it extends the cutting edge far enough away from the body of the trimmer to provide the easiest and most accurate edge trimming I've ever experienced. Outlining my beard, moustache and sideburns is suddenly a far easier and more precise task. For any guy who either wants or needs cleaner lines on his facial hair, this is an excellent choice!

I'm still getting used to the length selector and how to get the desired look before having to take off the guide comb and switch trimmer heads to get a more precise cut, but I'm sure that will come with time. It operates in much the same way as my previous Norelco trimmer, but the body design of this trimmer fits much better in the hand, and the guide comb assembly provides a much more comfortable trim as I glide it over my chin. It's also a wonderful thing to have the fast 1 hour recharge time!

The only downside I've found so far is some irritation of the skin while using the extended trimmer head. It's a VERY sharp head and can nick you if you're not careful, but I put that in the still-learning-how-to-use-it category. This is truly a great trimmer, so to all my proudly facially hirsute brothers, I say don't believe the nay-sayers and pick this puppy up!

title: Makes my feet tingle
text:
Pumice stone (made in Korea)
It's a regular pumice stone; if you've seen one, you've seen them all. This one fits in the hand nicely and has a pleasant minty scent. I admit I've never found these very useful, and probably won't use it much because they're hard to clean. The one I received is smoother and a different shape from the one in the picture.

Wooden foot massager (made in China)
I used to have a similar one and lost it, so this was one of the reasons I bought the kit. I like this a lot because the ridges are not as deep/pointed as they are on some rollers. It's relaxing without being painful, and feels great on the sides of the feet too. I even like rolling it between my hands. My only complaint is that the wood is a tiny bit rough in places. Not anything I feel when using it, however.

Wooden foot brush (made in China)
I was disappointed in this brush because the one I received has flaws in the wood that make it look grimy. If I were buying this set in a shop, I would have looked through them all and picked one without a damaged brush. However, it's still functional and the bristles are a nice balance between stiff and soft. You can use it to clean your toenails or simply brush it on your feet to get the blood circulating.

Tea tree oil foot scrub (made in the USA)
This is really nice, it has a fine grit that works well without irritating. You get a full size tube and don't use a lot at a time, so this will last a while.

Tea tree oil foot balm (made in the USA)
This is the star of the show, it's heavenly. Smells refreshingly minty, makes your skin soft. Works on any dry skin, not just feet. I couldn't resist using a lot of this, so even though you get a lot, I have a feeling I'll be buying more fairly soon. I really notice the difference right away. I can easily see this becoming a must-have staple.

Bag
It comes in a plastic bag with a green cord drawstring. The plastic is thick enough to make it reusable, though the foot massager sticks out the top. It's nothing special, but sturdy enough to store the set.

Overall
All together, the kit is very relaxing to use after a stressful day. I'm definitely going to check out more of the Earth Therapeutics products that are made in the USA.

The balm and scrub are both vegan, however the brush has boar bristles, so this would NOT be a good gift for a vegan. However, it would be a great unisex gift for just about anyone else, especially people who are on their feet all day.

title: TLM Flawless Colour Changing Foundation
text:
Wow! Where has this been all of my life?

I purchased this because I was intrigued by the color changing aspect. I didn't want anything that felt like a heavy mask, but wanted something that offered some coverage. This is a home run!

I'm 51 years of age. As a teen I spent a lot of time outdoors, and I do mean a LOT. Without any type of sunblock, working long days on the farm, and just as many dousing myself with baby oil and water to "get color". Now my complexion has changed, partly due to years of sun damage and more so due to the fact that I'm no longer in my youth. My skin is dry & I have a lot of fine lines and red, blotchiness. I fall in a medium skin tone.

My teen daughter has beautiful fair skin that is prone to acne. She's only started wearing minimal makeup very recently, and didn't want anything heavy or difficult to wear.

I thought this the perfect opportunity to really test this product. Two females, different ages, different skin tones. How would it measure up?

Superbly! I didn't not feel that I was wearing a heavy mask. I cannot tell you the number of liquid foundations I have tried in the 35 or so years since I started wearing makeup, but it is a LOT, with disappointing results. Hours spent blending, blending, blending....trying to get those heavy foundations blended so as not to appear as though I was wearing a mask, with the lines around the jaw area, ears, etc.

With this I did not have to do that. It goes on lightly, blends effortlessly, and held up well all day until I took it off. I'm a gal who sweats. There's no pretty way of saying it. I don't glisten. I'm at that age where hot flashes are the norm; add to that that I live in the armpit of the South where humidity is 80% or so most days and the simplest of activities like loading/unloading groceries from the car results in a deluge of sweat!

I didn't take it easy when I wore this. Believe me, it was tested. But at no time did I have to reapply, or feel like I'd lost any of it as I went about my day. It was truly THAT good.

My daughter is equally thrilled with it. Did it disguise her few blemishes? No, but it did cover the redness of them and makes her look more "put together".

I'm placing my order for a second bottle of it as soon as I post this, so that each of us will have our own.

The powder brush is a bit smaller than I would personally like for powder. It’s not quite dense but in a brush that is used for powder products that’s okay. When I’m buffing in the powder I don’t want the brush to be too dense or it will move the foundation around. I’ve been using this brush for blush because of it’s smaller shape and it’s working great.

Now the final two- the foundation brush and the sponge. I decided to do half of my foundation with the brush on one side, and the other half with the sponge on the other side.

The foundation brush is a typical brush of it’s kind. It did not make the foundation look streaky and applied very smooth.

The sponge is the most interesting piece in this set. It doesn’t feel super soft like a Beauty Blender or a Real Techniques sponge. It feels like a softer stress ball and feels a bit rubbery. I’ve never had a sponge like this. I soaked the sponge in water and drained the excess as I would do with any sponge. It felt heavier but did seem to soften a bit and did expand in size. I dabbed the foundation on my face and pressed the sponge around to press the product in and I got a really smooth finish. The sponge did not seem to absorb much product.

title: Helped my recurring chalazion and stye problem

I’m writing this review for people like me who struggle with recurring chalazions and styes:
I started getting chalazion 5 years ago on both eyes and I don’t know what even started it. It was very frustrating because these bumps would form on my eyelid and nothing worked on them. I got surgery once to get rid of one on my lower eye lid. They stayed for months and warm compresses and eye massages that doctors recommended me did nothing.
I read many research papers to see what I can do to help my condition and here is a summary:
1. this eye wash helped so much. Since I started using this eye wash two months ago my chalazions are almost gone and very unnoticeable. I wash my eyes every mornings and before going to bed and also whenever it starts to itch.
2. One doctor prescribed an antibiotic called “Doxycycline” I think that also helped my condition
3. I make tea with tea leaves and I let it cool, then I use a cotton ball to put the tea inside my eyes. I use 3-4 drops in each eye.
4. mix of one drop of tea tree oil and 4 drops of olive oil and put it on your eye lid. I wash it after 15 mins.

That’s a summary. Some people say warm compresses help them but for me, I did not see noticeable results. I used to wash my eyes with baby shampoo and it worsened my condition. only this eye wash helped. My condition has improved 80% since I took the steps I mentioned.

title: In less than 24 hours I'm obsessed!
text:
I've had this day cream for less than 24 hours... so I may be jumping the gun but I'm already so amazed I just had to review!

I am in my mid-20's with sensitive dry skin that breaks out in zits and/or hives if you simply just look at it wrong. My previous face cream has either been discontinued or moved to some obscure unfindable website. So I took a leap of faith trying this rose day cream. And oh my goodness, I am so happy I did! My face has never been so soft and clear and... glowy! I feel like I have an entirely new face, and in under 24 hours no less!

This cream is very concentrated. I only need to gently tap the cream with my fingertip once or twice to cover my entire face and neck. It may smell like something your grandmother or great grandmother would have enjoyed... if your grandmother had good taste. It is an absolutely delightful true rose smell (reminds you of the roses your beau would give you) and not at all overpowering. The cream feels a bit greasy at first and you may have to wait a minute to be able to apply make up afterwards but once it settles in, it takes about as long as it does to towel dry your hair, your face feels and looks like dewy perfection. I can't believe nobody told me about this stuff! I guess I'll have to start telling my friends about it myself. I wish I had before and after pictures to show you what a difference it made.

Upon further investigation of the company, Rose Valley Land, I'm now pining after their eye cream and shower gel. I may end up buying every product they have over the next few months as I finish off what I already have.

title: So far so awesome: Day 1
text:
Notes out of the box;
* Very nice, low profile footprint design.
* 7 inches long, 5 inches at widest part of the oval, 2.5 inches tall.
* Fits up to .75 oz polishes with all shaped bottle necks (bam! take that iZen Pro!)
* Silver plastic, no idea on solvent resistance (yet).
* Uses both AC adapter or batteries for cordless operation.
* 5600 shakes per minute promises the box and spec detail.
* 3 detachable, adjustable rubber securing straps.
* 1 on/off button, with a lighter pressure 'pulse on' feature.

Operation:
* Cinch to strap on.
* Pretty impressive agitation for one so wee.
* Noise level mild especially in comparison to my incessant bottle agitation whining. "Ow! My arms! Blah, blah, blah." I'd be more specific, but I was operating it right on a stainless steel counter to put it through the noise test. It'd be unladylike to compare it to a 'personal massager' out loud wouldn't it? Did I just type that? Oopsy, my bad. Quieter over a mat, silicone, towel or cork tile by miles. I did that too.

Result:
Before had separation, some streaky clearness and clinging pigment near the neck. I gave it my regular human powered roll/tap/roll for the following 'before shaker' application demo. (See posted pics)

Left, regular human agitation. 5 freaky coats and I had to wrangle dual directions and mucho smoothing in application. I tried really hard to give it more care actually because I wanted to be ungenerous to ForPro. But, human agitation was a streaky, bubbled shrink-back, difficult, wrinkling mess at every application and cure. Just like last time I dared to be decadent. I purposefully used a problem child color of an otherwise fabulous gel polish line. Plus, I left the cleansing paper towel wipes in the photos to demonstrate the horrid vs acceptable cure difference. Like eww! That's dangerous. It even wiped off in spots!

Right, ForPro shaken. 3 coats. Application was easy and like normally behaved other vampy, dark, well agitated gel polishes. Say what? I thought I'd see some improvement, but I didn't really expect this great of one. The color is wearable and I like it now.

All things are equal in my test, except I was more careful in application of the human shaken swatch, which has 2 more coats for a subpar, unusable result. I had to, it was having a tantrum in streaky pants before ForPro.

Other notes:
ForPro requires a phillips head screwdriver to open the 4 AA battery housing. Probably because it shakes so much? Still, a nice cordless option to the AC adapter also included. Yay that. *Batteries not included.

And, I think any warranty would be online via ForPro website only? This didn't come with instructions or warranty card in the box. Mostly a no-brainer plug and play.

It's unscathed by alcohol meaning any gel polish mishaps can wipe right off. I blotted the underbelly to remove dust lightly.

Clear rubber feet stay put while leaving no marks. That's awesome. Especially compared to Robarts that jiggle off tables and sound like landscaping machines.

I like ForPro so far. I think it saves product and my shake stress physiology. Prettier result in fewer, easier coats :).

It did a good job on both a chunky glitter and a streak-prone frost in a conventional lacquer brand. I did shake them once to break surface tension first though. I also rotated the bottles and let them shake twice. The beads were rolling free in both and additive distribution was even and good after. Thanks ForPro! Please last an eon now.

title: Seems like it is built to last
text:
The table itself is very solid and heavy. Seems like it is built to last. It came packaged very well and was delivered on a pallet. The size is really good, plenty of room on the table top and leg room is ample. The table does not rock, but sits firmly, proving it was built square. The built in vent is very helpful. When my wife and sister do each others nails they would often joke that they were going to die from all the nail dust....well this vent will now prevent an early death!

The desk itself has two outer drawers that slide out. The one in the middle tilts out and is simply an access cubby to turn the vent switch on and off.

The critiques I have are minor. 1) The glass top didn't fit the table top exactly...it was off by a little, maybe 1/8". I flipped it over to see if it fit better and it was still off. The vent still fit in the hole ok. 2) There is no 1 1/2" hole inside the middle cubby to allow the electrical cord to go through so you can plug it in to an outlet. I'll have to drill that myself. I'm also going to do some other "convenience" modifications which involve installing more outlets near the bottoms of the legs so there won't be cords draped all around for the lamp, UV, Dremel, and fan. There will essentially be one cord providing power to the table, and then the other accessories will plug into the table.

Overall, I give it a 4 1/2 stars rating. If the glass fit better and the middle cubby had an access hole for the fan cord, that would make it a 5 star. I can't choose 4 1/2 so i'll mark it a 5. It's more 5 than 4 anyways.

I guess I could talk about the money a bit. Yes, this was expensive. $400 plus $150 s/h plus $65 to deliver to a residential address (which I didn't know about. To the manufacturer: you should disclose this additional cost upfront). No matter what table I looked at, they all were going to have a high shipping cost. So then it was a matter of choosing between a $200 table and $400 and up because for some reason these manicure tables are expensive, even the cheap plywood models on wheels. So I opted to pay more for quality. It seems like it will last as long as we need it, and it matches the decor of the room.

title: Very good soap
text:
I would call this a very good soap. Not quite excellent, due to a couple of peeves, but very close. No 5 Star, but 9 out of 10.

The scent is quite enjoyable and is as labeled, a bay rum and orange. While it is not overpowering; I kind of would have preferred the orange to be a bit toned back to let more of the bay rum through. But I would count that more of a personal preference.

It works more or less as one would expect for cleaning. I found that it formed a light lather with just hand rubbing and would need a washcloth to build a thicker foam. After cleaning, it would rinse off easily with no leftover films or feelings other than just clean.

This soap is also very good for a wet shave. While I am relatively new to wet shaving and only have used a puck of Col Conk to compare to. Once that puck of Col Conk was gone, my bar of this soap was just about done and I tossed the last sliver into my bowl. This soap lathers up beautifully thick with a badger hair brush, and then after application, would stay foamed on the face for the full shave. If anything, I would say this soap is superior to the Col Conk for shaving, and the Conk was a good product and is highly rated.
Heck. If Frannie sold this soap in a round cake suitable for a shave bowl, I would probably stick with it for shaving.

I've used manual toothbrushes for most of my life, but about nine months ago my dental hygenist prompted me to try an electric as a potential time-saver.

I first went with an inexpensive Oral-B which ran on AA batteries, and found it was a bit easier to use than a manual. The small round brusheads are easier to fit behind my back teeth, and electric toothbrushes in general seem to stimulate the gums a bit more. The big advantage for me is that it's faster; I used to brush for 3-4 minutes with a manual, and I find 2 minutes with an Oral-B seems to work just as well.

I didn't find it was earth-shakingly different, though. Since my dental hygiene before switching was "near-perfect" (I get checkups every three months and only rarely does my hygenist have to do anything at all) neither I nor my dentist have noticed any differences. I'm not convinced that electric brushes in general are more effective than a properly-used manual.

The cheap Oral-B brushes are... really cheap, and I think they're overpriced given how often they fail. If you want to spend $50-$100 a year replacing toothbrushes, that's certainly one way to do it. I tried two of them, and both of them failed in different ways within 3 months.

I next tried a top-of-the-line Sonicare; a local store offered a 30-day money-back guarantee so I figured it was worth a try (they don't sell any non-cheap Oral-B products or I would've done that instead). Yes, it was probably built well... and heavy, and the handle was immense compared to the Oral-B. I found it very awkward to use, and I don't think it was doing a very good job of cleaning because I noticed substantially more gunk from flossing than before I started using it.

I don't mean to complain about the Sonicare or claim it's a bad product. My point is that there *are* differences, and you may very well find one electric works better than another. My hygenist mentioned that some people greatly prefer the Sonicare brushes, and they can't be that bad all around because many people are successfully using them. They just didn't work for me (more accurately, I should say the one I tried didn't work).

The 8850 is built quite a bit better than the cheap Oral-B brushes and it should definitely last longer. It's certainly more waterproof (I had problems with water getting into the housing of the others). The size fits my hand well, and it seems just as easy to use as their others. I also like the variable-speed feature, though I wish there were a way to set it once rather than having to reset it every time I use it.

Plan on securing the base to a wall. If it's sitting on a sink or shelf it'll probably need cleaning more often, and it's pretty easy to knock over. Also note that the tongue cleaner or vibrating pick attachment don't quite fit in the attachment holder; it's apparently meant for brushes only, which could be a minor irritation if you use them regularly.

The timer feature might be useful, but that depends greatly on how you brush. I don't use quadrants, instead I brush my lower teeth (doing the fronts, then the tops, then the backs), then the uppers. Thus the 30 second timer doesn't help me very much, and I could never quite figure out what the 2-minute timer was for--what happens when the two minutes are up and I haven't finished the backs of my upper teeth yet?

I've never needed to use anything other than the ultrasoft heads, and since I usually brush 4-5 times a day I prefer using the most gentle brush I can find. (The general advice is that stiffer brushes don't clean any better anyway.) The other attachments (tongue scraper, vibrating pick) seem OK, but I prefer using floss, a manual gum stimulator, and a plain tongue scraper instead.

The pick replacements are very expensive and, in my opinion, just aren't a viable alternative to floss. Some people prefer using a vibrating tongue scraper because they don't stimulate the gag reflex as much.

The Oral-B head replacements in general are expensive, and they really do need replacement every three months (mine start visibly fraying around that time). It's worth taking that into account when looking at prices, because they're a substantial investment. And shop around, occasionally they can be found for much less than the usual retail prices.

If you haven't used an electric (or an Oral-B) before, I'd suggest trying one of the cheap/disposable electric brushes first... and you may want to try two or three different brands so you can get a feel for which style you prefer. Money-back guarantees are important here, because some people seem to really dislike certain types of brushes.

If you've used and like the cheap Oral-Bs and want something that will last for more than a month, the 8850 would be a good alternative. I'm not convinced the uber-3D cleaning action (or whatever they're calling it this week) really works any better than their others... but it probably doesn't hurt, and the two-year warranty on the 8850 is a win.

title: My under eye area is very dry so I love to try a new eye cream
text:
My under eye area is very dry so I love to try a new eye cream. I’m pretty picky about what eye creams I feel work for me and what doesn’t. Admittedly I didn’t research Valentia True Glow Eye Cream before trying it but I had heard of the brand.

Claims: Reduces Fine Lines and Wrinkles, Lightens Dark Circles, Depuffs Eye Area, Tightens eye area, Nourishes and Hydrates.

The True Glow Eye Cream includes organic and natural ingredients, is vegan friendly, made in the U.S.A. using sustainable energy and cruelty free.

There are some ingredients that were chosen for the Valentia True Glow Eye Cream that are believed to work together to achieve optimum results. Per Valentia those ingredients are:
– ASTAXANTHIN: A powerful antioxidant that increases moisture levels, smooths fine line and wrinkles, and restores elasticity to the skin.
– RESISTEM: Natural Plant Stem Cells repair and protect the skin from harsh environmental pollutants and stress related aging.
– VITAMIN C: Leaves the skin smooth and visibly brighter for a well-rested and bright eyed look.
– ORGANIC ROSEHIP OIL: Provides intense hydration to reduce the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles.
– ARNICA: A key anti-inflammatory agent to the restorative process that works to diminish the appearance of dark circles.

The ingredient list is quite lengthy so I have not researched them all. The preservatives are 3 of the last 7 ingredients: Glyceryl Caprylate, Ethylhexylglycerin and Lonicera Japonica (Honeysuckle) Extract.

Valentia True Glow Eye Cream has very nice packaging. The tinted glass container is good because some ingredients degrade over time due to lighting. The pump dispenser keeps the cream protected from air.

The eye cream is a peach color and has a light citrus scent that I find pleasant. The consistency is thicker than I anticipated considering the bottle has a pump. I use the eye cream morning and evening. It absorbs easily and there’s no irritation. My skin feels soft and it works well under makeup. My under-eye circles are courtesy of hereditary so I didn’t expect any changes there (and I didn’t have any). As with any skincare product I recommend taking a photo before you begin to use a new product, use it for 6-8 weeks then look at that photo to see if you notice any difference.

The only reason I'm giving this 4 stars is because my under eye area is so dry and my skin absorbs this (and most eye creams) like a serum. I still need to use a richer eye cream on top. But when I use this alone it still has nice hydration and I would recommend purchasing this product (I feel that the skin under my eyes is drier than the average person).

I was given the opportunity by Valentia to try this eye cream at no charge for my (honest) opinion so I decided to give it a try. I take product reviews seriously because I understand potential buyers are reading this and I want you to trust all reviews or articles I’ve written.

This Retinol serum is a combination of retinol and natural ingredients for a high-strength serum containing repairing agents for wrinkled, non-elastic, and stressed skin. It is designed to provide smoother-looking skin and rejuvenate aged and dull skin.

In addition to retinol, this serum contains Aloe, Hyaluronic Acid, Vitamin E and Green Tea for gentle and effective hydration. Hyaluronic acid is a glycosaminoglycan, a very long chain of disaccharides (sugars) present in all connective tissues that is responsible for retaining moisture. As we age, levels of hyaluronic acid fall—some say by as much as 50 percent. Genetics, smoking, and magnesium and zinc deficiencies appear to accelerate this loss, but it happens to all of us to some degree.

One of the benefits of hyaluronic acid is its effectiveness at maintaining healthy, youthful skin. The reason is because hyaluronic acid is an essential component of the skin. Thanks to its ability to promote collagen production and retain hundreds of times its weight in water, hyaluronic acid keeps the skin plumped up and hydrated.

The combined benefits of these ingredients make for an amazing anti-aging and nourishing moisturizer for your skin.

title: I like it, I don't love it.
text:
I like this brush because it's really soft. I use it in the morning just to give my skin a little more "help" and to get the circulation flowing. It really doesn't do much exfoliating so I still have to use a more abrasive brush at night to get off all my sunscreen and other dirt that accumulates during the day.

This brush pretty much never dries and I'm thinking it's because there is such a high count of bristles. I tried putting it on an absorbent surface after use, I tried wringing it out after using it- nothing seemed to work. It would still be moist the next morning. I don't like this because moisture breeds bacteria and if you're using it on your face you definitely DON'T want that bacteria wreaking havoc on your complexion.

Also, I've had it for less than a month and the bristle part has already come unglued from the wooden handle. Granted, it's very easy to just stick some glue in there and put the brush back together but still it's a hassle.This brush is pretty inexpensive so I guess you get what you pay for. If you're going to be using it regularly you need to make sure you're cleaning it really well every couple of days by boiling hot water and letting the bristles soak to kill any of the icky bacteria caused by the brush's constant moist state after use.

This brush will not exfoliate to a high extent but if you have really sensitive skin this is the brush for you.

title: Great when used daily
text:
I have shaved my head (with a razor) for the last 10+ years. In the last couple of years I've become lazy about it -- letting what hair I have grow out and get sloppy between shaves.

I bought the Conair CleanHead just over a month ago.

The day I got it I put it on to charge and shaved my head with a razor. Starting the next day and every day (but one) thereafter, I've shaved my head with the Conair using no attachments. Each morning I spend a few minutes shaving off the prior day's stubble and I have a nice, smooth head for the rest of the day. BUT if I skip a day (only did it once) the shaving time triples or quadruples.

I have to clean the razor after each use (taking it apart is easy and there's a brush included). I sometimes have to touch up tight spots around my ears but not often. It's great for stubble but sometimes misses longer hairs.

My scalp is smooth and feels good -- I don't have the nicks, scrapes or sensitivity of a razor shave.

I'm (always) on the lookout for something better but, for now, I'm quite happy with this device for a daily, full-head shave.

text:
This wig is more black than purple in real life, but I think it looks better that way. It seems to be a nice, high quality costume wig able to fit various head sizes. The tall braid standing up is thick and plump, not likely to deflate or fall over on its own, but it does make the wig a little unbalanced. A real person will be able to compensate easily, but my little foam head here was struggling.

This set came with a wig cap, earrings (one had a defect on the "gem"), a necklace that was lightweight, a spider clip for the hair, and two braid clips. I wasn't really sure what to do with the braid clips or how to clip them into the hair, as there didn't seem to be any flexibility in the prongs to get hair between them, but some searching revealed that they probably should be twisted up around the braid. I did that, as pictured, and you can see how I was able to hide the way the main braid was held in place with a rubber band at the end.

All in all, this was a fun little set that I think a fan of the movie Hocus Pocus will get a laugh at. It might not be the most faithful recreation, but if you don't have the time or skills to make this hairstyle for yourself, it will suit a cosplay nicely.

title: A great combo of sharp, smooth, and longevity
text:
First off, let me say that I did not buy it here at Amazon, but locally here in singapore.

Exceptional, is what i would call it. I'm certainly impressed.

To-date, i've used Gillette Platinums (blue,white box), Gillette 7 o'clock Super Platinums (black packs), Gillette 7 o'clock Super Stainless, Voskhod, Astra SP, Concord, Croma, amongst a few others.

I would place the Gillette 7 o'clock Permasharps at the same top tier with Gillette 7 o'clock Super Platinum (indian), and the Gillette Platinum (russian).

But any blade, like a woman, needs the right approach to bring out her/its best. Hence, i'll describe my shaving regimen. (a better regimen might bring out even more from this blade perhaps.)

1. I always have a hot shower before shaving, thus bringing out the hairs more.
2. I use the Rex Ambassador safety razor at a (extremely mild) setting of 1, thus contributing to the smoothness of the shave.
3. I use a combination of shower soap (bar) with sunflower oil (cooking), hand-lathered till the lather is thin but dense, not watery. No brushes, shaving creams, shaving soap, scuttles, etc....completely unnecessary.
4. I only go with-the-grain except for my neck. (which would certainly contribute to the longevity of the blade).

My stubble is hard and wiry and i do daily face and head-shaves. I also do a once-weekly body shave, and a daily front shave from chest to netherregions.

After the shave, i pat-dry the blade with a microfibre cloth, and then strop it against the cloth on all 4 sides a couple of times each.

Ranking
_______

Sharpness -
1. G 7oc Sp
2. G 7oc Permasharp tied with Gillette Platinum

Smoothness -
1. G Permasharp (gets smoother on 2nd and 3rd day) tied with G Platinum
2. G Super Platinum

Longevity (for both head and face-shaves in terms of days) -
1. G 7oc Permasharp - 8 and counting
2. G 7oc SP - 8
3. G platinum - 6-7

I judge the blade's longevity in terms of the degree to which i can get a clean shave with a single swipe. I always do a 2nd swipe just to get any tiny stubble that might be left behind, but the first swipe must perform at 95%. So when i say that a blade lasts for 6 days, i mean that i get 95% only after 2 swipes and not 1.

So, in sum, i definitely recommend this blade. I just picked up 300 yesterday, and will pick up more up to a thousand the next time i go to the shop where i get it from here in singapore. (cost : $9.00 sgd per 100 blades here.)

I bought the "Vanilla Rainbow Sprinkles" fragrance on another website, as a substitute for Bath & Body Works' "Confetti Cake Pop", which had been sold out everywhere that I had looked online. I was under the impression that the two scents would be similar enough so as to not make much of a difference. I was, unfortunately, very wrong.

"Confetti Cake Pop" is awesome, and it smells just like what the packaging says, "creamy cake frosting." Delicious! "Vanilla Rainbow Sprinkles", on the other hand, is one of the few Bath & Body Works' scents that I heartily dislike. For one thing, the vanilla scent is very muted; not in a good way, as in subtle, but in a bad way, like "I can barely notice the vanilla in this perfume." If that was the only thing about "Vanilla Rainbow Sprinkles" that was off, I could live with it.

After I had sprayed it on myself, however, I became aware that there was a strong under-note of alcohol. I do not wish to smell like rubbing alcohol when I put on scent. Just awful. That bottle will be going into the trash can, and I will not buy "Vanilla Rainbow Sprinkles" in the "mist" (or in any other B&BW product) ever again. It is disappointing, as I usually have good luck with Bath & Body Works, and I enjoy many of their fragrances. I have to also comment that, unusually for Bath & Body Works, the artwork on the product label is very dull and is rather uninspiring.

Looking for a sweet, fun scent that is good enough to eat? Instead of "Vanilla Rainbow Sprinkles", I would recommend Bath & Body Works' "Sugared Snickerdoodle", if you cannot find "Confetti Cake Pop".

title: Many probiotic side effects are due to release and growth too early in the gut.
text:
Personal experience that may or may not be helpful.

If you have IBS, you may well have small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO). In either case, taking a probiotic that is not enteric-coated or coated for release AFTER your small intestine may make your symptoms worse because you are recolonizing your small intestine (this includes Align, and most on the market).

This product is enteric-coated, so should release after the small intestines to avoid putting bugs in the wrong place. Read product info carefully to confirm enteric-coated, since they have other products. They also have liquid versions that will dump the bugs in your small intestine.

If you're microbiome is jacked up, BIG doses of any probiotic may mess you up. I used the 12.5 billion version of this product (available elsewhere) to avoid over-doing it and it seemed OK for me, but maybe not you (see other review on backing off 25 billion). Take home message is always start small. Tread lightly.

If you react, this may be rapid growth in your small intestine with bloating.

If you react, you may be reacting to the prebiotics in the product, not the probiotic itself. Avoid prebiotics initially if very sensitive.

These bacteria may release d-lactate (brain fog).

They may make you feel worse regardless particularly if you're sensitive to histamine in food, since these strains make histamine as a byproduct of normal metabolism.

Bifidobacteria may not do this to the same degree, but these again should be engineered for release later in the gut (maybe Pearls Adult 50+ or others). Pearls Adult 50+ contain only bifidobacteria similar to those in Align. Align dumps in your small intestine.

S. boulardii is a yeast and seems to be more tolerable (to me) that may help repair and get combat bad bacteria, but it will not of itself rebalance your bacteria.

title: Been using for years
text:
I bought my first box years ago (when I seem to remember it being the old packaging being labeled as brow safe?). I just finished up another box (3rd? 4th?) and noticed that it’s not meant to be used on the brows. It’s not difficult to keep far away from your eyes, just exercise caution.

I used to apply it for the recommended couple of minutes and got decent results, but now that I’m used to the performance I’ve left it on for as long as 40 minutes and have had the same color payoff but much longer lasting color. I have clear blonde brows despite being a natural dark brunette, so anything I can do to prevent fading helps.

Recommendations:
- Block/outline your brows with a white eyeliner before applying so you can just fill in the shape without having to be too precise with the actual dye- this also keeps skin staining within the area of the brow and less noticeable
- Dye at night or when you can stay in for a couple of days if you’re worried about skin staining
- Dont exfoliate the day of dyeing and the skin stain will come up easier
- use a cotton bud lightly dipped in skin salve/Vaseline to scrub up skin stain rather than washing it away to avoid early fading on brow hairs- even just applying a bit to brows and leaving it on for a while before wiping it away can really get it off much easier AND avoid irritating the skin
- wipe away areas you want to be lighter half way through your dyeing process (Ex: if you want the inner part of the brow to be lighter than the tail, wipe away some dye on the inner part and leave more to develop on the tail)
- You can reapply dye if you feel it didn’t tint enough in one session. Just leave any you didn’t use up on the counter and only discard extra after you’re satisfied with the color payoff (don’t save dye for another day, just go ahead and reapply right after taking off the first application if you feel you want more color)

title: Not a bad choice at all considering price point
text:
This is a pretty solid hair straightener considering the price point. One of my biggest pet peeves with cheaper hair straighteners is that the plates tend to not be smooth and you can feel it catching on your hair, basically a lot of times they don’t glide through like they should. However I did not have that problem at all with this one and It easily glided though my hair.

Holding it is easy and it feels comfortable in your hand. The temp adjusts from 300F-450F, and it heats up in about a minute. It has an auto shut off after 60 min, which is a pretty long shut off time but at least it has that built in. The button to control it is on the inside which I always prefer since that means I can’t accidentally press the button as I’m using it. The only downside with this is that it’s not good for creating curls or waves like most straighteners are these days. The shape of it makes it incapable of doing this. But overall I’m happy with it.

I've always used the least expensive model since I see no difference from the expensive ones, unless you are looking for "extras", like timer, lcd screen, etc. The vitality is a very good brush. I use the round head instead of the elongated. I rather brush my teeth with oral-b than any other eletric brush on the market. The sonic kind hurts my gum and it tickles a lot as well. Oral-B, and their entry level eletric brushes are the way to go. I can't brush my teeth with regular toothbrush anymore. Brush heads are cheaper on ebay but I found out they don't last as long as those you buy at grocery stores around $20 for 3. I buy the precision clean brush in bulk on ebay for around $1 each. They last a good 2 months. The ones at walmart/amazon and such last 3 months or more. The bad thing about the vitality rechargeable and all the older oral-b I own is that you need to recharge it after 3-4 days of 2-3 daily brushings. I think this is annoying. I didn't want to leave the brush recharging after every use. So I bought the ORAL-B Pro-Health that uses two AA batteries. It is simply AMAZING. The quality is the same as the rechargeables, but it is even better. The batteries lasts forever on the pro-health. I put 2 rechargeable AA (2000 MA) and the thing kept going and going without a noticeable lack of power for a good 2 months. It is the best. The vitality rechargeable brush gets very slow after 3-4 days. Not with the pro-health. Buy the pro-health. It is the way to go if you like this kind of ORAL-B design. Another thing is ORAL-B equipment lasts forever. I only have one eletric brush where the original rechargeable battery died on me. And since they are the entry level brushes, I just buy another one of the same. No need to buy another battery.
Again, go with the ORAL-B PRO-HEALTH eletric toothbrush.

title: Warped from Containing Polish Remover
text: After containing Mineral Fusion nail polish remover (one of the most popular, most effective removers on the market), this bottle stopped dispensing as well as it had. Upon inspection, we realized the acetone had started warping the all the parts so that the lid wouldn't totally close anymore, too much acetone started coming out per pump, and, most dangerously of all, the bottle itself had begun warping and starring. What's happening is it is liquifying the plastic and causing it to become molten, but on a very slow level, with the plastic molecules moving because of the organic chemistry of the acetone interacting with this particular type of plastic. It was only a matter of time before it bottomed out in my bathroom cabinet all over everything. Basically, this should be made of the same type of plastic as bottles that hold acetone and for long periods of time, at that. Furthermore, the straw should be of a sturdier material.

After a week I decided I absolutely LOVED these pieces because the post doesn't feel like it's eroding my enamel or my gums, and I think you literally have to be pulling on your jewelry and twisting it aggressively for it to really tear up the back of your lip. After my swelling has gone down I've realized the posts for these pieces are short enough for me to practically never bite them when I'm chewing and long enough for my lip to not feel in any kind of danger. The studs are sturdy and I really don't think they'll fall out. Only thing I'm sad about is that I lost the clear one in my haste to put another piece in my unhealed piercing.
