title: Great beginner sets!
text:
To start with: this is an actual great little starter kit. This offers people the opportunity to play with both gel and polygel, while coming with a small light. Being honest - when I first started working with gel I wasn't sure if I liked it or not, so a kit like this would have been super helpful.

The gels themselves have nice self leveling. The colors are nicely pigmented two coaters. They are fairly tacky, so make sure you put on a top coat (which I always recommend) or be prepared to wipe down with alcohol. They do take a bit longer to set, but they do set nicely.

The sequins are a nice touch, and the top coat and base coats are very close quality to others I have (similar to Beetles). The top coat isn't quite a no wipe, but it shines up beautifully with a little bit of alcohol.

The tools are perfect, and the polygel colors are beautiful. They set nicely, and file perfectly. The duoforms are in lots of good sizes, so I don't have any issues finding the perfect sizes (my hands are weird, each finger has different size which is annoying to need 10 different sizes, but hey.

I don't quite understand why there's the nail foils since there's no glue for the foils. The top coat isn't quite tacky enough for foils. The striping tape is a very nice touch.

The light works fairly well. The onyl problem is its a one button, so its only 45 seconds or 60 seconds. I have a lot of other lights, so while I was happy to try this one out, and it'll be great for travel, I like my bigger lights for other daily use.

Overall, this is a great little kit for trying out gels and polygels. I would advise that you pick up more files and a bigger light in the future with more settings and timers, but overall, this is great for getting started. The travel case fits everything nicely, and makes it convenient to take on vacation. The gels also last about 2 weeks which is a huuuuuge plus.

title: Horrible in every way, only for super sensitive skin. Will not give you exfoliation or deep pore cleansing
text: Four years ago I bought a generic version of the Clarisonic called the Nutrasonic. My little Nutrasonic quickly became my favorite four speed facial powerhouse. I loved my Nutrasonic (and still do) but sadly the company has decided to discontinue the brushes so my favorite little machine is no more. Hence I started shopping for a replacement and as before when I bought my Nutrasonic I was dead set on not getting a Clarisonic because of the high price of the machine. I came across the Philips Pure Radiance on Costco’s website and decided to order it thinking I would be happy with it since not only Costco but Amazon has rave reviews for the machine. I got the Philips yesterday and let me tell you this facial brush sucks big time. If you are used the battery operated facial brushes they sell at Wal-Mart, then you may like this weak inadequate machine, but if you are used to a powerhouse cleaner and exfoliater you will absolutely hate this machine as I did. First off, the Philips has only two speeds which are pretty slow. The brushes are super soft (even the supposed stiff pore cleansing brush) and the annoying timer that turns off the machine every 20 seconds to apparently remind stupid people to move to a different spot.  This machine was so weak and truthfully, I hated everything about this cleansing system as it did not leave my skin feeling clean what so ever. If you have super sensitive skin then perhaps this machine will be okay for you but those desiring a pore cleansing will be greatly disappointed. Beyond how weak the machine is in hindsight I should have thought about my current dilemma before ordering the Philips and that being the long term availability of brushes. Since facial cleansing systems are not Philip’s main seller I can guarantee that this machine will be like my Nutrasonic in a few years and have no brushes available. Sadly there is nothing nice I can say about this machine and can only say that if you are used to the Wal-Mart type of facial cleaners and not a Clarisonic then you will probably like this, but otherwise if you are used to the deep cleaning of a quality facial system you will certainly hate this machine. Of course I am taking this one back and have broken down to buying a Clarisonic for two reasons, the power of the machine and the future availability of the brushes. I can’t wait to get my new 4 speed Clarisonic Pro that I ordered off of E-Bay that cost me the same price as this Phillips did but will actually clean my acne prone aging skin.

I love these types of curls. They don't last a super long time, just 24 hours or less, but that's enough for me. **Tip I learned from someone else's review: take out the fasteners before rolling up each curl. Then, once it's rolled up tight, insert the fastener and close it. Do the same in reverse when you're ready to take the curlers out. Take out the fastener, then unroll your hair.** You'll find that your hair will not get stuck or pulled out like it would have if you tried to roll and unroll your hair with the fastener still inside the roller.
Another tip: don't wrap the hair too tightly around the curler. keep it loose enough so that the curler is not squished flat. That way you'll actually be able to put in and take out the fastener. Plus, your hair will dry faster if it was wet before curling.

title: Just OK
text:
I have used Norelco shavers for many years and prefer them to all other models I have tried. This review comes from much experience with the brand.

This Arcitec design looks fancy and works well, but gets three average stars because it really works no better than the previous non-space-age, less expensive designs. The 1050, 1060, and 1090 all operate the same, they just have a different display: none is better than the other, and don't waste money on the Cleaner accessory. It is fairly comfortable to hold (I prefer the feel of the original model because this is one is smaller), and looks fancy sitting on the counter, but it does not do a better job. It requires cleaning after each use as there is no space for the hairs. I have always cleaned my shavers after each use anyway. Unless you just want the apperance, it is not worth the extra money.

Technically: The triple-blade per round head (each cutter has three spinning blade areas) does not do any better than a double cutting blade. Kind of like a Saturday Night Live skit in the 70's, Jim Belushi said, "Buy a triple bladed razor. For those that will believe anything". Lift-and-cut is a ridiculous concept and a marketing ploy, but Norelco's do a nice job. Norelco went back to more diagonal openings with this model, which is good. Many other newer models have lots of little pin-holes which are worthless, as the hairs have no time to enter a small hole with shaving motion. You would have to set it directly on a hair to cut it. The less pin-holes the better.

Feel: The head design feels better on the neck, and has not caused razor-burn if I do not stretch the skin tight like I need to with the original model. It takes the same time to shave as my older unit, and I get no better results, no faster. It takes the same time to get a smooth shave, and the same persistance in some areas.

Function: It is a little bit easier to shave under the nose, above my mustache, but not a major difference. It is much harder to trim my sideburns with this unit as the heads almost cut my hair on my head above the ears the way it is shaped. Very poorly designed trimmer, so I use my older shaver for that.

Battery: Early, new battery life is good, as with most new battery devices. But, it states to not over-charge. Meaning, you need to be around when recharging to unplug it after it is charged; not good for those that shave and must go to work. The other units would shut off after charging.

Cleaner/Charger: Again, one needs to be around when it is finished to not over-charge. The cleaner is not necessary and a waste of time, money, and chemicals. I use a razor brush from an older unit, brush it out quickly over the wastebasket (one can't blow it out without getting hair dust all over the bathroom, and it can't be shaken into the wastebasket as easily as the older models), and I spray it quickly with Remington Silicone Lubricant (I can only find it at Wal-Mart, which is the only thing I ever go there for, by the way).

Overall: Buy it for looks and keep your old one in the drawer for sideburns. Nicer on the neck.

I would return it, BUT, it was a gift, AND I like the look of it. I know, I know!!

Update 12-29-07
I purchased a Braun 9595 through J&R on Amazon, and it has a 60 day trial return guarantee. This is the first micro-screen razor I have used and it is better in all respects to the Norelco Arcitec except for the fancy styling. It is fast and comfortable, and my face feels razor smooth. I was able to return the Arcitec and am really happy with this Braun 9595 model.

title: Purchased this item in Marshall's for $6.99
text: So as I have stated in previous skin care  product reviews, I am EXTREMELY vain. That is probably due to the fact that I suffer with Adult Acne. Never had acne until I reached my mid 20's. So as a fair skin woman in her mid 30's my focus is to lessen the severity of my outbreaks, and to keep my skin looking youthful and CLEAR! Like other women in my predicament I have spend loads of money on what seems like millions of products sometimes they work, then after a couple of months they cease to have any effect. So besides incorporating multivitamins into my life (B complex, Flaxseed oil, MSM, DMAE, etc) which I take pretty consistently, I drink plenty of water or as much as I can take, eat fairly healthy (no soda, no juice, no candy, no chips, little to no fast food) and of course I exercise. All these things will play into how healthy your skin will and can be! So on a recent trip to South Carolina, I ran into a Marshall's and I always check out the skincare section. Now within the last couple of months my skin will begin to clear up completely then BAM I will get a medium red nodule, or inflamed whitehead.... UGH! And though you are not suppose too I always pop mine to relieve the pain and pressure. I always do it with clean hands, and typical wash my face with my 10% sulfur soap I purchased here on Amazon. So when I ran into this Brightening product for $6.99 it caught my eye. With all the sulfur and scrubs and acne drying products my skin was looking pretty dull and kinda flaky. I needed something to help diminish my acne scars, moisturize and smooth out my skin... and the fact that this product claimed to help with anti aging was the icing on the cake... so I took it home and gave it a whirl.... its been about 2 1/2 weeks I have used this product 2x a day each day as it is not heavy and provides the extra moisture I need. I have noticed significant difference in the color and size of my scars. my skin feels smooth and soft. I feel good about this product sofar I have had no adverse reactions to this serum. With any product it takes a keen eye and diligence to becoming successful in your skincare goals. I will see how I feel about this product once I finish the bottle. If this product continues to show me positive gradual results I might purchase another product as this is cheap and effective. As we head into a new year I am looking to go more organic in my skincare products and spend alil less than I have this year and previous years.

title: Fight night sweats
text:
I've put up with night sweats for many years, toughing it out, tossing off sheets, occasionally running my hands under cold water or using a cold washcloth when it got bad. These pads are a perfect non-medication -- and dry! -- solution. I bought two. They stay by my bedside and when I get too hot, I place them under my knees or neck, wherever I think they will help. They are thin and comfortable and keep cool for several minutes, enough to cool me down. I've never put them in the fridge. That might be too much for me. A few minutes back out in the air, and they are ready to cool again. I've had them a few days, so this is not a review about their long-term reliability. I'll post back later on that. Four stars until I see if they continue to work.

A month later...
The pad works very well. It won't hold a chill forever, but usually enough to halt a hot flash or nightsweat. The room temp affects the success. It's summer and, although I have central air, sometimes it"s a bit warm (and my whole body temp is warmer) and the pad heats up faster. It also takes longer to cool down in that circumstance. That's why I'm glad I bought two. I don't fret about night sweats anymore. These are a good, affordable solution.

The best spots for me to place the pads are: back of my knees and under my feet.

title: Leaked Out
text:
I was excited to get my package today...but was quickly disappointed when I discovered that the toner had leaked all over the box and half of it was already missing.

NOTE: nothing in this box was sealed! The box itself wasn’t even sealed. The opening you see in the photo is literally a hole in the box (no plastic film) and none of the bottles had any kind of sealant or plastic wrap to prevent the lids from coming loose or the products from being tampered with. I suspect this is why the toner leaked out everywhere.

That being said, I tried out the products tonight and was highly impressed with the emulsion and the face cream. Both are heavy and rich and super moisturizing. A little goes a long way with the face cream as well so I think that tiny container will actually last for quite a while. The toner and essence were okay, but didn’t leave enough of an impact to really form any kind of first impression about them. I could honestly see myself buying larger versions of the emulsion and face cream though!

Despite my love for the emulsion, I had some difficulty getting it out of the container. It didn’t have a pump on it like the essence did and is of such a thick consistency that I was literally banging the bottle on the palm of my hand trying to use gravity to force it out.

All in all, the products are okay but the packaging and bottle style aren’t exactly top notch. I’m not fond of receiving unsealed products.

title: Not as good as the old Advantage
text:
I'm a long-time blade shaver, but every 3-4 years I go on an electric shaver kick and use it for about a year. I've never found a single electric razor that shaves as close as a blade, but I used to own a Norelco Advantage that gave a decently close shave that was pretty comfortable and didn't irritate my neck.

This is supposed to be the upgrade to the Advantage, but after just a few days of use my neck is chewed up far worse than it ever has been with any other electric. It's annoying enough that I'm not willing to "wait it out" for the 30-day trial period that Norelco recommends, and I'll be returning it next week.

That being said, I can see from the other ratings that many people have had a lot of success with this shaver. Part of my problem may be that I'm a shaving perfectionist and if I'm not getting a close shave in a given area I'll go over it again a few times until the hairs are cut off. It boggles my mind that I can run an electric shaver over a patch of stubble and the stubble will sit there, unaffected, as if nothing at all had happened. You don't see that happening with blades...

So in summary:
Pros: auto-filling lotion cartridge, waterproof, quick charging, does glide well over face (no irritation WHILE shaving, but boy you'll feel it later)
Cons: seems to cause ingrown hairs at a higher rate than its predecessors, very high neck irritation, lotion seems to drip off of razor head while shaving, not a very close shave. NO ELECTRIC IS EVER AS CLOSE AS A BLADE, so I wish that Norelco and Braun would stop claiming such.

title: Great Color That Lasts for HOURS!
text:
I usually don't wear more than mascara on a daily basis because I'm not a huge fan of my makeup smudging and fading halfway through the day. NYX's glam shadow sticks have completely changed my opinion about wearing eyeshadow on a daily basis and I'm extremely surprised with my results!

I've always found that powder eye shadow fades and smudges after a few hours without using a pricey primer, and even when I do use an eye primer the shadow near the crease of my lid always fades near the end of the day. These shadow sticks are AMAZING for their staying power! I've never had to touch-up my eye makeup when using them, since the pigment stays exactly where I put it. When I first received the package I swatched each stick on my forearm to test the color and see if I would have any reaction to it. Not only did they not irritate my skin, but the color stayed on my arm all night through an hour's worth of dishes and six hours working in a kitchen! I had five colored lines on my arm until the next morning when I finally decided to use makeup remover on them and take them off completely. In over ten years of wearing makeup I've never had that sort of result from any eye shadow from any brand.

These sticks are extremely easy to work with, even with how long they last! I've found it very easy to blend the pigment from these sticks with my usual brushes, and the colors in this pack compliment each other nicely. The colors themselves are somewhat metallic and very rich, even with only one layer. Each color glides on smoothly and evenly, just as easy as using a crayon!

NYX's glam shadow sticks are my new favorite eye shadow and I've actually been brave enough to wear them to work! I did receive these eye shadows at a discount but price doesn't change how long they last, nor does it effect my review.

I've tried a half dozen of their "recipes". All of their products provide the ultimate soak. No chemical additives whatsoever, only natural oils. The smell is strong when the pouch is opened, but transforms into a subtle but pleasant scent once in the water. I have a deep clawfoot soaking tub, and tend to soak for 45 minutes or so (adding more hot water now and then as I go along). For that I put a cup and half or so of the salts in, and it ends up being a wonderful bath! Put on some mellow music, burn a little incense alongside, and you'll be in heaven.

Skin becomes super soft and hydrated, not in the least bit 'perfumey', and my entire body/mind/spirit is so relaxed after. It's absolutely therapeutic!

It's probably more expensive than most, but very high quality, and worth not having chemical perfumes and additives. If you buy the larger 8lb bags, a few at a time, the cost approaches what most other products might cost and that's a very fair bargain for what you get.

title: Perfect
text:
As someone who travels 90% of the time, and shaves their head, this product is great. I've had to resort to shaving in front of hotel mirrors instead of using my "home" routine of shaving in the shower. This product fixed that.

It fits in my luggage nicely. Very durable, so far hasn't broken or scratch. I just toss it in with my shirts and slacks - no sharp edges on the mirror, so it hasn't damaged my clothes.

It hangs on all the shower heads I've used so far. You can slide the "hook" down the shower head too in order to help get the best angle for use (tilts the mirror forward and back, but there is no "up" range past perpendicular to eyesight).

It fogs up some, but a quick splash of water fixes it for a few minutes.

Great product, happy to be able to shave in the shower even when I travel now.

Update:

Been using this for quite some time now. Nothing has really changed from the original review. It doesn't have the fog-free effect like my home mirror, but a quick rinse in a hotel shower fixes the fog issue for a couple minutes. That said, it's not a miracle preparation and must be used twice a day on clean skin as the base layer to your daily moisturizers for it to work best. My throat skin was sagging and it was easily visible in photos taken while on a studio tour, I was horrified at my appearance and after significant internet research, felt that this product was capable of doing what I hoped for at a price-point I could afford. So I ordered it and used it lavishly the first, and happily within two weeks my sagging throat skin was again firmly up against my throat itself. As I've stayed with using it, it has remained so while used in tandem with the Anew Platinum face moisturizer line I've progressed to using. I also touch it to the circles around my eyes with it to firm them up, as well as on my brow-bone/upper eye lids to keep my lids off my upper lashes and also to harness under-eye bags from becoming puffy from restless nights. Again it's worked and my eyes've remained reasonably smooth and line-free by using it with the Anew Multi Performance Eye Cream that's worked well for me during the past couple of years. I believe most moisturizer users try to extend their beauty products by using them sparingly which underserves their intended purpose - I know I have! But to use it generously the first several weeks allows them to saturate & nourish our thinner, more delicate facial skin so it can be refreshed with these formulas intended to help us look our very best always. I used 2 bottles of this serum during the first month, then 1 1/2 bottles the next  6 wks, and have settled on not quite a bottle from 4 - 6 wks depending on the weather. With diligence and generosity this product has worked for me. As I'm now 60, and after a 36 yr career of working outside in all weather, I'm thrilled when people marvel that I'm actually my age because in their words, "you look so young!" I'm sold. Adds at least 5-minutes of goof-off time in my morning routine. I'll take every minute I can gather. Perseverance might payoff with a straight razor shave, but the time saved here to goof off in the AM pays off immediately!

It's revolutionary.

title: Nice Brush | Similar To We Love Doodles & Chris Christensen | Cats Love It | Easily Removes Hair
text:
If I didn't already own & love my "We Love Doodles" brand of big slicker brush, I would have rated this brush at a full 5 stars. Mostly what I don't care for this brush vs Doodles is the handle. It is a little more narrow so it's a teensy bit less comfortable to hold. I have carpel tunnel. I've been grooming cats furever & grooming English angora rabbits for well over a decade.

🐱For short & long haired cats, this brush works great. All of my cats love this brush & my Doodles brand. I can comb all of them except for my 14yo with a surprising amount of pressure & they roll around purring. Tons of hair gets picked up into the tines. Unlike some styles of brushes & combs, no hair is left behind around the tail area.

Removing the hair from the brush is very easy. Start at one side from the bottom to loosen & then move to the other side. Keep working your way around & it comes off in a nice clean loose mat. I actually prefer these types of slicker brushes over self cleaning brushes & also over brushes with the little plastic beads on the ends. If you groom your animal properly, you don't need little balls on the ends of the tines. Those balls also make it a little harder to get the brush fully clean of hair.

Cosmetically, I like the look of the brush much better than my Doodles brush. This is all black with a more classy branding in small white text on the head. We Love Doodles is blue & loudly brands itself on the head.

🐰I don't recommend this style of brush for English angora rabbits. I have found that my bunnies seem to be more comfortable with smaller slickers with shorter tines. You'd think with their dense long coats, you'd want something large with long tines, but it really doesn't work out like you'd expect. At least for me it doesn't.

🐰Recommended for English Angora Rabbits:

🐇Doggy Man sells a small soft slicker brush that my angora rabbits love. It's plastic with a little blue ring on the handle. I have purchased/replaced many of them over the years (the handles tend to break over time) because they work well.
🌐 https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B001NLVFH2
🐇I also recommend if money allows, a small slicker brush by Chris Christensen. I've never needed to replace it.
🌐 https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B00GU7NKWW

Personally, I'd shop between this brand (Rita's), We Love Doodles, & Chris Christensen. Chris Christensen is top of the line. They are worth it if you have the money. We Love Doodles has been the middle ground for me. They were originally priced at $50, but the price has been a lot lower for a while now. Rita's is currently the second most expensive & probably the lowest quality of the three brands. However, I've been using it for the least amount of time, so it's too early to know for sure. So far I like all three.

title: great set of hair clips--flexible hold and durable for styling
text:
I LOVE these!! I have recently gotten into dyeing my hair crazy unicorn colors and I've gotten sick of ruining my really expensive hair clips with all of the permanent dyes. So I decided to invest in this 6-piece set of clips since I've seen my hair stylist use these when she is separating my hair into different pieces.

Anyway, I have really long and thick hair. So when I'm dyeing my hair, which I do at home, I really need to section the hair pieces off to make sure I get all of the strands saturated with color. Otherwise, well, I'm not really into striped hair at the moment and uneven dye jobs that LOOK like I did it myself at home after drinking too much wine ;)

I got the RED color because I have purple hair and wanted the clips to stand out. I do not plan to wear these out of the house--they are only for my styling needs at home. Otherwise, I would recommend getting a darker color because the plastic isn't super nice or stylish looking. I like that these clips open easily and don't have a super strong grip. Some of my clips are way too tight and I end up pulling my hair out or getting my hair stuck in the coils. I like the more flexible feel of these and that they have more give, so I can move them around. Even though they are flexible, they still hold the hair in place, but just do it less harshly, if that makes sense.

I like the set of 6 because I tend to lose track of my clips and so this way, I will have a nice sized supply and won't always be running around my house searching for clips.

I was able to purchase this item at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased review. I hope you found my review helpful and that I provided enough detailed information so that you can determine whether or not this product is right for you and your lifestyle needs. title: Excellent for price, but somewhat misleading advertisement
text:
I just received this dermatoscope yesterday. For the price, it is excellent. It is a simple to use, contact dermatoscope that gives the user a bright, clear image of skin lesions. I like that it is LED since those seem to last forever, and it even has a lifetime guarantee on the light source. It is comfortable to hold and the carrying case fits well in my white coat.

My reason for not giving 5 stars is that the product description claims that it can be used with or without oil. I suppose this is technically true, as I use alcohol as my immersion fluid of choice. However, if this scope is used without any immersion fluid (as implied by "oil-free epiluminescence microscopy"), it is basically just a 10x magnifying glass. The purpose of dermoscopy is to help visualize structures below the stratum corneum. If the light is not polarized (which it is not in this dermatoscope), then an immersion fluid is necessary to reduce light reflection/refraction/scatter by tiny irregularities at the skin surface in order to see the deeper structures. If you want a true oil-free dermatoscope, you will need one with polarized light (note that these are generally much more expensive and do not necessarily produce a better image). I truthfully did not expect the claim "oil-free" to hold true, but purchased it anyway since I don't mind using immersion fluid and the price cannot be beat. Therefore, I'm not disappointed, but if you are considering purchasing this mostly due to the "oil-free" claim, I'd advise against it.

Basically, if you want a dermatoscope that will give you a great image at a great price, this is your product. If you do not want to use oil or another immersion fluid, make sure you purchase a dermatoscope that is polarized.

Update: October 2013 - After using my dermatoscope for three and a half years in residency and private practice dermatology, the contact plate (where the glass contacts the skin) broke. When I contacted the manufacturer they responded quickly and even offered to send me a free replacement. I continue to be pleased with this dermatoscope and the customer service that stands behind it.

title: It actually does something.
text:
So, essences have always been a bit of a mystery to me (and, honestly, seemed like hokum) but my curiosity always led me back to research them. I've even bought them over the years and abandoned them because I just didn't know how to use them or if they were working. (And these are other best sellers with high price tags.) I finally revisited essences, caved in, and bought this super seller just to see if there was a fuss to be made over it. There is.

The very first time I applied it, I had a minor healing blemish on my cheekbone and it tingled at that spot. (Cool, it's not just water, lol.) I applied all my other stuff and knew it at least imparted moisture - my skin felt supple and hydrated. I noticed a change after just about a week using this - my skin was more even, a bit smoother (I have roughness on my cheeks that never seems to go away, no matter what), and dewy. I went camping for a few days - the dirty kind - and, after neglecting it, my skin needed help. I noticed everything bounced back much faster than it ordinarily would. I typically get a breakout after a trip like that but my skin stayed clear, it was just rough and sallow. Once home and finished with my usual routine, everything was back to normal and radiant again.

I know there are conflicting thoughts on how best to apply it; I won't put it on a cotton pad as I feel that would just waste too much product. (I first used this on May 6th and the picture is from 3 days ago - that's ALL I've used in about a month.) Right now I'm using one little drip of product for my whole face and neck; I just pour it in my hand, pat my hands together, and apply to a slightly damp face after toner. I must be experiencing what people are describing as a "water burst," because I put that tiny amount on my face and it's like I'm splashing water from a running faucet, that's the only way I can think to describe it; like the amount of wetness I'm getting exceeds the amount of product I used. I'm going to put some in a spray bottle with a fine-mist nozzle and use it that way, which is also how I'm going to travel with it. (Though, I've traveled with this large bottle and it's never leaked - and it lays on its side in my bag.)

For the price and the small amount I use, I will absolutely be repurchasing this.
(For reference, my once very-oily skin became dry then combo over this last winter, and now it's back to moderately oily, so it runs the gamut. I also have some unevenness, roughness on my cheeks, and dullness - all of which are improving everyday, and even my one or two monthly hormonal blemishes have been minimal and, if I get any small breakout, it's gone in a day or two and never fully forms to begin with.)

Update 10/23/17: the 2nd picture is from last night; more than 5 months of daily use (sometimes twice a day)
Update 4/12/18: the 3rd picture is from last night - May 6th will be a year since I bought this bottle and I still have about 1/4 left. (Sorry, can't get those pictures upright no matter what.)

title: A True Gentleman's Walking Stick
text:
Alpacca is also named German Silver or Nickle Silver. Consisting mostly of copper, nickle and zinc content. In my brief research I find that Alpacca does not contain any actual silver. Though some may be silver plated. But do not think of it as cheap imitation silver. It is more akin to a subset of brass.

This Alpacca cane is the pricier big brother to the plastic headed walking stick of the same design. The plastic brethren of this stick was love at first sight. The flared head and modest fluting simply screams elegance. Nowhere have I found a more elegant walking stick for the 'top hat' era.

As reported with flared head sticks, it is better suited for show. The slightly rounded top makes putting any kind of real pressure uncomfortable without leather gloves. However, it does provide modest balance if weight bearing is not your walking issue. The silvery smooth head does not make the cane top heavy.

The rubber tip is pretty standard and is useful for standing the 3/4" wide cane on flat surfaces. On the negative side, it takes away from the distinctiveness and gives an "old man" quality. I ordered my cane through a vendor who does silver ferrules (plated brass tips) and upgraded the business end of this cane to become a "Gentleman's Walking Stick". Silver ferrules raise the value and elevate the distinctive beauty.

This Alpacca cane lacks the distinctive charm of a chrome collar. My vendor states he routinely heats up such heads for removal, but the extra cost hardly seems worth the upgrade. It was mostly due to removal of the head. Unlike the screw top plastic cane, the Alpacca head is hollow and intended for permanent mounting, using pitch.

As it stands, this cane is suited for mild assisted walking. Use it more for classy strolls, theater, special occasions and dancing. Do not forget the white leather gloves!

Addendum:
On Saturday, 2/7/2015 I finally revealed this walking stick for a big birthday celebration. My black and white clothing style makes me look good, but there is a "whoa" factor when seen with this stick and a pair of white leather gloves. It helps that I had the tip refined with a ferrule and small rubber tip. I love it.

I love blending lavender in particular with chamomile, as it has an almost instantaneous calming effect. Also love to blend it with bergamot, ylang ylang, mandarin, and a drop of lime.

The bottle is very large, a dark brown color to protect the oil from UV rays which can damage the oils and decrease the shelf life. My favorite way to dispense oils is with the eye dropper (the euro droppers found in smaller bottles tend to gush several drops at once, so that’s definitely not my preference) – you can really control how many drops you dispense with these eye droppers.

title: Great, but use before showering
text:
I bought this trimmer after my old Norelco stopped charging. For the record, I maintain a full beard with this. Overall, I am satisfied with the product, but there are some caveats.

Vacuum: Like me, you may be interested in the included vacuum, rather than getting hair all over the place. It works pretty well for this! I'd say about 90% of the hair is trapped in the canister, about 3% on the sink, and about 7% left in my beard. For this reason, I recommend using the trimmer before you shower. Otherwise, you will get little hairs all over your shirt during the day. If you only have a goatee or similar, it may not be quite as bad. It's not much hair, but the little vacuum can't solve everything.

Noise: The noise level is loud, but not really any noisier than an electric toothbrush. To me, it's really no big deal. With the bathroom door closed, you can only hear it when close to the door anyway. I even run it in turbo mode most of the time, and still don't have an issue with this. Of course it would be great if it were completely silent, but really it's not that bad.

Trimming: Like all Norelcos, it does a great job trimming. The included adapter(s) handle just about everything I could imagine needing. I am a hairy guy, and have not felt any pulling or ripping of the hairs, just a clean trim.

Power: I typically get several weeks worth of trimming (every 2-3 days) on a single charge. To maintain the battery, always ensure you fully drain it before recharging. Using turbo mode drains it slightly more quickly. I can go a whole vacation without needing to recharge, which is nice, but the included travel bag is handy just in case.

So, overall I'd give it 4.5 stars, only because of the leftover hairs. It would be nice to have a slightly more powerful vacuum, but I realize it's difficult to get the hairs that are trapped in a beard. I love the trimmer, and have not seen anything else out there that would beat it.

text: I received this product a few days ago but wanted to use it more than once before writing my review.  I also wanted to have my daughter try it as well, because we have two different skin types.  I was given the opportunity to try this product as part of a promotional program at a discounted price in exchange for writing an honest and unbiased review.  I wanted to insure that the review I gave was accurate - I know that money is hard to come by these days and I wanted to be as accurate as possible when describing the product.  It arrived well packaged and in a timely manner.  The box holding the tube looked sturdy and professional - it looked like what you would expect from a high quality product.  I product dispenses easily and is easy to apply to the skin.  It goes on smoothly and evenly, doesn't dry out of make your skin feel tight, and doesn't have a strong or unpleasant odor.  My daughter and I tried the mask together - I have very dry skin, along with some fine lines and wrinkles, her skin tends to be oily and she had a few blackheads and larger pores.  We left our masks on for 15 minutes and washed them off with warm water.  The mask was very easy to remove and left our skin feeling very soft and looking radiant.  An additional bonus for me is the fact that mask contains argan, avocado, and jojoba oils.  Those added oils left my skin well nourished and moisturized.  I applied a light moisturizer because it didn't feel like a heavy one was needed.  My daughter was also pleased with the results.  She had concerns that the additional oils may cause her skin to break out or leave it feeling oily.  The mask washed off her face very easily, her skin felt smooth, her blackheads were gone, and her skin looked radiant.  We concluded that this mask is helpful for any skin type and we are planning another mother/daughter spa day soon.  We both liked the product and plan on continuing to use it.  I can recommend it without hesitation.  It's a great product!

title: Has artificial fragrance, smells amazing
text:
TLDR: GET THIS mask if you know you dont react to fragrance and simply like the smell of honey. DO NOT get this mask if you are looking for a mask with lots of honey and no added fragrance ingredients.

My skin loves honey. I have therefore tried many honey masks in pursuit of one that my face loves the most. I almost returned this face mask because when I recieved it, one of them seemed to have leaked through the plastic package they were bundled in. However, after deciding that my face needed honey and it wasn't really worth it to return it, I decided to give these guys a go.

Let me first say that this mask is the best smelling mask I have tried yet. I cant believe how lovely it smells, it took me back a bit. This concerned me of course as when something smells amazing it usually has fragrance added to it. When looking at the ingredients, I found that it does have "fragrance" in the ingredients, though it is farther down on the list of ingredients so it is not very much.

Near the bottom too, however, is propolis. Which is the only ingredient related to honey in this mask. Which was rather disappointing as this means this mask has hardly any honey in it.

I probably wont reorder this unless my skin somehow loves it.

First off, I love the color, it looked just like the picture online. The blue is a calming baby blue, almost like a light wash denim. They were easy to apply. I did have to trim one of them because I have a more boxy nail shape on one of my fingers but that's nothing a pair of scissors can't fix. The alcohol prep pad was very thick and easy to use. The nail file was also solid quality for a disposable file. The strips were able to be applied removed, and readjusted without messing up the strip or your nail.

Now for some negatives. Most of this stuff is not bad, its just coming from someone who has been using color street for a few years now. First off, these are single sided nail strips so you cant easily get 2 uses out per side. Separating the nail strips from each other is a bit of a challenge since the protective plastic is a little thick. Overall these strips were a little thick, so filing was hard. Lastly, the blue almost seems printed on, if you stretch the nails a little, the color shows up more white and it looks printed and not solid nail polish.

With all that in mind, I would say none of the negatives are deal breakers. I just wanted to list them so you knew what you were getting into. The sunflowers are nail stickers that I bought off Amazon.

I started using the Wen Tea Tree Cleansing Conditioner when I saw an infomercial about it and thought it might help with my dry hair and scalp issues. I initially bought a bottle of the regular Wen Cleansing Conditioner from the Wen TV infomercial and while the product was lovely it was less than wonderful for my dry itchy scalp. I had been using Neutrogena T Gel Shampoo which helped but was rather harsh and drying. While I was on Amazon searching for more Wen products I found the Wen Tea Tree Cleansing Conditioner. This Wen product said it would address my dry, itchy scalp and gently cleanse and conditions my dried out hair. Wen delivered on this promise and more! I am coming to the bottom of my fourth 16 ounce bottle and just saw a one gallon size advertised on Amazon. In spite of the expense I think I may just buy the gallon as my hair has never been this silky smooth and easy to style even though I now have a longer, shoulder length bob haircut.
I especially like the fact that I can use the Wen as a leave in conditioner if I want to simply by doing a second wash and partial rinse out at the end of my luxurious Wen Tea Tree shower. Unlike other leave in conditioners I have used in the past, Wen does not leave the same heavy residue that interferes with my final styling product. It only makes my styling product work better and my blow dry session no longer turns into a scorched earth session! Wen also smell marvelous due to the Tea Tree Oil. The regular Wen Cleansing Conditioner also has a nice light scent. I only wish Wen was easier to find and purchase. title: Nice Shave...but beter than a razor?
text:
At various times in my life I have rotated between using a razor vs a cordless shaver. While I prefer the closeness of a razor a cordless shaver does save time and money. The Arcitec 1090 is Norelco's high-end cordless shaver that has oodles of features.

Likes-

- Time display showing remaining battery life.
- Ease of cleaning the heads after use
- Suction cups on the base to hold the unit firm to counter-top
- Nick-free shaving
- The charging pod makes an ideal traveling case

Needed Improvements and/or dislikes-
- Not the closest shave - after shaving my face feels similar to what it is like 12 hours after using a razor
- Not sure why there is such a large cost difference between the Arctitec 1090 and the 1050. The 1090 has a time display and the charging pod, but I have hard time seeing that as to justifying the cost difference.
- Not sure if this product is actually an upgrade from the older "Lift-and-Cut" technology they previously advertised. My impression is that the new shave is about a wash with the old one.

Final Summary- While I enjoy the ease and comfort of the Norelco Arcitec 1090 I am not sure if the added features make it worth the additional cost over the 1050 - and thus costing it one star. However, as a whole I have no problems giving the product a hearty endorsement!

title: It actually works!  This is pretty amazing on my curly hair!
text:
I am always sceptical when I see advertisements on TV for products that seem 'AMAAAAZZZZING! MUST BUY NOW!!'
I wasn't too sure what to expect with this. I thought it was gimmicky, but I am happy to be proven wrong.
This is so much easier to use than a flat iron.
I like that it has a digital LCD that shows you what temperature the brush is heating up to. It gives the heat range that your hair styling should be at depending on thickness, etc. I set mine to 230, the hottest setting and it worked great for my thick, curly hair.
It heats up very quickly and the hand grip is comfortable. The cord rotates from the end and the grip on the back of the wand feels nice in the hand.
The rubbery nubs on the ends of the bristles offer some flexibility, but they are not as flexible as your hairbrush. They are also shorter, too.
The way that you do this is to start with clean, well brushed hair. As the bristles are short, they will not detangle for you. Have your hair prepped and ready. If you use a smoothing serum, it would be perfect to add it before you start with this.
You simply brush it over your hair like you would a hairbrush. You can brush from underneath or on top to make sure that all the hair gets close to the heated plate of the brush.
You can spend more time on areas that you want straightened more but I found that my doing my hair in pieces (held up with an alligator clip) worked best for me.
In order to get to the roots at the scalp, it was very easy. The brush is easy to angle towards the scalp and it gets about 1/2" away from the scalp easily and starts straightening from there.
If you hair is damp, you will see some steam, but you'd expect that with a curling iron or flatiron, too.
This actually worked so well, my kids wanted to try it out and they loved it!
The only concern that I had was that if you hair is the type to come out when you brush it, it will come out when you use this, too. The issue was removing the hair from the straightener. It is HOT. I had to work quickly to sweep the excess hair from the brush to toss. I will keep a wide tooth comb by this the next time I use it so I can run it over the bristles and remove the hair.
All in all: I give this a strong thumbs up!
I can't speak about the others on the market, but this one really does what it says it will do. It is way better than a flat iron. It covers more ground and feels more comfortable in the hand. Its a natural movement to brush your hair and this is no different.
Excellent new beauty tool! Very happy that this does what it claims to do! Part of my daily hair regime now!

The power cord is much too short and I had to use an extension cord to give myself some wiggle room away from the wall outlet. title: Looks delicious and smells great!
text:
After years of mistreating my hair with hair color products and a bleaching mishap a month ago, I was looking for something to re-fortify my hair while conditioning and giving me extra moisture. So I bought the Hairgurt Intense Repair Deep Conditioner in Almond honey. Let me just tell you that it really does look edible!! And it smells edible! It's not a strong smell and it leaves no trace of scent afterwards. The texture is also that of food--it looks and feels like whipped butter.
But we don't buy this to eat it so how did my hair do? My hair did very well but not better than with other less costly products. That is why this gets 4 stars instead of 5. My hair is normally wavy but is not coarse. Due to hair coloring as I mentioned, it had taken a beating and my wave actually diminished but my hair became coarser and very frizzy. After using this hairgurt the first day, my hair did feel smooth afterward for the rest of the day. It dried a bit frizzy but not much. I do not blow dry my hair. However, after going to bed at night, sleeping on cotton pillowcase, my hair was super coarse and frizzy the next day. I did not give up. I used the treatment for 3 more days but always with the same result. I've had better results with other treatments I bought at a local beauty supply store. However the hairgurt DOES work, if only for the day. Maybe it will be better with continued use and if I continue and get better results, I will then update my review.
Please ask any questions and I will do my best to answer. Thank you.

title: Still a classic quality Norelco trimmer.
text:
I used to have an old Norelco trimmer that used for years until it just wouldn't charge anymore and bought this as the "new and improved" replacement and for the most part . . . it is.
Here is the short:

Pros: Classic Design, Same quality and function, powerful vacum
Cons: Not good for trimming to skin w/o Guard.

The Long:

Its form, design and cut remind me of my old Norelco (which is great) with only one major difference, the vacuum. In order for the vacum to work there is a plastic vacum "sleeve" or "guard" that goes up to the teeth. The other reviewers complained about close trimming without the full guard and I do agree that it is awkward to pull down the vacuum sleeve for a close trim but I found that on both this model and my old one, the teeth on the trimmer were too big for a comfortable close trim anyway, so I do not use that feature. I instead use a fine tooth slid-up trimmer on another shaver for that. I disagree with the noise complaints, I thought the vacuum was only slightly louder than the actual trimmer and there was plenty of suction at the lower setting, which you can't hear over the trimmer. Overall, a great classic Norelco trimmer.

title: Weak sticks
text: These cotton swabs have pushed the limit of lowering quality beyond what I can accept.  The length of these swabs is 1/8" shorter than the traditional size, though it's got about the same amount of cotton as most Chinese swabs.  There's still about four out of a hundred that will snap due to wood grain weakness, but I understand that's inherent in the wood, itself, as wood is a natural product and has inconsistencies that you need to accept if you're going to use the product.  The problem with these swabs is that they come on a wooden stick the thickness of which is a whole, new low.  I've been using cotton swabs on wooden sticks for three decades and I've never before met wooden sticks this thin and weak before.  With these swabs you've got a high risk of breakage even with the sticks that don't have wood grain issues simply because of how thin and weak they've made the sticks.  If you only intend to use swabs for extremely light pressure work these are fine, but they can't handle the pressure of normal or average tasks.  They've skimpped on quality a little too much for me to recommend this product.  I would not buy them again.

text:
This is a very thin, clear oil. It isn’t as thick as baby oil and runs almost like water. I would never put oil or an oil-based product on my skin because it clogs the pores. Some people might be able to get away with it, but even though I have dry skin, my skin will break out if I put oil on it, so I have skipped that test. I did rub it into my hands and it dries fast without leaving an oily slick.

What I did use this for is my hair, which is very thick and very dry. After shampooing, I poured a little bit of the oil into my hand and rubbed my hands together. Then I ran my hands through my hair, keeping the oil away from the scalp area. Afterwards, I blew my hair dry then applied more oil. Usually, I apply a gel in the same manner that calms the frizz and leaves my hair with a nice shine to it. However, the oil did not produce the same results. My hair still had flyaway ends with no gloss to it. My newly washed and dried hair always looks better the next morning after the hair product has had a chance to calm the frizzy hair shafts, but the morning after I used the oil, the results were no different than the night before.

I’ll stick to my gel product to end the frizziness of dry hair.

I've seen these for as little as $40 but most on Amazon are about $60. Installation was simple. I just used a thin flathead screwdriver, popped out one end and used my keys to hold it open (if you don't put something in to hold the one side it will pop back in when you go to open the other side). text:
Read my full review here http://www.fashionbeyondforty.com/2014/09/bella-bear-beauty-products-review.html
I am going to be straight up with you all. When I found out I was receiving these products to review I was sort of nervous. For one thing I have not used an eyelash curler since I was a teen. Second of all, I was really not sure at all about the hair remover. It looked like something that would be used in torture. Now that I have used them, (after my daughter took the initial test run and she turned out okay) I love them!

First of all they are pretty tools in pretty boxes! They are so girly and pretty and pink, and red, and I love that! I thought that being pink that my husband would leave them be as he is always using my tools, but nope, he got a splinter woodworking tonight and came out after getting it out of his skin and asked where the pink tweezers came from. I gave him the run down about it and he said they were a lot better than our other tweezers, which for the record were pretty good too!

Now I will say, the hair remover can be a bit painful but no more painful than trying to tweeze those delicate areas. It does the job a lot faster too. I have fair skin and light facial hair so unless in the sun you can barely see it but in the sun I look a bit furry, even at my lip line. I have used the hair remover on my upper lip and corners of my mouth and while it didn't feel great, it was not too bad and now I have a smooth lip! I also did my hairline and face. It works after you get the hang of it which didn't take long to do.

I was surprised with the lash curler. I remember the curlers from my youth, always sticking on my lashes, pulling them out, but I also do not remember them having the nice slick black stuff on them. I guess we have come a long way in non stick surfaces! I also learned my lashes are naturally longer on my right eye than my left. Interesting, never noticed that before. I can now have lovely curly lashes before applying mascara!

Lastly, the tweezers ... nothing can compare to a great tweezer! I hate when the ends do not come together completely, useless. These tweezers are perfect and really get the job done.

I like having my "girly" tools now, they are pretty to use, and I know it seems shallow, but when I have to pluck, tweeze, and remove hair from my face, I prefer to do it with something pretty rather than utilitarian!

And yes for the record I did get this free but I would never review something I do not personally enjoy using.

title: I REALLY hope they bring the original formula back because this new version is NOT equal to the original and certainly is not be
text:
I just bought this product at a Dollar Tree store, which USED TO carry the original formula of this lotion. I REALLY hope they bring the original formula back because this new version is NOT equal to the original and certainly is not better.

I am a BIG lotion user. My skin doesn't do well without it. I can't have dry feet and hands, it just doesn't work for me. I bought Suave lotion for years because of the agreeable cost (I'm cheap) and the acceptable quality of the product but when I lucked up on Dermasil at Dollar Tree, I found a gold mine! This stuff was top notch and I haven't looked at Suave since finding it, even though it costs a lot more. It was creamy, rich and thick, didn't evaporate and leave you reapplying continually and it was unscented, which made it great for adding your own fragrance to or using on your face if you're sensitive to fragrance. I routinely would buy 10, 10 oz tubes at a time just to keep a good supply on hand, to satisfy my pack rat compulsion and to take advantage of the price. I keep one at work, one in each of my travel bags, I keep some in a smaller container in my purse, I use it on my face with no negative results, it's great for my feet, you don't need a whopping amount of it, the original is just wonderful stuff!! So this weekend I went hunting for more and happened upon this version. The store only had two tubes of it and they were not 10 oz but I bought them anyway. As soon as I tried it I was extremely glad that I only had two tubes of this stuff to get through. It is not as thick or rich, it is not matte like the original either. It's kinda glossy as it comes out of the tube. And you know how you can feel cold air so much better when you use perfumed lotion? Check! And the crowning offense? It has a smell. A hint of chemical to brighten your day. The original has a faint hint of this same smell, which I only noticed after meeting the new version but this version has it a lot stronger. I wouldn't go near my face with this stuff. It's awful in comparison with the original...AWFUL!! I frankly don't know what I'm going to do with the two tubes I bought. I'll think of something. I'm just glad they were from Dollar Tree because I haven't lost any money to speak of.

If you can find the original, grab all that you can! The original formula is STILL wonderful lotion. This new so-called "Advanced Treatment" molarky, however, is for the birds. I don't know what happened, the good ingredients shot up in price, ceased to be available or what but every formula change is not a GOOD formula change. Uuuuuuugh, that smell...

title: works well, but has a minor design flaw
text:
I have used ionizing brushes for over 30 years—since they were first sold by Sharper Image. The negative ions work very well to flatten the surface of the cuticle of each hair, making the hair less likely to break or split, and also softer.

This particular brush works well, but the one I received has a minor design flaw: the brush part pops off so easily that I have to hold it tight with my thumb, making it less ergonomic than it might be... not an issue for me. As for the vibrating part, I couldn't tell, but that's not what I bought it for. This brush generates NO heat, which is exactly what I wanted. Unlike some similar products, there are NO seams that could catch the hair.

TIPS FOR ALL IONIZING BRUSHES:
(1) if they don't need electricity (cord or batteries), they're not the real deal
(2) heating elements, just like heated blow-drying, tend to dry out your hair and make it more brittle: even oily hair can get dried out
(3) brush your hair SLOWLY to get the best result
(4) if your hair is flatter after using it, and you don't like that, bend over and brush it upside down to get more volume

title: Follow the instructions!!!
text:
First let me say: READ my review CAREFULLY to avoid an eyebrow malfunction like I experienced. Second, the tint works great!! Third, I’m grateful for the bike chain degreaser I still had hibernating in my cupboard, 20 years later. Read on:

I tinted my eyebrows thinking that it was OK to get some on the skin above and below my eyebrows and that it would wash off easily. After all, when I self-color my hair, the excess color wipes off my skin with no problem!! Ya, nope not true of this eyebrow tint. The excess wouldn’t come off!!! In hindsight, I had a very Low IQ moment. The instructions do tell you to test a patch of your skin before using it on your eyebrows. I didn’t do that. You should!!

After I washed the tint off and attempted to wash the excess tint off, I saw a female Groucho Marx in the mirror. I tried removing the excess tint with 3 different face soaps, then regular body wash soap, then baking soda, then toothpaste.

Tier 2: Shout with bleach, Comet spray w/bleach. Then Lysol wipes... moved onto nail polish remover. Then hairspray. But what actually did it was the 🚲 bike degreaser I use on my bike chain. Thank goodness because I was about ready to just dump an entire Costco-sized bottle of bleach on my face and let a higher power step in!!

Worth noting: it was an eyebrow tint product from Slovenia so it probably doesn’t have the same ease of removal standards as American hair color products!

Great product but just be very careful not to overdo it and don’t get it on the skin near your eyebrows!! Aim carefully at JUST your eyebrows!!

PS. I am sparing you a picture of my mishap...you’re welcome!! 😊🤣

title: Rusted within 48 hours
text:
I used the small, black five star g-whiz twice in 48 hours. I rinsed the blades off with tap water. Next morning, the blades had rust on them. I got a full refund by Amazon since I bought it directly from them. End of story.

Wahl customer support, I want to buy and like your products, but now I've got to ask which of your products do not have this problem. I just want a cordless battery powered trimmer that won't rust. As sales and business owners, it really doesn't make economic sense to sell something with metal in it guaranteed to rust as soon as it hits water, since people are going to do a 180 and get a refund.

Maybe the metal does have the benefit of being easier to machine and result in higher quality blades, but it's really not an option to have easily oxidized metal in a product that gets washed frequently.

I'm open to buying Wahl trimmers again, but I need recommendations for which models won't have fundamental engineering design flaws. I'll spend the money, just tell me what actually works.

P.S. the trimmer works fine otherwise. Maybe a little wimpy in terms of power output, but no hair pulling. Pretty noisy, but who cares. Just lubricate it properly. It's smaller than the Remington MB4900, but the blade width is almost as long. It's lightweight and very small, so I guess if you have gigantic man-hands it might not offer the best ergonomics. I actually prefer non-permanent batteries, so that was a plus for me. The trimmer heads aren't easily removable for cleaning. I don't think the body is very waterproof (aside from the obvious aforementioned blade rusting), so be wary about using it in the shower.

Well. When I used it the two times, it dude pull out some small blackheads and looked like it did a decent job. I've always been a little skeptical of these kinds of products and I don't feel like it does that much in general. I kind of use these for placebo and catharsis. It's comforting to see these strips pull ANYTHING out of your skin, so it makes me feel better about it. But it is completely acne-clearing and black head cleansing? Not really.

These are inexpensive, you get a bunch of them, and they are nice to use. I recommend it but if you have somewhat large pores and oily skin like me, don't expect much passed "Oh.....well that's nice." I wish it did more. But these are okay.

title: Amount of Product Seems Deceiving, But...
text: For anyone complaining about the amount of product in this... this lip butter contains 6.2 grams. A traditional Chapstick brand lip balm in a tube and even Blistex at the drugstore has 4.25 grams. The lip butter tube is a lot wider than Chapstick, so it appears to have less product when really it contains more than what you’d typically get for a lip balm in a swivel tube. Of course it’s more expensive, but that shouldn’t come as a surprise if you choose to buy a lip balm at Sephora (I purchased mine off Amazon because it’s slightly cheaper), and I don’t feel it should be rated any less just because of the price. If you want a lip balm that simply gets the job done, there are plenty of affordable options at the drugstore. This smells absolutely amazing and leaves your lips feeling silky smooth. It also leaves a nice shine, so I love layering it on top of liquid lipsticks for added hydration and a subtle gloss. I have really full lips that tend to get chapped quickly, so lip balms are a must for me but I prefer a thicker formula like the Bite Agave Lip Balm. I know some people say that one is too thick, but I find I have to apply less whereas with the lip butter, I’m constantly applying (but I don’t mind cause it smells and makes my lips feels so good!). If this was a bit richer/thicker, I’d give it a 5/5. However if you don’t like an extremely thick formula and don’t mind fragrance in your lip balms, you’d really enjoy this!!

title: Give your face a beauty massage!
text:
Before receiving Jane & Co.'s Roller and Gua Sha, I had never really used anything like it on my skin before. For me, it was simply wash, dry, moisturize and occasionally use makeup.

The roller and Gua Sha that I received is supposedly made of Jade. To me, it looked more like New Zealand Nephrite or even Aventurine. The packaging and product are nicely done, complete with a handwritten note from the proprietress of Jane & Co.

There is a small pamphlet with a set of instructions that includes a contact number where you can send a text to receive a complete guide on how to use both the roller and the Gua Sha. Instantly, you are given a URl to download the free eBook to go with the product.

To use either the roller or Gua Sha you simply chill the implements in the refrigerator or freezer. This extra coolness helps to shrink the pores and ease any puffiness that might be present.

Wash your face as normal to avoid pushing any dirt or impurities in your skin with the roller. Dry your face and apply a moisturizing oil such as coconut oil, jojoba, or argan oil which are particularly nourishing to the skin.

Take your now-cool roller and roll over your face, from the center outward. The included instructions suggest to pay particular attention to the area around the nose and under the eyes to aid in the draining and circulation of the lymph glands in those areas.

To use the Gua Sha, again, cleanse the face, and moisturize with an oil that is beneficial for the skin. Never, Never NEVER use mineral oil on the face (or anywhere else on the body for that matter).

Using moderate yet firm pressure in a gentle scraping motion to ease out tension from the face. I confess I haven't quite gotten the hang of the Gua Sha yet, but I am still working on it. The coolness of these facial tools feels excellent on my skin and it definitely is a relaxing practice to get into regularly.

This was my first time using a cellulite cream so I was a little intimidated. There is a slight fragrance to the product but not overwhelming. The texture feels creamy and absorbs into the skin. This product promises to firm, tighten, smooth and inhibit the formation of cellulite, quickly. I did not see immediate results after the first two uses however at 10 days into using this product I can see some results. The area that is receiving treatment feels firmer and smoother. I will continue to use this product in hopes that the tightening begins soon and no new formation of cellulite. The amount needed is a small amount so this container will last a long time. Overall I am a fan. With the results I am able to see already and the promise of more and at this rate I believe this will be a product that keeps its promise. The only reason I did not provide a 5 star review was due to the length of time needed to continuously rub the product into the skin (especially those harder to reach areas). Otherwise I was happy with this product. I received this product in exchange for my honest review
~Kathy

title: This would make a GREAT gift!
text:
In an effort to stretch the amount of time in between haircuts for my husband, I've begun giving him little beard trims here and there to straighten it out or shape it up. I'll also trim some of the curls around/above his ears and at the neckline so that it's less messy for work. I don't do anything drastic by any means, but I have a steady hand for that sort of cut.

Before, I was using whatever scissors I had around (I know, that's blasphemy in some circles). The most recent were KitchenAid kitchen shears (that I don't use for food items because I like my other kitchen scissors better), believe it or not. They are pretty sharp, so it's not quite as bad as it may sound.

At any rate, I knew that made for a sad hair trim, so I decided to upgrade. This kit happened to also have a beard comb, so that was just a bonus.

Oh man... I've been impressed across the board here. When I opened the Amazon box, there was a very nice display box by the manufacturer, with a magnetic lid and an opening made perfectly for the items. It makes for a great first impression, so this would be awesome as a gift.

You can tell just by looking that the scissors are nice, but when you pick them up, it's like the metal is buttery and soft to the touch. It feels classy, if that makes any sense. And while I've barely used them so far (I trimmed him up super recently), let me tell you... it's like night and day. It's such a smooth cut. This is how it's meant to feel when you cut hair - I just know it. I've never looked forward to giving a hair trim so much!

He already had a wooden beard comb, so I personally wasn't all that enthused about it like I was the scissors, but I have since been informed by him that the teeth are smaller on this one than on the other, which makes for a different beard combing experience. Now he has options, which he appreciates.

Oh, and the case is nice as well. :) Seriously, you'll feel good about giving this as a gift. From the moment they unwrap the box, they'll be pleased with what they see.

Please note, I received this item at a discount in exchange for my honest, unbiased opinion. I wouldn't steer anyone wrong, so if you have found this review to be helpful, please click the Yes box below. Thanks!

text:
I love Plant Therapy as a company for their pure, often organic, plant based ingredients.

The company that produces my favorite shea butter blended body butter decided not to produce it anymore. Or if they are, I can't find it anywhere. I scoured the internet looking for a replacement, read lots of reviews, did my research.

I decided on Plant Therapy's unscented body butter because I liked the idea of using my own essential oils to scent it if I wanted...or not!

The consistency is just okay. It's not particularly thick or rich. It moisturizes "okay". I wouldn't say it's any different or better than some hand lotions I have.

The unscented part is perfect. Don't detect a thing.

What bugs me the most (and if this part weren't happening, I would have scored this product much higher) is that it beads up after I massage it in. At first I thought I had really dry skin and it was flaking off as I rubbed it in. Nope. It's the cream. I have to use a towel to wipe off the annoying little beads that roll up and stick all over my hands.
It's annoying, and makes me not want to reach for it.

Sorry, Plant Therapy, I wish I loved this product more!

title: Isaic Invisible Wire Hair Extensions for Women 24 Inch Straight Heat Resistant Synthetic
text:
These arrived in a super cute plastic drawstring bag. Included were a pack of bobby pins, 2 stretchy nylon ponytail bands and 2 different sized wires to attach to the hairpiece.
The shade I selected (dark brown) is on the lighter side of 'dark brown' and I consider it more warm toned than a cool brown. It is thinned out at the ends to appear more natural but my piece is quite crooked and a little shorter in the middle. This is probably fine considering it will sag some during wear in that area and appear straight. I will have to trim it some because there is a significant difference between some of the long and short pieces.
The hair is really staticky and tangles easily. It feels silky in the lengths but a little rough at the ends. I suspect a razor may have been used to thin out the ends and caused the hair to feel rougher at the ends. There is a slight odor that will likely dissipate after some time outside of the plastic packaging.
It has four bendy wig clips attached to the lace foundation, which is nice for an secure installation. The clips have rounded rubberized tips that help secure in soft, fine or thin hair better and prevent digging at the scalp. I did notice that the clips that would lie on the sides of the head are not at the top most portion of the hairpiece. This may cause the weft to lift away from the scalp and show under your natural hair layer. The provided bobby pins will help some, but you will have to place them strategically to conceal them under thinner hair. I have added a picture to show a closer look at the clip on the weft.
I did not test the heat resistance of this extension because I plan to keep it straight and don't want any kinks I might add to the hair from heat styling.
Overall, it's a decent wired extension for the price if you're willing to accept or work with the negatives. For under $16 it's an inexpensive solution to adding length or thickness to your natural hair.

title: Portable and, once you get the hang of it, easy to use
text:
My hair type is fine but somewhat full and is shoulder length.

Before attempting to use this device I watched numerous YouTube videos of others using this it (or similar ones made by different manufacturer). I know that helped me A LOT in terms of figuring out how to best use this device. Oh and even these YouTubers, who review hair tools all the time, would sometimes get their hair caught in the barrel.

But once I got into a groove I found I could get my whole head curled in 10 and 15 minutes. Yes, by the 15-minute mark the battery was very low but I never fully ran out of power. Apparently this is a problem with this sort of device from other manufacturers as well.

My curls held up fairly well throughout the day but I'm going to try it on a higher heat setting next time to see if they will stay a little more curly even longer.

Will this be my "go-to" curler 24/7? No.

But I do love the fact that it is pretty easy to use, there is NO CHANCE of burning your finger/hand/head/ear/etc., and I especially like the cordless/portable aspect of it. If I'm getting ready with my friends or I'm sharing a hotel room with friends or family it would be extremely useful have a cordless device. Plus sometimes I just want to sit in front of the TV and do my hair and that's not always possible with some hair tools.

Yes, there was some leakage, but I took care to keep water away from the base. I also used rechargeable batteries, as I find battery failure the biggest problem with rechargeable devices.

title: Great Razor but "Automatic Charging" IS NOT Automatic
text: This is my first electric razer since shaving with a blade for the past 20+ years. I really like the convenience of shaving without cream, water, etc. The razor is nice and light and is very comfortable shaving. With a little practice, it gives a nice, clean shave. So far, I have not required any pre or post shaving lotion/cream to stay comfortable. It's also very easy to clean the heads..just put them under running water and out comes the hair. My only gripe is the "automatic charging" claim. Everytime you want to charge the razor, you have to plug it in. They recommend unplugging the charger when not in use because it shortens the battery life otherwise. It would be nice if you could just leave it plugged in and forget about it. However, so far it recharges very quickly, only taking about 15 minutes 1x/week and the "full charge" blinky light tells you when to unplug it. A previous review reported using it for 3 weeks without charging. If you run the battery dead, it takes only 3 minutes charging for 1 shave, so you don't have to worry about the charge state too much. Besides that one gripe, it's a great razor and I highly recommend it. While shaving with a blade I was skipping days because of the hassle. Now it's a shave every day, and I actually look forward to shaving!
